news.Title: Alphabet Stock Rises as Google Adds Two New TPU Variants
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Alphabet Inc. ( NASDAQ:GOOGL ) rose 2.26% in premarket after Bloomberg reported that Google is introducing two new versions of its tensor processing units, the custom AI chips it offers as an alternative to Nvidia Corp.'s ( NASDAQ:NVDA ). The TPU 8tx and 8i Max will be available next year, Google chip chief Amin Vahdat said in an interview.

Is GOOGL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The two are versions of this year's TPUs reconfigured for tasks customers have asked for. The 8tx handles secure work for government agencies and regulated industries, and pairs with a CPU from Advanced Micro Devices Inc. ( NASDAQ:AMD ) to encrypt data at the chip level. The 8i Max puts two TPU chips in a single package to run applications that need long context windows, such as drug discovery and coding. Google's chip unit once released a new AI processor every two years, but this year it launched two at once.

TPU customers include Apple Inc. ( NASDAQ:AAPL ), Meta Platforms Inc. ( NASDAQ:META ) and Oracle Corp. ( NYSE:ORCL ), which said last month that its cloud customers could use TPUs from next year. Bloomberg Intelligence expects TPU sales to top $135 billion by 2028, from an estimated $12 billion this year. Supply remains tight. Google said in its earnings report that every TPU it has available is already contracted to a customer.

news.Title: Amazon Generated $202 Billion in Quarterly Sales. Most of Its Operating Profit Came From Just 1 Business.
news.Content:
Take a moment and think about the last time you used Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN). Did you buy something? Pay for something to watch on Amazon Prime? Maybe you checked on the status of a package? All of these services make it easy to think of Amazon as an e-commerce business.

However, the company's latest results reveal something many people may not fully grasp: Most of its profit comes from a segment many people never knowingly use. It's Amazon Web Services (AWS), and it deserves a place in the sun.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Amazon rents the technology other businesses need

Explaining AWS and what it does can get complicated, so think of it this way: AWS rents out the computing power and storage businesses need to run online services. By renting, businesses can save money by avoiding the cost of building and maintaining the expensive equipment and facilities needed to run websites, store customer data, or support applications.

In addition, as artificial intelligence (AI) grows, AWS is becoming increasingly important. Organizations are scaling up their use of AI, and AWS provides much of the technological muscle to meet the surging demand. This raises an interesting question: How important is AWS to Amazon?

A smaller share of sales produces most of the operating profit

The answer is very important. AWS comprises about 23% of Amazon's revenue , but it contributes 63% of Amazon's operating profit. Therefore, AWS is a central concern for Amazon investors. When one segment drives roughly two-thirds of a company's profitability, investors scrutinize that segment's health.

One reason AWS stands out is the nature of Amazon's overall business. Its e-commerce segment drives a staggering amount of revenue, roughly $650 billion. However, historically, it hasn't been very profitable. Even with a recent widening, it generates an operating margin of about 8%. AWS, in contrast, has always been lucrative. Its operating margin stands at about 38%.

The reason is simple: Cloud computing benefits from enormous economies of scale. Once a data center is operational, it can take on many new clients. Those customers often sign enterprise subscription agreements with Amazon, delivering steady, highly profitable revenue. E-commerce, in contrast, is less profitable because of logistics, physical labor, and fuel costs.

Story Continues

Growing this business comes with a very large bill

However, AWS has a downside: its cost. Adding new facilities and equipment to fuel AWS's growth is expensive -- extremely expensive. It requires construction of enormous buildings, electrical systems, state-of-the-art equipment, and research. In the end, it means hundreds of billions of dollars -- $220 billion for 2026 -- in capital expenditures for the company.

AMZN Capital Expenditures (TTM) data by YCharts.

The point is that Amazon hopes to recoup this money many times over as the demand for AWS's services continues to grow, but, in the short term, markets are increasingly concerned that Amazon could be overspending.

Amazon's valuation is nearing multi-year lows

While Wall Street might fret over the size of Amazon's capital investments in AWS, its stock valuation could be a signal to investors. It currently trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 21.6. That's well below its three-year average of 39.3, and it's approaching its all-time-low P/E multiple of 18.2.

In other words, Amazon's giant investment spree could present long-term investors with a historic opportunity, or its low P/E multiple could be a warning sign. We simply don't know.

Buying Amazon stock today is a bet on AWS's future

When someone buys Amazon stock, they're not just buying an e-commerce company. Indeed, as Amazon's latest capital investments prove, the company is betting big on AWS. Amazon is as much a technology services supplier as it is a retailer. Buying Amazon stock now means believing in the company's vision: that its colossal investments in AWS will not only pay for themselves, but also lay the groundwork for decades of profits to come.

news.Title: Berkshire Hathaway's Top AI Holding Is Poised to Outperform
news.Content:
Even in his final years running Berkshire Hathaway , Warren Buffett continued to show he could expand his circle of competence. For the famed investor, the learning process never stopped.

This is precisely what he did when he initiated the buying of Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG) in Berkshire Hathaway's portfolio in the third quarter of last year, a move that current CEO Greg Abel followed up with additional purchases. Between the Class A and Class C shares, the artificial intelligence (AI) hyperscaler represents the conglomerate's fourth-largest position.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Berkshire Hathaway's top AI holding, Alphabet, is poised to outperform the market. Here's why.

The low valuation reflects uncertainty

The market might be starting to worry about AI spending. Alphabet's capital expenditures (capex) will total roughly $200 billion in 2026. Next year, management projects it will rise substantially. No one could have predicted five years ago that the capital-light internet giant would embark on a major spending spree.

Free cash flow is negative, coming in at $9.1 billion in the red during the third quarter. Alphabet has started to fund its AI aspirations with external capital. Long-term debt rose 169% from the end of last year to $125.1 billion.

The AI stock, which has soared 124% in the past 36 months (as of Nov. 4), now trades at 28% below its peak. Shares dipped following the announcement of Q3 financial results, as investors digested a miss on both the top and bottom lines, with Google Search sales slowing to 12%.

This exact setup plays into the hands of long-term investors who look at the next five years. It's impossible not to get interested in the current valuation. Alphabet shares trade at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 18.5. There's a lot of uncertainty surrounding AI. But this is a compelling entry point for one of the world's most outstanding businesses.

AI is the growth engine

According to sell-side analysts' consensus estimates, Alphabet will grow its operating income at a compound annual rate of 28.1% from 2025 to 2028. For a company of this scale, that growth rate is impressive. Revenue surged 25% year over year in the most recent quarter.

Alphabet's leadership position in AI is demonstrated by its Google Cloud segment, which posted a robust 103% Q3 sales gain. That continues a streak of accelerating growth, indicating how much demand there is from customers for AI capabilities. The backlog sits at $561 billion.

Story Continues

Google Cloud benefits from the AI boom by being able to sell specific software and hardware to enterprise clients. Additionally, Alphabet's full suite of products and services also improves with the integration of AI.

While the next few years are impossible to forecast and introduce heightened uncertainty, this company is in a favorable position as it rides the AI wave. The stock can be a big winner.

news.Title: Intel took 25 years to get back to its dot-com peak — and lost it in 6 months: Chart of the Day
news.Content:
Half off sounds like a deal. On Wall Street, it can be the start of a much bigger sale.

Right now, Intel ( INTC ), Arm ( ARM ), Sandisk ( SNDK ), and CoreWeave ( CRWV ) are among the AI darlings trading at less than half their 2026 highs, and chip stocks just lost nearly 30% in five weeks .

Stocks are rallying early Monday, and most chip stocks are extending Friday's bounce. Nvidia ( NVDA ) is a notable exception , initially falling 8% but clawing back losses, while Intel rallies over 3%.

Veteran trader Michael Martin isn't biting. "Lower prices mean lower market cap. It doesn't mean better value," said Martin, founder of TraderMindset.com, who works with Wall Street legend Victor "Trader Vic" Sperandeo .

"I keep hearing Gordon Gekko's voice in the back of my mind — 'A fool and their money are lucky to get together in the first place,' " he told Yahoo Finance.

His bigger worry is traders who talk themselves into holding on. "Don't confuse investor language with trader language," he said. "If you're a trader, be a trader."

Intel's long, strange trip

Martin's favorite example is Intel. "A lot of people think like, wow, Intel was 125. I can get it now for half that. It's a bargain," he said. "But at 55 or whatever it is, you can see 40 long before you're gonna see 140."

Intel's own history backs him up. The stock peaked at about $75 in August 2000, was down to half by October, and kept going, bottoming near $13 in 2002.

It didn't close above that dot-com peak again until April 24, 2026. Loyal holders got a victory lap to about $141 in June before the AI selloff dragged the stock back below its old high on Oct. 30. Intel closed Friday at $56, still up about 50% this year.

Intel had plenty of company. Five other dot-com leaders also kept falling after first being cut in half, from another 30% for Microsoft ( MSFT ) to another 88% for Amazon ( AMZN ), according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

None of that makes investor language wrong. Amazon now trades at nearly 50 times its 2000 peak.

But that's an investor's clock. Trouble starts when a trade gets judged on one.

How to keep a trade from becoming an accident

Martin, a discretionary trader for four decades, offers guidelines, not rules.

Size it small. If you're just scalping or trading a bounce, think $100 for every $100,000 in an account, or one-tenth of 1%.

Don't take losses home. "If you buy something on Tuesday … if it's showing a loss by Friday, it has to trade."

Know your clock. Younger investors "can buy quality names and hold them forever." Near retirement, "your first order of business here is to play superior defense."

Story Continues

When in doubt, sit it out. "Harvest some cash here and wait."

Martin's last guideline comes from hedge fund legend Paul Tudor Jones: risk $1 only where you see $5 or more of upside, a risk-reward ratio of at least 5-to-1. It "doesn't mean it's gonna show up," Martin said, but the payoff has to be there before you trade.

"You need to see massive amounts of asymmetry in this type of a market."

Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.

Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com .

news.Title: Nvidia stock sinks 4% as chipmaker investigates CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with alleged Chinese spy
news.Content:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock fell as much as 8% before trimming losses on Monday after the chipmaker's board announced it would investigate the relationship between CEO Jensen Huang and a woman whom the intelligence community believes could be a Chinese Spy.

In a Sunday memo to employees, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair, apologizing to his family and staff while pledging full cooperation with an independent board review. Wall Street analysts quickly flagged the heightened 'key-person risk' for the world's leading AI chipmaker.

"Jensen is the core DNA of Nvidia, and its AI success and ambitions are heavily tied to him staying on as CEO. Jensen is not replaceable," Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives wrote on Monday morning.

A look across the semiconductor sector showed the risk damage was largely contained to Nvidia. Shares of rival AMD ( AMD ) bounced 8% following a rating upgrade to Buy from Oppenheimer analysts. Broadcom ( AVGO ) rose 6%, while Intel ( INTC ) edged up 2%.

Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ( TSM ), which manufactures Nvidia chips, rose nearly 2%, while semiconductor equipment maker ASML ( ASML ) also gained 3%.

Storage maker SanDisk ( SNDK ) moved up 1%. Memory chip maker Micron Technology ( MU ) rose more than 1%, while SK Hynix ( SKHY ) was little changed.

Other chip-related stocks include processor maker Qualcomm ( QCOM ) and semicondcutor designer Arm Holdings ( ARM ), both moving minimally.

Meanwhile, Alphabet ( GOOGL ) shares rose more than 2% in early trading on Monday after the tech giant introduced two new tensor processing units, or TPUs. Alphabet has been accelerating its homegrown AI chip business, introducing four TPU systems in a single year.

news.Title: Tesla to return some Cybertruck deposits, as enthusiasts swoop in ahead of halt
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Amid a rush of new reservations for the Cybertruck, following news that production of the unconventional vehicle will end soon, Tesla's (NASDAQ:TSLA) announced it will return some deposits.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

CEO Elon Musk announced Monday on X that the company has more Cybertruck orders than it can fulfill before shutting down the vehicle's production line in approximately eight months.

"The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate," Musk wrote. He added that Tesla would try to manufacture as many trucks as possible before closing the line but would have to return deposits to many customers.

The announcement follows Tesla's decision last week to wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory. Rather than continuing to devote manufacturing capacity to the distinctive electric pickup, Tesla plans to redirect those resources toward increasing production of its Cybercab autonomous robotaxi.

It's Not About Profitability, Musk Insists

Musk was quick to push back against reports suggesting the Cybertruck is being discontinued because it is unprofitable.

According to the Tesla chief, the decision comes down to opportunity cost. He argues that the complexity involved in manufacturing the Cybertruck makes it more valuable for the company to use that factory capacity to produce additional Cybercabs.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The explanation comes against the backdrop of disappointing sales. Tesla delivered the first Cybertrucks in late 2023, but U.S. sales fell 48% in 2025 to 20,237 vehicles, according to Kelley Blue Book.

Could the Final Cybertrucks Become Collector's Items?

The planned production shutdown could create an interesting twist in the Cybertruck's story. While some reservation holders may be disappointed to learn they won't receive their trucks, collectors and Tesla enthusiasts may see an opportunity to own a piece of the company's automotive history.

With production potentially ending within months, the remaining Cybertrucks could represent the final examples of one of the most unconventional vehicles ever brought to market. The distinctive stainless-steel design, polarizing styling and ambitious promises surrounding the truck could give surviving examples a place in automotive collections.

Story Continues

Whether that translates into long-term collector value remains to be seen. Production numbers, future demand and the condition of individual vehicles will all matter. Still, the prospect of a relatively short production run may encourage some buyers to secure a Cybertruck while they still can.

Musk himself expressed admiration for the unconventional pickup, declaring: "There will never be another vehicle like it."

For Tesla, however, the priority is shifting. The company has roughly eight months to build as many Cybertrucks as possible before turning its attention toward the Cybercab. For customers and collectors alike, the countdown may already be underway.

news.Title: Amazon AWS Revenues Up 39% in Q3 as Cloud Rivals Gain Pace: Hold Stock?
news.Content:
Amazon AMZN reported a 39% year-over-year surge in Amazon Web Services ("AWS") revenues to $46 billion in the third quarter of 2026. That was the cloud unit's fastest growth in nearly five years, and it lifted AWS' annualized revenue run rate to $184 billion. The acceleration comes as cloud rivals Microsoft MSFT, Nvidia NVDA and Alphabet GOOGL step up their AI infrastructure push, prompting the question of whether investors should hold the stock or wait for a better entry point.

AWS remained the company's profit engine, with segment operating income rising to $17.8 billion from $11.4 billion a year ago, implying an operating margin of roughly 38.7%. Consolidated net sales grew 12% to $201.9 billion, while operating income climbed to $28.1 billion, translating into a record operating margin of 13.9%. A Prime Day shift into the second quarter reduced third-quarter growth by about 400 basis points.

Amazon shares have returned 12.3% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the Zacks Internet – Commerce industry and the Zacks Retail-Wholesale sector's growth of 2.9% and 4.5%, respectively. This outperformance reflects investor confidence in accelerating AWS growth and record consolidated margins, though heavy AI spending and free cash flow pressure have kept the stock's gains relatively measured.

AMZN's Year-to-Date Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AI Demand Strengthens AWS Fundamentals

AWS' AI portfolio is gaining traction across the enterprise base. Spending by Fortune 500 companies on Amazon Bedrock rose nearly 7X year over year, while total token volume grew nearly 17X. Bedrock added OpenAI's GPT-6 family and Anthropic's latest Claude models. Tens of thousands of customers now use Bedrock AgentCore, and they deployed twice as many agents in the third quarter as in the prior three quarters combined. Amazon also introduced TorchNeuron, enabling developers to run existing PyTorch code on Trainium without rewriting it. Additionally, AWS signed new agreements with Meta, OpenAI, Oracle, Qualcomm, Verizon and NATO, among others.

Recent AWS Developments

Amazon's newsroom highlights steady momentum in October and November 2026. On Oct. 8, AWS launched its Golden Age of Science Accelerator, committing up to $50 million in cloud credits to support the expansion of the Genesis Mission. Classmethod signed a five-year collaboration to help Japanese enterprises adopt AI. Further, AWS expanded Kiro's reach in education through BINUS University in Indonesia. In November, AWS launched Semarak AI Malaysia, a national program bringing AI tools to government officers, students and local software companies. AWS also made its AI-powered security service, Continuum, generally available and agreed to acquire DuckLabs, the company behind DuckDB.

Story Continues

Steep Valuation and Competition in Cloud are Overhangs

From a valuation standpoint, AMZN stock appears overvalued, trading at a forward 12-month price/earnings ratio of 23.43X, higher than the industry's 20.33X. Amazon has a Value Score of D. The premium suggests that much of the near-term AI optimism is already priced in.

AMZN's Valuation Appears Steep

Competitive pressure, however, remains a key watchpoint. Microsoft continues to leverage its enterprise software relationships to win AI workloads, while Alphabet is pairing its cloud platform with in-house AI models and chips. Nvidia, which also signed a new agreement with AWS, plays a dual role as a critical accelerator supplier and a provider of its own cloud services. As Microsoft and Alphabet accelerate data center buildouts and Nvidia deepens its AI computing presence, AWS must sustain innovation and capacity additions to defend market share. Competition, however, is intensifying. Microsoft's Azure revenues surged 48% to $33.2 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, while Alphabet's Google Cloud revenues jumped 103% to $30.7 billion in third-quarter 2026, backed by a $561 billion backlog. Nvidia's Data Center revenues soared 117% to $89 billion in second-quarter fiscal 2027. Although AWS remains the largest cloud platform, Microsoft and Alphabet are growing faster, while Nvidia, also an AWS partner, is ramping its Vera Rubin platform across rival clouds, including Google Cloud and Azure.

Q4 Guidance and Capex Temper AMZN's Near-Term Visibility

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Amazon expects net sales between $240 billion and $247 billion, indicating 12-16% year-over-year growth, including an unfavorable foreign exchange impact of approximately 60 basis points. Operating income is projected between $28.5 billion and $33.5 billion compared with $25 billion in the year-ago quarter, while advertising revenues are expected to grow in the high teens. Management expects AWS revenue growth to exceed 40% in both 2027 and 2028, signaling robust long-term demand.

However, the investment burden is substantial. Amazon expects 2026 cash capital expenditures of approximately $220 billion, with third-quarter cash capex alone reaching $75.9 billion, primarily for AWS and AI infrastructure. Although trailing 12-month operating cash flow rose 29% to $168.3 billion, free cash flow swung to an outflow of $42.4 billion from an inflow of $14.8 billion a year earlier.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMZN's 2026 earnings is pegged at $12.90 per share, indicating an 79.92% increase from the figure reported in 2025. This strong earnings trajectory supports the share price outlook. Investors should hold AMZN despite the premium because AWS' accelerating, highly profitable growth offers durable long-term earnings power.

Amazon.com, Inc. Price and Consensus

Amazon.com, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Amazon.com, Inc. Quote

Conclusion

Amazon's accelerating AWS growth, expanding AI adoption and record margins provide solid fundamental reasons to stay invested. However, elevated capex, negative free cash flow, intensifying cloud competition and a stretched valuation limit near-term upside. AMZN currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting existing investors should hold the stock while new investors wait for a better entry point. news.Title: What's in Store for These 3 Networking Stocks This Earnings Season?
news.Content:
Increasing investments in enterprise digitalization, AI-led network upgrades, higher demand for cloud computing, big data, network security and next-generation connectivity solutions are reshaping the outlook for participants in the Zacks Computer - Networking industry.

The proliferation of AI workloads and hyperscale data centers is accelerating investments in high-speed interconnects, optical networking and Ethernet switches. With the explosive growth in data traffic, demand for advanced routing, switching and network optimization solutions is expected to remain strong.

Further, growing deployments of fiber networks, Wi-Fi 7 and secure networking solutions are expanding the addressable market. AI workloads require a major upgrade to observability infrastructure. There is a greater need for continuous monitoring of hybrid environments and tighter security amid rising attacks. This is likely to favor prospects for prominent industry players.

Nonetheless, cautious IT spending amid heightened uncertainty over global macroeconomic conditions and volatile supply-chain dynamics due to tariff troubles continues to be concerning for the participants.

The Computer Networking industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. For the third quarter of 2026, the tech sector's earnings are expected to be up 45.4% as per the latest Earnings Preview report

A few major networking companies are scheduled to report their quarterly results in the coming days. Let's see how things might have shaped up for these players, including Cisco Systems CSCO, RADCOM Ltd RDCM and Digi International DGII, before their announcements.

Networking Stocks to Watch

Cisco is slated to report first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 12, after the closing bell. In the last reported quarter, the company's non-GAAP earnings per share beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.3%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal first-quarter revenues sits at $18.09 billion, up 21.5%. It generated revenues of $14.88 billion in the prior-year quarter. The consensus mark for earnings is currently pinned at $1.33 per share, indicating an increase of 33% from the year-ago quarter.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Cisco expects revenues between $18 billion and $18.2 billion. Non-GAAP earnings are projected between $1.32 and $1.34 per share.

Cisco's fiscal first-quarter performance is likely to have benefited from demand for AI Infrastructure solutions, with hyperscaler demand acting as a key catalyst. In the last reported quarter, hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders totaled $4 billion, taking fiscal 2026 orders to $9.3 billion, roughly 4.5 times the fiscal 2025 level. Strong demand for its Silicon One based systems and Acacia optical networking solutions is expected to support growth. Fiscal 2026 hyperscaler AI orders were about 60% Silicon One-based systems and 40% optics. Acacia generated more than $1 billion in orders in the fiscal fourth quarter.

On the last earnings call, CSCO noted that accelerating agentic AI is driving a "networking super cycle" resulting in increasing demand for its Networking stack to support inferencing across cloud, on-premise and edge environments. Acacia business has also been witnessing strong growth as hyperscalers deploy both 400G and 800G coherent optics.

Security revenues grew 14% in the fiscal fourth quarter, supported by Splunk, network security and SASE solutions. Management expects security revenues to grow in the mid-to-high single digits in the fiscal first quarter.

news.Title: MercadoLibre's Growth Strategy Puts Profit Margins to the Test
news.Content:
MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI is prioritizing customer engagement and marketplace expansion even as these investments weigh on margins. In the third quarter of 2026, net revenues and financial income increased 45% year over year to $10,750 million, yet operating income slipped 6% to $676 million. Operating margin declined 40 basis points sequentially to 6.3%, reflecting the cost of more free shipping, expanded fulfillment capacity ahead of peak season and increased affiliate marketing spending in Brazil.

Management identified a 60-basis-point sequential margin headwind from net shipping costs, including expenses associated with network expansion. Lower free-shipping thresholds encouraged customers to place smaller, more frequent orders, reducing revenue per shipment even as volumes increased. Higher energy prices added transportation costs, while fulfillment square footage expanded nearly 20% quarter over quarter ahead of peak demand. The expansion also brought temporary recruitment expenses. Meanwhile, sales and marketing spending rose 40 basis points sequentially to 11.6% of revenues as MercadoLibre stepped up affiliate investment in Brazil.

Despite these cost pressures, MercadoLibre reported measurable improvements in logistics efficiency. In Brazil, items sold increased 45% year over year, while cost per shipment fell 5% year over year in local currency and 14% from the first quarter of 2025 before the lower free-shipping threshold took effect. Management also reported that free & slow shipments in the R$19-R$79 price range in Brazil became variable contribution-positive as a group for the first time in September. Shipments per route reached a new high during the quarter.

These improvements show that MercadoLibre is working to lower delivery costs by handling more orders and improving efficiency. However, the company continues to balance the costs of expanding its shipping network and attracting customers against the efficiency gains from higher shipment volumes.

How Does MercadoLibre Stack Up Against Its Industry?

MercadoLibre, which competes with Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN and Sea Limited SE, has seen its shares tumble 17.2% over the past three months compared with the industry's 8.7% decline. While Amazon shares have fallen 6.7%, Sea Limited has plunged 34% in the aforementioned period.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Does MercadoLibre's Current Valuation Suggest?

From a valuation standpoint, MercadoLibre's forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 28.66, higher than the industry average of 20.31. However, the stock is trading below its 12-month median level of 33.91. MercadoLibre is trading at a premium to Amazon (forward 12-month P/E of 23.43) and Sea Limited (14.97).

Story Continues

What Do Earnings Estimates Signal for MercadoLibre?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MercadoLibre's current fiscal-year earnings per share has increased by 12 cents to $38.21 over the past seven days. However, the consensus estimate for the next fiscal year has declined by 10 cents to $55.09 during the same period.

The consensus estimate for MercadoLibre's current fiscal-year sales indicates year-over-year growth of 45.1%, while the consensus estimate for earnings per share suggests a 3% decline. For the next fiscal year, the consensus estimates project sales and earnings growth of 28.9% and 44.2%, respectively.

MELI's Investment Case

MercadoLibre's strong marketplace growth, rising customer engagement and expanding fintech ecosystem support its long-term prospects. Improving logistics efficiency and increasing purchase frequency strengthen its competitive positioning. However, elevated shipping costs, continued investments and margin pressure constrain near-term profitability. Its premium valuation also warrants caution despite encouraging revenue growth and improving operational efficiencies. MELI currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). news.Title: 黃仁勳風波壓不住台股！陳龍曝止跌訊號浮現：看好這幾檔超跌股
news.Content:
台股今（9）日在美國科技股反彈、國安基金啟動第10次護盤及金管會祭出限空措施等利多激勵下，展開強勁反攻，加權指數終場大漲1960.06點，收在41661.70點，創下史上第二大收盤漲點，成交金額達8379.29億元。盤中最高衝上42349.36點，一度大漲逾2600點，上市櫃共有237檔個股亮燈漲停。 資深分析師陳龍 認為，這波急跌已讓市場籌碼大幅洗牌，多項止跌訊號陸續浮現，先前遭無差別殺低的優質超跌股，有機會逐步展現應有價值。

【融資追繳壓力升高 國安基金進場激勵反攻】

回顧日前台股連續重挫，市場恐慌情緒升高，融資追繳戶數也明顯增加。11月5日單日融資追繳戶數達2352戶，整戶擔保維持率降至159.77%，創近3個月低點，隔日大盤再度遭遇重挫，市場賣壓沉重。

不過，隨著國安基金宣布啟動史上第10次護盤，加上金管會祭出限空等穩定措施，美國科技股也出現反彈，台股9日強勢回升。台積電（2330）終場上漲100元，收2235元，漲幅4.68%，聯發科（2454）、台達電（2308）、國巨（2327）等權值股也強勢攻上漲停，帶動多頭氣勢。

陳龍在《股市尊龍》節目中指出，這波下跌雖然讓投資人承受不小壓力，卻也讓市場過度擁擠的槓桿籌碼快速出清。他以電影《明天過後》形容這段過程，就像市場短暫進入冰河時期，雖然寒冷難熬，但經過一輪洗牌後，籌碼結構有機會變得更加乾淨。

【黃仁勳風波只是短線噪音 AI需求沒有消失】

針對近期黃仁勳個人新聞及相關國安疑慮引發市場對AI供應鏈的擔憂，陳龍認為，這類消息可能在短時間內影響投資人情緒，卻不代表AI產業需求就此反轉。

他指出，AI發展並非只靠單一企業或個人推動，OpenAI、Anthropic等科技業者持續投入算力建設，背後更有全球企業對AI應用的龐大需求支撐。即使美國政策或部分建設計畫出現變化，算力需求仍可能轉往其他地區發展，全球AI資料中心建置趨勢並未因此消失。

陳龍認為，AI是繼電力與網際網路之後的重要產業變革，短期政治因素或市場雜音或許造成震盪，但不應直接與產業長期趨勢畫上等號。

【止跌訊號陸續浮現 優質超跌股有望反彈】

陳龍表示，觀察這波台股反彈，融資大幅減少、國安基金進場、台積電止跌，以及中小型股大量漲停等現象，都讓市場出現止跌回升的訊號。他認為，先前大盤急跌造成不少基本面不差的個股遭到錯殺，隨著恐慌情緒降溫，股價有機會逐步回歸基本面。

他也點名幾檔個股作為觀察例子。 群聯（8299） 宣布買回庫藏股，展現公司對自身價值的態度； 世芯-KY（3661） 法說會釋出營運展望，預期第4季營收有機會再創新高，2027年營收也看好成長； 台達電（2308 ）則在這波反彈中強勢攻上漲停，矽光子相關概念股 同欣電（6271） 也亮燈漲停。

陳龍認為，當市場從極度恐慌逐步回穩，投資人更應回頭檢視企業基本面與產業趨勢，而不是被短線利空牽著走。

news.Title: INTC Stock Down 57% in the Past 6 Months: Should You Exercise Caution?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC has plummeted 56.5% over the past six months compared with the industry's decline of 19.1%, lagging peers like NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD. While NVIDIA stock is down 14.9%, Advanced Micro has lost 2.1% over this period.

Six-Month INTC Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Soft Q4 Guidance Triggers Rout

Intel faces near-term challenges as its subdued fourth-quarter 2026 outlook raises concerns about slowing demand and margin pressures. The company expects revenues between $15 billion and $16 billion for the fourth quarter, down from $16.5 billion reported in the third quarter. Management expects Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) segment revenues to decline more than 20% sequentially. Guidance incorporates an estimated $300 million revenue impact from a manufacturing disruption at its Israel facility.

Non-GAAP earnings are projected at 25 cents per share, significantly below the preceding quarter's 52 cents. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to contract to 38% from 44.1% in the third quarter, indicating mounting profitability pressures. Weakness in the PC market, exacerbated by elevated memory prices and component shortages, is weighing on demand. Management expects the PC slowdown to persist at least through the first half of 2027. Moreover, supply constraints are limiting Intel's ability to capitalize on robust demand for its data center processors.

U.S.-China Trade Spat Hurts Top-Line Growth

China accounted for more than 24% of Intel's total revenues in 2025, making it the company's second-largest market after the United States. However, China's purported move to replace U.S.-made chips with domestic alternatives significantly affected INTC's revenue prospects. The directive to phase out foreign chips from key telecom networks by 2027 underscores Beijing's accelerating efforts to reduce reliance on Western technology amid escalating U.S.-China trade and tariff tensions.

As Washington tightens restrictions on high-tech exports to China, Beijing has intensified its push for self-sufficiency in critical industries. This shift poses a dual challenge for Intel, as it faces potential market restrictions and increased competition from domestic chipmakers. In addition, weaker spending across consumer and enterprise markets, especially in China, resulted in elevated customer inventory levels.

Foundry Business Spurs Revival

Despite the hiccups, Intel is making significant progress in its turnaround efforts, supported by improving execution and growing momentum in its foundry business. In the third quarter of 2026, Intel Foundry revenues surged 58% year over year to $6.7 billion, driven by higher wafer volumes from Intel 18A, Intel 3 and Intel 4 process nodes, along with increased advanced manufacturing activity. The segment's operating loss narrowed to $1.85 billion from $2.32 billion a year earlier, indicating improving cost efficiency. The growing adoption of advanced manufacturing nodes and better utilization of fabrication facilities are expected to strengthen Intel's competitive position and support its efforts to restore sustainable growth.

Intel's aggressive push into next-generation semiconductor manufacturing is another key catalyst for its long-term growth prospects. The company has commenced high-volume production using its Intel 18A technology, while the enhanced Intel 18A-P process entered risk production in June 2026. Intel is also advancing its next-generation 14A technology, releasing the 0.9 process design kit in October to facilitate customer evaluation and chip development. Collaborations with ASML, Applied Materials and Lam Research are strengthening its manufacturing capabilities, while advanced packaging innovations are positioning it to capitalize on rising demand for AI and high-performance computing chips. These initiatives could help Intel attract external foundry customers, diversify its revenue streams and improve economies of scale.

Story Continues

INTC to Gain From Solid Industry Investments

The proliferation of generative AI applications is driving significant investments in data center infrastructure. Although GPUs remain at the center of AI computing, CPUs continue to play an important role in supporting AI workloads. This is creating incremental opportunities for Intel's Xeon portfolio. The momentum is encouraging as AI-related infrastructure spending is likely to remain healthy, providing Intel with an opportunity to capitalize on rising compute requirements.

Intel's innovative AI solutions are set to benefit the broader semiconductor ecosystem by driving down costs, improving performance and fostering an open, scalable AI environment. The company is ramping Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake products based on its advanced 18A process technology. Increasing adoption of these products, coupled with an eventual enterprise PC refresh cycle, should support the client business over the long run. The company is also expanding its presence in edge computing and physical AI applications, including robotics. These emerging markets could broaden Intel's addressable opportunity beyond traditional PCs.

Estimate Revision

Earnings estimates for Intel for 2026 have moved up 149.2% to $1.47 over the past year, and the same for 2027 has increased 55.3% to $1.77. The positive estimate revision depicts bullish sentiment for the stock.

End Note

Intel's innovative AI solutions hold immense promise for the broader semiconductor ecosystem. By addressing the challenges of scalability, performance and interoperability, it is paving the way for widespread AI adoption across enterprises worldwide. Management is focusing on simplifying parts of its portfolio to unlock efficiencies and create value. Solid capital infusion in the industry is helping Intel revive its foundry business to spur growth. The uptrend in estimate revisions further portrays positive sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

However, margin woes amid strict export restrictions, unfavorable product mix and elevated customer inventory levels weigh on its bottom line. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), Intel appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and investors could be better off if they exercise caution and stay invested for long-term gains. news.Title: 曾預示科技股退潮 如今這項指標又閃黃燈！賣壓恐波及整個美股
news.Content:
市場上持續醞釀、卻多半未受注意的資金輪動，突然加速了。

鑑於先前美股個股間的相關性已降至極低水準，上週四大盤出現強烈拉回並不令人意外，市場回歸均值不過是時間問題。當相關係數偏低時，意味著行情已不再像往常一樣，帶動個股普遍水漲船高。

SPDR標普500 ETF（SPY）與景順標普500等權重ETF（RSP）的比值，幾乎精準預示了資金轉進科技股的高峰，以及隨後的退潮。

如今，這項比值正逼近下一個關鍵水準，可能促使資金重新流向科技股與超大型權值股，也可能意味著整體市場將面臨撤資賣壓。

SPY與RSP比值逼近關鍵回檔點

SPY與RSP的比值，已來到自2025年6月以來交易區間的最下緣。接下來究竟會跌破區間、進一步收縮，還是回升擴大，仍有待觀察，但這道下緣的重要性已不容忽視。

標普500指數給予市值較大企業的權重，高於市值較小的企業；標普500等權重指數則賦予每家公司相同權重。因此，SPY與RSP的比值，可用來衡量大型權值股究竟是在支撐還是拖累標普500指數。

比值跌破下緣，意味著SPY持續落後RSP，但無法單憑這點判斷兩者的漲跌情況。可能是SPY下跌、RSP跌得較少，也可能是SPY下跌、RSP上漲，或是兩者都上漲，但RSP漲得更多。

不過，考量到科技股與超大型權值股一直是人工智慧（AI）交易及大盤上漲的主要推力，這意味著AI類股可能再度成為表現落後的族群。

相關性回升 權值股恐落後

比值收縮，意味著市場相關性可能隨時間提高，也就是標普500成分股開始朝相同方向波動。

回溯至1990年，標普500指數與標普500等權重指數之間的60日滾動相關係數，從未如此低迷。這項過去通常接近1的相關係數，在11月3日降至僅0.56。

這兩項指數追蹤的是同一批標普500成分股，只是計算方式不同。若兩者的相關係數要重新回升至接近1，走勢就必須開始趨於一致、朝相同方向移動。

如果比值持續跌破下緣，同時相關係數回升至接近1，先前主導兩項指數走勢分歧的超大型權值股，很可能成為表現落後的族群。

目前情勢顯示，即使這波資金輪動告一段落，科技股暫時重獲青睞，漲勢也不太可能無限期延續，相關交易仍可能在未來某個時間點繼續退潮。

隱含相關性也處於低檔

衡量標普500前50大成分股選擇權定價關係的芝加哥選擇權交易所（Cboe）3個月隱含相關性指數，也顯示近期市場相關性極低。

news.Content:
Investing.com -- JPMorgan has removed Alphabet from its Analyst Focus List and added Meta Platforms, betting that AI-driven advertising gains and emerging monetization opportunities make Meta the more attractive internet stock.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Analyst Doug Anmuth said the bank remains Overweight on Alphabet but sees stronger near-term earnings momentum at Meta following third-quarter results. Amazon and Meta are now JPMorgan's preferred picks across its internet coverage.

"Coming out of 3Q earnings, Meta's relative advertising strength is more evident than ever," Anmuth wrote in a November 9 note.

Meta's advertising revenue jumped 26% year over year in the third quarter, with North American growth accelerating to 33%. The company generated approximately $13 billion in incremental advertising revenue, roughly twice the additional dollars generated by Google Search, JPMorgan estimated. The bank expects Meta's Family of Apps advertising revenue to surpass Google Search in the fourth quarter and beyond.

JPMorgan attributed Meta's strength to AI-driven improvements in ad retrieval, ranking and targeting, which are boosting advertiser conversions. Its large advertiser base and exposure across industries also provide some insulation from weakness in specific advertising categories.

Beyond its core advertising business, the bank sees potential in Meta's AI products. Its Muse assistant has attracted 10 million sign-ups in the U.S. and Canada, with a 25% daily-to-monthly active user ratio. Anmuth also highlighted the enterprise opportunity for Meta Model API and Muse Code.

Alphabet's AI monetization challenge

Alphabet's removal from the list reflects concerns about the pace of AI monetization rather than a deterioration in JPMorgan's overall view. The bank reiterated its Overweight rating but warned that improvements in AI-powered search monetization could take time.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Google Search revenue growth slowed to 12% in the third quarter, from 19% in the first quarter and 17% in the second, despite Google reporting its fastest query growth in five years. Management cited foreign exchange as the largest factor behind the deceleration, alongside weaker spending from Asian retailers following changes to the EU's de minimis exemption and reduced media and entertainment spending after the World Cup.

Story Continues

Investors must now assess whether Google's AI Mode can generate comparable advertising economics to traditional search. While longer, more contextual queries could improve advertiser conversions, AI agents could also consolidate multiple searches into a single transaction, reducing advertising opportunities while increasing computing costs.

JPMorgan also flagged pressure on Alphabet's cash flow from its AI infrastructure spending. Free cash flow was negative for a second consecutive quarter, while management maintained its 2026 capital expenditure forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion and said spending would increase significantly in 2027.

Google Cloud remains a bright spot, with revenue surging 103% year over year and backlog reaching $561 billion. However, the bank cautioned that TPU system sales contributed meaningfully to growth, without a separate disclosure of their revenue and margins. It also expects margins to face pressure from additional computing capacity arrangements through at least the first quarter of 2027.

Cloud growth offers evidence of AI returns

JPMorgan sees increasingly tangible returns from AI investments across the internet sector, particularly in cloud computing and advertising.

AWS revenue grew 39% year over year in the third quarter, while Google Cloud expanded 103%. Their combined backlogs exceeded $1.1 trillion, providing substantial visibility into future demand. Amazon now expects AWS revenue growth of more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028.

For JPMorgan, however, Meta offers a more immediate way to capture AI returns. Its technology is already improving the economics of its core advertising business, while new consumer and enterprise products offer additional growth opportunities.

The bank's revised Analyst Focus List is now Amazon and Meta, leaving Alphabet Overweight but no longer among its preferred internet stocks.

news.Title: Rambus (RMBS) Forms 'Hammer Chart Pattern': Time for Bottom Fishing?
news.Content:
Shares of Rambus (RMBS) have been struggling lately and have lost 12% over the past week. However, a hammer chart pattern was formed in its last trading session, which could mean that the stock found support with bulls being able to counteract the bears. So, it could witness a trend reversal down the road.

The formation of a hammer pattern is considered a technical indication of nearing a bottom with likely subsiding of selling pressure. But this is not the only factor that makes a bullish case for the stock. On the fundamental side, strong agreement among Wall Street analysts in raising earnings estimates for this memory chip designer enhances its prospects of a trend reversal.

Understanding Hammer Chart and the Technique to Trade It

This is one of the popular price patterns in candlestick charting. A minor difference between the opening and closing prices forms a small candle body, and a higher difference between the low of the day and the open or close forms a long lower wick (or vertical line). The length of the lower wick being at least twice the length of the real body, the candle resembles a 'hammer.'

In simple terms, during a downtrend, with bears having absolute control, a stock usually opens lower compared to the previous day's close, and again closes lower. On the day the hammer pattern is formed, maintaining the downtrend, the stock makes a new low. However, after eventually finding support at the low of the day, some amount of buying interest emerges, pushing the stock up to close the session near or slightly above its opening price.

When it occurs at the bottom of a downtrend, this pattern signals that the bears might have lost control over the price. And, the success of bulls in stopping the price from falling further indicates a potential trend reversal.

Hammer candles can occur on any timeframe -- such as one-minute, daily, weekly -- and are utilized by both short-term as well as long-term investors.

Like every technical indicator, the hammer chart pattern has its limitations. Particularly, as the strength of a hammer depends on its placement on the chart, it should always be used in conjunction with other bullish indicators.

Here's What Increases the Odds of a Turnaround for RMBS

An upward trend in earnings estimate revisions that RMBS has been witnessing lately can certainly be considered a bullish indicator on the fundamental side. That's because empirical research shows that trends in earnings estimate revisions are strongly correlated with near-term stock price movements.

Story Continues

The consensus EPS estimate for the current year has increased 4.8% over the last 30 days. This means that the Wall Street analysts covering RMBS are majorly in agreement about the company's potential to report better earnings than what they predicted earlier.

news.Title: Google's chip business is on a faster track than Nvidia's own AI boom
news.Content: Nvidia ( NVDA ) is investigating its own CEO. Google is busy building the chips that could take its customers. Nvidia is down more than 5% premarket, trading at its lowest level since April 7, as its board looks into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy . Alphabet ( GOOGL ) is up about 2%. It's the latest chapter in Wall Street's first $4.5 trillion CEO scandal . Google introduced two new tensor processing units, or TPUs — its homegrown AI chips — on Monday. The TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max join the 8t and 8i it unveiled in April, the first time Google has introduced four TPU systems in a single year. Both new chips ship next year. Think of it as a chip menu. The 8tx keeps data encrypted for governments, banks, and other regulated businesses, paired with processors from AMD ( AMD ). The 8i Max squeezes two chips into one package for requests with long context windows — the amount of information an AI model can juggle at once. The forecasts are the eye-popper. Bloomberg Intelligence sees TPU sales rising from about $12 billion this year to more than $135 billion by 2028, not counting chips rented through Google Cloud. That's more than 11-fold in two years. Nvidia's data center business grew nearly eightfold in the first two years of the AI boom, from $15 billion in fiscal 2023 to $115 billion in fiscal 2025. The chips are already flying off the line. Epoch AI estimates TPU shipments doubled in computing power in a single quarter this year, to roughly 800,000 chips. Anthropic is the headliner. Its IPO filing shows about $161 billion of lease payments tied to TPUs, which Raymond James says makes it the biggest custom-chip customer of Google's design partner, Broadcom ( AVGO ). Meta ( META ), OpenAI and Oracle ( ORCL ) are buyers too. Google used to roll out about one data center TPU a year. Now it has one for every job. Nvidia still has the bigger engine. Its next-generation Rubin chip is rated at 35 petaflops — a measure of raw computing speed — compared with about 10 for Google's 8i and about 20 for the 8i Max, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. Google is selling on price. SemiAnalysis found that Google's current Ironwood TPU delivers up to nearly three times as much AI output per dollar as Nvidia's Blackwell chips when running AI agents, though Nvidia's top system still wins when speed is everything. Forecasts aren't sales, and Nvidia still sells far more AI chips than anyone else. Nvidia's next big moment comes Nov. 17, when it reports third quarter results, a day before a requested closed-door House briefing on CEO Jensen Huang . Investors will want to hear whether customers are hedging their bets. As Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon wrote to clients, "Jensen is not an ordinary CEO; he IS NVIDIA." news.Title: 台股翻紅！反指標女神竟「買這檔」　全網一片哀嚎
news.Content:
財經中心／高淑婷報導

台股上週走勢低迷，整週累跌5510.19點，讓不少投資人看著綠油油的持股直喊苦，9日終於迎來強勁反彈，加權指數終場大漲1960.06點，收在41661.70點。然而被網友戲稱「反指標女神」的財經網紅巴逆逆，卻在臉書公開最新交易動向，透露自己買進元大台灣50正2（00631L），而先前停損賣出的亞翔竟衝上漲停，讓她忍不住直呼「我錯了」，也釣出網友留言「感謝你賣掉了」。

巴逆逆在臉書曬出台股交易明細，照片中可見她大量買這股，引來網友關注。（圖／翻攝自巴逆逆@臉書）

巴逆逆9日上午曬出交易明細，畫面可見多筆元大台灣50正2的買進委託紀錄，部分已顯示全部成交，其餘則為委託成功。她信心滿滿寫下「相信政府」、「相信台灣」、「相信台股」，接著激動喊出「衝啊啊啊啊啊啊啊啊～」，不過話鋒一轉，又感嘆「我停損的亞翔居然要漲停了」。隨後，她再度發文，曬出亞翔亮燈漲停的畫面，忍不住認錯喊「我錯了」、「我明天就把你買回來」，還附上大哭表情符號，委屈表示「我抱著你的時候就沒看你漲停過啊」。亞翔今日終場收在漲停價588元，上漲53元，讓她賣出後錯過行情的心情，引起不少股民共鳴。

貼文曝光後，網友也紛紛前來留言，表示感謝巴逆逆賣出亞翔，才有機會讓它漲停。（示意圖／民視新聞網）

貼文曝光後，網友紛紛湧入留言區，有人感謝她賣出亞翔，也有人笑虧「真有你的，亞翔賣了就拉漲停耶」。不過，看到她預告隔天要買回，留言區隨即出現一片求饒聲，有人喊「不要再買了，求你」，也有人表示「那麼多股票創低，妳可以先考慮其他嗎？」。從停損後遇上漲停，到忍不住想重新買回，巴逆逆接連公開的操作與心情，再度讓留言區成為股民抒發心情、互相打趣的討論焦點。

news.Title: Elon Musk Makes Stunning Tesla Cybertruck Decision
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) CEO Elon Musk is preparing to pull the plug on Cybertruck production by mid-2027, marking a dramatic reversal for one of the electric vehicle maker's most ambitious products. The decision could accelerate Tesla's transition toward autonomous transportation, but it also raises uncomfortable questions about the pickup's disappointing sales and the company's ability to deliver on its next major bet. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TSLA. Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Musk confirmed Monday that Tesla plans to shut down the Cybertruck production line in approximately eight months, despite claiming that customer orders continue to exceed manufacturing capacity. Tesla will introduce an additional production shift at its Texas factory to fulfill as many outstanding orders as possible before the shutdown. However, many customers will receive deposit refunds because the company cannot complete every reservation before production ends. The announcement brings a surprising conclusion to a vehicle that attracted enormous attention when Musk unveiled it in 2019. Deliveries began in late 2023, but sales have struggled to approach management's original expectations. According to Cox Automotive, U.S. Cybertruck sales fell 48% to just 20,237 vehicles in 2025, compared with Musk's earlier ambition of selling at least 250,000 annually. Sales have reached approximately 16,000 vehicles so far in 2026. Musk disputes suggestions that the Cybertruck is being discontinued because it is unprofitable. Instead, he argues that its manufacturing complexity makes producing additional Cybercabs a more valuable use of Tesla's resources. That distinction matters because Tesla is increasingly positioning autonomous transportation, rather than conventional vehicle sales, as central to its future. What investors should watch Tesla investors should monitor how quickly the company transitions Cybertruck production capacity toward Cybercab manufacturing. The shift could reduce manufacturing complexity and free up resources, but its financial benefits remain uncertain. Investors should also watch Cybercab production volumes, regulatory approvals and deployment progress, which will determine whether Tesla can turn its autonomous ambitions into meaningful revenue. Meanwhile, the financial impact of outstanding Cybertruck refunds remains unclear because Tesla has not disclosed the size of its reservation backlog. Wall Street maintains a Moderate Buy consensus on TSLA, with an average price target of $409.49, implying approximately 14% upside. Ultimately, the Cybertruck shutdown puts greater pressure on Musk to demonstrate that Cybercab can deliver the commercial success his electric pickup failed to achieve. news.Title: 輝達跌、超微漲！黃仁勳調查案衝擊AI交易 市場低估後續風險？
news.Content:
美股周一(9日)盤前走勢不一，輝達(NVDA-US)因董事會啟動黃仁勳相關調查而下跌約4.5%，超微(AMD-US)則獲券商調升評等，上漲2.3%。儘管那斯達克期貨走高，外媒評論提醒，調查可能持續籠罩輝達與AI交易，市場尚未充分反映後續風險。

大盤獲得油價回落支撐。美國總統川普表示，「極不可能」下令進一步攻擊伊朗，帶動油價下跌，緩解部分通膨疑慮，推升美股期貨，但晶片與AI概念股表現仍有落差。

輝達董事會周日宣布，針對黃仁勳疑遭外國情報活動鎖定一事展開獨立調查。此前媒體報導，他與一名涉嫌為中國情報機構工作的企業主管發展親密關係。董事會強調，目前沒有理由認為國家安全或公司機密受到損害；投資人則關注調查是否影響黃仁勳繼續掌舵。

超微同時迎來利多。Oppenheimer分析師Rick Schafer將評等調升至「優於大盤」，目標價訂為600美元，預估2027年資料中心營收將大增135%。超微盤前漲至458.86美元，與輝達形成鮮明對比。

其他晶片股仍承壓，英特爾(INTC-US)、邁威爾(MRVL-US)、高通(QCOM-US)、晟碟(SNDK-US)與美超微(SMCI-US)盤前均下跌。AI雲端業者CoreWeave(CRWV-US)與IREN(IREN-US)也名列跌幅較大的個股。

評論指出，輝達在AI投資熱潮中扮演近似「央行」的角色，其對產業的支持使調查風險不只限於公司本身。AI雲端股走弱，可能同時反映這層疑慮，以及資料中心面臨的新政治不確定性。

不過，那斯達克期貨與半導體ETF仍上漲，自研晶片的Google母公司Alphabet(GOOGL-US)(GOOG-US)及亞馬遜(AMZN-US)也走高。評論認為，眼前有限的衝擊，不代表風險已消退；調查可能延續數周甚至數月，為原已震盪的AI交易增添變數。

news.Title: 台股大漲外資繼續賣「到底誰在買？」　專家：避開大跌比抓到大漲重要
news.Content:
台股今（9）日在國安基金授權護盤及限空令等救市政策齊發下迎來強勢反彈，開盤隨即站回4萬點大關，盤中在台積電等權值股帶頭強攻下，一度大漲超過2,600點至42,349.36點，尾盤雖然漲幅略有收斂，終場仍大漲1,960.06點收在41,661.70點，擺脫上週崩跌陰霾並站穩4萬1千點整數關卡。

但三大法人方面，外資賣超逾900億元。理財專家葉育碩則表示「台股大漲1960點但外資賣超900億，那是誰在買」，葉育碩指出，台股今天上漲1,661點，成交量約8,393億元，指數反彈幅度很大，但成交量並沒有跟著等比例放大。

葉育碩表示，三大法人合計賣超945.26億元，外資今天賣超將近901億，三大法人加起來也站在賣方。他表示，「那問題就來了，今天台股大漲1960點，到底是誰在買」，葉育碩進一步表示，投信買超267億是一股重要的承接力量，至於其他買盤，還得從市場整體成交結構來看。

葉育碩並提出一個「有趣的數學問題」今天大部分股票都出現反彈，甚至不少個股直接亮燈漲停，「假設你手上的股票之前跌了50%，今天終於迎來一根漲停板；請問你的帳面損益變成多少」，他並公布答案，答案是-45%。

葉育碩提到，從-50%變成-45%，看起來好像回血不少，但距離回本還有非常漫長的一段路，「因為股票跌50%，需要上漲100%才能回本」，這也是為什麼股市裡，避開大跌往往比抓到大漲還重要。

葉育碩強調，「漲停一天很爽，但如果前面已經跌掉一半，今天這根漲停板頂多算是幫你從加護病房轉到普通病房」。

news.Title: Elon Musk Sets Massive 2032 Chipmaking Target for Tesla, SpaceX
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Elon Musk is preparing an extraordinary expansion into semiconductor manufacturing, with Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) and SpaceX ( NASDAQ:SPCX ) reportedly targeting production of 1 million chip wafers per month at their planned Terafab facility by 2032. The ambitious project could give Musk's companies greater control over critical AI hardware, although industry experts are questioning whether the aggressive timeline is achievable. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TSLA. Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Tesla is expanding beyond electric vehicles into autonomous driving, robotics and artificial intelligence, while SpaceX develops rockets, satellites and space-based communications systems. Both businesses increasingly depend on powerful semiconductors to support their technological ambitions. According to a November 9 Nikkei report, Terafab's planned capacity includes approximately 700,000 wafers per month for memory chips and more than 300,000 for logic chips. To put that into perspective, its proposed memory capacity alone would rival Samsung Electronics' estimated monthly DRAM output of 650,000 to 700,000 wafers. The facility's total production target would also be roughly 40 times the 25,000 wafers per month planned for Japan's Rapidus semiconductor plant. Musk is targeting the second half of 2028 for the beginning of mass production. However, reaching that milestone could prove difficult. Terafab procurement officials reportedly traveled to Japan earlier this month to coordinate semiconductor equipment purchases and delivery schedules. Some suppliers have been asked to deliver machinery within months, an unusually demanding schedule for an industry where building advanced fabrication facilities typically takes more than three years. The enormous scale and compressed timeline raise questions about execution, equipment availability and funding requirements. What investors should watch For Tesla investors, Terafab represents a potentially important long-term strategic investment rather than an immediate earnings catalyst. Investors should monitor equipment orders, construction milestones, capital expenditure commitments and progress toward the 2028 production target. A successful facility could eventually reduce dependence on external chip suppliers while supporting Tesla's autonomous driving and robotics ambitions. However, semiconductor manufacturing requires enormous upfront spending, specialized expertise and consistently high production yields. Delays, cost overruns or weaker-than-expected manufacturing efficiency could strain Tesla's financial resources. The central question is whether Musk can turn an exceptionally ambitious production target into a commercially competitive semiconductor operation. news.Title: AAOI Stock Rises 7% Post Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold?
news.Content:
Applied Optoelectronics AAOI shares have risen 6.9% since it reported third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 5, 2026. The surge reflects robust demand for its data center and CATV products, driven by strong 400G and 800G transceiver shipments, AI infrastructure investments and increased sales of 1.8 GHz CATV amplifiers in the third quarter of 2026.

Click here to check the details of Applied Optoelectronics' third-quarter 2026 results.

Applied Optoelectronics stock has rallied 43.8% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's appreciation of 4.1% and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's decline of 2.9%.

The outperformance can be attributed to robust demand for AAOI's high-speed optical transceivers, driven by accelerating AI data-center investments. Rapid adoption of 400G and 800G products, expanding hyperscaler relationships, and a multiyear agreement for 1.6T transceivers further strengthened its growth prospects. The company is also benefiting from increased manufacturing capacity and improving profitability.

AAOI Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AAOI Benefits From AI-Led Optical Networking Demand

Applied Optoelectronics is benefiting from accelerating optical networking demand, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments and hyperscale data center upgrades. The growing adoption of 400G, 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers is strengthening Applied Optoelectronics' position in the data center market and supporting robust revenue growth.

In the third quarter of 2026, data center revenues increased 254% year over year and 45% sequentially to $155.6 million. Revenues from 800G products nearly quadrupled sequentially to $47.5 million, while 400G revenues nearly doubled to $93.4 million. This momentum highlights strong demand for advanced optical connectivity solutions supporting AI workloads.

The company's growth prospects received a boost from a multi-year agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscale customer for 1.6T transceivers. AAOI expects this agreement to generate $1 billion to $1.5 billion in revenues through May 2029, subject to customer demand and supply conditions. The transition toward 1.6T products should support higher average selling prices and improved margins.

AAOI is aggressively expanding manufacturing capacity to capitalize on these opportunities. It expects monthly production capacity for 800G and 1.6T products to exceed one million units by the end of 2027. Growing opportunities in co-packaged optics and high-power lasers provide additional long-term growth avenues.

Story Continues

AAOI's Earnings Estimates Show Upward Trend

AAOI's robust demand for its next-generation data center products, particularly driven by the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure and the company's continued product innovation, is expected to benefit the company's top-line growth.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Applied Optoelectronics expects revenues between $385 million and $420 million. Datacenter revenues are projected to be between $270 million and $300 million, while CATV revenues are expected to be between $105 million and $115 million.

Applied Optoelectronics expects non-GAAP earnings per share in the range of 48 cents to 63 cents. The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at 59 cents per share, unchanged over the past 30 days. The company reported a loss of 1 cent in the year-ago quarter.

AAOI Faces Margin Pressure and Rising Competition

Despite its expanding portfolio, Applied Optoelectronics faced margin pressure in the third quarter of 2026 due to an unfavorable product mix. Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 28.7% from 31% a year ago, falling below management's guidance of 29-30.5%. A faster-than-expected customer transition from 800G to 1.6T transceivers resulted in lower-than-anticipated 800G sales and a higher proportion of 400G products. 100G transceiver revenues also declined as a customer faced switch shortages linked to industry-wide memory supply constraints. Manufacturing capacity limitations and supply-chain bottlenecks also restricted the company's ability to fully capitalize on strong demand.

AAOI is also suffering from stiff competition from companies like Fabrinet FN, Lumentum LITE, and Coherent COHR, which are also expanding their footprint in the optical networking market.

Fabrinet is benefiting from strong demand for AI-driven data center infrastructure, particularly data center interconnect, optical transceivers, and high-performance computing. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Data center revenues jumped 78% year over year to $777 million. Data center revenues increased 16% sequentially and accounted for approximately 53% of total revenues.

Lumentum's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. In October 2026, Lumentum announced a collaboration with Astera Labs and Corning to demonstrate 1060 nm VCSEL-based PCIe-over-optics connectivity at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The technology aims to improve bandwidth density, power efficiency, and signal quality while addressing connectivity challenges in large-scale AI infrastructure

Coherent is benefiting from strong AI infrastructure spending, rising demand for 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, and growing adoption of optical connectivity across data centers. Rapid growth in its Scale Across business, the ramp-up of PhotonLink and optical circuit switches, and expanding indium phosphide manufacturing capacity are supporting revenue growth and margin expansion.

Applied Optoelectronics shares are also trading at a premium, as suggested by its Value Score of F.

What Should Investors Do With AAOI Stock?

Applied Optoelectronics' strong AI-driven optical networking demand, growing hyperscaler relationships and expanding manufacturing capacity support its long-term growth prospects.

Moreover, Wall Street's consensus price target implies roughly 211.19% upside from current levels.

However, margin pressure, supply-chain constraints and intense competition from companies like Fabrinet, Lumentum and Coherent remain headwinds.

Applied Optoelectronics currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting that it may be wise to wait for a more favorable entry point in the stock. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Apple's Market Value Grew From $350 Billion to $4 Trillion During Tim Cook's 15 Years as CEO. Here's What That Growth Curve Means for Apple's Next Chapter Under John Ternus.
news.Content:
When Tim Cook took the helm at Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), many people questioned whether the longtime Apple executive could bring the company as much success as the late Steve Jobs had.

Cook was a much different CEO than Jobs was, but it's safe to say that he far outpaced anyone's expectations. Under Cook, Apple rose from a $347 billion tech giant to a $4.6 trillion behemoth when he retired -- making Apple one of the most valuable companies in the world.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Apple's new CEO, John Ternus, faces some of the same initial skepticism as his predecessor, with many wondering whether he can deliver the same value Cook did. And while Ternus could prove to be a great CEO, it's highly unlikely he'll replicate the last decade and a half of Apple's success. Here's why.

The math just doesn't add up

Going from a $347 billion company to $4.6 trillion is more than a 13X increase in the company's valuation. For Ternus' tenure to match that, it would mean Apple would eventually be worth around $60 trillion. That would put Apple's valuation 88% higher than the annual GDP of the U.S.

The math for that level of growth doesn't add up.

What's more, Apple is facing some pretty significant headwinds that Ternus is dealing with right out of the gate. First, memory prices have risen quickly as tech companies buy up all the available memory for data centers. Even Apple, which can secure large amounts of supply at reduced prices, is grappling with this problem, and it's eating into its coveted high margins.

Apple's management said on the company's Q4 2026 earnings call that margin pressure will continue on its products because of the memory shortage and expects its product margins to be 45% to 46% in the December quarter, which would mark three straight quarters of decline.

One of the leading memory chip companies, SK Hynix , has already sold out half of its memory supply for both 2027 and 2028 and says the supply and demand imbalance will continue through 2030. That may mean we haven't seen the last of Apple's margin declines.

Even more consequential for Apple's market value over the long term is that the company is still trying to figure out its place in the artificial intelligence era.

To keep pace, Apple recently launched Siri AI, which is a far more capable chatbot than before, and can answer questions and perform on-device tasks for Apple users. Apple recently opened Siri AI to developers as well, which will make it even more capable.

Story Continues

Still, Apple could be left behind in the AI race as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Alphabet continue to release highly capable AI models that can do far more than Siri. Apple is also facing increasing competition from Meta , whose popular Muse agent is far better at accomplishing tasks than Siri.

Ternus could still bring a lot of value to Apple

I'm not counting Apple out of the current AI boom, though. Its conservative approach to spending, compared with its peers, is paying off. The company's non-GAAP earnings per share rose 14% to $2.10 per share in the fourth quarter, and sales rose 12% to $114.5 billion. And the company hasn't amassed the huge amounts of debt its peers have.

Ternus also appears to be accelerating the timeline of the company's product launches. In the two short months since taking over, Apple has launched the iPhone Duo, a touchscreen MacBook Pro, and the Apple HomeView smart home device.

Like Cook, Ternus will be judged on how much value he brings to the company. But like his predecessor, he doesn't need to succeed in the same way as previous leadership -- and he should be given plenty of time to prove himself.

Just don't expect him to turn Apple into a nearly $60 trillion company.

news.Title: Google expands AI chip lineup as Nvidia faces CEO spy scandal
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Alphabet Inc.'s Google is expanding its artificial intelligence chip portfolio, stepping up its challenge to Nvidia Corp. just as a controversy involving Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang adds another source of uncertainty for the market leader.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Google is introducing two new variations of its tensor processing units, or TPUs, designed to address growing demand for confidential computing and AI applications that need to process larger amounts of information, Bloomberg News reported Monday.

The new TPU 8tx and 8i Max offerings are designed for different workloads, reflecting Google's view that the next phase of artificial intelligence will require increasingly specialized hardware.

The TPU 8tx targets secure, confidential computing, with potential applications among government agencies and companies operating in regulated industries. The system also incorporates chips from Advanced Micro Devices Inc., as part of a collaboration between the two companies.

The 8i Max, meanwhile, is designed to run AI applications requiring longer context windows, allowing models to consider substantially more information when responding to queries. Such capabilities are particularly relevant for drug discovery, mathematical applications and coding tools.

Neither offering represents an entirely new silicon design. Instead, Google has reconfigured its existing hardware to address specific requirements emerging from customers, according to Bloomberg.

"This really follows the thesis that we have here at Google, which is that the future is going to be about specialization, and the upsides for specialization continue to be significant," Google chip chief Amin Vahdat told Bloomberg.

The announcement marks an acceleration in Google's chip development. The company previously introduced a new generation of AI processors roughly every two years, but this year unveiled two generations of specialized processors simultaneously, with the latest variations expanding the lineup further.

Google gains ground as Nvidia faces fresh uncertainty

The timing is notable for the semiconductor industry, where Nvidia's dominance is facing increasing competition from companies developing their own AI accelerators.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Story Continues

Google has emerged as one of the most credible challengers, benefiting from years of internal chip development and growing interest from AI developers seeking alternatives to Nvidia's processors.

The opportunity extends beyond Google's own AI operations. Demand for computing capacity remains substantial, while the emergence of AI agents is creating new requirements for inference, memory and security. Specialized processors could allow customers to optimize performance and costs for particular workloads rather than relying on general-purpose solutions.

Nvidia, meanwhile, continues to benefit from demand that exceeds available supply, leaving considerable room for competitors to establish businesses without necessarily displacing the market leader.

But the company faces a separate challenge Monday following reports that Huang may have been targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation.

Nvidia's board announced Sunday that it would launch an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The announcement followed a report concerning his relationship with a business executive whom US authorities reportedly suspected of gathering information for Beijing.

Huang also acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a message to employees, apologizing to his family and colleagues.

Nvidia said its board had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets had been compromised and expressed confidence in Huang's leadership. The CEO has pledged to cooperate with the investigation.

The controversy is weighing on Nvidia shares, which were down 5.70% Monday, while Alphabet shares were up 2.4%.

The divergence reflects two separate developments: Google's expanding ambitions in AI infrastructure and the unexpected leadership and reputational uncertainty confronting Nvidia.

For Alphabet, the latest TPU expansion strengthens its position in a market that could become increasingly fragmented as AI workloads evolve. For Nvidia, the immediate concern is less about losing its technological lead overnight than maintaining investor confidence in a business whose extraordinary growth has been closely associated with Huang's leadership.

Google still has a considerable distance to travel before matching Nvidia's scale and software ecosystem. But its latest move underscores that competition in AI semiconductors is increasingly about offering the right processor for each task, rather than simply producing the most powerful chip.

news.Title: Can IBM's Latest Quantum System Boost Illinois' Innovation Future?
news.Content:
International Business Machines Corporation IBM has reached a major milestone in its quantum computing expansion by unveiling its first quantum computer in Illinois. The IBM Quantum System Two, powered by the company's Quantum Nighthawk processor, is now operational at Hyde Park Labs in Chicago, hosted by the University of Chicago.

The IBM Quantum System Two will initially give researchers, businesses and academic institutions across Illinois access to advanced quantum computing capabilities. It will eventually relocate to the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP), where it will serve as the anchor system of the National Quantum Algorithm Center. Through this deployment, the company aims to accelerate the development of scalable quantum algorithms and explore applications across industries.

The company is working with Deloitte, AbbVie, EPRI, Fermilab, Northwestern University and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign on research in drug discovery, molecular simulation, power-grid optimization and high-energy physics. It is also supporting workforce development through its planned FutureNow Chicago center at IQMP, in partnership with City Colleges of Chicago. The center is expected to create 750 jobs in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data science, quantum computing and other emerging technology fields.

The project marks an important step in IBM's efforts to expand its quantum computing infrastructure. The initiative further strengthens the company's collaboration with Illinois' research and business communities while supporting the growth of its quantum technology ecosystem.

How Are Competitors Advancing in Quantum Computing?

IBM faces competition from Microsoft Corporation MSFT and Alphabet Inc. GOOGL. Microsoft is focusing on building more stable and efficient quantum computing systems through advances in qubit technology. Its research aims to address complex challenges in chemistry and materials science. Microsoft is exploring partnerships to accelerate the development of practical quantum computing solutions.

Alphabet is advancing quantum computing through its Google Quantum AI research division, focusing on improving processor performance and minimizing errors. The company is exploring quantum computing applications in advanced computing, simulations and optimization. Alphabet's research efforts include developing new computing approaches that could expand the capabilities of quantum systems.
