news.Title: This Stock Is a Nearly Guaranteed Winner From the AI Infrastructure Buildout
news.Content:
Investing to profit from the AI build-out can be difficult. There are so many options, ranging from computing companies to application plays to energy companies. All of these are bound to benefit in one way, but choosing the best isn't easy. However, I think there's one company that may cut through all of that noise and provide a top investment opportunity: Taiwan Semiconductor (NYSE: TSM).

It looks like a practically guaranteed winner in the AI build-out, and it's easy to see why.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Taiwan Semiconductor has a grip on the chip industry

Taiwan Semiconductor is a logic chip fabrication company: Simply put, it manufactures the chips designed by its clients, most of which lack any foundries of their own. All of the major AI computing unit manufacturers -- Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), AMD (NASDAQ: AMD), and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO), and others -- utilize TSMC's services.

They have to, as no other chip foundry has the capacity to serve as a viable alternative. During Q2, TSMC's massive manufacturing infrastructure allowed it to take in 72.5% of chip foundry revenue in the world. That capacity dominance makes it difficult for any other company to rise and steal its leading clients away.

However, even if it were more of an option, TSMC's clients don't have many reasons to want to switch foundry partners, either. TSMC has best-in-class technology and a reputation for fantastic production yields. That makes it a great company to partner with. There's a reason why TSMC has grown to become the giant that it is.

As for the AI build-out, as long as companies continue to need more and more computing capacity, TSMC will see large orders for chips. It has projected that from 2024 to 2029, revenues from its AI chip business will grow at a compound annual rate in the mid-to-high 50% range, and during the company's Q3 conference call, CEO C.C. Wei said that its growth rate "probably will be higher."

That will benefit shareholders immensely.

Lastly, the stock isn't priced outrageously.

TSM PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

At 23 times forward expected earnings, Taiwan Semiconductor is trading at a discount relative to its typical level at this time of year. So, not only is it a great long-term investment in the AI build-out, but it's also a timely buy. Opportunities like this don't often appear, and investors should take advantage of the stock while it's a bit cheaper than historical levels. While TSMC may not provide the best long-term AI returns, I am confident that it is practically guaranteed to do well.

By acquiring specialized multi-agent orchestrators, major tech platforms aim to lock in developer ecosystems, streamline complex software development lifecycles, and enhance the training feedback loops of their underlying foundation models.

About Meta Platforms

Meta Platforms operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger, connecting billions of users worldwide. Led by Mark Zuckerberg, the company generates most of its revenue through digital advertising while expanding into artificial intelligence (AI), generative AI models, smart glasses, and virtual reality through its Reality Labs division.

META Stock Performance

Meta's stock has experienced a volatile trading environment in 2026 as investors weigh strong advertising growth against rising AI infrastructure expenses. Shares closed at $630 on Nov. 4, giving the company a year-to-date (YTD) return of approximately 4.3% through that session. The stock remains below its 52-week high of $779.82, reflecting pressure from concerns about capital expenditure, profitability, and the timeline for monetizing AI investments.

Results Beat Estimates

Meta reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $64.60 billion, up 26% year-over-year (YoY) and above Wall Street's estimate of $63.34 billion. Reported diluted earnings per share came in at $3.83, compared with the analyst consensus of $6.54. However, earnings included a one-time $9.89 billion legal charge related to an agreement with 52 U.S. state attorneys general. Excluding this expense, diluted EPS would have been approximately $7.40, indicating stronger underlying earnings performance.

The company's operating metrics reflected continued strength in its advertising business. Advertising revenue climbed to $63.06 billion, while ad impressions increased 10% YoY, and the average price per advertisement rose 14%. Family daily active people reached 3.64 billion, up 3% from the previous year. However, total costs and expenses surged 68% to $51.61 billion, reducing operating margin to 20% from 40% a year earlier. Capital expenditures reached $34.91 billion, while free cash flow turned negative at $2.12 billion. Meta ended September with $82.45 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities.

Story Continues

Looking ahead, management expects Q4 2026 revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, supported by continued momentum in digital advertising and AI-driven improvements. The company raised its full-year 2026 expense outlook to $175 billion–$179 billion, including the legal settlement charge, and projects capital expenditures of $135 billion–$145 billion as it expands AI infrastructure and data center capacity. Management also expects Reality Labs losses to decline to $18 billion–$19 billion in 2026 and approximately $15 billion in 2027. The company's ability to convert substantial AI investments into sustainable revenue growth will remain a key focus for investors.

Meta Acquires AI Coding Startup Conductor to Strengthen AI Capabilities

Meta Platforms is reportedly expanding its artificial intelligence ambitions through the acquisition of Conductor, an AI coding startup, according to an Axios report published Nov. 4, 2026. Founded in 2024, Conductor develops technology that enables software engineers to coordinate and manage multiple AI coding agents simultaneously, potentially helping developers automate complex programming tasks and improve productivity. Financial terms of the acquisition have not been disclosed. Conductor is led by CEO Charlie Holtz and CTO Jackson de Campos, who are both expected to join Meta following the deal. The reported acquisition highlights Meta's growing focus on AI-powered software development tools as it strengthens its artificial intelligence infrastructure, developer capabilities, and competitive position in the rapidly evolving generative AI market.

Should You Buy META Stock?

Meta's reported acquisition of AI coding startup Conductor reinforces its commitment to expanding AI capabilities and strengthening its position in the generative AI market. The deal could enhance developer productivity and support Meta's broader AI ecosystem as competition intensifies. Wall Street remains bullish on META stock, with a "Strong Buy" consensus and a mean price target of $858.25, indicating 39% potential upside from its current market price. Of 55 analyst ratings, 46 are "Strong Buy," two are "Moderate Buy," and seven are "Hold," reflecting strong confidence in Meta's growth prospects.

news.Title: Democrats prepare to go after Apple, Meta and Elon Musk companies
news.Content:
Wall Street toasted the Democratic sweep at first. On Nov. 4, the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 3% as investors digested two years of divided government, with Amazon, Microsoft and Apple among the biggest gainers.

That mood flipped fast. By Nov. 5, the Nasdaq had entered a correction, with traders fretting that a Democratic Congress could slow data center projects that have powered the AI rally. But for some of the country's biggest companies, a rough day on the market is not the main concern right now. Subpoenas are.

Grok, Maduro and Musk's widening federal footprint

The House is laying the groundwork to examine President Donald Trump's use of Grok, Musk's AI chatbot, in planning the military operation that captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, The Washington Post reported.

Also read: Bank of America doubles down on its Apple stock bet

It goes back to December 2025, when Trump met privately with Musk. The president spent hours putting questions to Grok about his presidency and his legacy, and at one point asked how Venezuelans would react if the U.S. captured Maduro, according to TechCrunch. The operation came the following month. When people celebrated in the streets, one official said Trump came away thinking Grok was ingenious.

This was not Grok's first brush with Washington, either. Back in July 2025, xAI launched a product called Grok for Government, built for federal, state and local agencies, and was one of several AI companies to pick up a Department of Defense contract worth up to $200 million each.

That business now sits inside a much larger company. SpaceX acquired xAI in an all-stock deal in early February 2026, folding Grok and the X platform under the same roof as Musk's rockets and satellites.

The AI unit is also fighting an NAACP lawsuit alleging it ran gas turbines without an air permit in Southaven, Mississippi, and a federal judge refused to dismiss the case on Oct. 30, as reported by TheStreet.

Apple's App Store and the ballroom donors

Apple is drawing scrutiny for hosting tracking apps used by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The report did not name the specific apps lawmakers have in mind, and Apple did not immediately respond to the paper's request for comment.

A second front opened before the new Congress has even been seated. Sen. Richard Blumenthal, who is set to chair the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, called on Apple and other donors to Trump's White House ballroom project to turn over records or face possible subpoenas in January, Reuters reported.

Story Continues

The pressure lands while Apple shares sit near record territory. The stock climbed more than 6% during the Nov. 4 session, one of the strongest moves in the Dow that day. That rally gives the company more to protect if a drawn-out fight in Washington starts weighing on sentiment, Reuters reported.

Blumenthal's push targets the ballroom donors as a group rather than Apple alone. Still, Apple stands out because it now appears on two separate lists, one tied to immigration enforcement and another tied to the president's building project.

Meta's data center secrecy faces a reckoning

Lawmakers are also eyeing Meta over its demands that local governments sign nondisclosure agreements related to data center development. That angle is likely to resonate in towns where residents learned about massive projects only after key decisions had been made.

The issue already has a paper trail.

A Senate investigation led by Sens. Elizabeth Warren, Chris Van Hollen and Blumenthal found that Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft routinely sought NDAs during data center development, and argued the deals restricted public scrutiny of tax dollars and utility rates, according to Time. Microsoft told investigators it would stop seeking them with local governments, while Google and Meta declined to commit to ending the practice.

More Wall Street:

Arista Networks stock gets fresh backing from Jim Cramer and Wall Street

Oracle stock sinks as Wall Street confronts a $20 billion AI problem

Wall Street just got a candid look at who is winning the AI race

Meta has more riding on the question than most. The company confirmed on July 13 that its Hyperion data center project in Richland Parish, Louisiana, had crossed $50 billion, up from a $10 billion estimate when it was announced in December 2024, as reported by TheStreet. Louisiana had already approved a 20-year sales tax exemption for eligible data centers in late 2024.

Energy advocates have argued that Meta's project will push up utility bills for the average customer. Meta disputes that consumers bear those costs directly, and an Entergy press release says they do not.

Meta, Apple and other big tech brace for a January rush

Lawyers expect corporations, rather than federal agencies, to carry much of the load.

Jamie Bair of Crowell & Moring said investigators often get no answers from the administration, while companies tend to receive more detailed letters and are more apt to respond, revealing their dealings with U.S. officials along the way, The Washington Post reported. A memo from the Groundwork Collaborative, a think tank, flagged large tech companies as "high-value" targets.

Investors are already pricing in part of that risk. SpaceX and Tesla shares each fell roughly 5% in premarket trading on Nov. 4 after Musk's record election spending came up short. Tech selling deepened the next day, with the Nasdaq dropping more than 5% as Wall Street weighed the "headline" risks around AI.

Startups are preparing as well. Venture capitalists have advised Silicon Valley companies to close funding rounds before the end of the year in case money dries up if executives are called into hearings or Pentagon spending is curtailed. For companies that spent two years courting the White House, January now looks less like the start of a new session and more like a deadline.

news.Title: Tesla's FSD (Supervised) Attach Rate Hit 75% on New Vehicles. Here's Why That Single Number Could Matter More Than Robotaxi for the Stock in 2027.
news.Content: Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) reported that more than 75% of its new vehicle deliveries in North America included a paid Full Self-Driving (Supervised) subscription sign-up in the third quarter of 2026. That's an increase of nearly 20 percentage points from the previous quarter's attach rate. For a company spending billions developing autonomous vehicles, artificial intelligence , and humanoid robots , this might be one of the most encouraging numbers in its latest earnings report. And unlike the robotaxi, FSD (Supervised) is already generating revenue from customers driving vehicles they own. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Tesla's software business is gaining traction Tesla ended the third quarter with approximately 1.74 million active paid FSD customers worldwide, up from 1.48 million in the second quarter and 1.04 million a year earlier. That's roughly 67% annual growth. Tesla also reported that about half of its paid FSD customers were using subscriptions rather than paying up front. Those subscribers generate revenue month after month, potentially creating a predictable software business alongside Tesla's automotive operations. Consider this hypothetical scenario: If Tesla eventually reaches 2 million paying monthly subscribers at $99 per month, that would translate into approximately $2.38 billion in annualized subscription revenue. At 3 million subscribers, the figure jumps to $3.56 billion. These aren't Tesla's revenue forecasts. They illustrate what a larger subscription business could generate, assuming customers keep paying throughout the year. And software revenue could carry attractive margins because Tesla doesn't have to manufacture another vehicle every time someone subscribes. There's still a catch with that 75% figure Tesla's reported attach rate measures sign-ups at delivery. It doesn't tell investors how many customers continue paying after the initial period. In fact, management acknowledged during its earnings call that new vehicles come with a free FSD trial and that the company isn't yet providing detailed customer retention or cancellation rates. Yes, a 75% sign-up rate is impressive, but a 75% long-term retention rate for paying customers would be far more valuable. FSD also remains a supervised driver-assistance system and is not to be seen as autonomous. Drivers must pay attention and be prepared to intervene. It isn't the same as the fully autonomous service Tesla hopes to expand through its robotaxi business. That said, there's been no indication that supervised FSD has presented much of an obstacle for customers who have opted for the subscription. Story Continues Why 2027 could be a turning point Tesla's robotaxi operation is expanding, but the company still faces uncertainty surrounding regulatory approvals, operating costs, geographic expansion, and eventual profitability. Indeed, FSD subscriptions offer something more measurable. Tesla already has millions of customers paying for the technology, and its installed vehicle base provides opportunities to sell subscriptions beyond new-car buyers. So for 2027, I'd actually watch three numbers: total paid FSD customers, the percentage paying monthly, and customer retention. If subscriptions continue growing while cancellations remain manageable, Tesla could build a multibillion-dollar software revenue stream without waiting for robotaxis to reach nationwide scale. While that wouldn't necessarily justify Tesla's valuation on its own, it would give investors a growing, identifiable source of revenue to evaluate as the company's more ambitious autonomous driving plans continue to develop. news.Title: 台股週一能反彈？恐「先漲再下殺」情境曝　專家這樣看
news.Content:
美股崩跌，台股6日一度狂瀉3737點，創下史上盤中最大跌點紀錄，終場仍重挫1873.08點，收在39701.64點，跌幅4.51%，創史上第4大收盤跌點，失守4萬點整數關卡。週一9日開盤倒數，許多投資人無不關心到底重挫後能否反彈？有網友認為，有可能是，先漲一波騙人進場，接著再下殺。財信傳媒董事長謝金河分析，殺過頭的股價會修正回來，且AI的賽道上沒有回頭路，股價修正後仍然會走回原來的軌道。

資深財經媒體人阮慕驊說，國安基金宣布進場，費半跌深反彈漲4%，台指期貨夜盤只漲1.6%，台積電ADR漲超過6%。台積電全週下跌10%，ADR最大週跌幅13.5%，週五收盤縮小跌幅全週下跌7.6%。並問大家，照這樣推算，台積電下週一合理漲幅應該是多少？

網友們紛紛留言，「猜週一先漲一波騙人家進場，週二再下殺個長黑， 然後盤整一段時間等散戶沒注意，沒有人要玩股票的時候一根長紅就上去了」、「週一開盤變數太多了，小心謹慎為宜、就算下週一開高、也不要輕易追買或賣出」、「大家應静待止跌訊號」、「先漲後跌，星期五買到低點先出賺一波」、「跌到合理價，外資應該也會轉賣為買，現在內資進場，擺明開始互相搶籌碼國安基金進場不會馬上拉抬股價，因為還沒吃飽，來回震盪繼續吸籌碼」及「不能太樂觀，大盤季線向下彎，2330應會再下跌」等。

阮慕驊也問，國安基金宣布第十次進場護盤，大家看法如何？網友們指出，「會不會反而被提款？」、「破壞市場」、「反彈完繼續南下」、「重點是護得了嗎？這是國際趨勢」、「加上美股反彈，國安基金進場～雙好」、「外資那麼龐大很難撐，反而限空效果比較好」、「反彈後減碼出清」。也有不少人表示，現在太早了。

財信傳媒董事長謝金河指出，美國期中選舉落幕，民主黨大勝給世界帶來的第一堂課是反AI，先前要求暫緩資料中心建置的候選人當選，美國股市在選後第二個交易日暴跌，那指和費半都出現史詩級下跌。台股再度重演去年4月17日的戲碼，股市開盤跳空3735，台積電也開出2020元的跌停價，滿地都是跌停的個股。南韓股市一開盤4911.28，跌幅近10%，日本日經指數盤中暴跌4033.75。這場參與AI賽局的國家無人倖免。

謝金河認為，經過這場肅殺，殺過頭的股價會修正回來外，美國在AI的賽道上沒有回頭路，股價修正後仍然會走回原來的軌道。

news.Title: How to Play SpaceX Stock after Democrats Sweep Midterm Elections
news.Content:
Elon Musk spent big to shape the midterms, but the results did not go as planned. Musk was the biggest donor to GOP candidates and causes, with contributions topping $470 million, according to the Financial Times. Most of the candidates backed by Trump lost, according to a CNBC report.

Wall Street noticed as shares of SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA) were down significantly. In fact, the two stocks lost more than $450 billion in combined value over the last two trading sessions.

More News from Barchart

Intel Stock Faces a New Threat That No One Saw Coming

Oracle Just Walked Away From a $7 Billion Tencent Deal. Here's What It Means for ORCL Stock.

Dear Applied Materials Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 12

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

So is this dip a warning or a buying opportunity? The answer depends on which part of the SpaceX story you trust.

Why SpaceX Stock Fell After the Midterms

According to CNBC:

Democrats won control of the House and the Senate, and the losses hit even closer to home for Musk.

In Texas, where SpaceX and Tesla are headquartered, Democrats James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa beat longtime Musk allies Ken Paxton and Gov. Greg Abbott

Investors now worry Musk could face new congressional probes and stricter rules for his companies.

Hinojosa "made data centers a major campaign issue," Deutsche Bank analysts wrote. She called for a pause on new approvals until lawmakers pass stricter rules on water use, electricity costs, and local control.

SpaceX and Tesla are building artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure in Texas, which includes plans for Terafab, a data center and a chip factory in Grimes County. SpaceX also plans a supercomputer at Starbase.

Deutsche Bank warned that SpaceX's Texas compute capacity could face delays and capital expenditures might also rise to meet tougher rules.

CNN also reported that Musk and SpaceX were told to preserve records about limits placed on a military version of Starlink in Ukraine. And scrutiny could complicate a SpaceX and Tesla merger. Musk said on the Oct. 20 earnings call that Tesla would need a vote of 50% of all shares to complete the potential merger.

Musk's net worth topped $1 trillion soon after SpaceX went public. His net worth is currently estimated at $800 billion as per Forbes.

What SpaceX's Q3 Results Show

Valued at a market cap of $1.7 trillion, SpaceX reported revenue of $14.6 billion in Q3 of 2026, an increase of 161% year over year. Over the last 12 months, it swung from a $1.1 billion loss to a net income of $4.4 billion in Q3.

Story Continues

It reported an adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization) of $8.8 billion, an increase of 306% year over year. Starlink added 1.6 million consumer subscribers and ended Q3 with 13.6 million subscribers.

The AI segment reported revenue of $7.6 billion, while the company ended the quarter with a backlog of $63 billion, $42 billion of which is expected within a year. SpaceX also guided first-quarter 2027 revenue to $33 billion to $37 billion. However, it also expects to spend more than $35 billion in capital expenditures in Q4 of 2026.

Why AI Compute Demand Backs the Bull Case for SPCX Stock

CFO Bret Johnsen said new compute deployments pay back in under a year. Musk said short contracts are renewing at higher dollars per watt and explained that SpaceX could rent out its compute several times over.

Musk expects about 3 gigawatts of compute online by the end of this year. He is "highly confident" of adding another 10 gigawatts next year, which would bring the total to 13 gigawatts.

Johnsen said at the Goldman Sachs conference on Sept. 10 that most compute deals run about 90 days with a 90-day exit. Short contracts let SpaceX raise prices as demand grows. But they also let customers leave quickly.

Johnsen pointed to capacity coming online in Memphis and Southaven. The transcripts do not say what share of the 13 gigawatts is in Texas, which might be key for SPCX stock investors.

Starship is also expanding to Louisiana, where Musk said the internal goal for a first launch is 2028.

How to Play SpaceX Stock Now

Here's a framework that SpaceX stock investors can follow.

Separate politics from performance: The drop came from policy fear and not an earnings miss.

Watch Starship Flight 15: Musk said on the Oct. 20 earnings call that Flight 15 is expected in November. SpaceX plans to try to catch both the booster and the ship. President Gwynne Shotwell said SpaceX expects the FAA license to cover a tower catch for both stages.

Track Texas policy: A data center pause is the clearest threat to compute timelines and capex.

Expect big swings: SpaceX and Tesla lost about $456 billion in combined market value in just days. Only invest what you could hold through a sharp drop.

Note the orbital hedge: Johnsen said SpaceX targets its first orbital compute satellites next year, which could ease reliance on ground power and permitting.

The midterms changed the political weather around SpaceX. Investors should watch capex spending and whether Starship delivers another big win to change the mood.

Out of the 40 analysts covering SpaceX stock, 27 recommend "Strong Buy," three recommend "Moderate Buy," eight recommend "Hold," one recommends "Moderate Sell," and one recommends "Strong Sell." The average SPCX stock price target is $253, which is above the current price of $124.

news.Title: 國安基金進場就是最低點？專家曝3指標須緊盯 台積電營收將公布
news.Content:
台股近期遭血洗，從10月6日的高點49968點，一路跌破4萬，6日收盤為39701.64點，國安基金旋即決議啟動護盤機制，政府也推出限空令欲救市。不過財經網紅股海老牛拿出過去國安基金進場數據，有4次又跌超過一成。他提醒，想要進場有3指標要看，包括外資賣超有沒有縮小、台幣匯率能否守住33元、融資籌碼有沒有洗乾淨。

股海老牛在臉書發文表示，上周五打開券商App，很多人的反應是想刪掉。起因是美國AI股大逃殺，台股一周跌了5510點，跌幅達12.2%，收在39701點，4萬點沒守住，且台指淨空單還衝向約10萬口。老牛在市場這麼多年，一周跌這麼多真的不常見。但美股在周五出現反彈，周一台股有望迎來反彈。

他也貼心整理接下來需要關注的重要資訊，分別為周一限空令上路，國安基金同步護盤；周二台積電10月營收、晚上公布美國CPI（消費者物價指數）；周三美國PPI（生產者物價指數）。股海老牛認為，此次國安基金護盤比較像止血帶，治不了病。因此想要進場會先看三件事，外資賣超有沒有縮小、台幣匯率能否守住33元、融資籌碼有沒有洗乾淨。

股海老牛還提到，這周剛好也是上市櫃公司Q3財報跟10月營收大舉出爐的時候，成績單比盤面一片綠更重要。因為股價一周跌12%，公司獲利不會一周跌12%。把手上持股的營收獲利拿出來看看，如果沒變，就別被價格嚇跑。如果這波跌到你睡不著，問題可能是部位太大了。

news.Title: 台股歷經黑色星期五　明開盤前3風險
news.Content:
受到費城半導體指數與台積電ADR持續破底影響，台股週五（6）日早盤跳空重挫約2600點，盤中一度大跌逾3700點，最低下探37837點，再創波段新低。不過，隨後逢低買盤進場，指數一度拉升至40435點，但尾盤仍不敵賣壓，終場重挫1873.08點，收在39701.64點，成交值放大至約1.24兆元。

觀察19大類股走勢，僅化學生技醫療類股逆勢上漲0.71%，電機機械下跌5.33%、電子類股下跌4.93%、航運類股下跌4.06%，成為主要弱勢族群。櫃買市場表現更為疲弱，儘管盤中同樣出現下影線，但終場仍收黑，下跌17.45點、跌幅5.43%，收在304.02點，成交值縮減至1769.87億元。法人指出，電子權值股雖然全面重挫，但台積電（2330）與鴻海（2317）開低走高，並爆出大量；聯發科（2454）、台達電（2308）、聯電（2303）及日月光投控（3711）也陸續打開跌停，聯發科盤中更一度回升至平盤。後續只要電子權值股不再破底，將有利台股展開反彈。

金融航空轉弱 軟體綠能抗跌

金融股方面，富邦金（2881）、國泰金（2882）均跳空跌破季線，法人認為，股價必須盡快重新站回季線，否則自5月以來的波段漲勢恐將告一段落。近期表現相對強勢的航空股也出現轉弱跡象，長榮航（2618）、華航（2610）雙雙跌破週四大量低點，短線預期將進入震盪整理。

盤面強勢族群則集中在軟體，以及受到美國民主黨期中選舉勝選題材帶動的製藥與太陽能股。力新（5202）、智聯服務（6751）、廣豐（1416）、達能（3686）及元晶（6443）亮燈漲停；邁達特（6112）、精誠（6214）、藥華藥（6446）、茂迪（6244）及倉和（6538）漲幅均超過5%。值得注意的是，儘管盤面下跌家數仍高達1700檔，但出現紅K的個股也超過1500檔。法人指出，若個股成交量明顯放大，或原本跌停的個股打開跌停，且尾盤仍能收在相對高點，有機會出現底部訊號。

千點下影收腳 聚焦底部訊號

相關觀察個股包括大立光（3008）、玉晶光（3406）、廣達（2382）、群聯（8299）、十銓（4967）、川湖（2059）、友達（2409）、創意（3443）、華碩（2357）、長榮（2603）、文曄（3036）、上銀（2049）及元太（8069）。相較之下，持續鎖住跌停的個股尚未出現止跌訊號，法人建議暫時避開散熱、光通訊、ABF載板、砷化鎵及IC封測等弱勢族群。

技術面方面，台股週五跳空再創波段新低，但盤中開低走高，終止連續六根黑K，收盤守住年線及7月股災低點39384點，並留下約千點下影線，成交量也大幅增加。法人認為，短線若指數不再破底，便有機會止跌回升，但必須重新收復41513點缺口及短期均線，才有機會出現較明顯反彈，否則仍將在缺口內震盪整理。操作方面，後續持續觀察電子與金融權值股能否止穩，以及成交量放大、跌停打開後能否維持相對高檔等訊號。對於尚未打開跌停、仍持續破底的族群，則建議暫時避開。

news.Title: Apple’s iPhone Demand Surges, But AAPL Still Isn’t a ‘Strong Buy’
news.Content:
Apple (AAPL) reported a strong fourth-quarter performance, with revenue and earnings posting double-digit growth despite supply-chain constraints and rising memory costs. The iPhone remained a key growth driver, supported by resilient consumer demand and sustained product momentum.

Although strong product sales and continued expansion across its services ecosystem strengthen Apple's growth outlook, analysts' sentiment toward the stock remains divided, with some analysts adopting a more cautious stance.

More News from Barchart

Why Michael Burry Says Fiserv Stock Could Surge as Much as 94% From Here

Bloom Energy Stock Rallies as Barclays Turns Bullish on California Power Partnership

Oracle Just Walked Away From a $7 Billion Tencent Deal. Here's What It Means for ORCL Stock.

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

Apple shares have gained more than 28% year-to-date, significantly outperforming its Magnificent Seven peers. This relative strength partly reflects the market's favorable assessment of Apple's comparatively disciplined approach to artificial intelligence (AI) investments. Unlike several technology giants committing substantial capital to AI infrastructure, Apple has maintained a more measured spending strategy, helping it avoid some of the cost and profitability concerns weighing on its peers.

Nevertheless, AAPL's notable appreciation has driven its valuation higher, which explains why analysts are divided, and Apple stock still isn't a "Strong Buy."

Apple's Growth Outlook Remains Resilient Despite Supply Constraints

Apple's latest quarterly results highlight the resilience of its business model, supported by continued demand for its hardware products, an expanding services ecosystem and a growing global customer base. Revenue increased 12% year-over-year to $114.5 billion. This growth came despite foreign exchange pressures and supply constraints affecting the iPhone, Mac and iPad, suggesting underlying demand remains strong.

Hardware remained the primary growth contributor, with product revenue rising 12% to $82.9 billion. iPhone revenue increased 17% to $57.6 billion, reflecting strong demand across developed and emerging markets. Growth was broad-based, while the active iPhone installed base reached a new high. Record upgrade activity in markets such as the U.S., China, India, and Japan indicates that Apple continues to benefit from customer loyalty and its ability to encourage users to adopt newer devices.

Story Continues

Mac revenue grew 24% to $10.8 billion, supported by demand for the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro. Performance across emerging markets was encouraging, pointing to further opportunities as Apple expands its presence among first-time Mac buyers and existing customers upgrading their devices.

Beyond hardware, services revenue increased 10% to $31.6 billion. The installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices provides a substantial platform for monetization. Paid subscriptions exceeded 1.5 billion, while strength across cloud, payments, advertising, video, and music reflects the breadth of demand for Apple's ecosystem.

However, profitability remains an area worth watching. Apple reported a gross margin of 47.9%. Its margins included about a one-percentage-point benefit from tariff refunds. Excluding this benefit, margins declined sequentially, mainly due to higher memory costs. This suggests rising component costs could pressure profitability in the quarters ahead.

Nonetheless, Apple's ability to generate solid cash flow positions it well to return significant cash to its shareholders. It returned $28 billion to shareholders in Q4 through dividends and share buybacks.

Looking ahead, management expects Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue to grow between 7% and 10%, despite continued supply limitations. Overall, Apple's growth story remains intact, supported by strong customer loyalty, healthy demand and a growing services business.

AAPL's Solid Fundamentals Support Growth, but Valuation Warrants Caution

Apple's fundamentals remain solid, with robust iPhone demand, continued services growth, and a record installed base supporting its long-term outlook. Despite supply-chain constraints and rising memory costs, the company delivered solid revenue growth and maintained its ability to generate substantial cash flow.

Its disciplined approach to AI investments also provides a potential advantage by limiting exposure to the heavy capital expenditure and profitability pressures facing some of its technology peers.

With optimism surrounding iPhone demand, earnings growth and Apple's competitive positioning already reflected in the share price, the scope for further upside may be more limited. AAPL stock is trading at a forward earnings multiple of 35.4, which is high relative to its EPS growth trajectory. Meanwhile, higher component costs and potential margin pressures remain important risks to monitor.

Consequently, despite its solid fundamentals and promising growth prospects, AAPL stock still isn't a "Strong Buy" at present.

news.Title: It’s Game Over for DJT Stock as Trump Becomes a Lame-Duck President Following Midterm Losses
news.Content:
U.S. stocks soared on Nov. 4, as the midterm election results started coming in. The Dow Jones Index ($DOWI) rose 3% and posted its biggest post-midterm rally in 44 years. The rally was quite broad-based with few exceptions. For instance, artificial intelligence (AI) data center companies' share prices fell amid fears of tighter regulations. Among others, Applied Digital (APLD) fell 6.7% while CoreWeave (CRWV) shed nearly 10%. Nvidia (NVDA) — which has been the bellwether for AI trade — fell over 3% and is trading below $200, a price level I previously noted as an attractive entry point.

DJT and Elon Musk Names Plummet After Midterm Results

It was a sombre day for Elon Musk-run companies, and both Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) fell by over 3%. The world's richest person donated nearly half a billion dollars this election to Republicans, but his backing didn't help as Democrats flipped both the Senate and the House. While SpaceX listed only this year, Tesla was the ultimate "Trump trade" before the relationship between President Donald Trump and Musk soured, eventually culminating in the latter's exit from the White House.

More News from Barchart

Why Michael Burry Says Fiserv Stock Could Surge as Much as 94% From Here

Bloom Energy Stock Rallies as Barclays Turns Bullish on California Power Partnership

Oracle Just Walked Away From a $7 Billion Tencent Deal. Here's What It Means for ORCL Stock.

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Trump Media & Technology Group (DJT), which has been slumping from one low to another, predictably had a terrible day and lost nearly a quarter of its market cap yesterday, entering the penny stock category. The market cap of Truth Social's parent company fell to $1.25 billion, shaving tens of millions from Trump's net worth.

I had never been a fan of President Trump's enterprise, and in an article in 2024, when he was moving closer to securing the GOP nomination for the presidential election, I noted that it would be prudent to stay clear of Digital World Acquisition — the special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) that announced a merger with Trump Media and Technology Group (TMTG).

Last month, as DJT fell to all-time lows, I noted that it still wasn't late to exit the stock. The stock has since continued to dwindle, and the midterm election results have only added fuel to the fire. With the stock now trading at fresh record lows, let's explore whether it's time to buy the dip.

Story Continues

How to Play DJT as Trump Becomes a Lame Duck President

Just as the "Musk premium" drives the valuations of companies Elon Musk heads, DJT's business and valuations are interwoven with Trump, who is now staring at a lame duck presidency for over two years.

Looking at TMTG's businesses, apart from Truth Social — an X lookalike that failed to capture the popular imagination — it runs the Truth+ streaming platform and has a financial services arm, Truth.Fi. The company also functions like a Bitcoin treasury firm and held $1.2 billion worth of Bitcoin (BTCUSD) and other digital assets at the end of June. In total, DJT held around $1.9 billion in gross financial assets at the end of June, but the number falls to $893 million after adjusting for debt. If the company's business wasn't complex enough, it has proposed a merger with TAE Energy, a nuclear fusion company, touting it as key to its long-term success.

DJT never really functioned as a "normal" enterprise, and those buying the company were essentially betting on Trump. It's no coincidence that the company's different business lines, including the proposed merger with TAE Energy, stand to benefit from the Trump administration's policies.

For four years, the company was led by David Nunes, a Trump confidante and former Republican congressman from California. In April, DJT appointed Kevin McGurn as its interim CEO. He brings significant experience in streaming and advertising, unlike Nunes, who was previously in the dairy farming business.

In his first earnings call in August, which was eventually the company's inaugural call with analysts and came over two years after going public, McGurn signaled that DJT would start functioning as a normal listed company and promised regular updates and communication. However, I don't find anything attractive about the business, and would avoid the stock despite the recent sell-off. A lot of DJT's businesses rely on Trump's policies, including the controversial decision to sell faster access to his Truth Social posts. With Trump expected to lose authority after the midterm elections, and his actions inviting greater scrutiny, the game might be over for DJT, even with undemanding valuations and accounting for the massive net financial assets it holds on its balance sheet.

news.Title: Elon Musk Says Tesla Will End Cybertruck Production -- Here's Why
news.Content: Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) CEO Elon Musk formally unveiled the Cybertruck in 2019. Actual production didn't begin until 2024. Next year, production will formally end, according to a new tweet from Musk. Musk shared on social media that the electric vehicle (EV) maker will wind down "production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year." Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Why is the Cybertruck going extinct? Slow sales are largely to blame. According to estimates, Tesla is only selling a few thousand units per quarter. If the Cybertruck were a mass success like the Model 3 and Model Y, it likely would not be getting the axe. But there's another obvious reason that Tesla is winding down production for one of its least successful models ever. Here's why Tesla is ending Cybertruck production Tesla's $1.4 trillion valuation isn't based on its success as an automaker. Instead, the market is pricing in plenty of growth for other opportunities, namely AI, humanoid robots, and self-driving cars. All of these initiatives will be capital-intensive to scale. Freeing up capital by ending a low-volume, low-potential model is a wise decision for Tesla as it pivots its priorities toward the future. Just as importantly, Tesla will then be able to use the factory space to focus on Cybercab production. Musk said so directly, tweeting that ceasing Cybertruck production is designed specifically "to make room for increased Cybercab production." Some experts believe that the robotaxi market will eventually be valued at $8 trillion to $10 trillion globally. Success in that market can move the needle for Tesla in a way Cybertruck demand never could. news.Title: 台股大跌如恐怖攻擊！唐綺陽揭轉折點示警：發財夢已成過去
news.Content:
台灣股市本週迎來史詩級暴跌，讓不少投資人哀鴻遍野。對此，星座專家唐綺陽直言，這次大跌已達「恐怖攻擊」等級，她提醒，距離週末轉折點還有數天，屆時將迎來「火木合相」最高峰，火星能量持續放大發酵，呼籲大眾務必提高警覺，切勿衝動決策。

唐綺陽8日上午發文指出，這波股市波動直接衝擊無數投資人的荷包與未來生活規劃，讓人感到無比焦慮與受挫，因上週星象受「火星觸擊木星與土星」影響，引發了社會氛圍的劇烈震盪，而在台灣應驗的正是股市大挫，再加上近期適逢水星與金星逆行天蠍與天秤座，許多人在情緒上都有深層的不適感，甚至出現「被人弄了卻無力還手」的沉痛與無奈。

不過，唐綺陽也為陷入低潮的大眾帶來曙光，預告星象轉折時間點就在本週末，也就是11月14日（週六），水星天蠍與金星天秤將同步恢復順行。其中水星順行將讓雙子座與處女座擺脫被動牽制，雖然依然忙碌但效率大增，不再傷腦筋；而金星順行則讓金牛座與天秤座擺脫悶沉，天秤座更能重啟計畫、恢復聲望與自我價值。

對大眾而言，這波水天蠍逆行也昭示「股市最恐怖的局面」，代表順行後，發財夢已成過去，呼籲大家必須建立全新的理財心態重新開始。此外，唐綺陽特別提醒，隨著木星停滯減速，膨脹與吹牛的事物開始收束，盲目的信心與過度期待將回歸現實，講求腳踏實地。

唐綺陽指出11月15日（週日）將迎來「火木合相」最高峰，在個人星盤中「25至27度有星者」為直接受衝擊的事主，可能帶來爆紅關注或暴衝意外，需注意跌打損傷與工傷，並留意周遭情緒激動的人。

最後，她勸大家本週還在逆行、火木合的階段，一定要耐住性子、忍住衝動，切勿急著請辭或找人對質，靜待週末轉折點迎接新篇章，「祝大家都平安度過本週，並有重生信心，祝福大家」。

news.Title: AIDC審查恐拉高成本、美股急洩別慌？摩根解析：標普500回檔仍在歷史常態範圍
news.Content:
美國政治風向成為科技股新震央！市場擔憂民主黨掌握國會後可能提高AI監管強度，衝擊數據中心建設與科技業資本支出，11月5日美股全面重挫。標普500指數單日大跌4.4%，500檔成分股高達430檔收黑，那斯達克指數下跌5.5%，費城半導體指數更暴跌12.3%，避險資金急湧美債。據統計，截至11月6日，標普500指數雖較10月初高點修正約6%，仍低於今年3月8.7%的修正幅度；摩根資產管理表示，這波修正凸顯AI市場敘事正在轉變，投資人不宜將資產集中押注單一AI題材。

摩根投信環球市場策略師林雅慧表示，市場目前最擔心民主黨掌握國會後，AI安全、數據中心建設、能源使用與電網成本等議題面臨更嚴格檢視。特別是AI數據中心需要大量電力，若審批時間拉長、電網升級成本提高，甚至要求科技業者承擔更多基礎建設支出，都可能拉高AI資本支出成本，進一步壓縮投資報酬率。

林雅慧指出，這種影響不會只停留在美國。過去數年AI資本支出狂潮，讓台灣、韓國、日本的半導體、記憶體、伺服器及AI硬體供應鏈成為最大受惠者；一旦市場開始下修AI基礎建設擴張預期，東北亞供應鏈將成為資金重新定價的第一線，美國的AI監管疑慮可能快速轉化為亞洲科技股的估值壓力。

根據彭博資訊與摩根資產管理統計，各大科技巨頭資料中心支出成長幅度逐漸放緩，包含Amazon、Google、Meta與Microsoft等企業在2027至2028年間的支出成長率落在7.47%至13.03%不等，Core Weave成長率為4.17%，Oracle甚至出現6.73%的負成長，整體資料中心支出成長率估落在8.91%。

不過，急跌究竟是AI基本面反轉或市場情緒快速降溫，仍需時間驗證。林雅慧補充，截至11月6日，標普500指數雖較10月初高點修正約6%，仍低於今年3月8.7%的修正幅度；回顧1980年以來標普500指數年度內平均最大跌幅約達14%，顯示目前震盪並未超出歷史常見修正範圍。

摩根資產管理強調，當市場不再只以數據中心、晶片與資本支出為AI成長買單，而是採用速度、實際營收、獲利能力與投資報酬率做為評價基準時，與其繼續押注單一AI產業或市場，投資組合更應透過全球股票、不同產業與債券進行分散，避免當AI敘事轉彎時，整體資產同時承受衝擊。

news.Title: Tesla Stock Hasn't Closed at a Record in Nearly 11 Months. Here's How Its Past Record Droughts Ended.
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) last closed at a record on Dec. 16, 2025, at $489.88 a share. That was 327 days ago, or nearly 11 months. With Tesla shares trading near $346 as I write this, the stock would have to gain about 41% just to tie it.

Long gaps between records are nothing new for the EV maker, though. Since its IPO in June 2010, Tesla stock has gone 300 days or more without a record close six other times, based on daily split-adjusted closing prices.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Every one of those droughts eventually ended. But what happened next was very different. Two of them gave way to rallies of over 600%. The other four were followed by a new drought within months, and twice within days.

And the difference between the two groups probably boils down to whether Tesla's profits were turning higher.

Image source: Getty Images.

Long waits are common for Tesla

The first two droughts came early in the electric-vehicle maker's life as a public company. The stock spent 474 days without a record from Nov. 24, 2010, to March 12, 2012, and then exactly 300 days from April 3, 2012, to Jan. 28, 2013. The next two lasted longer, at 942 days from Sept. 4, 2014, to April 3, 2017, and 821 days from Sept. 18, 2017, to Dec. 18, 2019. Most recently, shares went 1,133 days from Nov. 4, 2021, to Dec. 11, 2024, and then 364 days from Dec. 17, 2024, to last December's record.

That makes the current 327-day wait the second shortest of the seven. The middle of the six past droughts is around 650 days, or almost twice as long as this one has lasted.

Of course, the drops along the way were steep. In the 2021-to-2024 drought, the stock's lowest close was around 74% below its prior record.

And in every one of the six, shares closed at least 31% under the old high at some point. This time, the low so far was $298.32 on July 29, around 39% below the December record.

What happened when the droughts ended?

Two of them ended in huge runs. Once the 300-day gap closed on Jan. 28, 2013, Tesla stock kept setting records until Sept. 4, 2014, rising around 652% in that time.

And once the drought ended on Dec. 18, 2019, shares climbed about 1,464% to the November 2021 record that started the longest wait of all.

The other four runs were short. The March 2012 record led to just 22 days of new highs before the next drought began. The April 2017 record brought around five and a half months of records and a 29% climb.

Story Continues

The December 2024 run of records lasted six days. Last December's record ended one drought and began the current one the same day.

In other words, a new record on its own hasn't said much about what happens next. For shareholders, I'd say this matters more than the length of any drought.

Profits made the difference

What the two big runs share is a turn in profits.

In May 2013, Tesla said it had become profitable in the first quarter "for the first time in our ten year history," earning $11 million. The stock gained about 24% the day after the letter came out.

The 2019 run followed a similar swing. The company made $143 million in the third quarter of 2019. That was a sharp turn from losses of $702 million and $408 million earlier that year. Even more, its net income hit $721 million in 2020 -- after losing money in each of the four years before that.

But the four short runs had nothing like that behind them. The company lost $396 million in 2012 and almost $2 billion in 2017.

And its operating income (profit from the business before interest and taxes) was falling in both 2024 and 2025, down 20% and then another 38%.

That trend hasn't turned yet. In the first nine months of 2026, Tesla's operating income totaled about $2.1 billion, down about 30% from the same period in 2025.

What does this history suggest for anyone owning the stock now?

I don't think 11 months without a new high is a reason to sell on its own. After all, waits this long have been normal for the growth stock, and every one of them has ended.

But the next record might matter less than what's behind it. One that comes with operating income climbing again may look a lot more like 2013 or 2019. Without that, a new high might fade as fast as the last two did.

news.Content:
凱基投顧指出，就技術面觀察，台股自10月6日歷史高點49,968點展開修正，到11月6日盤中最低37,837點，波段回檔幅度達24.28%，顯示中短期趨勢已明顯轉弱。不過，隨加權指數與短、中期均線的負乖離快速擴大，短線已逐步具備跌深反彈的技術條件。

凱基投顧指出，後續觀察重點首先在於40,000點能否重新站回。這個點位已由原先的心理支撐轉為反彈過程中的重要壓力關卡，收復後才有望進一步擴大反彈空間；而後則觀察能否迅速回補11月6日留下的40,435-41,513點空方缺口，可視為短線跌勢能否有效修復的重要指標。

在籌碼面部分，融資去槓桿程度同樣值得關注。凱基投顧指出，上市櫃融資餘額去化幅度仍不足以確認市場浮額已完成充分清洗，意味高槓桿交易所帶來的籌碼風險尚未完全解除。因此，後續只有技術面與籌碼面同步改善，才有機會將短線跌深反彈走勢轉化為延續性較佳的波段反彈行情。

凱基投顧認為，目前市場仍處於高度不穩定階段，操作上應以降低槓桿、維持資金流動性為優先。後續若費半指數不再創低、外資賣壓明顯收斂，以及融資去槓桿告一段落這三項條件同時成立，屆時才具備較充分的條件逐步提高整體股票曝險。

至於選股方向，凱基投顧建議，最好由過去偏重題材與想像空間，轉向實質獲利成長與基本面能見度。近期10月營收、第3季財報及法說會對後續營運展望將陸續公布，將成為評估個股基本面強弱的重要依據。

news.Title: 台股一周狂瀉5,510點！法人曝下檔關卡 反彈可看這些族群
news.Content:
台股跌破40K，上周大跌5,510點、跌幅12.1%，收在39,701點。群益投顧指出，台股連七跌改寫波段新低，短線技術面延續弱勢，指數區間38,000-42,000 點，建議保守觀望靜待落底，等待反彈訊號再酌量適度搶短。

群益投顧分析，市場擔憂美國民主黨在期中選舉大勝後，將加強AI與資料中心監管，引爆晶片及AI類股賣壓，台股受到衝擊。從資金流向來看，部分資金流向航空、成衣、生技及金融股。

華南投顧指出，台股指數雖走弱，但先進晶片需求因AI在全球的發展仍強勁，且川普對禁止AI法案有否決權，民主黨雖期中選舉大勝，但人數未達三分之二，難以推翻川普的否決。台股波段跌幅已達20.6%，投資人可逢低布局台積電（2330）和晶圓代工概念股，如廠務工程、半導體設備和材料類股。

華南投顧分析，全球高效能運算（HPC）與AI客戶需求強勁，長約機制使短期受政策變動影響有限，相關廠商包括台積電、聯電（2303）、力積電（6770）、世界先進（5347）等。在封測類股方面，雲端服務供應商（CSP）大廠對高階封裝需求高，隨協力廠產能開出，確保高階產品線出貨順暢，例如日月光投控（3711）、力成（6239）、京元電（2449）等。

另外，華南投顧指出，市場擔憂民主黨將加強AI與資料中心監管，資金由晶片及AI基礎建設類股轉往民生必需品類股，傳產股可望受惠，例如儒鴻（1476）、聚陽（1477）、統一（1216）等。

news.Title: 反AI恐慌襲捲股市！謝金河指1關鍵：會修正回來
news.Content: 財經中心／李筱舲報導 美國期中選舉結果揭曉，民主黨大勝席捲參眾兩院，卻在金融市場引爆「反 AI」恐慌海嘯。受部分主張暫緩資料中心建置、甚至主張暫停 AI 發展的候選人當選影響，美股那斯達克（Nasdaq）與費城半導體指數出現史詩級暴跌，亞洲股市也無一倖免。對此，財經專家謝金河發文分析，民主機制具備自動調整功能，短線市場「殺過頭」後股價終將修正回軌道。 美國期中選舉結果出爐，「反AI」風潮引發美股和亞股市恐慌性拋售。（圖／民視資料照） 期中選舉吹「反AI」風潮！美亞股市遭恐慌性拋售 謝金河指出，這場驚嚇給全球市場上了重要一課。民主黨大勝後，多位新當選官員拋出對 AI 產業不利的政策主張，包括反對資料中心建置的州長當選，密西根州勝選的穆斯林醫生 Abdul El-Sayed 更曾主張「美國應停止發展 AI」。此外，更有政客提出將馬斯克移送法辦、企業收歸國有，以及加州醞釀加徵超高富人稅等激進主張，引發市場對美國政策走向的極度恐慌。川普眼看股市慘跌，也出面痛批民主黨造成股市動盪。 謝金河指出，美國在 AI 賽道上沒有回頭路，股價修正後仍然會走回原來的軌道。（圖／民視資料照） 民主體制有調節機制！殺過頭股價將重回軌道 面對市場哀鴻遍野，謝金河認為不必過度悲觀。他分析，民主體制下每個人雖然都可以大鳴大放，但社會最終會發揮自我調整機制，朝對大家有利的方向修正。例如先前反對資料中心的 德州新當選州長已澄清「並不討厭資料中心」，既有的不反對、僅對新申請案加強監管 ； 德州年輕的新當選參議員也公開表示願意與馬斯克對話溝 通。 謝金河強調，經歷這場肅殺後，恐慌情緒極可能在短線見頂，6日 VIX 恐慌指數拉高 70% 後將回落，美股與台股殺過頭的股價會逐漸修正回來。他直言， 美國在 AI 賽道上已經「沒有回頭路」，短線政策波折與估值衝擊不改長線趨勢，股價修正後仍然會走回原來的軌道 。 《民視新聞網》提醒您：內容僅供參考，投資人於決策時應審慎評估風險，並就投資結果自行負責。

news.Title: Intel, Arm, and Marvell Have Each Been Cut in Half Since June. Only 1 Is a Stock I'd Buy Now.
news.Content:
Intel (NASDAQ:INTC), Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM), and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) all set record closes in June. Five months later, each stock is worth less than half as much.

Intel closed at $58.27 on Nov. 4, off around 59% from $140.94, its record close on June 22. Arm ended that day at $191.80, around 56% under its June 18 record close, and Marvell finished at $159.80, about 50% below where it closed on June 4.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

All three fell between around 4% and 7% on Nov. 4 alone, then slid further on Nov. 5. Investors were weighing whether Democrats' midterm wins might slow the build-out of artificial intelligence data centers, especially after Texas elected a governor who campaigned for a moratorium on new ones.

Falls this steep can make all three look like bargains. But each stock is still up over 40% in 2026. And only one of them expects its sales growth to keep speeding up, even as its stock got cheaper.

Marvell is that one, and it's the only one of the three I'd buy right now.

Image source: Getty Images.

Intel's PC problem

Intel's third quarter was strong, with revenue up 21% year over year. The problem is the outlook it gave on Oct. 29. Intel sees non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings of $0.25 per share for the fourth quarter, under half the $0.52 it earned in the third quarter.

PCs are the biggest reason. Higher memory prices have pushed up what new PCs cost, and Intel expects revenue in its PC chip segment to drop over 20% from the third quarter. Its chief financial officer, David Zinsner, sees the weakness lasting until at least mid-2027.

Yes, demand for Intel's server chips still tops what it can supply. But at around $54, Intel stock trades at around 36 times the earnings expected for 2026 and about 30 times the earnings expected for 2027.

Is Arm's royalty slowdown priced in?

Arm reported its fiscal 2027 second quarter (the three months ended Sept. 30) on the evening of Nov. 4. Revenue climbed 27% year over year to $1.44 billion, and its adjusted earnings per share increased 33% to $0.52.

The figure I'd follow most closely, though, is royalty revenue (the fees Arm gets for every Arm-based chip its partners ship). Royalties grew just 8% from a year earlier to $670 million, a sharp slowdown from 22% growth in fiscal Q1. Arm said memory prices hit the smartphone market and offset some of its gains elsewhere.

Story Continues

Licensing revenue, however, jumped 50% to $773 million, and management called licensing an important leading indicator of future royalty growth.

Sure, that might prove true. But at around $170, Arm stock trades at around 56 times its expected earnings for next fiscal year (ending March 2028). Even after a drop of around 60%, investors paying that price are arguably relying on royalties to speed up again soon.

Marvell's sales are speeding up

Marvell's numbers are going the other way. Its revenue growth has climbed each quarter of fiscal 2027 so far, from 28% year over year in the first quarter to 37% in the second (through Aug. 1). On Nov. 2, Marvell said fiscal third-quarter revenue is tracking with its $3.15 billion forecast, now within 2% either way. That'd be around 52% above the year-ago quarter. What's more, Marvell's August forecast called for $1.10 in adjusted earnings per share, up around 45% from $0.76 the year before.

The same day, Marvell agreed to buy optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) in an all-stock deal that values Lumentum at around $115 billion, including its debt. Lumentum shareholders would get 4.5 Marvell shares for every Lumentum share, leaving today's Marvell shareholders holding around two-thirds of the combined company. Closing is expected in the first half of 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approval.

At around $141, Marvell stock trades at around 19 times the earnings expected for fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028), based on Marvell's business alone.

Which one would I buy?

Intel's server chips and Arm's licensing business are each doing well. But Intel's profits are set to fall steeply this quarter, and Arm's royalty growth just slowed to 8%. At today's prices, I think both stocks still cost too much for these problems.

Marvell is the only one of the three whose latest forecast calls for its sales growth to speed up again. And based on next year's expected earnings, its price-to-earnings ratio is around a third of Arm's.

In the end, I think Marvell stock is worth buying here, maybe a bit at a time as the Lumentum deal moves toward closing.

news.Title: 5 Worst Dow Stocks To Buy According to Analysts
news.Content:
Yahoo Finance reported on November 5 that the Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled 3.4%, or more than 1,800 points, while the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq Composite sank 5.5% into correction territory. Chip stocks took the brunt of the damage, as the leading AI chipmaker fell 9% to pace Dow decliners and another chip designer plunged 17%, the outlet reported.

The slide erased the gains from a day earlier, when the Dow had jumped nearly 1,600 points after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, Yahoo Finance wrote on November 4. Even so, the blue-chip index finished Thursday just 1.9% below its record closing high of 54,349 from early August.

The Dow's Safe-Haven Run Cracks

For most of the week, the Dow had looked like the sheltered corner of the market. Yahoo Finance reported on November 2 that the Dow edged up 0.4% while the Nasdaq dropped roughly 1% as investors rotated out of technology names and into consumer cyclical and financial services shares. One household consumer brand has divided opinion lately, and we covered why a well-known TV host is staying away from the sneaker maker after losing money on it .

On Thursday, that cushion gave way, as the focus turned to what a Democratic Congress could mean for the AI buildout, and for the data centers driving it in particular. Data center power and infrastructure stocks fell by double digits, and the Nasdaq 100 was recently more than 10% below its October closing high. The reversal was fast. Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at an equity research firm, pointed out that the VIX volatility index posted its biggest one-day jump in more than two years. It took the Nasdaq just six minutes to erase its entire post-election rally.

A Jobs Report Steadies the Tape

Friday brought a partial rebound. Yahoo Finance reported on November 6 that the US added 165,000 jobs in October, and the Nasdaq gained 1.9% while the S&P 500 rose 1% and the Dow added 0.1%. You might also be interested in reading our piece on why a billionaire money manager and a TV host both still like the iPhone maker .

The stronger jobs data lifted Treasury yields and kept Federal Reserve policy at the center of market attention, Reuters reported on November 6, as the price-weighted index of 30 major US companies held roughly flat.

We shared the expanded list of the 10 Worst Dow Stocks To Buy here . You can see the 5 worst stocks below.

Our Methodology

For this article, we used Finviz to screen the 30 components of the Dow Jones Industrial Average and calculated each stock's average upside potential, based on analysts' average price target. We picked the 10 stocks with the lowest upside potential and ranked them in descending order of upside. We also list each stock's short interest and number of hedge fund holders as of Q2 2026.

Story Continues

Note: All data was sourced on November 6, 2026.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

5 Worst Dow Stocks To Buy

5. Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 111

Short Interest: 1.70%

Average Upside Potential: 2%

Advertising and online sales are changing what a Walmart dollar earns. Global eCommerce sales rose 23% in the fiscal second quarter, and global advertising grew 38%, with the US Walmart Connect ad business up 43% excluding Vizio.

Operating income rose 28.8%, boosted by tariff refunds that the retailer said it would put back into lower prices. Management raised its sales and operating income growth guidance for the year, and said it will keep prioritizing investment in price during the second half. Operating cash flow reached $19.7 billion for the first half of the year, which helps fund those price cuts.

Walmart US also posted strong growth across digital. Walmart International also grew, with Sam's Club China reaching record membership counts and Flipkart's advertising business expanding. Sam's Club US showed steady membership growth and more transactions, and nearly half of Walmart's marketplace business now flows through its fulfillment services, which gives outside sellers a reason to stay on the platform. Walmart reports its next quarter later this month, when investors will see how the price investments and the digital businesses are working together.

Our analysis on Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) can be found here: Walmart (WMT): Can Suppliers Keep Funding Its Inventory Growth?

4. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 169

Short Interest: 0.90%

Average Upside Potential: -1%

A new CEO, a record September quarter and a fresh iPhone lineup have given Apple momentum into the holidays. Revenue reached $114.5 billion, up 12%, and iPhone sales set a September-quarter record. Services hit an all-time high, and the installed base of active devices reached a record in every major product category and region.

Profit was strong as well. Diluted earnings per share rose 14%, and the company generated $28 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter and returned $28 billion to shareholders. Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh said fiscal 2026 capped a year of double-digit earnings growth and all-time record revenue.

Chief Executive John Ternus pointed to the lineup carrying Apple into the holiday season: the iPhone Duo, which he called the most transformational iPhone since the original, the iPhone 18 Pro models, the first Macs with touch, and an all-new Siri AI. Apple also reported a September-quarter record for iPhone upgraders worldwide, and said it gained Mac share globally. Apple also said it grew in the vast majority of the markets it tracks, with September-quarter revenue records in the Americas, Europe, Greater China and the rest of Asia Pacific.

Read our analysis on Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) here: Apple (AAPL): Can Longer iPhone Ownership Still Produce More Profit per Customer?

3. Travelers (NYSE: TRV )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 50

Short Interest: 2.79%

Average Upside Potential: -3%

Underwriting discipline is paying off at Travelers. Core income reached $9.18 per diluted share in the third quarter, a core return on equity of 22.1%, and the underlying combined ratio came in at 84.1%. Underwriting results were strong across all three of the insurer's segments.

Even with higher catastrophe losses from severe wind and hail storms, the company produced strong results, helped by favorable development on prior-year reserves and higher net investment income. New business hit a third-quarter record, which shows the insurer is still winning customers as it prices carefully, and renewal pricing remained orderly. Premiums held steady even after the sale of the Canadian operations earlier in the year, and grew when that sale is excluded. Management said retention and returns reflected excellent execution. The company reported underwriting income of $1.4 billion before taxes, and underlying underwriting income was even higher.

Cash is flowing back to owners. Travelers returned excess capital to shareholders during the quarter, including $1.5 billion of share repurchases. Chief Executive Alan Schnitzer said the results reflected very strong underwriting performance and that the momentum gives him real confidence heading into 2027 and beyond.

2. Amgen (NASDAQ: AMGN )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 66

Short Interest: 2.48%

Average Upside Potential: -5%

Seventeen Amgen products grew at least 10% in the third quarter, and the same number now run at more than $1 billion a year. Total revenue rose 8%, driven by volume growth rather than price, which points to demand for the medicines rather than a one-time boost.

Newer drugs are carrying the climb. Imdelltra, a medicine for small cell lung cancer, grew 128% from a year earlier, while Repatha and Evenity each grew by more than a third. Uplizna sales nearly tripled, and Tezspire and Blincyto also posted double-digit gains, so growth is coming from several therapeutic areas at once. Non-GAAP operating margin edged higher even as operating expenses rose, and the GAAP operating margin climbed 9.9 percentage points. The company also advanced important clinical programs during the quarter.

Profit grew faster than sales, with non-GAAP earnings per share up 14%, and the company generated $3.7 billion of free cash flow in the quarter. Chief Executive Robert Bradway said the strength of the commercial portfolio, together with important clinical advances and a promising late-stage pipeline, reinforces confidence in durable growth well into the next decade.

Our analysis on Amgen (NASDAQ:AMGN) is here: Amgen (AMGN) Sales Grew 10%, but Can Earnings Catch Up to the Price?

1. Nike (NYSE: NKE )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 56

Short Interest: 8.82%

Average Upside Potential: -8%

Gross margin is climbing at Nike even as sales shrink, the early sign of a turnaround that bulls are watching. Gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 42.8% in the fiscal first quarter, helped by lower warehousing and logistics costs, while selling and administrative expense fell 3%. Management said the quarter matched its expectations. Chief Executive Elliott Hill added that Nike is taking deliberate actions to strengthen Nike Sportswear, Jordan Brand and Greater China for the long term.

The company is also cutting costs on purpose. Its new operating model, called Pace, is expected to deliver about $2.5 billion in cumulative savings through fiscal 2031. Hill said the Sport Offense is producing measurable progress across priority sports, and wholesale revenue grew in North America.

Nike returned about $610 million to shareholders through dividends in the quarter, and ended it with $8.4 billion in cash and short-term investments. Chief Financial Officer Dave Denton said results were supported by the improved gross margin and disciplined cost management, and that the company will keep strengthening its product portfolio, improving productivity and allocating resources with discipline.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of NKE as an investment, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than NKE that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock .

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) CEO Elon Musk said in a post on X on Friday that the company will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory around the middle of next year. The goal is to make room for more Cybercabs, Tesla 's two-seat robotaxi. Musk didn't say if Tesla would build the truck somewhere else.

The Cybertruck isn't the first vehicle to give up its place this year. In January, Musk said Tesla would stop production of the Model S and Model X. The company has since replaced those lines at its Fremont, California, plant with production of its Optimus humanoid robot.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

At first glance, this is a big shake-up of Tesla's lineup. Measured by sales, though, it isn't.

Vehicles other than the Model 3 and Model Y (mostly the Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck) made up about 3% of the EV maker 's 1.64 million deliveries in 2025.

Measured by factory space, the change is much bigger. And I think the gap between those two measures matters more for the stock than for the car business.

Image source: Getty Images.

Lines built for far more

Showing how much room these three vehicles took up, Tesla's installed-capacity table at the end of 2025 rated its Model S and Model X line at 100,000 vehicles a year and its Cybertruck line at over 125,000. Combined, they could build more than 225,000 vehicles yearly, or almost 10% of the more than 2.35 million vehicles Tesla's car plants were rated for.

But Tesla made just 53,900 vehicles outside the Model 3 and Model Y in all of 2025 -- under a quarter of what those lines were built for. And deliveries in this group dropped 40% from 2024, to 50,850.

The slide kept going in 2026. Other-model deliveries fell from 16,130 in the first quarter (probably boosted by final orders for the S and X) to 12,364 in the second quarter and 8,295 in the third. The third-quarter total was down 48% year over year.

The Cybertruck, of course, never got close to filling its line. Tesla doesn't break out sales by model, but Cox Automotive estimated U.S. Cybertruck sales at around 20,000 in 2025, down from about 39,000 in 2024. Musk once said the truck would one day sell 250,000 a year.

Put another way, even if the Cybertruck goes away forever, Tesla is giving up very little to free up this space. Tesla's automotive sales revenue fell just 1% year over year in the third quarter. And its quarterly filing linked slightly lower deliveries mostly to fewer Model S and Model X sales.

Story Continues

Arguably, handing underused lines to new products is a sound move.

What's replacing them?

In Fremont, Tesla said in its third-quarter update that Optimus production had started on its high-volume lines, calling the bots coming off them its first production-quality robots. The plan, set out in January, is for that first line to one day make 1 million robots a year.

In Texas, Cybercab production began earlier this year on a line Tesla rates at over 125,000 vehicles a year, matching the Cybertruck line it'll take room from. Tesla has started adding these Cybercabs to its own Robotaxi fleet in Austin.

Neither product has its own revenue line in Tesla's results yet. Tesla took in around $104 billion in revenue over its past four reported quarters, and about 72% of it still came from its car business. The Model 3 and Model Y made up 98% of third-quarter deliveries. And total automotive revenue, which also includes regulatory credits, dropped 3% year over year in that quarter.

Tesla stock already assumes the swap pays off

The stock, however, is priced as if both new products will succeed. With shares trading at around $358 as of this writing, Tesla's price-to-earnings ratio is above 160 based on the 2027 earnings forecast. By comparison, the forward price-to-earnings ratio of the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) is about 19.

A car business with falling revenue can't support a price-to-earnings ratio so high by itself. It only makes sense if Cybercab and Optimus grow into large, profitable businesses.

Sure, Tesla could pull it off. A robot line targeting 1 million units per year would be a massive business if demand materializes. But Optimus production has only just begun, and Tesla hasn't said what either new product earns.

Ultimately, the Cybertruck decision makes sense for the business. Still, it shows how much of the stock's value now depends on products for which Tesla doesn't yet report sales. Measured against Tesla's car business today, I think the stock is still far too expensive.

news.Title: Did Apple Just Get a Boost From Democrats? Data Center Moratoriums Could Benefit the iPhone Maker
news.Content:
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) issued a warning to investors when it shared its fourth-quarter earnings results at the start of November. Its huge profit margin on device sales could head in the wrong direction for the foreseeable future. The culprit: memory chips.

Memory chip pricing has soared over the past few quarters, driven by growth in AI data center spending . AI accelerator chips get packaged alongside high-bandwidth memory chips, which are effectively stacks of standard DRAM memory chips -- the same types of chips found in Apple's iPhone and MacBook, among other devices. Demand for those chips, while supply remains limited, has led to massive price increases, and Apple is finally starting to feel the pain.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The recent election, however, could provide some relief for Apple, given the growing potential for Democrats to impose AI data center moratoriums across the country.

Delays in data centers could open up more supply for Apple

Democrats took control of both the House and the Senate in this year's midterm election, paving the way for more federal regulation and policies that could curb the growth of AI. The more immediate impact, however, could come at the state level. Four of the biggest states for AI data center developments -- Texas, Ohio, Georgia, and Arizona -- will have Democratic governors once they're sworn in in January.

Many of those governors have announced plans to increase oversight and regulation of new data center construction (Texas did so even before Tuesday's election), aiming to mitigate any negative impacts on citizens. Venture Capitalist Brad Gerstner suggested that 25% to 35% of next year's data center build-out could be at risk of delays as a result of new governments across the country.

That could provide some relief for Apple. If data centers aren't going under construction, that means there's no place to put new server racks, and less demand for high-bandwidth memory chips. Reduced demand should put downward pressure on prices, limiting the impact of memory chip pricing on Apple's gross margin.

Apple management danced around whether it had already locked in pricing for some memory supply. All three major memory chipmakers, Micron , SK Hynix , and Samsung , have shifted to signing long-term agreements to establish pricing ranges and provide more confidence in building new capacity. While that caps their near-term upside, it protects them from a major price collapse as they work to increase the total supply of memory chips.

Story Continues

Management did reveal that it increased purchase commitments by $33 billion last quarter, but not all of that is necessarily related to memory chips. Still, reports indicate that Apple did sign long-term agreements for at least some memory chip supply to ensure it would have enough chips to meet its expected device demand.

Take the long view

In the grand scheme of things, the memory crunch could play only a minor role in Apple's long-term earnings growth. Supply and demand will eventually reach equilibrium again, and Apple should see its component prices and gross margin return to normal levels.

Earlier this year, I wrote that Apple is best positioned among consumer electronics device makers in the face of rising memory prices. It had the option to hold prices steady to grab market share or raise prices to exercise its pricing power. It chose the latter, and amid a supply shortage for its components, that's a smart move. In the long run, the higher prices will stick, but the higher bill of materials won't.

That points to rising gross margin over the long run, even if the short term could see some pressure on its bottom line. The potential relief from a moratorium on data center building is just another bump in that upward trajectory. (In this case, to the positive side).

Investors should remain focused on Apple's fundamentals. Its ability to raise prices, introduce new products on both the high end (iPhone Duo) and low end (MacBook Neo), grow its services business, and effectively keep customers in its ecosystem are the factors driving earnings growth. That should result in sustained free cash flow, most of which it will return to shareholders through buybacks and dividends.

Recent developments sent shares to new all-time highs last week following their post-earnings pullback. There's a reason investors are paying a premium for the stock right now. The future remains bright for the iPhone maker.
