news.Title: 5 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires
news.Content:
In the first half of the year, memory was the hottest AI trade. Hyperscalers poured billions of dollars into data centers where high-bandwidth memory was one of the tightest bottlenecks in the supply chain. Most of the memory stocks rallied as a result, though the returns have been muted in the second half of the year so far, accompanied by high volatility.

Some on Wall Street say memory makers are sold out till 2030. Others say only till 2028. While the exact status of the industry can be debated, there's little doubt about the willingness of stock market investors to pay a higher multiple for memory stocks. This debate has been done to death, and memory makers continue to trade at extremely low forward earnings multiples, implying that the earnings cycle has peaked.

So what's the truth? Is it the end of the boom? Or is the structural shift in the memory business finally here? If you would rather avoid the high-risk nature of AI stocks, particularly memory and storage, you could look at companies that are doing the exact opposite, i.e., bringing in healthy cash flows and carrying low debt in our list of 10 Stocks With Low Debt and Strong Free Cash Flow .

But if you want exposure to the best memory stocks, read on. In my quest for the answer to the above questions, I reached out to a person who regularly interviews industry experts to find out answers to questions like these. I asked a famous Substack and X analyst, P Equity Research , whether 'this time was really different'. Here's what he had to say:

There are essentially 3 important conditions these memory makers set in their LTAs: volume, price, duration. They are all negotiating LTAs to fix volume, a price floor, and duration of contract to get rid of past boom and bust cycles in the industry. As long as the Capex cycle holds strong, yes, they are sold out for 2028 and will be potentially beyond that.

If companies have indeed fixed the boom-and-bust nature of the business through LTAs, the next question is whether extra capacity from both US and Chinese memory makers reduces, or even entirely eats up, the margins. The answer to that depends more on the AI capex progress rather than the new supply. As long as companies continue to invest heavily in AI infrastructure, the new capacity should not cause margins to collapse. This is, however, a fear that has already caused the market to go down, leaving some AI infrastructure stocks down over 70% from their all-time highs. P Equity Research also pointed out an added risk:

Story Continues

I would expect spot prices to start sliding from highs over the years, which is completely normal. Will supply of memory remain tight? Yes. Will prices be just as high? I highly doubt it. More supply will increase the bargaining power of the customers by a little, and allow them to renegotiate their LTAs after the current ones expire.

While these risks are real and quite clearly affecting the market, I would like to point out that expecting new entrants to simply add capacity is easier said than done. The only competition is likely to come from China's CXMT and YMTC, so I put that question to P Equity Research, who had an interesting take on the history of the memory business:

Over the decades, the players in memory have essentially consolidated from around 20 in the 1980s to only 3 today that are well known and in business for a long time, and then came CXMT and YMTC. Why would someone want to enter a business that is historically unprofitable and hard to manage? I would say this is a natural barrier to entry that the memory business has. If someone wants to enter the industry now, it would be too late, in my opinion. CXMT and YMTC have entered due to margins. It's natural for high-margin businesses to lure competitors, but this is not like the GPU market where Nvidia has high-margin chips and 10 other competitors show up. It's risky to enter the memory business, and people know that.

So how are billionaire investors treating memory stocks with so much negativity surrounding the business? That's exactly what I wanted to find out with my article, 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires.

So, what are the best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires? We provided the expanded list of 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires here. The top 5 stocks are provided below.

Methodology

To come up with my article, 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires, I first looked up multiple memory ETFs to list all memory stocks. In this list, I include stocks that derive at least 30% of their revenue from memory-related products and services. My list also bundles memory and storage stocks together. That is because some storage types also utilize memory chips and, more importantly, they face the exact same cyclicality that memory stocks are notorious for. They are listed in ascending order of the number of billionaires holding them in their portfolios.

5. Seagate Technology Holdings plc (NASDAQ: STX )

No. of Billionaire Holders: 31

Seagate Technology Holdings plc (NASDAQ:STX) is well positioned to benefit from the expanding need for data storage as AI and cloud infrastructure require more capacity. Its fiscal Q1 2027 results highlight the strength of this demand. Revenue rose 61% from a year earlier to $4.2 billion. On a non-GAAP basis, earnings per share grew 194% to $7.68. Data center sales contributed $3.4 billion, and Seagate delivered a record 198 exabytes of nearline capacity. For the December quarter, management expects revenue to reach approximately $4.8 billion.

The stock fell 5% despite the strong quarterly results. Investors were concerned that shipment growth fell short of expectations. However, Bank of America reiterated its Buy rating and $1,200 price target, considering the slowdown temporary as the company shifts to newer HAMR technology. The stock is also featured among our 10 Oversold AI Stocks: Where Wall Street Analysts Are Spotting 50%+ Upside , which further supports BofA's bullish view.

Seagate also attracted a new investment from Tiger Global Management. The firm, led by Chase Coleman, held approximately 285,100 shares worth $275.1 million at the end of Q2 2026. This makes STX another storage stock backed by a billionaire investor.

4. SanDisk Corporation (NASDAQ: SNDK )

No. of Billionaire Holders: 34

SanDisk Corporation (NASDAQ:SNDK) gives investors exposure to the other half of the memory shortage: NAND flash. This is the storage technology that keeps your data safely stored even if the device is turned off. In the context of high-bandwidth memory technology, SanDisk helps store the massive amounts of data that are loaded into HBM. The stock is number 4 on our list and is the only US-based NAND flash maker apart from Micron.

The company was spun off from Western Digital in 2025, leaving it as a pure-play flash business, which is why it gets so much attention from investors looking for a high-risk, high-return bet on memory and storage. China's YMTC is one of the two new Chinese entrants that the expert named, but here's the scarier part. Historically, NAND has been way more cyclical than DRAM, so if hyperscaler capex slows, SanDisk is likely to be worse off. For now, retail investors and billionaires alike continue to bet on this high-risk stock. SanDisk was also one of the 11 AI Stocks That Will Go to the Moon .

3. Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ: LRCX )

No. of Billionaire Holders: 39

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) is well positioned to benefit from demand tied to AI infrastructure and advanced memory technology. The company generated $8.22 billion in revenue for the September quarter, up 54% year over year. Non-GAAP earnings per share also climbed 77% to $2.20. Going forward, management projects December quarter revenue to reach approximately $8.6 billion.

The longer-term demand outlook also looks favorable for LRCX. The company forecasts wafer fabrication equipment spending of more than $200 billion in 2027. DRAM is expected to lead industry growth, followed by advanced foundry and NAND. These trends should create further demand for the deposition and etch tools the company supplies. However, the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending remains a concern. If customers reduce their investment plans, demand could weaken.

At the end of Q2 2026, billionaire Philippe Laffont's Coatue Management held approximately 9.44 million Lam shares valued at $4.1 billion. The fund had trimmed its holding during the quarter.

2. Applied Materials Inc (NASDAQ: AMAT )

Applied Materials doesn't manufacture any memory chips, but it is still the second-best stock on our list of the 10 best memory stocks to buy according to billionaires. That's because it provides most of the things that allow manufacturers to build the memory chip. This includes thermal management solutions, etching tools, and deposition equipment that are essential for any DRAM or NAND chip. While the business is usually less volatile compared to memory, the stock has lost almost half its value in just under 5 months, and nearly one-third of its value in the last 30 days.

Despite the recent concerns, semiconductor equipment makers are expected to do well. Jefferies analysts think growing AI adoption will slowly fight off all the concerns over slowing hyperscaler capex, power infrastructure, and delays in data center construction. The firm has lowered its 2028 wafer fabrication market estimates from $250 billion to $220 billion, but even the low estimates should provide strong growth heading into the next two years. If the slowdown in growth concerns you, you could also look at our 10 Best Aggressive Growth Stocks to Buy According to Wall Street Analysts .

1. Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ: MU )

No. of Billionaire Holders: 41

Micron tops the list of the 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires. That's not surprising considering it is the only US-based manufacturer of high-bandwidth memory(it actually only holds about 20% market share in the global HBM business). As a result of its US manufacturing base, it is also a beneficiary of the CHIPS Act. The company is reshaping its business around data center customers as opposed to its previous consumer business, and the long-term agreements that the expert pointed out provide the right base to execute that shift, in addition to the government support via the CHIPS Act.

The biggest risk with Micron is hyperscalers cutting capex, a risk that all memory makers continue to carry. Clearly, billionaires think Micron is the best placed to survive through that risk. They aren't the only ones backing Micron, though. The company also made it to our list of 10 Stocks That Will Go to the Moon According to Reddit , suggesting retail investors are equally confident about the company's future prospects. The stock is trading at a forward P/E of 4.8x, a multiple that prices in all the risks I have pointed out in my article.

news.Title: Q3 Earnings Update: Broad-Based Growth, Key Sector Outliers, and What's Ahead for Q4
news.Content:
The bulk of the Q3 earnings season is now behind us, with results from only about 12% of S&P 500 members still to come at this stage. This week brings results from more than 700 companies, including 12 index members. The notable companies reporting this week include Applied Materials, Cisco Systems, and Berkshire Hathaway, to name just three.

The picture that emerged out of this earnings season is one of broad-based growth momentum. While the growth pace remains strong, it does not compare favorably with other recent periods, particularly when some of the outlier results are excluded. Most importantly, the revisions trend remains positive, with estimates for 2026 Q4 and full-year 2027 continuing to rise.

Looking at overall expectations for the quarter, combining the actual results from the 441 S&P 500 members that have reported already (through Friday, November 6th) with estimates for the still-to-come companies, Q3 earnings are currently expected to increase by +28.4% from the same period last year on +14.4% higher revenues, the 8th straight quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index.

The Tech sector continues to be a major growth contributor, but the momentum is broad-based, with 15 of the 16 Zacks sectors on track to enjoy positive earnings growth and 9 generating double-digit earnings growth in Q3.

The quarterly chart below details actual results alongside Q3 2026 growth expectations and forward projections.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

As noted earlier, the revisions trend has been positive, sustaining the favorable trend in place for almost a year. Estimates for Q3 increased after the quarter got underway, and we are seeing a similar trend at play for 2026 Q4 estimates. We should note, however, that the latest development on this front is negative, with estimates over the preceding week losing some ground, as the chart below shows.

Since the start of October, Q4 estimates have declined for 12 of the 16 Zacks sectors, with only four sectors enjoying positive estimate revisions. These four sectors are Energy, Tech, Finance, and Conglomerates. Excluding the Energy sector's substantial contribution, the index's aggregate revisions trend would have been negative.

The notable sectors suffering negative estimate revisions since the start of October include Transportation, Autos, Consumer Staples, Construction, and others.

We should note that while Q4 estimates have moved higher in the aggregate since the quarter got underway, the magnitude and breadth of positive revisions are weaker than in the comparable period for Q3.

Story Continues

Sector Focus: Broad-Based Strength

The 9 sectors expected to enjoy double-digit earnings growth in Q3 are Aerospace (up +157%), Energy (+147.9%), Tech (+45.4%), Basic Materials (+34.4%), Transportation (+10.5%), Industrial Products (+18.4%), Consumer Discretionary (+18.5%), Utilities (+14.7%), and Business Services (+12.5%).

Q3 earnings growth for the S&P 500 index drops to +23% from +28.4% once the Energy sector's contribution is excluded from the index. Excluding the Tech sector, Q3 earnings growth for the rest of the index drops to +19.4%. Excluding both the Tech and Energy sectors, Q3 earnings for the rest of the index would be up +10.2% on +7.2% higher revenues.

For the Mag 7 group, we have actual results from 6 members, with Nvidia as the only member left to report on November 17th. Looking at expectations for the Mag 7 as a whole, combining actual results from the 6 members that have reported with estimates for Nvidia, total Q3 earnings for the Mag 7 are expected to increase by +17.3% on +23.5% higher revenues, as the chart below shows.

Excluding the Mag 7 group's contribution, Q3 earnings for the rest of the index would actually improve to +32.2% (from +28.4%).

The chart below shows quarterly earnings and revenue growth expectations for the Tech sector as a whole.

The Q3 earnings growth rate drops to +29.5% from +45.4% once the substantial contributions from Nvidia NVDA, Micron MU, and Alphabet GOOGL are excluded, as the chart below shows.

Q3 Earnings Season Scorecard

Through Friday, November 6th, we have seen Q3 results from 441 S&P 500 members, or 88.2% of the index's total membership. Total earnings for these companies are up +24.8% from the same period last year on +13.4% higher revenues, with 82.1% beating EPS estimates and 74.6% beating revenue estimates.

The comparison charts below show the earnings and revenue growth rates for these companies compared to other recent periods.

The very strong earnings and revenue growth pace for this group of 441 S&P 500 members is mostly due to Micron, whose Q3 earnings increased +1075.7% from the year-earlier level. Alphabet's results in the preceding period benefited from a large unrealized gain. Excluding the Micron and Alphabet contributions, Q3 earnings for the remaining index members that have reported would be up +21.5%.

The comparison charts below show Q3 earnings and revenue growth for this group of companies, excluding Micron and Alphabet, across all periods.

The comparison charts below show the Q3 EPS and revenue beats percentages for these companies compared to other recent periods.

The Earnings Big Picture

The chart below shows the aggregate growth picture for the S&P 500 index on a calendar year basis.

Nvidia, Micron, and Alphabet have substantial weightage in the annual earnings growth pace for the index as a whole. The chart below shows the substantial contribution of these three Tech players to the index's earnings growth pace.

As we noted earlier, estimates for full-year 2027areexperiencing the same positive and broad-based revisions trend that we noted earlier in the context of 2026 Q4. The chart below shows how aggregate 2027 earnings expectations have evolved since the start of July.

news.Title: Morgan Stanley resets Cisco stock price target before earnings
news.Content: I spend much of my working day online, moving among research, market data, writing, and trading platforms. I've come to appreciate how much I take a reliable internet connection for granted until a page stops loading or a video call starts lagging during a meeting. It is easy to overlook the equipment keeping everything connected, even though so much of my work depends on it. That network runs on equipment like Cisco's. Cisco (CSCO) ended fiscal 2026 with $63.3 billion of revenue, up 12%. Fourth-quarter revenue was $17.3 billion, up 18%. AI infrastructure orders reached $9.3 billion for the year, including $4 billion in the fourth quarter. CEO Chuck Robbins called it "another record year," and said Cisco is well-positioned to support customers wherever they deploy AI. However, after a big run, good news may no longer be enough. Also Read: Jim Cramer delivers unmistakable verdict on vital tech giant Cisco stock falls as Morgan Stanley steps to the sidelines In a note shared with me at TheStreet, Morgan Stanley downgraded Cisco to Equal-weight from Overweight and cut its price target to $120 from $135, an 11.11% drop. The bank wrote that checks remain solid, but the bar for upside is higher. Shares closed at $103.61 on Nov. 4, then fell 7.62% to $95.72 after the downgrade, according to Yahoo Finance . More Morgan Stanley Stories: Morgan Stanley issues a fresh warning about AI stocks Michael Burry's favorite stock gets a 26% Morgan Stanley reset Nvidia's AI power problem is turning into its biggest edge But the stock has still run hard. Cisco is up 26.08% this year versus 7.42% for the S&P 500, and 34.70% over one year against 8.20%. Morgan Stanley says Cisco has been rerated to parity with the S&P 500 at about 19x forward earnings. It had been Overweight since April 2024, when the stock traded at a discount of more than seven turns. Cisco reports fiscal first-quarter results Nov. 12 after the close. It guided to revenue of $18.0-$18.2 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.32-$1.34. Morgan Stanley expects $18.3-$18.4 billion in revenue, a 66% gross margin, EPS of $1.36-$1.38, and an AI revenue target raised to $8 billion from $7.5 billion. The bank sees few chances to beat full expectations. 2 Cisco worries: demand pulled forward and thinner margins Worry one is timing . Partners report unusually strong demand in campus and data center networking. But Morgan Stanley said it is hard to tell how much customers are buying early ahead of price increases, as seen in recent results from Fortinet Inc. (FTNT) and F5 Inc. (FFIV). Story Continues Partners also say the campus refresh cycle is no longer early. A Dell'Oro report indicated that campus Ethernet switch revenue grew by double digits in the first quarter due to rising shipments and higher prices, and that DDR4 memory shortages will affect networking supply chains through 2027. Morgan Stanley's CIO survey shows some cooling, though Cisco still leads peers. Net spending intentions fell to +28% from +57% and data center intentions to +37% from +55%. Meanwhile, campus upgrade intentions rose to +36%. Related: Morgan Stanley reveals Cisco's quiet edge over rivals I see the same dependence on reliable tech in my own work. Every research task, market update, and trading session relies on systems that should work without interruption. You could see businesses continue to invest in network upgrades, even when budgets are tighter and spending decisions become more selective. Worry two is margin . AI sales to hyperscalers, the giant cloud companies, have gross margins of about 30% to 40%, well below Cisco's traditional business. Morgan Stanley expects AI revenue of $9 billion in fiscal 2027 and $12 billion in 2028, above management's $7.5 billion outlook, and 12.5% of revenue next year. That dilutes consolidated gross margin about 1.8 points in fiscal 2027, and 0.8 points more in 2028. Partners also say Cisco is pricing more aggressively in AI cloud, which helps growth but limits profit. Dell'Oro said AI back-end switch sales surpassed front-end sales for the first time in the second quarter, and it expects the market to be supply-constrained for at least one to two years, not demand-constrained. Cisco plans to raise TSMC's leading-edge chip wafer volumes about 10 times in fiscal 2027, according to the note. Morgan Stanley flags engineering turnover on Silicon One as an execution risk. Morgan Stanley's $120 target and what could change it The $120 price target is based on a 21x multiple of Morgan Stanley's 2028 EPS estimate of approximately $5.70, rolled forward from its 26x multiple on 2027 EPS of $5.25. The bull case is $150, at 25x $6.00, if Cisco becomes a bigger AI player and pricing offsets mix. The bear case is $65, at 13x $5.00, if campus slows, hyperscaler discounting continues, and margins compress. Morgan Stanley could be wrong if AI spending shifts toward on-premises for security reasons or agents generate far more network traffic. It expects fiscal 2027 revenue of about $73.25 billion, up 16%, and EPS of $5.14, up 18%. If you are reading this, the bank sees multiple years of double-digit growth, but growth will lean on AI revenue as pricing comparisons arrive in fiscal 2028. The numbers to watch on Nov. 12 are overall orders and gross margin, not just AI. news.Title: Google-backed miner reveals $710M profit, operating loss surges 257%
news.Content: TeraWulf reported nearly $710 million in quarterly profit while posting an $88.2 million operating loss, as a large noncash accounting gain drove its bottom line. The former bitcoin-focused business now gets most of its revenue from data-center leases. Its next expansion depends on completing buildings, securing financing and turning signed contracts into rent. The company's third-quarter results , released Nov. 6, show $709.9 million in net income attributable to TeraWulf, compared with a $455.1 million loss a year earlier. Revenue rose about 51% to $76.2 million. Those figures describe different parts of the business. Revenue measures sales, operating income accounts for the costs of running the business, and net income also includes financing costs and gains or losses outside operations. What produced the profit The largest positive item was a $728.4 million change in the value of warrant and derivative liabilities. Warrants give their holders a right to buy shares under specified terms, and changes in the value of these obligations can produce accounting gains or losses without bringing in cash. The same income-statement line produced a $424.6 million loss in the third quarter of 2025. This quarter's positive figure therefore does not represent money collected from AI customers. TeraWulf also recorded a $95 million gain on the sale of its 50.1% stake in the Abernathy joint venture. Neither item forms part of revenue from its mining or data-center businesses. Its operating loss widened from $24.7 million to $88.2 million. Total operating costs and expenses reached $164.5 million, more than twice quarterly revenue, including $29.6 million of depreciation and $9.7 million of property and equipment impairments. Adjusted EBITDA was negative $12.8 million, compared with positive $18.1 million a year earlier. That company-defined measure removes interest, taxes, depreciation and several other items, including warrant-value changes, and is neither net income nor cash flow. For the first nine months of 2026, TeraWulf still reported a $657.6 million loss attributable to the company. A profitable third quarter did not erase losses earlier in the year. AI rent has overtaken bitcoin revenue Data-center lease revenue rose to $63 million from $7.2 million in the comparable quarter. Its share of company revenue increased from about 14% to 83%, based on the reported figures. Bitcoin-mining revenue moved the other way, dropping to $13.2 million from $43.4 million, a decline of about 69%. TeraWulf is repurposing parts of its Lake Mariner mining infrastructure in New York for AI and other high-performance computing customers. Story Continues The company develops and operates the buildings, power connections and related infrastructure. It says its model does not depend on buying the AI computing hardware itself. At Sept. 30, Lake Mariner had 102 megawatts of critical IT capacity online and generating revenue. Critical IT capacity measures the power available to computing equipment, rather than the total electricity supply secured for an entire campus. Another 336 megawatts were under construction at Lake Mariner. The company expects phased delivery and rent commencement for CB-4 in the fourth quarter, with CB-5 beginning phased delivery in early 2027. Its disclosed construction-cost guidance is $8 million to $10 million per critical IT megawatt for WULF Compute. These are development costs incurred ahead of the future rental income. What Google is backing The largest announced lease is with Anthropic at the Justified campus in Hawesville, Kentucky. TeraWulf puts the initial 20-year commitment at roughly $19 billion for about 401 megawatts of critical IT capacity. That $19 billion is contracted revenue over two decades, not money received this quarter, cash already available for construction or a measure of profit. Under agreements announced Nov. 4 , Google provides contractual credit support for anticipated project debt financing. TeraWulf says the arrangement strengthens its ability to obtain competitive financing, rather than announcing that all of that financing has already closed. Fluor's construction agreement covers three buildings, including engineering, procurement, construction, testing and commissioning. Phased completions are expected to start in late 2027 and continue through the second quarter of 2028. The agreement includes delivery milestones and cost reporting. TeraWulf says guaranteed maximum pricing is being established as engineering and procurement progress, so the announcement should not be read as a final fixed price for every part of construction. The cash needed before rent arrives The cash-flow statement shows $178.9 million used in operating activities over the first nine months, compared with $35 million a year earlier. Purchases of and deposits on plant and equipment totaled $2.23 billion, up from $445.2 million. Those are nine-month figures, not third-quarter spending. They show why a noncash earnings gain cannot substitute for construction funding. TeraWulf ended September with $1.60 billion in cash and cash equivalents, plus roughly $753 million of restricted cash. The combined $2.36 billion figure is often rounded to $2.4 billion, but the restricted portion is separately identified on the balance sheet. The Abernathy sale provided $250 million during the quarter. Another $150 million is expected by Dec. 31 and about $130 million, subject to adjustments, by April 30, 2027. The company subsequently increased committed revolving credit from $250 million to $400 million. A further $150 million expansion feature is uncommitted and conditional, not another $150 million already available. At Muskie in Kentucky, contracted power has doubled to one gigawatt, subject to state approval, with the second 500-megawatt phase expected in 2029. Contracted power there should not be confused with the 102 megawatts already earning revenue at Lake Mariner. Chairman and CEO Paul Prager said Lake Mariner is delivering capacity and generating revenue, while Justified has the customer and construction framework to proceed. The next scheduled tests are nearer-term Lake Mariner deliveries, followed by Justified's first completed buildings in late 2027. news.Title: Arm leans on cloud giants as a memory shortage hits phones
news.Content:
Phones have become costlier to build this year, and the reason sits far from any phone store. Memory chips, which hold photos and run apps, have grown scarce as their makers chase AI data center orders.

Higher memory prices could raise the cost of the parts inside a smartphone by 15% or more, Counterpoint Research estimated, according to Bloomberg . This week, that pressure showed up in the results of Arm Holdings (ARM).

The British chip designer reported fiscal second quarter results on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Royalty revenue grew just 8% to $670 million, and its shareholder letter cited "the impact of memory pricing on the smartphone market" as a drag.

Also read: 5 tech stock stalwarts have tumbled over 50%

The twist is where that pressure comes from. The cloud giants behind Arm's fastest royalty growth are the same buyers whose demand is pulling memory production away from phones.

The memory crunch reached Arm through phones

Arm mostly does not make chips. It designs blueprints that companies such as Qualcomm (QCOM) build on, then collects a small royalty on each chip shipped.

That model works when phone sales grow. Fewer phones built means fewer chips shipped, and fewer royalty payments.

The memory squeeze pushes in exactly that direction. Memory makers have steered production toward premium AI server chips, while tech giants pay extra for multiyear supply deals, Bloomberg reported.

IDC projected the global smartphone market will shrink 12.9% in 2026, the sharpest drop on record, according to the same report . Qualcomm flagged China, where cheaper phones compete hardest on cost, as a likely hot spot. For shoppers, that can mean paying more for the next phone upgrade.

Data centers now carry Arm's royalty growth

Yet the same spending is also behind Arm's fastest-growing royalties. Data center royalties doubled from a year earlier, the shareholder letter said, as more Arm-based chips went into servers.

Arm expects its share of the server market at the largest cloud providers to top 60% by the end of 2026, according to the letter. That is a sharp turn for a company built on phones.

In effect, Arm's two businesses partly offset each other. A slower AI buildout would likely ease memory prices and help phones, but it would also cool data center royalties. That ties Arm stock to both the phone in your pocket and the servers behind AI.

Arm is raising its data center bet, too. Its own server chip, the Arm AGI CPU , is on track for first commercial deliveries in the fiscal quarter ending March 2027, the letter said.

Story Continues

Arm also said its confidence in reaching up to $2 billion in revenue from that chip over fiscal 2027 and 2028 has grown. That progress did little to protect the stock on Thursday.

Why Arm stock fell harder than its results

On paper, the quarter was strong. Total revenue rose 27% to $1.44 billion, Arm's best second quarter ever, according to the letter.

Most of that lift came from licensing fees, not royalties. Arm calls licensing an early signal of future royalty growth. Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya put that lag at 12 to 24 months, CNBC reported .

Investors still sent the stock down about 13% on Thursday, Nov. 5. The weaker royalty number landed on the iShares Semiconductor ETF's worst day since March 2020, according to CNBC.

CNBC tied the wider slide to worries that this week's election results could bring more regulation of the AI buildout. Memory maker Micron Technology (MU) fell even harder than Arm, a sign that the selling reached well beyond one phone problem.

More Artificial Intelligence:

AI's biggest business opportunity may not look like AI

AI racks are outgrowing old power: 2 chipmakers have a strategy

BofA splits software into winners and losers as AI agents arrive

Arm also tends to magnify market moves. StockAnalysis puts its beta, a gauge of how sharply a stock swings against the broader market, near 4. That helps explain why a rough market day hit Arm so hard.

After Thursday, shares sat more than 60% below their 52-week high. Even so, Wall Street trimmed its numbers without walking away.

JPMorgan, Barclays, and Wells Fargo cut their price targets, the level analysts expect in a year, but kept their ratings, according to StockAnalysis .

Bank of America, which rates the stock Neutral , cut its target to $230 from $260, still well above Thursday's close. That gap suggests the market is pricing in more phone pain than many analysts are.

Arm's next test arrives with its own chip

Arm guided fiscal third quarter revenue to $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million, according to the letter. How much help phones provide depends on memory supply, and that timing rests largely with memory makers, not Arm.

Meanwhile, Arm is about to start selling chips of its own. The letter said Arm remains "focused on expanding capacity to meet growing customer demand." That makes the chip an execution test as much as a design one.

The AI buildout is reshuffling the parts everyday devices depend on. Arm shows how serving both the cloud and consumers can bring growth on one side and costs on the other.

Arm's first shipments of that chip early next year will show whether its data center side can grow fast enough to cover for the phones.

news.Title: If I Could Buy and Hold Only 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Through a Democratic Congress, It Would Be This One
news.Content:
The 2026 midterm elections have introduced a layer of uncertainty for artificial intelligence (AI) investors. With Democrats winning control of both chambers of Congress, lawmakers are preparing to introduce legislation addressing AI safety, electricity costs, and the expansion of data centers across the United States.

For companies such as Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA), and Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX), the implications could be significant.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Much of the AI revolution has been driven by investments in semiconductors, cloud computing, and data center infrastructure. There's one technology giant pursuing a different strategy. If I could buy and hold just one AI stock throughout the next two years of a divided government, I'd consider Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL). Let's dig into why.

Apple's AI strategy is different from its competitors

Most of the largest AI developers are spending unprecedented sums of money building AI infrastructure. Nvidia supplies the graphics processing units powering these facilities, while Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta are investing hundreds of billions of dollars each year to expand their computing capacity. Tesla is also spending heavily on autonomous driving and robotics.

Apple is taking a different approach. Rather than competing to build data centers, Apple is focused on bringing AI capabilities directly to its existing products. This includes integrating generative AI features into the iPhone, the Mac, and Siri, while relying on partners for additional computing capabilities.

The financial implications of this strategy are compelling. During fiscal 2026, Apple's capital expenditures (capex) declined 29% to roughly $9 billion. Meanwhile, research and development (R&D) spending increased 32% to $45.8 billion, reflecting continued investment across software and AI.

The takeaway here is that Apple is investing heavily in innovation without committing nearly as much capital to physical AI infrastructure as its hyperscaler peers. That difference could become important if Congress pursues legislation that makes building new data centers more difficult.

Story Continues

Why Apple looks more resilient to AI regulation

Data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity and water, raising questions about utility costs, environmental impacts, and whether local communities should shoulder the financial burden of new development. Many Democratic lawmakers are indicating that they intend to pursue additional oversight when the new Congress convenes.

It's important to note that President Donald Trump retains veto authority, meaning sweeping federal restrictions are not guaranteed. Nevertheless, even the possibility of tighter regulation introduces uncertainty for big tech.

Slower data center construction could affect demand for Nvidia's chips. For cloud services providers such as Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet, new restrictions could hinder expansion plans and make budgeting more challenging.

By contrast, Apple already has a global installed base across billions of devices through which it can push AI-powered features. Rather than building an entirely new customer ecosystem, Apple can introduce updated capabilities to people who already own its products. This creates a unique opportunity to encourage device upgrades, strengthen customer loyalty, and potentially expand its budding services business.

Apple's cash flow is the biggest reason to own the stock

While Apple's AI strategy is interesting, the company's underlying financial performance is what makes the investment thesis compelling. During its fiscal fourth quarter (ended Sept. 26), Apple generated $114.5 billion in revenue, representing 12% growth year over year.

iPhone revenue increased 17% to $57.6 billion, while services revenue reached $31.6 billion. These figures illustrate an important point: Apple does not need AI to become an entirely new business segment overnight.

AAPL Free Cash Flow data by YCharts

The company's existing products and services already generate meaningful revenue, providing management with the financial flexibility to invest in emerging technologies without jeopardizing the core operation. Moreover, Apple's relatively modest capex profile allows it to preserve more cash for dividends, share repurchases, and future product innovation.

While the next two years could bring changes to the regulatory environment surrounding AI, Apple stands out because the company doesn't need to win the AI infrastructure spending race to benefit from the technology. It just needs to make AI useful enough that consumers continue buying its products and paying for its services.

For investors, that flexibility is especially valuable. That's why Apple is my top buy-and-hold AI stock in the current political landscape.

news.Title: What Black Hills (BKH) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Black Hills Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Adjusted Q3 earnings rose to $0.57 per share from $0.45 a year earlier, and Black Hills reaffirmed its 2026 guidance of $4.25–$4.45 per share.

The Google data-center agreement includes a planned $1.8 billion investment in 564 MW of gas generation and management of a private microgrid; Black Hills estimates about $150 million in net income in 2030 and $2.4 billion in unlevered free cash flow through 2048.

Black Hills is pursuing further data-center load opportunities and expects to invest about $700 million in transmission by 2029. Its NorthWestern Energy merger has received six of seven required approvals, with a Montana decision pending.

Alphabet's $1.8 Billion Black Hills Deal Powers AI Data Center Push

Black Hills (NYSE:BKH) reported higher third-quarter adjusted earnings and reaffirmed its 2026 outlook as it laid out the expected financial benefits of an agreement to supply a planned Google data center in Wyoming.

The utility expects its generation investment and microgrid management fees associated with the project to deliver approximately $150 million in net income in 2030, Chief Financial Officer Kimberly Nooney said on the company's earnings call. The estimate is net of financing costs, which she said are passed through under the agreement.

→ Amazon Has Erased Its Earnings Sell-Off, But Is the Biggest Opportunity Still Ahead?

The 127-Gigawatt Problem: Why AI Needs Its Own Power

Black Hills also awaits the final regulatory decision needed to close its planned merger with NorthWestern Energy. Chief Executive Officer Linn Evans said the Montana Public Service Commission has until Nov. 12 to issue a written decision.

Third-quarter earnings and outlook

Black Hills reported third-quarter earnings of $0.54 per share under generally accepted accounting principles, including $0.03 per share in merger-related transaction costs. Adjusted earnings rose to $0.57 per share from $0.45 a year earlier.

→ Washington Made a $2 Billion Quantum Bet, But Can Either ETF Match It?

3 Under-the-Radar AI Infrastructure Stocks Powering the Next Buildout

Nooney said higher margins, driven primarily by new rates, rider recovery and favorable weather compared with the prior-year quarter, more than offset higher operating, financing and depreciation costs.

For the first nine months of 2026, adjusted earnings were $2.89 per share, up from $2.68 a year earlier. The company reaffirmed its full-year adjusted earnings guidance of $4.25 to $4.45 per share and said it was confident it could deliver growth in the upper half of its long-term annual earnings-per-share target of 4% to 6%.

Story Continues

→ Energy Transfer's Earnings Miss May Be Hiding Its Strongest Advantage

Black Hills had $685 million available under its revolving credit facility at quarter-end. It issued approximately $70 million of equity through its at-the-market program during the first nine months and is evaluating refinancing options for $400 million of notes due in January 2027, Nooney said.

Google project drives investment plans

Black Hills has executed agreements to serve Google's planned southern Wyoming data center, which is expected to begin taking service in late 2027 and reach its full ramp in late 2030. The project's contracted peak load and ramp schedule are confidential, Chief Utility Officer Marne Jones said.

The company plans to invest $1.8 billion through a nonregulated affiliate in 564 megawatts of natural gas generation at its existing Cheyenne Prairie Generating Station. Construction is expected to start in 2027, with the facilities entering service in phases through the latter half of 2029.

Black Hills will also manage approximately 2.1 gigawatts of third-party resources serving the data center through a private microgrid. The approximately 2.7 gigawatts of total resources include reserve margins, Jones said. Management expects to begin earning microgrid fees in late 2027 and a cash return on its generation investment during construction.

Nooney said the company expects the Google project to generate an estimated $2.4 billion in unlevered free cash flow through 2048, after accounting for the $1.8 billion generation investment. She declined to break out how much of the projected 2030 net income would come from generation returns versus management fees, citing confidentiality.

The agreements include cost pass-throughs, collateral and financial assurances, protection against stranded asset risk and early termination provisions, Jones said.

More large-load opportunities and transmission spending

Black Hills' current financial plan includes about 600 megawatts of data center load, driven largely by Microsoft's expansion and Meta's new data center. The Google project is additional to that plan and will be incorporated into the company's updated 2027–2031 financial plan, which management expects to present in February.

The company is negotiating another 600 megawatts of potential load and assessing at least 2.5 gigawatts of earlier-stage opportunities, Jones said. Those exploratory opportunities are not yet in active negotiations and include potential expansion following Microsoft's land purchase in the Cheyenne area.

Black Hills also expects to invest approximately $700 million in transmission by 2029 to support large-load growth. It has requested approval for the $606 million Aeolus project and the $80 million South Cheyenne project. A proposed tariff would recover transmission-related costs directly from the large-load customers benefiting from the facilities, Jones said.

Rate reviews and merger approval

Jones said Arkansas regulators approved $17.9 million in new annual gas revenue, with rates effective Oct. 12. Approved settlements for South Dakota Electric provide $27.4 million in new annual revenue in South Dakota and $4 million in Wyoming; final rates in both jurisdictions take effect Dec. 1.

The company's 99-megawatt Lange II generation project is in the final stages of construction and is expected to enter service in the fourth quarter, Jones said.

On the NorthWestern merger, Evans said Black Hills has received six of seven required approvals. The companies completed a four-day Montana regulatory hearing in May after reaching settlements with several key interveners.

About Black Hills (NYSE:BKH)

Black Hills Corporation (NYSE:BKH) is an energy company headquartered in Rapid City, South Dakota. Through its Black Hills Energy businesses, the company provides regulated electric and natural gas utility services to residential, commercial and industrial customers.

Black Hills operates electric utilities and natural gas distribution systems across parts of Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska, South Dakota and Wyoming. Its activities include generating and purchasing electricity, transmitting and distributing power, distributing natural gas, and developing and maintaining the infrastructure needed to serve its utility customers.

The company traces its history to the Black Hills region and has expanded through the development and acquisition of utility operations in the central and western United States.

news.Title: Stock market today: Nasdaq and S&P 500 rebound, Dow slips to cap bruising week for AI stocks
news.Content:
US stocks stabilized, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq doing their best to end the week on a positive note. But it wasn't enough to stave off the S&P 500's worst weekly performance since June.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.4% on Friday, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.3%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) gained more than 1% after the tech-heavy index slipped into a correction on Thursday.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq rebounded from a bruising session on Thursday as investors assessed Democrats' election sweep . At the center of Thursday's deep sell-off, which erased $3 trillion in market value, were concerns about a slowdown in data center construction and in AI spending.

On Thursday, chip stocks Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD ( AMD ), Micron ( MU ), and Sandisk ( SNDK ) recouped some losses from the prior session's broad selloff, in which the VIX Volatility Index ( ^VIX ) surged.

Oil prices have also been in play, with global benchmark Brent crude ( BZ=F ) futures falling below $100 per barrel. Energy traders continue to assess the outlook for the war in the Middle East, with the risk of a re-escalation weighing on sentiment.

Not to be overshadowed, the Labor Department reported that the US added 165,000 jobs in October , above a revised 60,000 figure the month before and the 65,000 jobs economists expected.

Correction: An earlier version of this article incorrectly stated that the Nasdaq had its worst week since June. While the S&P 500 did, the Nasdaq recorded a steeper weekly decline in October. We regret the error.

LIVE COVERAGE IS OVER 18 updates

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 9:02 PM UTC Ines Ferré

Dow slips, S&P 500, Nasdaq rebound but post weekly losses

The major averages closed mixed on Friday, posting weekly losses following a bruising sell-off in the prior session.

Chip stocks rebounded, clawing back some of their recent losses. Still, the gauge tracking the largest semiconductor companies ended in negative territory, as did chip heavyweights Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD ( AMD ), and Intel ( INTC ),

This recent volatility has also fueled speculation that AI developer Anthropic may need to lower its valuation ahead of its expected public debut later this month.

Despite Friday's recovery, the AI trade remained fragile. Technology ( XLK ) and Energy ( XLE ) stocks, two key beneficiaries of the AI boom, fell 7% and 11% for the week, respectively.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 8:19 PM UTC Ines Ferré

These 4 Trump-backed chip stocks have seen steeper losses than the beleaguered sector

Yahoo Finance's Ben Werschkul reports:

Chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) is putting a notable drag on the burgeoning US government investment portfolio, shaving close to $20 billion off the government's stake in the chipmaker.

But it's not the only one. The Trump administration's other semiconductor investments have also incurred sharp losses that outpace the beleaguered sector.

Chipmaker GlobalFoundries ( GFS ), photonics company Aeluma ( ALMU ), and silicon carbide specialist Wolfspeed ( WOLF ) have all seen losses of at least 40% over the past six months, according to Yahoo Finance data.

That's in excess of PHLX Semiconductor ( ^SOX ), a capitalization-weighted index of the semiconductor sector, which is down about over 18% over the same span.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 7:18 PM UTC Ines Ferré

S&P 500, Nasdaq rebound, but remain on track for worst weekly decline since June

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.7% on Friday while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) rose roughly 1.6%, but both indexes were on pace for their worst weekly performance since June 5.

The major averages rebounded after a several-day sell-off on Thursday in which semicondcutor stocks led the overall market lower.

On Thursday, chip stocks rebounded but were still on track to end the week with losses after Democrats won control of the House and Senate on Wednesday, raising concerns about potential regulations that could slow the pace of data center buildouts.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:40 PM UTC Ines Ferré

White House hails 'skyrocketing' labor demand after blockbuster October jobs report

Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger reports:

The White House says the job market is turning a corner and demand for workers is on the rise.

"Demand for labor is skyrocketing," Kevin Hassett, director of President Trump's National Economic Council, said in an interview, noting that not only was the jobs report strong, but initial jobless claims are also at their lowest since World War II, and more people are leaving their jobs because they have higher confidence in finding a new one.

The quits rate rose 2.1% in September.

But the big news out Friday: The economy added 165,000 jobs in October , compared with expectations of around 70,000, as the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, compared with expectations of 4.2%. That's much higher than the average monthly gain of 48,000 over the past 12 months and well above the roughly 30,000 jobs needed to hold employment steady. Over the past three months, payrolls are averaging 137,000.

While job gains were healthy, wages haven't kept pace, though they did catch up last month to the pace of inflation, which grew 3.1%.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:40 PM UTC David Hollerith

Stocks had their worst day in 18 months — here's what that means for your portfolio

The AI trade ran off a cliff Thursday. Most of the stock market was nowhere near the edge, Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre reports:

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell more than 4% Thursday, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash. About $3 trillion in stock market value disappeared in a single session.

Chipmakers took the hardest hit. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) dropped 12%, its worst day since March 2020, and Nvidia ( NVDA ) fell 9% , its worst day since the DeepSeek scare in January 2025.

The trigger was Washington. Democrats won control of Congress this week, and candidates in both parties campaigned against AI data centers, the giant buildings those chips go into. Investors worry that new rules could slow the building boom that sent chip stocks to records.

But look past the AI stocks, and the picture gets a lot calmer.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 5:15 PM UTC Ines Ferré

Iren stock rebounds as company's Q1 AI cloud revenue surges

Iren ( IREN ) stock surged on Friday as the data center operator reported strong growth in its artificial intelligence cloud business in its fiscal first quarter.

Iren shares jumped as much as 20% on Friday, rebounding from a roughly 17% decline in the previous session amid a broader sell-off in the AI trade . Despite the recovery, Iren shares remain down more than 50% year to date as investor concerns over AI infrastructure spending, financing requirements and data center expansion have weighed on the sector. The company, which has transitioned from bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) mining into AI cloud and data center infrastructure, has been particularly affected by the recent pullback in neocloud stocks.

Iren, whose customers include Microsoft ( MSFT ), reported $200 million in AI revenue during the three months ending Sept. 30, up from $71 million in the previous quarter and $7 million in the year-earlier period.

However, the company posted a quarterly loss of $263 million, wider than the average analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:34 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Musk bids farewell to Cybertruck as Tesla bets on robots and self-driving

Yahoo Finance's Pras Subramanian reports:

So long, Tesla ( TSLA ) Cybertruck, we hardly knew ye.

Yes, it is official. The Tesla Cybertruck will soon be no more, per a post from CEO Elon Musk on his X account.

"Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk wrote early Friday morning.

For many in the industry, this isn't a surprise even with Musk's grand pronouncements about the vehicle. Musk once boasted that Cybertruck demand was " so far off the hook, you can't even see the hook ," and the company said it had over 1 million preorders.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 3:46 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Anthropic's IPO valuation could plunge to near $1 trillion amid market turmoil

Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports:

Yesterday's bruising market sell-off sent tech stocks plunging on questions about what the newly elected Democratic majority in Congress means for the data center build-out and AI.

The pain was so acute it's bled into Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) upcoming IPO. According to Bloomberg and The Wall Street Journal , investors are now eyeing a potential market valuation of between $1 trillion and $1.3 trillion for the AI startup.

That's far below the $ 2 trillion buyers were projecting just last month when stocks were flying high.

Anthropic, which publicly filed its S-1 investor prospectus last Monday and updated it this week with more recent revenue and spending numbers , is widely expected to launch its IPO sometime before the end of the month.

But that could slip to a later date due to the broader market sell-off.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 3:02 PM UTC Ines Ferré

Nvidia, AMD, and Micron stocks lead chip sector higher following worst sell-off since 2020

Chip stocks rebounded on Friday after suffering their worst sell-off since 2020. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) bounced 4% following a 12% plunge on Thursday.

Shares of US chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) jumped nearly 6%, erasing part of their 10% slide in the prior session. AMD ( AMD ) also rebounded 8% after suffering a 17% fall. Nvidia ( NVDA ), which declined 9% in the prior session, jumped 6%.

Semiconductors bounced back after much of the AI trade was hammered on Thursday as investors digested what a Democratic win in Congress means for the data center build-out in the US.

Memory and storage names Sandisk ( SNDK ), Micron Technology ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) shares tumbled alongside Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) following Thursday's wipeout on Wall Street.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:35 PM UTC David Hollerith

Stocks stabilize as tech claws back some losses

US stocks were mixed at Friday's open as investors looked for more signs that market conditions have stabilized after Thursday's sharp AI-led sell-off.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.9%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.4%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) rose more than 1.4%.

Technology shares attempted to rebound after Thursday's rout, which pushed the Nasdaq back into correction territory and erased much of Wednesday's post-election rally.

Investors were also parsing the October jobs report for clues on whether the labor market remains strong enough to keep another Federal Reserve rate hike in play.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 1:58 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Blockbuster October jobs report keeps Fed rate hike in play for December

A much stronger-than-expected October jobs report solidifies expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December, as officials are already focused on higher inflation.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics report released Friday showed that 165,000 jobs were created in October , compared with expectations for around 70,000, as the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, compared with expectations for 4.2%. That's much higher than the average monthly gain of 48,000 over the past 12 months and well above the roughly 30,000 jobs needed to hold employment steady. Labor force participation inched up to a hair above expectations at 61.9%.

Job gains in both August and September were also revised higher by 84,000. The bulk of jobs added were in the sectors of professional and business services, healthcare, and transportation and warehousing. Manufacturing added 19,000 jobs.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 1:38 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

US adds 165K jobs, blowing past expectations

The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, a jump from the revised job growth of 60,000 the month before. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expected the economy to have added 65,000 jobs.

The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%. Wage growth increased 0.4% from September.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 1:24 PM UTC Brian Sozzi

The VIX volatility index just spiked 70%. Here's what history suggests comes next.

If you are looking for something positive after Thursday's shocking stock beatdown , you have come to the right place ahead of the weekend.

History suggests stocks tend to do well after the extreme volatility we saw two days removed from the Election Day blue wave.

The VIX volatility index ( ^VVIX ) — better known as Wall Street's fear gauge — jumped as much as 70% on Thursday. A move this large has only happened eight times since 1991, according to data from CBOE.

Here's what happened to the S&P 500 on average after the eight prior extreme moves:

1 month later: +3.0% (7 of 8 times positive)

3 months later: +7.1% (6 of 8 times positive)

6 months later: +10.4% (8 of 8 times positive)

1 year later: +14.7% (7 of 8 times positive)

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:37 PM UTC David Hollerith

Wall Street is overreacting to data center backlash, Yardeni says

The stock market's Thursday rout in artificial intelligence boom trade may have been an overreaction to growing political opposition to data center construction, according to one prominent bull.

AI and chip stocks plunged Thursday as major indexes erased their post-midterm election rally. One key worry is that about 45% of planned US data center capacity faces possible restrictions after tallying newly elected state governors who have promised to stop or pause construction, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

But Yardeni Research is calling those mounting restrictions a setback.

"We view the political backlash as another constraint on AI investment, alongside financial and physical bottlenecks. But these are speed bumps, not roadblocks, even though Wall Street seems to be pricing in the latter," Yardeni Research wrote in a Friday note to clients.

"We think that's overdone," the strategists said, referring to Thursday's sell-off as a "buying opportunity." The firm is sticking with its year-end target of 7,900 on the S&P 500.

Yardeni pointed to Texas, a major data center hub, where newly elected governor Gina Hinojosa said Thursday afternoon in a CNN interview that already permitted projects would be allowed to finish construction.

The distinction matters. Permitted data center projects account for "essentially all of Texas's planned data center capacity in 2027 and likely much of 2028," according to Yardeni.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Friday's jobs report is expected to show the labor market chugging along

Employment data scheduled for release on Friday is expected to show the labor market remains steady. Yahoo Finance's Claire Boston previews what to expect from today's jobs report:

Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect that the economy added 65,000 jobs in October, an improvement from September's underwhelming 29,000 additions. The unemployment rate is expected to hold steady at 4.2%, while wage growth is seen improving 0.3% from September.

Those numbers would be consistent with the "low hire, low fire" environment that has defined the labor market for the past several years. While few companies are hiring aggressively, most aren't conducting major layoffs either.

Recent initial jobless claims have looked "exceptionally benign by historical standards," Bank of America economist Shruti Mishra wrote in a note.

"Despite recent high-profile layoff announcements, the absence of any pickup in claims suggests economy-wide layoffs remain contained," she added.

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Tesla's EV arc could be a blueprint for the post-data center backlash

Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban writes:

When President Trump and his allies in Congress moved to end the EV subsidy, automakers braced for a crash in electric car sales. Tesla ( TSLA ), the US leader, was especially vulnerable because it didn't have gas-powered vehicles to lean on, and keeping prices as low as possible was crucial to competing with EV rivals.

But those initial worries gave way to optimism.

In a new regulatory environment, one that was more hostile to EVs, Tesla used the disappearing $7,500 tax break as an advantage . It lost a valuable subsidy, but used its scale to win a war of attrition, thereby consolidating the market. Other firms needed the subsidy even more, and though Tesla got hurt, the damage was less than its peers' in many ways.

On top of that, a new barrier to entry was in place, and Tesla's competitive moat got wider.

That's a roadmap for how Big Tech could navigate the data center backlash. And it helps explain why many investors are bullish on hyperscaler stocks despite a nationwide referendum against data centers and notable victories from candidates opposing them .

Fri, November 6, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Airbnb 'back in growth mode,' CEO says after strong quarter. Stock jumps after hours.

Airbnb ( ABNB ) stock jumped after hours after the peer-to-peer home rental company touted strong growth across its business and raised its full-year outlook amid healthy global travel demand.

"Airbnb is back in growth mode," CEO Brian Chesky said in a release to investors. "It's rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that's exactly what we're doing. In Q3, we delivered our fastest revenue growth in more than three years, with acceleration across our business, including our most established markets."

In the third quarter, Airbnb reported earnings per share of $3.16, surpassing Wall Street analyst estimates of $2.85 per share, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data. Revenue grew 19% to $4.87 billion, also beating estimates of $4.74 billion.

"In North America, nights booked grew at their fastest pace in four years," the company said. "We're also seeing more guests return to Airbnb, and more people try it for the first time."

The strength of the company's quarter led it to raise its guidance for the remainder of the year.

In the fourth quarter, Airbnb expects revenue to grow 16%-19% to a range of $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion, exceeding the Street's midpoint estimate of $3.16 billion.

For the full year, Airbnb forecasts revenue growth in the high teens and adjusted EBITDA margins to increase to approximately 36%.

news.Title: Reddit’s (RDDT) Short-Term Pains May Lead to Long-Term Gains
news.Content: Reddit's (RDDT) short-term pains may lead to long-term gains, in my view. The leading social media platform lost more than 25% of its market value soon after it reported Q3 earnings on October 30 . This crash followed traffic headwinds from Google's (GOOGL) AI Overviews and the rollout of its new artificial intelligence (AI) Mode features, which negatively impacted Reddit's user growth. However, on November 4, Reddit stock surged 6% after the company announced that it is testing ad placements on Reddit search pages. This is a major step forward in monetizing its existing user base. The company is also planning to double down on forcing non-logged-in users to create accounts and log in to the platform. I am bullish on Reddit as I believe its recently announced strategies will trigger strong earnings growth. Reddit Is Under Threat from AI Although I am bullish on Reddit long term, there's no denying the company faces a major challenge as search engines embrace AI answers. The biggest culprit is Google. The aggressive rollout of AI Overview and AI Mode have fundamentally changed SEO principles. As confirmed by Reddit's management, Google continues to crawl Reddit to support AI answers. However, this does not translate into any user growth for Reddit. Promotion 55% Off TipRanks Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks Learn more about TipRanks Premium Commenting on this during the Q3 earnings call, CEO Steven Huffman said, "Google is crawling us as hard as ever. So the demand hasn't changed from their point of view either. The reality is: the AI Mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody as far as I know. So it's just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver. Now it's not. So now that changes the equation for sure." Google search referrals have historically played a big role in Reddit's user growth. The company's user acquisition funnel usually begins with a Google query, which leads to a Reddit click, which results in a non-logged-in user acquisition. Over time, Reddit converts these users into logged-in users through its appeal. This business model is now under pressure, as AI Overview and AI Mode threaten the company's user-acquisition funnel. Reddit Is Doubling Down on Monetization One of the reasons behind my bullish stance on Reddit despite the threat posed by AI is the company's focus on improving monetization of its active users. The company is trying to achieve this objective in two ways. First, as CEO Huffman revealed on the Q3 earnings call, Reddit is gradually transitioning to a fully logged-in-only experience. The company is initially testing this in select markets outside the United States. Story Continues The core objective of this initiative is to encourage logged-out Reddit users to create Reddit accounts and sign in to the platform. Converting its massive anonymous user base into a trackable, engaged audience should boost its monetization potential. According to company filings, Reddit served 130.3 million daily active unique users in Q3 , with 76.8 million, almost 59% of total active users, using the platform without logging in. On the earnings call, Reddit confirmed that almost 80% of revenue comes from logged-in and app users (only 41% of total active users), highlighting a significant unrealized revenue opportunity. Second, Reddit is testing direct ad placements on search pages, which is likely to improve monetization further in the long run. Reddit threads are used by high-intent users. Ads shown right within the search pages are more likely to be relevant to active users and get attention than ads in a more passive feed. If executed correctly, this strategy could help Reddit offset the negative impact of weak user growth in the foreseeable future. AI Is Creating New Opportunities for Reddit My bullish stance on Reddit is supported by the company's potential to benefit from AI through content licensing agreements. Although AI search results are hurting user growth, Reddit is well positioned to monetize its massive library of user-generated questions and answers. One classic example is the company's licensing deal with Google for $60 million per annum . This partnership gives Google real-time access to Reddit's Data Application Programming Interface (API), allowing Google to utilize Reddit's over 1 billion posts and 16 billion comments to train its Gemini models. In addition to Google, OpenAI has also struck a partnership with Reddit to access its content. Reddit's Valuation Leaves Margin for Error My bullish stance on Reddit is strengthened by the company's cheap valuation. Reddit is currently valued at a forward P/E multiple of 12.16x . For comparison, social media giant Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) trades at a forward P/E multiple of 20.24x . Although Meta certainly deserves to trade at a premium to its peers given its unmatched scale and proven monetization expertise, I believe Reddit is too cheaply valued at a time when the company is beginning to double down on monetization. In the short term, Reddit's strategy of aggressively converting logged-out users into logged-in users is likely to create friction. This strategy may even lead to a short-term decline in active users. However, in the long term, Reddit is likely to end up with a higher monetizable user base. When this happens, Reddit's valuation is likely to benefit, as the market will see its user base as higher-quality and authenticated, commanding premium targeted ad rates. Is Reddit a Buy, According to Wall Street Analysts? Based on the ratings of 24 Wall Street analysts, the average Reddit price target is $159.81 , which implies upside of 70% from the current market price. Takeaway Reddit stock crashed following the Q3 earnings report, but gained momentum on November 4 after the company announced the rollout of ad placements in search pages. This marks a new initiative by the company to aggressively monetize its user base. Although Google's AI search strategy threatens the company, I believe Reddit's valuation is cheap enough to bet on it as monetization gains pace. Although short-term user growth may be disappointing, I believe Reddit is well-positioned to report strong earnings growth in the coming years. This should pave the way for a valuation re-rating. news.Title: Intel Stock’s (INTC) Deep Sell-Off Shows Signs of an Overreaction
news.Content:
Intel Corporation (INTC) stock's deep sell-off shows signs of an overreaction, in my view, as the market may be overlooking the progress the chipmaker has made in its recovery. Since its June peak, the company's market capitalization has fallen by more than half. In late October, shares cratered nearly 30% in a single session after the company issued disappointing fourth-quarter guidance. The fear now is that its recovery could take much longer than expected.

Yet isn't there some market overreaction? Despite the weak guidance, Intel delivered a solid third quarter , with 78% growth in its data center segment and significant improvements in manufacturing efficiency.

Risks remain, particularly the foundry business's heavy losses, ongoing production constraints, and massive capital spending that continues to weigh on free cash flow (FCF). Still, I see a buying opportunity after the sell-off, at the current price of $52.25 . Projected 2028 adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.99 valued at a five-year average forward P/E of 27x supports an $80.73 price target, implying potential upside of 55%.

Promotion

BLACK FRIDAY SALE

Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Learn more about TipRanks Premium

The Sell-Off Didn't Come Out of Nowhere

Intel's recent sell-off didn't happen without reason. After it released its third-quarter results on October 29 , the semiconductor giant's shares plunged a staggering 28.6% in a single trading session on October 30.

Essentially, Intel provided guidance that fell well short of expectations. While Wall Street analysts projected Q4 revenue of about $17 billion, Intel's management guided to just $15 billion to $16 billion. Meanwhile, adjusted EPS guidance of $0.25 came in well below Wall Street's expectations of $0.44.

As if that weren't bad enough, management warned of production constraints, prolonged weakness in the PC market, and difficulties generating FCF in 2026. In fact, FCF was negative $1.47 billion over the last 12 months.

A Strong Quarter, but a Cloudy Outlook

At the same time, it's worth pointing out that the problem wasn't necessarily the Q3 results themselves, which, frankly, were good and even quite strong in some respects. For example, revenue and adjusted EPS rose 21% and 126%, respectively, year-over-year. Adjusted gross margin also reached 44%, up 4.1 percentage points.

Story Continues

The bigger concern is the possibility that Wall Street may need to revise its 2027 and 2028 projections downward. In fact, over the last three months, 2027 revenue estimates have been trimmed by roughly 3% to $69.27 billion, implying 12% year-over-year growth. Surprisingly, though, 2028 revenue estimates have actually been revised upward by nearly 2% over the same period. Consensus now points to $83.7 billion, implying 20.9% annual growth.

Intel's Data Center Segment Tells a Different Story

To determine whether this sell-off reflects temporary problems or a permanent deterioration in the business, look at Intel's data center business.

In Q3, revenue from the Data Center and AI segment reached $7.3 billion, up 78% year-over-year. Meanwhile, Client Computing revenue reached $8.1 billion, representing a 5% year-over-year decline.

Yet the devil is in the details. The Data Center & AI segment generated $3.04 billion in operating profit in Q3, compared to just $964 million a year earlier. In other words, operating profit more than tripled. This supports a key argument that Intel appears to be moving away from relying so heavily on the traditional PC market to drive growth. Also, its server business is rapidly becoming a much more important driver of revenue and profitability.

A Better Problem to Have

What's most interesting is that this data center growth didn't come simply from selling more processors. According to Intel, average selling prices (ASPs) for server chips rose an impressive 54% in Q3, while volume grew 10%. Much of the ASP increase came from a more favorable mix of premium products, rather than just price hikes. This helps explain why the segment's operating profit grew so much faster than revenue.

There's another detail I find particularly bullish. Demand continues to outpace production capacity. Intel also reported growth among hyperscalers, enterprise customers, and new cloud providers, despite ongoing supply constraints. Management expects these constraints to persist through 2027 and into 2028. Meanwhile, it projects annual growth of more than 30% in industry-wide server CPU volumes in both 2026 and 2027.

In other words, Intel's problem in this business seems to be more about its ability to meet demand than a lack of it. That, in my view, is a much healthier problem to have.

The Foundry Bet Is Starting to Pay Off for Intel

In addition to data centers, Intel's foundry business is another key part of its turnaround strategy. The goal is to compete with TSMC (TSM) in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Recent progress has been encouraging, too. In Q3, Intel reported that manufacturing costs for its 18A process had fallen by roughly 40% since Q1, thanks to better yields and improved production efficiency.

This is already a significant step forward, although there's still much to prove. Intel Foundry reported $6.7 billion in revenue for the quarter, but only $411 million came from external customers. Its operating loss also remained substantial at $1.85 billion, although that was down from $2.32 billion a year earlier.

This is precisely where Intel's valuation starts to make sense. Following Q3, the sell-side consensus calls for adjusted EPS of $2.99 in 2028. As a benchmark, I use Intel's own five-year average forward P/E of 27x , which I believe is reasonable if the turnaround stays on track. Applying that multiple to projected earnings gives me a price target of approximately $80.73 per share, or 55% upside from the current $52.25 over the next 12 months.

Is INTC a Buy, According to Wall Street Analysts?

Following Q3, some analysts downgraded Intel shares , adding to Wall Street's skepticism. According to TipRanks, the INTC forecast still shows an overall Hold consensus. Of the 33 analyst ratings issued over the past three months, only seven are Buy, while 25 are Hold and one is Sell. Interestingly, the average Intel price target stands at $91.62 , which, despite the skepticism, still implies a massive 75.35% upside from current levels.

Intel's Turnaround Is Still Worth Betting On

Intel's turnaround is far from a done deal, and its stock remains highly volatile. However, there's a big difference between a company struggling to find demand and one struggling to keep up with it. Stronger server sales, less dependence on PCs, improving margins, and progress in the foundry business suggest the recovery is gaining traction.

Of course, the road ahead remains bumpy, with heavy capital spending, foundry losses, and production constraints. Still, at current price levels, I see these headwinds as more related to capacity than weak demand, making the recent sell-off an attractive buying opportunity and supporting my bullish stance on INTC.

news.Content:

The decision marks an abrupt reversal of a major commitment first unveiled in June 2024 to build an integrated manufacturing hub in Rožnov pod Radhoštěm.

The scrapped initiative was designed to establish end-to-end silicon carbide production spanning crystal growth through finished power semiconductors. Existing silicon and silicon carbide operations at the Rožnov facility will remain fully operational and integrated within the chipmaker's broader global network.
