The defense-technology company surged about 21% Thursday after reporting its first quarterly results as a public company. Third-quarter revenue reached $194.4 million , beating expectations by $57.47 million, while GAAP earnings came in at $0.03 per share.

Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale believes the market is still valuing Lyntris too much like a traditional government IT contractor.

At roughly $9.40 before the rally, Gesuale estimated the stock traded near 9.1 times 2027 adjusted EBITDA , even though he expects revenue growth of about 31% next year. He maintained a Strong Buy rating and an $18 price target , implying roughly 59% upside from the price used in his note.

Lumentum is a more unusual setup.

Raymond James analyst Simon Leopold upgraded the optical-networking company to Strong Buy after Marvell agreed to acquire it in an all-stock transaction valued at an implied $115 billion enterprise value . Lumentum shareholders are set to receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share , with the deal expected to close in the first half of 2028.

The operating momentum remains strong too.

Lumentum reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $1.26 billion , up 136% year over year, with non-GAAP EPS of $4.57 . It also guided fiscal second-quarter revenue to $1.575 billion-$1.625 billion.

Leopold argues that weakness in Marvell has dragged Lumentum down too far relative to both the merger terms and its standalone value. Raymond James set a $1,328 target , implying roughly 160% upside from the price cited by TipRanks.

Investor Takeaway

I think the important point is that these are two completely different Strong Buy calls .

Lyntris is about a valuation gap: strong growth, defense-tech exposure, and a stock still well below its IPO price.

Lumentum is more complicated because the return now depends partly on Marvell's share price and the eventual completion of a huge all-stock deal.

That makes Lyntris the more straightforward fundamental bet, while Lumentum carries more merger, regulatory, and market-risk exposure.

For investors, the key things to watch are Lyntris revenue growth and margins, Marvell's stock price, Lumentum's optical-demand momentum, and whether the acquisition stays on track for a 2028 close .

Raymond James sees major upside in both.

The path to getting there is very different.

news.Title: MKSI Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and Capacity Expansion
news.Content:
MKS Inc. MKSI emphasized accelerating artificial intelligence (AI)-related demand, expanding manufacturing capacity and improving customer visibility during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management highlighted opportunities across semiconductor manufacturing and advanced electronics packaging.

The company also outlined stronger fourth-quarter expectations, supported by robust orders and improving operating leverage. Discussions with analysts focused on supply constraints, market share opportunities and the sustainability of margin expansion.

MKSI Sees Strong Momentum Heading Into Q4

President and CEO John Lee said demand across all three end markets exceeded or matched the upper end of management's expectations. Customer orders continue to strengthen, providing greater visibility into 2027 and beyond.

Fourth-quarter revenues are projected at $1.49 billion, plus or minus $40 million, representing approximately 44% year-over-year growth. Non-GAAP earnings are expected at $5 per share, plus or minus 38 cents.

Third-quarter revenues reached $1.41 billion, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.36 billion. Adjusted earnings of $4.18 per share surpassed the consensus estimate of $3.64.

MKS Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

MKS Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | MKS Inc. Quote

MKS Expects Semiconductor Growth to Outpace WFE

Semiconductor revenues increased 54% year over year to $638 million, supported by DRAM, advanced logic and NAND upgrade investments.

Lee highlighted strengthening demand for plasma, reactive gas, vacuum and power solutions. The company also secured design wins involving advanced logic applications and pulsed DC power technology.

During the Q&A, a Cantor Fitzgerald analyst questioned MKS' ability to outperform wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending. Lee indicated that semiconductor growth could approach 40% year over year, exceeding industry growth, with continued outperformance expected in 2027.

MKSI Expands Capacity Amid Packaging Demand

Electronics & Packaging revenues climbed 43% year over year to $415 million, reflecting strong demand for chemistry equipment and advanced PCB technologies.

Lee said chemistry equipment sales increased more than 75% year over year, with full-year revenues expected to exceed $300 million. Existing capacity is sold out through 2027, while bookings extend into 2028.

Management plans to double chemistry equipment capacity through its Guangzhou expansion, targeted for completion in the third quarter of 2027. During the Q&A, Lee explained that additional capacity should accelerate equipment revenue growth in the second half of 2027.

Story Continues

MKS Targets Higher Margins Despite Near-Term Pressure

Gross margin reached 47.7%, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded approximately 700 basis points year over year to 27.8%.

Executive vice president and CFO Ram Mayampurath attributed the improvement to higher volumes and operating leverage. However, growing sales of lower-margin chemistry equipment and manufacturing expansion costs remain near-term headwinds.

Responding to questions from Deutsche Bank and Wells Fargo analysts, Mayampurath indicated that higher-margin chemistry consumables should eventually offset these pressures. Management expects near-term incremental gross margins around 50%, with potential for higherlevels longer term.

MKSI Highlights Financial Flexibility and Shareholder Returns

MKS generated $243 million in free cash flow during the quarter, representing approximately 17% of revenues. Net leverage declined to 2.4 times trailing adjusted EBITDA.

Mayampurath highlighted continued debt reduction, including more than $450 million in year-to-date principal prepayments following an additional November payment.

The board also authorized a $500 million share repurchase program. Responding to a Wells Fargo analyst, Mayampurath emphasized that organic investment and debt management remain priorities, while repurchases provide additional capital allocation flexibility.

MKS Maintains Focus on Execution and Long-Term Growth

Management's commentary remained confident regarding AI-related investment, customer demand and manufacturing readiness. Lee emphasized that expanding capacity and securing design wins remain essential to supporting growth.

Supply chain constraints and equipment mix pressures warrant attention as operations scale. Management plans to provide additional details on profitability and longer-term opportunities at its Dec. 14 Investor Day.

What MKSI's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

MKSI currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), indicating favorable near-term performance potential based on earnings estimate revision trends. Its Value, Growth and Momentum Scores of B reflect attractive characteristics across all three investment styles.

The stock's VGM Score of A reinforces its favorable combined positioning. Historically, stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 alongside strong Style Scores have demonstrated better relative performance potential. However, MKSI's Zacks Rank could change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest results.

news.Title: AMD, Nvidia and Intel diverge as Morningstar resets the scorecard
news.Content:
Three of the most closely watched chip stocks are trading at very different valuations, and Morningstar's latest read on all three says the market has mispriced at least two of them.

AMD has closed the gap with its fair value estimate, while Nvidia and Intel still look undervalued by a significant margin. That gap is not a simple buy signal. It raises the question of which company is best positioned as AI spending shifts from raw training power to something more complex.

Morningstar raised its AMD fair value estimate to $570, putting the stock roughly at fair value with about 18% implied upside. Nvidia carries the largest discount of the three, with roughly 50% implied upside to its fair value target, while Intel shows about 40% implied upside. Morningstar assigns all three a "Very High" uncertainty rating, meaning the spread between the bull and bear cases remains wide.

AMD posts a record quarter on data center strength

AMD delivered its strongest quarter on record in the three months ended September 30. Total revenue came in at $13.38 billion, up 45% year over year, driven almost entirely by data center demand. The data center segment alone posted $8.5 billion in revenue, up 97% from a year earlier as hyperscalers accelerated spending on AMD's Instinct MI450 GPUs and EPYC server processors, according to AMD .

Also read: AMD CEO Su shares important supply news with stock market investors

Non-GAAP diluted earnings reached $2.09 a share, up 74%, while gross margin expanded to 56%. The company guided fourth-quarter revenue to roughly $17 billion, plus or minus 3%. AMD's data center business now accounts for 58% of total revenue, up from 42% a year earlier.

On the earnings call, CEO Lisa Su said AMD now expects data center revenue to more than double year over year in 2027, a forecast that marks an upgrade from earlier guidance of more than 80% growth issued before the Q3 results.

AMD shares were down about 2.6% in premarket trading on November 5, extending a broader pullback in chip stocks. The Nasdaq was also lower by roughly 1.6%.

The Anthropic deal anchors AMD's AI ambitions

AMD's biggest strategic commitment in 2026 was not a product launch but an investment. The company announced a partnership with Anthropic valued at up to $5 billion, covering 2 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPU compute and a collaboration on ROCm, AMD's open-source software stack for AI workloads. The first gigawatt of capacity is expected to come online in the first half of 2027, according to AMD .

Story Continues

Meta and OpenAI have each separately committed to 6 gigawatts of AMD GPU capacity, pushing AMD's total announced deployment commitments to roughly 14 gigawatts across its three largest AI customers. Those commitments reflect a broadening of the customer base that AMD has been building since it launched its MI300X accelerator last year.

The software gap remains AMD's most discussed risk. Nvidia's CUDA platform has a decade-long head start on AMD's ROCm, with a larger library of tools, optimized models and developer workflows.

Switching costs are real for companies already deep in the Nvidia ecosystem. The Anthropic ROCm collaboration is AMD's most visible effort to close that gap, but analysts widely acknowledge the distance is still significant, according to AMD .

Musk's SpaceX deal underscores Nvidia's lock on big buyers

Nvidia's moat was most evident in a deal disclosed in August 2026. Elon Musk said SpaceX would use Nvidia chips exclusively in its data centers, a decision that helped underpin the company's $40 billion GPU financing deal with Apollo Global Management.

That commitment, the largest committed GPU financing ever announced, illustrated the kind of anchor customer Nvidia can attract that AMD still struggles to match in head-to-head competition at the largest scales of spending, according to SpaceX .

Nvidia reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $96.2 billion earlier this year, up 106% year over year, with data center revenue reaching $89 billion. The company also said it has visibility into nearly $20 billion in total server CPU revenue this fiscal year as it pushes its Vera chip into the CPU market alongside its GPU business.

Intel's quarter beats but its guide falls short

Intel reported third-quarter revenue of $16.5 billion on October 30, up 21% year over year. Data center and AI segment revenue climbed 78% to $7.3 billion, reflecting accelerating demand for server processors. The stock fell 29% the day results were released, however, after fourth-quarter guidance of $15 billion to $16 billion came in well below the roughly $17 billion Wall Street had expected, according to Intel .

More Wall Street:

Nvidia and Micron are about to lord their successes all over Wall Street

Nvidia, Palantir, and Alphabet send waves through Wall Street

Wall Street elites will pocket windfall from record $46 billion profits

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya followed the report with a downgrade, cutting Intel to Neutral from Buy and reducing his price target to $100 from $145. Arya wrote that Intel is "not yet technically competitive" in AI accelerators, a gap he said is wide enough to limit how quickly the company can capture the data center spending surge that has lifted AMD and Nvidia, as reported by TheStreet .

Intel CFO David Zinsner said the company expects server CPU market share to remain above 30% in both 2026 and 2027, while CEO Lip-Bu Tan framed Intel's foundry business as a long-term opportunity that the company is building carefully rather than aggressively. The stock's sharp post-earnings decline reflected how little margin for error the market is giving Intel as AMD continues to gain ground in its core server processor market.

The PC slowdown hits AMD and Intel equally

Both companies are dealing with a deteriorating personal computer market on top of their data center ambitions. Gartner reported that worldwide PC shipments declined 22.4% in the third quarter of 2026 as component cost inflation raised average selling prices and pushed buyers to the sidelines.

AMD's client and gaming segment fell 8% in the quarter, with gaming revenue dropping to roughly $800 million from $1.3 billion a year earlier. Lisa Su said on the earnings call that AMD's planning assumption for 2027 is that the PC market will be "double-digit percentage down," though she added the company expects its own client revenue to hold up better than the overall market through its Ryzen lineup and growing commercial adoption.

Intel faces the same headwind, with both companies dependent on a PC market that is shrinking faster than the data center market is growing for either company. The Gartner decline underscores why analysts keep returning to data center execution as the only metric that matters for either stock over the next 12 to 18 months.

Related: Microsoft just gave Nvidia shareholders a reason to pay attention

news.Title: Apple, Meta, Musk Face New Threat From Democrats
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ), Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) and companies linked to Elon Musk could face a sweeping wave of congressional investigations following Democrats' victories in both chambers of Congress, raising fresh regulatory and political risks for some of America's biggest technology companies.

Is AAPL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

According to a November 6 Washington Post report, Democratic lawmakers are preparing investigations into corporate relationships with President Donald Trump's administration, including whether businesses received favorable treatment, government funding or lucrative contracts.

The potential investigations extend well beyond campaign donations and political relationships.

Apple could face questions over its hosting of applications used in connection with Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations, while Meta's nondisclosure agreements with local governments concerning data-center developments could attract scrutiny.

Musk's businesses, including Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) and privately held SpaceX and xAI, could also face questions about their government relationships. One potential line of inquiry involves Trump's reported use of Musk's Grok chatbot during the operation to capture Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.

The pressure is already building.

On November 5, Democratic Senator Richard Blum ( Trades , Portfolio )enthal requested documents from Apple, Meta, Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ), Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ), Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) and other companies concerning contributions to Trump's White House ballroom project, warning of potential subpoenas in January.

The incoming congressional majority would have greater authority to compel testimony and obtain corporate records. However, potential investigations do not establish wrongdoing, and their financial consequences remain uncertain.

Investors Takeaway

For Apple and Meta investors, the immediate concern is less about earnings disruption and more about legal expenses, executive distractions and reputational damage.

Meta's expanding AI infrastructure footprint makes scrutiny of data-center agreements particularly relevant, while Apple's exposure centers on its app-distribution policies and government relationships.

Musk-linked companies could face greater questions about federal contracts and potential conflicts of interest.

Investors should monitor formal subpoena notices, congressional hearing schedules and any disclosures of financial penalties or contractual changes.

The critical distinction is whether political scrutiny remains a headline risk or develops into investigations with measurable consequences for revenue, operating costs and future government business.

news.Title: Michael Burry Takes Profits on Major AI Bear Bet
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Michael Burry ( Trades , Portfolio ) has started taking profits on one of his biggest bearish technology bets.

The famed investor disclosed that he sold 25% of his put options on the VanEck Semiconductor ETF ( NASDAQ:SMH ) after a sharp selloff across U.S. chip and technology stocks.

But that does not mean Burry has turned bullish.

He said the remaining SMH put position has become very large, suggesting the trade still represents a major part of his bearish exposure.

That distinction matters because SMH owns many of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, including Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ), Taiwan Semiconductor ( NYSE:TSM ), AMD ( NASDAQ:AMD ), Broadcom and Micron ( NASDAQ:MU ) .

The timing also makes sense.

SMH plunged about 11.2% on November 5 , while the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% and the QQQ ETF dropped 6.5%, giving bearish positions a significant opportunity to lock in gains.

Burry had previously concentrated much of his bearish exposure into puts on SMH and the Nasdaq-100 with expirations in 2027, while arguing that the AI trade could be approaching a major market top.

He is also still holding puts on Palantir ( NASDAQ:PLTR ), Oracle ( NYSE:ORCL ), Caterpillar and QQQ , according to his latest disclosure.

At the same time, Burry is not broadly bearish on every stock.

He disclosed that he added to his position in MercadoLibre , buying shares below $1,500 after the company reported earnings.

Investor Takeaway

I think the key point is that Burry is trimming risk, not reversing his thesis .

Selling 25% of the SMH puts after an 11% one-day plunge is classic profit-taking.

The more important signal is that he still describes the remaining position as very large and continues to hold several other bearish technology bets.

That means investors should not read this as Burry calling a bottom in semiconductors.

Instead, it suggests he believes the selloff has already moved far enough to justify locking in some gains while still expecting further downside.

For investors, the key things to watch are whether Burry trims more of the position, Nvidia's next earnings report, semiconductor valuations, AI capex expectations, and whether the broader Nasdaq correction deepens from here .

He is taking some money off the table.

He is not leaving the trade.

The third quarter earnings season is over halfway done, and the reports continue to pour in. This week brought another shot of major earnings courtesy of Apple ( AAPL ), Palantir ( PLTR ), and AMD ( AMD ).

news.Title: Marvell Is Betting $115 Billion on 1 of AI's Biggest Bottlenecks
news.Content:
There are a ton of supply constraints in the artificial intelligence industry. As large language models grow bigger and more complex and the number of people using them grows, a handful of companies are working to supply as much compute capacity as possible.

There are a few bottlenecks limiting their ability to scale, though. Many people know about the memory chip shortage, which has led to booming profits for the chipmakers supplying that key component. But optical networking components may be an even bigger bottleneck. Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) CEO Michael Hurlston said at a conference that the shortage the key material for developing its lasers "will become even more acute than what we see from the memory guys."

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

That shortage has already shown up in its financial statement with booming revenue and profit margins. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL), which expects its optical interconnect chips to remain its biggest business for the foreseeable future despite a rapidly growing custom XPU business, seems to agree with Hurlston.

Access to its lasers could be key for Marvell's continued growth. In fact, the chipmaker just offered $115 billion to absorb Lumentum entirely. Let's see what this could all mean for investors.

The next-generation of AI connectivity

Marvell's bid for Lumentum gives it an enterprise value of $115 billion at the time of the offer. However, the deal is an all-stock offer, with Lumentum shareholders receiving 4.5 shares of Marvell stock per share of Lumentum stock. As a result, the closing value will depend on where Marvell trades.

So far, the market is not optimistic about the deal, sending shares of Marvell lower on the news. To be sure, Marvell is paying a significant premium for Lumentum, and shareholders will see considerable dilution, owning just 67% of the combined company after the deal goes through.

But the acquisition could bolster one of the most important parts of Marvell's business. Marvell sees connectivity remaining its biggest business, with the total addressable market growing at a 65% compound annual growth rate between 2026 and 2031. Optical interconnect chips turn electrical signals into light, which moves much faster. Lumentum makes the lasers and transmission modules for producing that light.

Story Continues

Lumentum and its chief rival, Coherent , are the two largest producers of the indium phosphide lasers that power today's fiber networks. The supply shortage has led to phenomenal financial results for both companies. Lumentum saw sales climb 109% in the fourth quarter, with gross margin expanding 14.1 percentage points and operating margin expanding 29.5 percentage points. The result was adjusted earnings growth of more than 400%.

Management expects the supply constraints to lead to further margin expansion this quarter. What's more, Hurlston says the supply constraints could last through 2028 with Lumentum's capacity sold out into 2029. It takes years to build out new capacity, and Lumentum is booking take-or-pay deals with its customers to ensure it maximizes the utility of new facilities that won't start producing new components for several years.

Marvell is securing its competitive position

Lumentum fills in some significant gaps in Marvell's interconnect business. Specifically, as it looks to "scale-in" with co-packaged optics (CPO) bringing the optical chips closer to the core processing units in AI data centers, the need for some of its chips is eliminated. Lumentum's lasers, however, are necessary for optical transmission, so they'll remain a key component of interconnect chips in all forms.

The combined company would have a complete portfolio of optical chips and packages, rivaling Broadcom . The ability to design CPO architecture and supply all of the components provides a hedge against disruption to its digital signal processing (DSP) chips.

Marvell's management says the combined company unlocks new opportunities for the business, expanding its total addressable market. Management's outlook calls for a $550 billion TAM by 2030 for the combined company, adding $60 billion to previous forecasts.

Investors should be wary of the risks, however. Perhaps the biggest risk is acquiring a company amid a booming earnings cycle. If the supply shortage isn't as severe as Lumentum's management believes or if demand slows faster than expected in later years, Marvell could be paying a very high premium for the company. Premium pricing for Lumentum's components could fall considerably once new production capacity comes online.

Investors should pay close attention to Lumentum's commentary over the next year, as the deal isn't expected to close until 2028. If the supply shortage is narrowing more quickly than expected, it could indicate that Marvell could have trouble charging the premium prices to end customers it needs to achieve its forecasts laid out in its presentation announcing the deal.

news.Title: GFS or MRVL: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
news.Content:
Investors looking for stocks in the Electronics - Semiconductors sector might want to consider either GlobalFoundries Inc. (GFS) or Marvell Technology (MRVL). But which of these two companies is the best option for those looking for undervalued stocks? Let's take a closer look.

Everyone has their own methods for finding great value opportunities, but our model includes pairing an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system with a strong Zacks Rank. The proven Zacks Rank emphasizes companies with positive estimate revision trends, and our Style Scores highlight stocks with specific traits.

Currently, both GlobalFoundries Inc. and Marvell Technology are holding a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy). This system places an emphasis on companies that have seen positive earnings estimate revisions, so investors should feel comfortable knowing that these stocks have improving earnings outlooks. But this is only part of the picture for value investors.

Value investors also tend to look at a number of traditional, tried-and-true figures to help them find stocks that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

The Style Score Value grade factors in a variety of key fundamental metrics, including the popular P/E ratio, P/S ratio, earnings yield, cash flow per share, and a number of other key stats that are commonly used by value investors.

GFS currently has a forward P/E ratio of 18.41, while MRVL has a forward P/E of 31.69. We also note that GFS has a PEG ratio of 0.90. This figure is similar to the commonly-used P/E ratio, with the PEG ratio also factoring in a company's expected earnings growth rate. MRVL currently has a PEG ratio of 2.88.

Another notable valuation metric for GFS is its P/B ratio of 1.66. The P/B is a method of comparing a stock's market value to its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, MRVL has a P/B of 6.32.

These are just a few of the metrics contributing to GFS's Value grade of B and MRVL's Value grade of F.

Both GFS and MRVL are impressive stocks with solid earnings outlooks, but based on these valuation figures, we feel that GFS is the superior value option right now.

news.Title: Arista Networks Cashes In on the AI Infrastructure Buildout
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Arista Networks, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Arista Networks reported 58.5% year-over-year revenue growth in Q3 2026, supported by strong demand for AI networking infrastructure.

Management expects AI fabric revenue to double to approximately $7 billion in 2027, alongside continued growth in enterprise networking.

Arista Networks' premium valuation and significant supplier commitments create risks if hyperscale data center spending slows.

Building artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure requires more than advanced processors. Connecting tens of thousands of processing units to function as a single, cohesive supercomputer requires a networking architecture capable of ultra-low latency and high throughput. For years, proprietary fabrics dominated this highly specialized space. Cloud service providers are increasingly pivoting toward open, standards-based Ethernet to link their sprawling AI clusters and avoid rigid vendor lock-in.

This architectural shift offers a distinct commercial advantage to networking providers that can meet the stringent demands of hyperscale data centers. Investors looking to gauge global capital expenditure momentum can look to the companies providing this critical connectivity.

→ Amazon Has Erased Its Earnings Sell-Off, But Is the Biggest Opportunity Still Ahead?

How Arista Networks Outpaces Legacy Tech

Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET) recently posted a third-quarter earnings report that handily beat market expectations, delivering $1.20 in earnings per share on record revenue of $3.66 billion. That top-line figure represents an approximate 59% year-over-year increase, signaling healthy, sustained demand for its networking solutions.

Management responded by raising fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $13.3 billion. Initial guidance for 2027 projects revenue growth of 38% to 40%, targeting roughly $18.5 billion. This upward trajectory highlights an industry shift. Hyperscalers are increasingly migrating away from closed, proprietary networking fabrics, opting instead for high-speed Ethernet switching platforms.

→ Washington Made a $2 Billion Quantum Bet, But Can Either ETF Match It?

The preference for Ethernet stems from its broad interoperability. Cloud builders prefer environments where they can mix and match components without being tethered to a single ecosystem. Arista Networks supports this flexibility through its Extensible Operating System.

This foundational software layer gives cloud operators the programmatic controls they need to optimize data flows, enabling rapid deployment while reducing overall power consumption across high-density facilities. By decoupling software intelligence from the underlying hardware, Arista Networks helps clients scale complex AI workloads without sacrificing network stability or efficiency.

Story Continues

→ Energy Transfer's Earnings Miss May Be Hiding Its Strongest Advantage

Chasing the $7 Billion AI Fabric Opportunity

The core driver behind this growth is the rapid adoption of AI fabrics. Management expects AI fabric revenue to double to about $7 billion by 2027. Arista Networks is seeing notable commercial traction with its Etherlink portfolio, having recently surpassed 100 active customers. Over the next few years, the company forecasts more than 10 gigawatts of deployment spanning multiple types of compute accelerators.

A large portion of this capital expenditure stems from industry heavyweights. During the recent earnings call, management noted that Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ: META) continue to account for more than 10% of revenue each. The leadership team also sees the potential to add one or two more hyperscale customers at that concentration level in the near future, underscoring the deep integration Arista Networks has achieved within the world's largest data centers.

Beyond the expansive data center buildouts, the enterprise campus business is showing resilient strength. Driven by a corporate demand for secure, automated, zero-trust network infrastructure, the cognitive campus segment is expected to grow by about 60%.

This growth trajectory places the campus division on pace to reach roughly $2 billion in revenue by 2027, diversifying the company's income streams beyond pure hyperscale dependency. This dual-engine growth model could provide a buffer if cloud capital expenditures moderate, with enterprise upgrades helping to sustain revenue growth.

Balancing Aggressive Growth With Profitability

Meeting this elevated level of demand requires a highly proactive approach to procurement. Inventory levels have increased to $3.2 billion, while forward purchase commitments expanded to a notable $11.4 billion. In a normal operating environment, tying up extensive capital in inventory and future commitments might appear as a balance sheet vulnerability. In a tight supply environment, securing component availability ahead of a projected 40% growth rate could provide a competitive advantage. It could help Arista Networks fulfill multi-year infrastructure buildouts while reducing the risk of component shortages that could derail client timelines.

Strong operating cash flow and a disciplined capital return program support this forward-looking supply chain management. Management is actively executing a $1.5 billion share repurchase authorization, with about $817 million remaining available. Buying back shares at this stage signals executive confidence in forward cash flow generation and provides an underlying layer of capital support for the equity.

On the profitability front, Arista Networks demonstrates significant operating leverage. The shift toward a heavier hardware mix in AI deployments is expected to moderate gross margins to 62% to 64% in 2027. Yet, operating margins are projected to hold steady at about 49%. This balance shows strict operating expense management and cost discipline, effectively offsetting the hardware margin drag and preserving bottom-line strength.

Is the High Valuation Justified for Arista Networks?

Investors analyzing Arista Networks' stock will notice a trailing price-to-earnings ratio hovering around 43. A multiple at this level prices in high expectations, requiring Arista Networks to continually execute against its ambitious multi-year growth targets.

The projected slight compression in gross margins remains a metric to watch, as hardware sales will likely outpace higher-margin software revenue in the near term during this physical buildout phase.

If broader macroeconomic headwinds force hyperscalers to dial back their capital expenditure plans, companies trading at premium multiples often face the sharpest valuation adjustments.

The current valuation sits against a backdrop of exceptional revenue visibility. The multi-year purchase commitments and deep integration into hyperscale AI plans provide a level of operational predictability rarely seen in enterprise technology.

Adding to the structural support, Arista Networks was added to the S&P 100 index in late 2026. This index inclusion could act as a mechanical catalyst, mandating passive institutional accumulation and providing a steady baseline of trading volume.

Investors looking to add exposure to the physical layer of AI infrastructure might want to add this networking provider to their watchlist. As cloud titans continue to fund large-scale data center expansions, companies supplying the essential connectivity remain well-positioned to capture the ongoing architectural shift.

news.Title: MCHP Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise on Demand Recovery
news.Content:
Microchip Technology MCHP reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of 97 cents per share that beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.2%. The company reported earnings of 35 cents per share in the year-ago quarter.

Net sales of $1.622 billion increased 42.2% year over year and surpassed the $1.608 billion consensus mark by 0.8%. Broad-based demand recovery, led by industrial and data center applications, supported growth. Bookings remained robust, with the book-to-bill ratio well above 1, while data center revenues jumped 55.7% year over year.

Microchip Technology Incorporated Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Microchip Technology Incorporated price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Microchip Technology Incorporated Quote

MCHP's Revenue Growth Gains Momentum

Sales increased 9.2% sequentially and exceeded the high end of management's prior guidance. Microchip benefited from improving customer demand across major end markets, supported by new design wins and product introductions.

Semiconductor products generated $1.55 billion in revenues compared with $1.108 billion a year earlier. Technology licensing revenues increased to $71.1 million from $32.4 million.

Mixed-signal microcontrollers remained Microchip's largest product line, generating $774.4 million in sales, up 32.5% year over year. Analog revenues increased 42.8% to $459 million, while other products contributed $388.1 million, up 65.6%.

Geographically, Asia led with $781.3 million in revenues, followed by the Americas at $460.2 million and Europe at $380 million. The distribution and direct channels each accounted for approximately 50% of product sales, highlighting a balanced channel mix.

Microchip's Data Center and Industrial Demand Strengthen

Industrial represented 34.6% of September-quarter product revenues and posted 50.3% year-over-year growth, making it the company's largest disclosed end market.

Data center accounted for 16.7% of revenues, supported by demand for connectivity, storage and embedded control solutions. Communications increased 43.5%, while aerospace and defense grew 41%. Automotive revenues rose 19.3%, reflecting growth across several customer markets.

Microchip's PCIe Gen6 switch and retimer design wins doubled sequentially to 24 programs from 12 at June-end. These products help move data between components in high-performance computing systems.

The company expects its total data center portfolio to grow 69.3% year over year to $1 billion in calendar 2026. Microchip also completed its acquisition of Hailo, an edge AI processor provider, during September, strengthening its portfolio of artificial intelligence solutions.

Story Continues

MCHP's Margin Expansion Drives Profitability

Non-GAAP gross margin reached 66.5%, expanding 980 basis points (bps) year over year and 267 bps sequentially. The improvement reflected stronger sales and ongoing operational efficiency.

Non-GAAP operating expenses totaled $437.9 million, compared with $369 million in the year-ago quarter. As a percentage of sales, expenses declined to 27% from 32.4%, highlighting disciplined spending despite higher revenues.

Non-GAAP operating income climbed to $639.9 million from $277.2 million a year earlier. Operating margin expanded 1,516 bps to 39.5%, reflecting improved operating leverage.

Microchip's Cash Flow and Leverage Improve

As of Sept. 30, 2026, Microchip had cash and short-term investments of $457 million compared with $240.3 million at March-end. Inventory stood at $1.117 billion, with inventory days at 184 versus 185 at the beginning of fiscal 2027.

Cash flow from operations totaled $419.2 million compared with $88.1 million in the year-ago quarter. Free cash flow increased to $396.1 million from $51.6 million, representing 24.4% of net sales.

Net debt to adjusted trailing 12-month EBITDA improved to 2.36x from 2.85x in the preceding quarter. Microchip returned $247.6 million to common stockholders through dividends and declared another quarterly dividend of 45.5 cents per share.

MCHP Guides Seasonal December Quarter

For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, Microchip expects net sales between $1.573 billion and $1.638 billion, implying sequential growth between negative 3% and positive 1%.

The midpoint of $1.606 billion represents approximately 35.4% year-over-year growth. MCHP noted that roughly $53 million in infrequent September-quarter revenues would not recur, making the underlying outlook stronger than normal December-quarter seasonality.

The company expects non-GAAP gross margin of 64-65%, operating margin of 37-38.5% and operating expenses of 26.5-27% of sales.

Non-GAAP earnings are projected at 87-95 cents per share. Capital expenditures are expected to be approximately $35 million for the December quarter and $100 million for fiscal 2027.

The company also highlighted lengthening supply-chain lead times and efforts to secure additional wafer capacity to support customer demand.

Zacks Rank & Upcoming Earnings to Consider

Microchip currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Forgent Power Solutions FPS, Telos TLS and NVIDIA NVDA are some other top-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. While Forgent Power and Telos sport a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) each at present, NVIDIA carries a Zacks Rank #2. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Forgent Power, Telos and NVIDIA are expected to report their quarterly results on Nov. 12, 9 and 17, respectively. Forgent Power shares have dropped 37% year to date (YTD). Telos shares have declined 6.5% YTD, while NVIDIA shares have decreased 2.3% over the same timeframe.

news.Title: SYNA Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Miss on Weak Demand
news.Content:
Synaptics Incorporated SYNA reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $1.26 per share, up 15.6% year over year from $1.09. The figure surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.44%.

Revenues increased 0.5% year over year to $294 million but missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 7.59%. Performance was affected by supply constraints, memory-related demand dynamics, and softness in smartphone demand, which weighed on the company's touch and wireless products.

SYNA's Q1 Operating Details

Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 110 basis points (bps) year over year to 54.3% from 53.2% in the year-ago quarter. GAAP gross margin improved to 47.8% from 42.6%.

Non-GAAP research and development expenses declined 6.1% year over year to $69.1 million. On a non-GAAP basis, selling, general and administrative expenses decreased 5.9% year over year to $28.6 million.

Synaptics Incorporated Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Synaptics Incorporated price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Synaptics Incorporated Quote

Non-GAAP operating income increased 20.4% year over year to $62 million from $51.5 million. Non-GAAP operating margin improved to approximately 21.1% from 17.6%, reflecting stronger profitability despite subdued revenue growth.

SYNA's Edge AI Initiatives Gain Momentum

Synaptics continued expanding its presence in Edge AI and Physical AI markets through new product launches, partnerships, and customer engagements.

The company introduced the Synaptics Astra SR200 series, featuring a new class of microcontrollers called xMCUs. These solutions enable larger AI models and richer multimodal workloads to run directly on devices, supporting growing demand for on-device artificial intelligence.

Synaptics also expanded its Coralboard ecosystem in collaboration with Google Research. The company made Coralboard SL generally available through partners and introduced Coralboard SR, powered by the Astra SR200 series.

Synaptics announced that its capacitive tactile sensing module and Astra Edge AI processors are supported by NVIDIA's Isaac Sim and Holoscan platforms, enabling multisensory processing capabilities.

The company highlighted growing opportunities for its tactile sensing controllers and video interface products in robotics, alongside increasing customer interest in its processor and wireless technologies.

SYNA's Cash Flow & Balance Sheet

As of Sept. 26, 2026, Synaptics had cash and cash equivalents of $367.7 million, down from $442.5 million as of June 27, 2026.

Total debt stood at $838 million, including $440.1 million in current debt and $397.9 million in long-term debt.

Net cash used in operating activities was $15.5 million during the reported quarter against cash generated from operating activities of $30.2 million in the year-ago period.

Story Continues

SYNA Withholds Outlook Amid Pending onsemi Acquisition

Synaptics did not provide forward-looking financial guidance or schedule a quarterly earnings conference call due to its pending acquisition by onsemi.

The companies initially entered into a definitive all-stock merger agreement on June 25, 2026. On Oct. 1, 2026, the agreement was amended to restructure the transaction into an all-cash acquisition.

Synaptics remains focused on expanding its presence in Physical AI and Edge AI markets through new product development and strategic partnerships. However, supply constraints, memory-related demand challenges and smartphone market softness remain near-term headwinds.

SYNA's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

Synaptics currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Some better-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector include Cisco Systems CSCO, Analog Devices ADI, and NVIDIA NVDA. Each stock presently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Cisco Systems shares have gained 24.3% year to date. Cisco Systems is set to report first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 12.

Shares of Analog Devices have risen 33.2% year to date. Analog Devices is set to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 24.

NVIDIA shares have lost 2.6% year to date. NVIDIA is set to report third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 17.

news.Title: 5 big analyst AI moves: Is the historic AI stock rout a buy opportunity?
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Here are the biggest analyst moves in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) for this week.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

AI rout is a buying opportunity, Yardeni says

Yardeni Research told investors the selloff in Thursday's session represents a buying opportunity, arguing that political backlash against data centers is a speed bump for the AI boom rather than a roadblock.

"Since September 15, we've counseled proceeding with caution in the stock market through the midterm elections," the firm wrote, adding that it had anticipated buying opportunities after Tuesday's elections. Stocks rallied Wednesday, driven by short covering, but then plunged, with the S&P 500's 4.4% decline its worst day since the April 2025 tariff shock and the Nasdaq's 5.5% drop pushing it into correction territory.

"The cold shower we warned might follow a democratic sweep arrived late," Yardeni said.

On Thursday, investors began "discounting the implications of the Democratic sweep for the economy's golden goose: the AI investment boom." Yardeni pointed to growing backlash against data centers, citing an NBC exit poll showing 76% of voters opposed new facilities in their communities.

"Perhaps most consequentially, Texas, which accounts for nearly 30% of planned US data center additions in 2028, elected Gina Hinojosa as governor after she promised to halt new approvals," Yardeni said. Goldman Sachs estimates that states facing possible restrictions account for around 45% of planned U.S. data center capacity.

Still, Yardeni believes the backlash, alongside financial and physical bottlenecks, are "just speed bumps" and that the selling is overdone. "Data centers will get built, albeit at a slower pace. Speed bumps should prevent the AI boom from moving too fast and crashing around the next curve," it said.

"That's why we view Thursday's sell off as a buying opportunity."

Analysts downgrade Marvell on concerns over all-stock deal with Lumentum

Earlier this week, TD Cowen and Bank of America have both downgraded Marvell Technology, citing concerns about the chipmaker's all-stock acquisition of Lumentum.

TD Cowen cut Marvell to Hold from Buy, slashing its price target to $175 from $350. Analyst Sean O'Loughlin expects the deal to dilute EPS by a mid-single-digit percentage in 2028, its first year, and worries it may come at or near the peak of an optical mini-cycle.

Story Continues

"Our downgrade is driven primarily by our negative view of the transaction itself in terms of structure and timing, rather than the quality of the asset Marvell is acquiring," he wrote.

O'Loughlin said Lumentum is likely to become a "crown jewel" within Marvell's portfolio, but noted that bottom-up consensus implies a roughly $100 billion optical transceiver market in 2027, compared with TD Cowen's $47 billion forecast. If the cycle turns, Lumentum's operating leverage could worsen the dilution.

Bank of America downgraded Marvell to Neutral from Buy and cut its price target to $225 from $400. Analyst Vivek Arya cited a potential extended stock overhang from the deal, along with a big drop in the SOX index over the past month.

Arya said the deal has strategic merit, creating a broader electrical-to-optical connectivity platform, but flagged a lengthy regulatory process with closing expected in the first half of 2028, limited EPS accretion as $1 billion in cost cuts falls short of offsetting about 50% share dilution, and potential customer conflicts.

"There was no mention of any large M&A in MRVL's recent analyst day, so the news comes as a considerable surprise," he said. "We question the impact on LITE's valuation once its laser shortages are inevitably resolved."

Citi says AI trade may stay under pressure post-midterms, prefers Europe over U.S. stocks

Citi told clients the AI trade could remain under pressure after the U.S. midterm elections, and said it prefers European stocks over U.S. equities for now.

The bank noted that markets typically pull back ahead of midterms and rally afterward, with seasonal analysis pointing to November-December S&P 500 returns of 3% to 4%. But this year's pre-election weakness had other causes.

"More importantly, the pullback ahead of the midterms was not mostly due to the election, but due to AI financing worries, and oil," the bank wrote.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Citi still expects data centers to get built given strong demand for computing power, but said their location, design and pace of construction may change after Democrats' gains. "This is far from ideal for the picks and shovels, including semis," the bank said.

Its "Generals" index, which tracks how many of the seven largest S&P 500 stocks trade below their 200-day moving averages, is close to triggering a cautionary signal, and Citi expects more rotation out of tech for now.

Citi said the election has not clearly changed the Iran war's trajectory, but a renewed escalation does not appear imminent, with a third U.S. aircraft carrier not due in the Gulf until mid- to late November.

"We prefer to use Europe, given that the AI story remains difficult, while the large move lower in oil should benefit European equities much more, also because it may lead to a more dovish ECB," Citi said. At the very least, it expects European stocks to outperform the U.S.

Citi cuts Adobe to Sell, sees "rising risk of a hard reset"

In a separate note, Citi has downgraded Adobe to Sell and slashed its price target to $207 from $250, saying it sees downside risk to consensus growth estimates into fiscal 2027 as a leadership transition coincides with mounting competitive and macro pressure on the Creative business.

"[We] see rising risk of a hard reset," Citi analysts said. Incoming CEO Anil Chakravarthy, who takes over Dec. 1, assumes the role "amid key leadership vacancies," including the CFO and the head of Digital Media.

The Wall Street firm expects a weaker fiscal 2027 outlook when Adobe reports fourth-quarter results in early December. "A 'hard reset' would pressure shares near term but provide time to rebuild leadership, refine strategy, and establish a more achievable base to accelerate," the analysts wrote.

The bank expects Adobe to lean more on top-of-funnel growth through AI and Firefly rather than its classic Creative Cloud suite, which has relied on price increases. That shift toward monthly active users will likely weigh on total ARR in fiscal 2027 and 2028, with the greatest impact in core Creative, compounded by weak small-business demand and competition from web-based and AI-native tools.

Citi estimates the user-growth emphasis could add 200 basis points of pressure to fiscal 2027 annual recurring revenue (ARR) growth, with pricing facing a further 50 basis point headwind as Adobe laps earlier Creative Cloud increases.

It cut net new ARR estimates for fiscal 2027 and 2028 by roughly $470 million and $500 million, to $1.5 billion and $1.35 billion, taking total ARR growth to 5.3% and 4.5% year-over-year, 200 to 300 basis points below Street estimates.

Citi also lowered its fiscal 2027 non-GAAP gross margin estimate by 70 basis points to reflect unmonetized AI inference costs, and sees sharply lower revenue in fiscal 2028 alongside modest margin degradation.

Wall Street analysts downgrade HubSpot on weak Q4 outlook

Four Wall Street firms have downgraded HubSpot after the software company's weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter outlook pointed to a worsening demand environment.

HubSpot's third-quarter revenue grew 17% at constant currency, a 2-point beat, but it guided fourth-quarter growth to 12%, below consensus of 13.8%. Management said budget scrutiny, price sensitivity and longer sales cycles had become more pronounced and are likely to persist into 2027.

The company added 5,300 net new customers in the quarter, below the 5,600 expected, and now expects fewer than 5,000 in the fourth quarter, while net revenue retention slipped to 101% from 103% a year ago.

BTIG cut HubSpot to Neutral from Buy and lowered its 2027 growth forecast to 11% from 14%. Analyst Nick Altmann said the stock looks appropriately valued at about 10 times 2027 estimated free cash flow.

KeyBanc downgraded the stock to Sector Weight. "We recognize this is late, but we believe there is little room for improvement between now and when we get formal 2027 guidance next February and are downgrading to Sector Weight," analyst Jackson Ader wrote.

Cantor downgraded HubSpot to Underweight with a $170 price target. Analyst Matthew VanVliet said the company's new European pricing effectively amounts to a price cut and that its AI tools are underperforming peers.

"We no longer see HUBS as a premier SaaS asset that deserves the benefit of the doubt," he said.

Separately, Morgan Stanley also cut HubSpot to Equal-weight from Overweight and trimmed its price target to $229 from $287.

news.Title: Airbnb Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates as Booking Demand Accelerates
news.Content:
Airbnb ABNB reported third-quarter 2026 GAAP earnings of $3.16 per share, up 43% year over year from $2.21 in the year-ago quarter. The figure surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 10.49%.

Revenues increased 18.9% year over year to $4.87 billion, beating the consensus mark by 2.52%. Growth was driven by strong nights stayed and a moderate increase in Average Daily Rate (ADR). Nights and Seats Booked increased 16% year over year to 155 million, reflecting accelerating travel demand across all regions.

ABNB Booking Trends Gain Momentum

Gross Booking Value (GBV) increased 21% year over year to $27.7 billion, both on a reported and foreign-exchange-neutral basis. ADR reached $179, increasing 4% year over year and 5% excluding foreign-exchange effects.

Mobile adoption remained a key growth driver. Nights booked through Airbnb's app increased 29% year over year and represented 66% of total nights booked, up from 62%. Growth among first-time bookers accelerated to 13%, the highest level since early 2022.

Airbnb, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Airbnb, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Airbnb, Inc. Quote

Nights and Seats Booked benefited from a 3% net lift from the expansion of Reserve Now, Pay Later. Excluding this impact, bookings grew approximately 13%, reflecting continued underlying travel demand.

Airbnb Sees Broad-Based Regional Strength

North America recorded low-double-digit growth in Nights and Seats Booked, its fastest expansion in four years. EMEA delivered mid-teens growth, supported by improving demand across major European markets.

Latin America and Asia Pacific each reported more than 20% growth in Nights and Seats Booked. Brazil's origin net nights booked increased more than 30%, while India posted growth exceeding 60%.

Expansion markets continued gaining momentum, with origin net nights booked growing at their fastest pace in nearly three years. India's first-time bookers increased more than 80%, while Japan recorded approximately 35% growth.

ABNB's Profitability Improves on Operating Leverage

Total costs and expenses increased 15.3% year over year to $2.85 billion from $2.47 billion. However, costs represented approximately 58.5% of revenues compared with 60.3% in the year-ago quarter. Product development expenses, as a percentage of revenues, declined approximately 70 basis points (bps), while sales and marketing expenses increased about 5 bps. Operations and support and general and administrative expenses, as a percentage of revenues, decreased approximately 84 bps and 30 bps, respectively.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 22.3% year over year to $2.51 billion. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 52% from 50%.

Operating income increased 24.4% year over year to $2.02 billion, while operating margin expanded approximately 180 basis points to 41.5%.

Story Continues

Airbnb's AI Push Strengthens Operating Efficiency

Airbnb continued integrating artificial intelligence (AI) across its platform to improve guest experiences, host productivity and customer support. The company introduced more than 50 products and features during the quarter, nearly 70% more than a year earlier.

ABNB's AI assistant, available in more than 50 languages, helped resolve approximately 40% of all customer support issues without human intervention, up from roughly one-third in the preceding quarter. Customer support cost per booking declined more than 17% year over year.

Airbnb also introduced AI-powered search, listing summaries, comparison tools and dynamic pricing capabilities. The company is developing a specialized AI travel agent designed to help guests plan and book trips, with an initial rollout expected in the first half of 2027.

Meanwhile, Airbnb expanded its hotel offerings to thousands of boutique and independent properties across more than 60 destinations. Hotels continued growing faster than the core homes business, creating additional opportunities for customer acquisition.

ABNB Maintains Strong Cash Generation

Airbnb ended Sept. 30, 2026, with $12.6 billion in cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments and restricted cash.

Net cash provided by operating activities increased 11.2% year over year to $1.51 billion. Free cash flow increased 5.7% year over year to $1.43 billion, representing a 29% margin.

Trailing-12-month free cash flow reached $4.90 billion, reflecting a 35% margin. Reserve Now, Pay Later continued affecting working capital by shifting guest payments closer to the stay date.

Airbnb repurchased approximately $700 million of common stock during the quarter. The company also announced a new $12 billion share repurchase authorization, supplementing the $2.7 billion remaining under its existing program.

Airbnb Raises Its 2026 Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Airbnb expects revenues between $3.22 billion and $3.28 billion, implying year-over-year growth of 16-18%, including an approximately 2-percentage-point foreign-exchange benefit.

Management anticipates mid-teens GBV growth, supported by at least low-double-digit growth in Nights and Seats Booked and a modest increase in ADR.

Adjusted EBITDA is expected to increase year over year, although adjusted EBITDA margin is projected to decline slightly due partly to the timing of marketing expenditures.

For 2026, Airbnb raised its revenue growth outlook to the high teens from at least the mid-teens. The company also increased its adjusted EBITDA margin expectation to approximately 36% from at least 35.5%, reflecting stronger revenue growth and operating leverage.

news.Title: QNT Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Surge Y/Y, Stock Rises
news.Content:
Quantinuum Inc. QNT reported an adjusted loss of 29 cents per share for the third quarter of 2026. This compares to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of a loss of 38 cents.

Revenues surged 233% year over year to $9.1 million, driven by strength in cloud platform services and research-related activities. The consensus mark for the metric was pegged at $8.15 million.

Following the announcement yesterday, QNT shares gained 2.7% in the after-market session.

QNT's Cloud Business Drives Revenue Growth

Quantinuum benefited from growing demand for its quantum computing platform, with government customers contributing the majority of quarterly revenues. Enterprise customers also represented a significant share, while customer concentration improved.

Commercial momentum extended across financial services, chemicals and pharmaceuticals. The company secured its largest cloud agreement to date, involving a multi-year commitment from a leading global financial institution for access to its quantum systems through the Apollo generation.

Quantinuum Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Quantinuum Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Quantinuum Inc. Quote

QNT also expanded its distribution network through a new agreement with a leading hyperscaler. Its partnership with Oracle progressed with the launch of a beta program supporting hybrid quantum computing and artificial intelligence applications.

Quantinuum's Bookings Strengthen Revenue Visibility

The company's year-to-date bookings reached approximately $104 million, reflecting growing commercial commitments across its customer base. Management expects full-year bookings to exceed $120 million.

Quantinuum also expanded engagements with Johnson & Johnson to explore quantum computing applications in cancer therapy materials and GE Vernova to advance research into superconducting materials. A collaboration with Abu Dhabi Maritime Academy and Quincus targets maritime logistics applications.

Management highlighted broader customer engagement across governments, national laboratories, universities and enterprises. These relationships support future revenue opportunities as customers develop applications for successive generations of quantum computing systems.

QNT's Rising Expenses Pressure Profitability

The adjusted cost of revenues, which excludes stock-based compensation and depreciation and amortization, totaled $2.3 million in the third quarter of 2026. Adjusted gross margin expanded 853 basis points (bps) to 74.6%, benefiting from revenue growth and a favorable cloud business mix.

Story Continues

Research and development expenses surged 130% year over year to $97.5 million. Sales and marketing expenses increased 273.5% year over year to $14.9 million, while general and administrative expenses jumped 315.2% to $22.1 million.

Adjusted EBITDA loss widened 77.8% year over year to $80.5 million. Total stock-based compensation amounted to $37.2 million during the quarter.

QNT's Financial Details

Quantinuum ended the third quarter of 2026 with cash and cash equivalents of $1.94 billion compared with $762.6 million as of Dec. 31, 2025. The company had no debt, providing financial flexibility to support quantum computing development, manufacturing expansion and commercialization efforts.

Net cash used in operating activities totaled $229.9 million during the first nine months of 2026 compared with $96.9 million in the year-ago period.

Quantinuum Raises Its 2026 Revenue Outlook

Quantinuum raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $31-$34 million from its previous projection of $28-$32 million, reflecting stronger commercial execution and increasing demand across customer categories. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 revenues is currently pegged at $30.1 million.

Management also reiterated expectations for revenue growth exceeding 100% in 2027, supported by bookings, backlog and anticipated contract revenue recognition.

Our Take

Quantinuum delivered encouraging third-quarter 2026 results, with a narrower-than-expected loss and revenues surpassing estimates. Strong demand for cloud-based quantum computing services and research-related activities drove robust revenue growth. The company's expanding commercial relationships, including its largest-ever cloud agreement and growing partnerships with hyperscalers, strengthened its growth prospects.

The company's solid bookings momentum and expanding customer base across government and enterprise markets provide greater visibility into future revenues. Supported by these developments, management raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance and maintained expectations for more than 100% revenue growth in 2027, which is encouraging.

However, rising research and development spending, higher operating expenses and widening adjusted EBITDA losses remain concerns.
