news.Title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Micron (MU) Next?
news.Content:
In a similar fashion to the last few years, artificial intelligence (AI) stocks have brought more market-beating gains in 2026. Few have performed as well as Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU). As of this writing (Nov. 5), Micron stock has gained 138% year to date -- making it the fifth-best-performing stock in the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC).

Micron's rally has been fueled by unrelenting demand for memory chips, which have become important components of AI data centers. With Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) recently announcing a stock split, investors may be wondering whether Micron could follow suit.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

I think Micron's latest capital allocation decisions suggest management has other priorities.

Why has Micron stock soared in 2026?

Micron's success can be traced to accelerating demand for dynamic random-access memory (DRAM). DRAM temporarily stores information that computers need to access. Unlike long-term storage, which preserves files and information even when a device is off, DRAM helps processors retrieve data while applications are running.

This is especially important for generative AI models, which need to process vast amounts of information at high speeds. Micron also manufactures high bandwidth memory (HBM), a specialized form of DRAM optimized for moving data between memory and advanced AI accelerators, including Nvidia GPUs.

As the hyperscalers build data centers, demand for both conventional DRAM and HBM has surged. However, adding additional memory isn't something suppliers can do easily. Building new manufacturing facilities and expanding production capacity require time and capital.

In addition, producing HBM consumes manufacturing resources that would otherwise be used for conventional DRAM. This has resulted in tight supply across the AI memory market, benefiting manufacturers such as Micron by allowing them to charge higher prices.

Sandisk's stock split raises an interesting question

Micron isn't the only memory company enjoying a record year. Sandisk, which specializes in NAND flash memory used for data storage, is also benefiting from demand for AI infrastructure. To date, Sandisk stock has gained 252% in 2026, making it the S&P 500's second-best performing stock.

On Oct. 29, Sandisk announced an 8-for-1 stock split , scheduled to take effect after the market closes on Nov. 19. Management explained that the split would make its shares more accessible to retail investors and employees.

Story Continues

It's important to understand how stock splits work. Let's say an investor owned one share of Sandisk stock worth $1,200 before the split. Once the split goes into effect, you would own eight shares worth $150 each afterward. Notice how the value of the investment doesn't change.

Given Micron's similar performance, it's understandable to wonder whether management might pursue the same strategy. After all, Micron stock surpassed $1,200 earlier this year, potentially making individual shares prohibitive for retail investors without access to fractional-share trading.

Why Micron probably won't split its stock anytime soon

Micron has already announced a significant capital allocation initiative. On Oct. 8, the company's board of directors expanded its existing share repurchase authorization to $35.16 billion. Repurchases under the program may begin on Dec. 9.

That specific date is important. Micron's CHIPS Act funding agreements impose restrictions on share repurchases during the first two years. Beginning Dec. 9, a different set of conditions applies, including limitations and uses around free cash flow.

Of course, a stock split and buyback program aren't mutually exclusive. Sandisk has pursued both. Nevertheless, Micron's upsized repurchase authorization gives investors a more direct financial development to monitor.

In addition, Micron's share price has declined considerably in recent trading sessions. Following the midterm elections, semiconductor stocks have experienced meaningful drawdowns amid concerns about the outlook for AI infrastructure spending.

MU data by YCharts

Micron now trades around $682, down 44% from its all-time high. This pullback now makes Micron stock considerably less expensive than it was just a few weeks ago. This lowers one of the practical arguments for splitting the stock.

While I wouldn't rule out a Micron stock split at some point, I don't think investors should expect an announcement simply because Sandisk recently approved one. For now, I'd focus on Micron's ability to sustain its earnings momentum rather than speculate about an impending stock split.

news.Title: Stock market today: Nasdaq, S&P 500 rebound after brutal sell-off as US adds 165K jobs
news.Content:
US stocks stabilized on Friday after a post-election rally turned into an artificial intelligence trade meltdown, sending tremors through markets. Investors also assessed a hotter-than-expected October jobs report.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) rose 0.1%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 1%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) gained 1.9% after the tech-heavy index slipped into a correction on Thursday.

The major indexes were on track to post substantial losses during the volatile election week that saw the Democrats retake the House and Senate . At the center of Thursday's deep sell-off, which erased $2.3 trillion in market value, were concerns about a slowdown in data center construction and in AI spending.

The hit chip stocks like Nvidia ( NVDA ), Micron ( MU ), AMD ( AMD ), and Sandisk ( SNDK ) most directly, but also spilled into broader markets, sending the VIX Volatility Index ( ^VIX ) up 70% to 28.

Oil prices have also been in play, with global benchmark Brent crude ( BZ=F ) and WTI crude ( CL=F ) futures falling below $100 per barrel. Energy traders continue to assess the outlook for the war in the Middle East, with the potential for a reescalation weighing on sentiment.

Not to be overshadowed, the Labor Department reported that the US added 165,000 jobs in October , above a revised 60,000 figure the month before and the 65,000 jobs economists expected.

LIVE 10 updates

31 mins ago Ines Ferré

Nvidia, AMD, and Micron stocks lead chip sector higher following worst sell-off since 2020

Chip stocks rebounded on Friday after suffering their worst sell-off since 2020. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) bounced 4% following a 12% plunge on Thursday.

Shares of US chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) jumped nearly 6%, erasing part of their 10% slide in the prior session. AMD ( AMD ) also rebounded 8% after suffering a 17% fall. Nvidia ( NVDA ), which declined 9% in the prior session, jumped 6%.

Semiconductors bounced back after much of the AI trade was hammered on Thursday as investors digested what a Democratic win in Congress means for the data center build-out in the US.

Memory and storage names Sandisk ( SNDK ), Micron Technology ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) shares tumbled alongside Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) following Thursday's wipeout on Wall Street.

58 mins ago David Hollerith

Stocks stabilize as tech claws back some losses

US stocks were mixed at Friday's open as investors looked for more signs that market conditions have stabilized after Thursday's sharp AI-led sell-off.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.9%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.4%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) rose more than 1.4%.

Technology shares attempted to rebound after Thursday's rout, which pushed the Nasdaq back into correction territory and erased much of Wednesday's post-election rally.

Investors were also parsing the October jobs report for clues on whether the labor market remains strong enough to keep another Federal Reserve rate hike in play.

Today at 1:58 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Blockbuster October jobs report keeps Fed rate hike in play for December

Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger reports:

A much stronger-than-expected October jobs report solidifies expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December, as officials are already focused on higher inflation.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics report released Friday showed that 165,000 jobs were created in October , compared with expectations for around 70,000, as the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, compared with expectations for 4.2%. That's much higher than the average monthly gain of 48,000 over the past 12 months and well above the roughly 30,000 jobs needed to hold employment steady. Labor force participation inched up to a hair above expectations at 61.9%.

Job gains in both August and September were also revised higher by 84,000. The bulk of jobs added were in the sectors of professional and business services, healthcare, and transportation and warehousing. Manufacturing added 19,000 jobs.

Today at 1:38 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

US adds 165K jobs, blowing past expectations

The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, a jump from the revised job growth of 60,000 the month before. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expected the economy to have added 65,000 jobs.

The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%. Wage growth increased 0.4% from September.

Today at 1:24 PM UTC Brian Sozzi

The VIX volatility index just spiked 70%. Here's what history suggests comes next.

If you are looking for something positive after Thursday's shocking stock beatdown , you have come to the right place ahead of the weekend.

History suggests stocks tend to do well after the extreme volatility we saw two days removed from the Election Day blue wave.

The VIX volatility index ( ^VVIX ) — better known as Wall Street's fear gauge — jumped as much as 70% on Thursday. A move this large has only happened eight times since 1991, according to data from CBOE.

Here's what happened to the S&P 500 on average after the eight prior extreme moves:

1 month later: +3.0% (7 of 8 times positive)

3 months later: +7.1% (6 of 8 times positive)

6 months later: +10.4% (8 of 8 times positive)

1 year later: +14.7% (7 of 8 times positive)

Today at 12:37 PM UTC David Hollerith

Wall Street is overreacting to data center backlash, Yardeni says

The stock market's Thursday rout in artificial intelligence boom trade may have been an overreaction to growing political opposition to data center construction, according to one prominent bull.

AI and chip stocks plunged Thursday as major indexes erased their post-midterm election rally. One key worry is that about 45% of planned US data center capacity faces possible restrictions after tallying newly elected state governors who have promised to stop or pause construction, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

But Yardeni Research is calling those mounting restrictions a setback.

"We view the political backlash as another constraint on AI investment, alongside financial and physical bottlenecks. But these are speed bumps, not roadblocks, even though Wall Street seems to be pricing in the latter," Yardeni Research wrote in a Friday note to clients.

"We think that's overdone," the strategists said, referring to Thursday's sell-off as a "buying opportunity." The firm is sticking with its year-end target of 7,900 on the S&P 500.

Yardeni pointed to Texas, a major data center hub, where newly elected governor Gina Hinojosa said Thursday afternoon in a CNN interview that already permitted projects would be allowed to finish construction.

The distinction matters. Permitted data center projects account for "essentially all of Texas's planned data center capacity in 2027 and likely much of 2028," according to Yardeni.

Today at 12:00 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Friday's jobs report is expected to show the labor market chugging along

Employment data scheduled for release on Friday is expected to show the labor market remains steady. Yahoo Finance's Claire Boston previews what to expect from today's jobs report:

Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect that the economy added 65,000 jobs in October, an improvement from September's underwhelming 29,000 additions. The unemployment rate is expected to hold steady at 4.2%, while wage growth is seen improving 0.3% from September.

Those numbers would be consistent with the "low hire, low fire" environment that has defined the labor market for the past several years. While few companies are hiring aggressively, most aren't conducting major layoffs either.

Recent initial jobless claims have looked "exceptionally benign by historical standards," Bank of America economist Shruti Mishra wrote in a note.

"Despite recent high-profile layoff announcements, the absence of any pickup in claims suggests economy-wide layoffs remain contained," she added.

Today at 11:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Tesla's EV arc could be a blueprint for the post-data center backlash

Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban writes:

When President Trump and his allies in Congress moved to end the EV subsidy, automakers braced for a crash in electric car sales. Tesla ( TSLA ), the US leader, was especially vulnerable because it didn't have gas-powered vehicles to lean on, and keeping prices as low as possible was crucial to competing with EV rivals.

But those initial worries gave way to optimism.

In a new regulatory environment, one that was more hostile to EVs, Tesla used the disappearing $7,500 tax break as an advantage . It lost a valuable subsidy, but used its scale to win a war of attrition, thereby consolidating the market. Other firms needed the subsidy even more, and though Tesla got hurt, the damage was less than its peers' in many ways.

On top of that, a new barrier to entry was in place, and Tesla's competitive moat got wider.

That's a roadmap for how Big Tech could navigate the data center backlash. And it helps explain why many investors are bullish on hyperscaler stocks despite a nationwide referendum against data centers and notable victories from candidates opposing them .

Today at 10:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell

Airbnb 'back in growth mode,' CEO says after strong quarter. Stock jumps after hours.

Airbnb ( ABNB ) stock jumped after hours after the peer-to-peer home rental company touted strong growth across its business and raised its full-year outlook amid healthy global travel demand.

"Airbnb is back in growth mode," CEO Brian Chesky said in a release to investors. "It's rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that's exactly what we're doing. In Q3, we delivered our fastest revenue growth in more than three years, with acceleration across our business, including our most established markets."

In the third quarter, Airbnb reported earnings per share of $3.16, surpassing Wall Street analyst estimates of $2.85 per share, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data. Revenue grew 19% to $4.87 billion, also beating estimates of $4.74 billion.

"In North America, nights booked grew at their fastest pace in four years," the company said. "We're also seeing more guests return to Airbnb, and more people try it for the first time."

The strength of the company's quarter led it to raise its guidance for the remainder of the year.

In the fourth quarter, Airbnb expects revenue to grow 16%-19% to a range of $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion, exceeding the Street's midpoint estimate of $3.16 billion.

For the full year, Airbnb forecasts revenue growth in the high teens and adjusted EBITDA margins to increase to approximately 36%.

news.Title: AAOI Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Datacenter and CATV Sales
news.Content:
Applied Optoelectronics AAOI reported third-quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings of 17 cents per share against a loss of 9 cents in the year-ago quarter. The metric beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 21.43%.

Revenues surged 127.5% year over year to $269.88 million and topped the consensus mark by 0.27%. The topline benefited from robust datacenter and CATV demand. Datacenter revenues more than tripled year over year, supported by accelerating 800G optical transceiver shipments, while CATV revenues reached a record high.

AAOI Datacenter Sales Surge on 800G Demand

Datacenter revenues reached $155.61 million, up 254.2% year over year and 44.5% sequentially. The business accounted for approximately 58% of total revenues, supported by growing demand for high-speed optical connectivity products used in AI infrastructure.

800G revenues reached $47.5 million, nearly quadrupling sequentially from $12.8 million.

Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. Quote

Meanwhile, 400G revenues rose to $93.4 million from $48.4 million in the preceding quarter. However, 800G growth fell short of management's expectations as a major hyperscale customer shifted demand toward 1.6T products faster than anticipated.

Applied Optoelectronics CATV Sales Hit Record High

CATV revenues reached a record $110.88 million, increasing 57.0% year over year and 37.6% sequentially. The figure slightly exceeded management's guidance range of $100 million to $110 million.

The company continued shipping significant volumes of 1.8 GHz amplifiers to its largest CATV customer and reached the milestone of shipping its millionth amplifier. Management also highlighted positive customer responses to its newer broadband technologies, including QuantumWave modules and QuantumLink software.

AAOI Margins Face Product Mix Pressure

In the third quarter of 2026, non-GAAP gross margin was 28.7%, down 230 basis points (bps) year over year and 110 bps sequentially. The metric fell slightly below management's guidance of 29% to 30.5%, primarily reflecting a higher proportion of lower-margin 400G products.

Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 49.3% year over year to $70.3 million. Research and development expenses rose 79.2% to $37.5 million, while sales and marketing expenses declined 23.1% to $7.4 million. General and administrative expenses increased 53.4% to $25.3 million.

Non-GAAP operating income reached $7.2 million against an operating loss of $10.3 million in the year-ago quarter. Management continues to target non-GAAP gross margins of approximately 40% over the longer term.

Story Continues

Applied Optoelectronics Expands Manufacturing Capacity

Total manufacturing capacity approached 330,000 units per month, up from approximately 200,000 units at the end of the second quarter. Management now expects installed equipment capacity for 800G and 1.6T products to exceed 500,000 units monthly by year-end, below its previous target of 650,000 units.

The company expects capacity to exceed 1 million units monthly by the end of 2027. However, its second-phase U.S. expansion faces delays related to electrical power availability and construction issues. Initial operations at its new 210,000-square-foot Sugar Land facility are expected to begin in December.

AAOI Secures Major Hyperscale Customer Agreement

Applied Optoelectronics signed a multiyear agreement with an existing Tier 1 hyperscale data center customer covering 1.6T transceivers. Management expects the agreement to generate between $1 billion and $1.5 billion in revenues over three years, depending on customer demand and supply availability.

The customer committed to purchasing at least 10% of its required 1.6T transceivers from AAOI, subject to certain conditions. Management expects 1.6T shipments to begin contributing to revenues in the fourth quarter, although digital signal processor availability remains a near-term constraint.

Applied Optoelectronics Balance Sheet Supports Growth

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $621.46 million, up from $508.76 million at the end of June 30, 2026.

The company made approximately $501 million in capital investments during the quarter, including $142.8 million in equipment prepayments. These investments primarily supported manufacturing expansion for 400G, 800G, and 1.6T products.

AAOI Offers Strong Fourth-Quarter Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Applied Optoelectronics expects revenues between $385 million and $420 million. Datacenter revenues are projected to be between $270 million and $300 million, while CATV revenues are expected to be between $105 million and $115 million.

Non-GAAP gross margin is projected to be between 29.5% and 31%. Non-GAAP net income is expected to be between $45.9 million and $60.4 million, translating into earnings of 48 cents to 63 cents per share based on approximately 96 million diluted shares.

AAOI's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

Applied Optoelectronics currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Some better-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector include Cisco Systems CSCO, Analog Devices ADI and NVIDIA NVDA. Each stock presently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Cisco Systems shares have gained 24.3% year to date. Cisco Systems is set to report first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 12.

Shares of Analog Devices have risen 33.2% year to date. Analog Devices is set to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 24.

NVIDIA shares have lost 2.6% year to date. NVIDIA is set to report third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 17.

news.Title: What AirSculpt Technologies (AIRS) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in AirSculpt Technologies, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

AirSculpt cut its 2026 outlook after Q3 revenue fell 8.7% to $31.9 million and adjusted EBITDA dropped to about $400,000. It now expects revenue of $144 million–$146 million and adjusted EBITDA of $9 million–$10 million.

Marketing challenges, including Google AI Overviews reducing website referrals, contributed to a 16% decline in leads and a 26% increase in cost per lead. Case volume fell 9.6%, while operational issues at several centers also weighed on results.

The company completed a refinancing that extends debt maturity to 2031, though at a higher interest rate, and ended the quarter with roughly $20 million in liquidity. GLP-1-related procedures accounted for nearly 10% of cases, which management sees as a potential longer-term growth opportunity.

AirSculpt Technologies (NASDAQ:AIRS) lowered its full-year revenue and profit outlook after third-quarter sales fell 8.7%, as fewer potential patients reached its website and several centers experienced operational problems.

The body-contouring company reported revenue of $31.9 million for the quarter. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization fell to approximately $400,000 from $3 million a year earlier.

→ Apple's Earnings Beat Comes With a Catch for Investors Heading Into the Holidays

Chief Executive Officer Yogi Jashnani called the results disappointing, saying performance fell short of the company's goals because of lower productivity from marketing investments and underperformance at a handful of clinics. Management said its revised outlook assumes the challenges seen in the third quarter continue through the fourth.

Search changes weigh on patient leads

Jashnani attributed much of the marketing difficulty to Google's AI Overviews, which he said increasingly keep consumers on Google's platform rather than directing them to AirSculpt's website. Leads fell 16% from a year earlier, while cost per lead rose 26%, he said.

→ Amazon Has Erased Its Earnings Sell-Off, But Is the Biggest Opportunity Still Ahead?

The CEO said search intent for aesthetic procedures remained relatively stable and that conversion rates held steady once prospective patients engaged with AirSculpt. Responding to an analyst's question about the economy, Jashnani said the consumer environment remained "choppy" and that the company's generally higher-income customers were not completely insulated.

AirSculpt is working to improve its visibility in AI-generated search results and is expanding local and community marketing. Jashnani said the company was seeing early signs of improvement, but that it would take time for those efforts to show up in revenue.

Story Continues

→ Palantir's $2.3 Billion Quarter Puts Its Premium Valuation to the Test

The company plans to host an open house across all 31 centers on November 12, combining in-person and virtual education with the goal of generating consultations and bookings. It also expects to spend an incremental $3 million on brand marketing compared with last year, down from the $5 million increase it previously anticipated.

Lower volume drives guidance cut

On a same-center basis, excluding the closed London location, third-quarter revenue declined approximately 7.5%. Case volume fell 9.6%, partly offset by a 2.3% increase in average selling price. The average price was approximately $12,900, Chief Financial Officer Michael Arthur said.

Gross margin expanded to roughly 60% from 57.5% a year earlier, reflecting operating efficiencies, cost discipline and the benefit of closing the London center. Selling, general and administrative expenses rose approximately $700,000 to $20.3 million, primarily because of higher marketing and professional expenses. Customer acquisition cost increased to roughly $3,800 per case from $3,100.

AirSculpt now expects full-year 2026 revenue of $144 million to $146 million , down from its previous forecast of $151 million to $157 million. It lowered its adjusted EBITDA outlook to $9 million to $10 million from $12 million to $14 million.

Arthur said fourth-quarter results will depend on how quickly the company adapts its marketing strategy and improves execution at the affected centers. Jashnani said the center-specific issues varied across marketing, sales and operations; some fixes were underway or complete, while others could take months.

GLP-1 procedures and refinancing

AirSculpt performed 250 procedures related to GLP-1 weight-loss medications during the quarter, representing nearly 10% of total cases. The offerings address concerns such as stubborn fat, loose skin and loss of volume. Jashnani said the services are available in almost all centers, although one or two are not offering them or are not doing so at scale.

The company believes procedures addressing GLP-1 side effects could represent a potential $100 million revenue opportunity across its existing centers over the longer term. Jashnani said patients seeking those procedures often require more education and a different marketing and sales approach; he did not provide a timeline for an acceleration in volume.

AirSculpt also completed a refinancing that extends its debt maturity to 2031. The new $44 million facility consists of a $39 million term loan and a $5 million revolving credit facility. Arthur said the interest rate is SOFR plus 775 basis points, about 300 basis points higher than under the previous facility, and will decline as leverage decreases.

The company ended the quarter with approximately $15 million in cash and $5 million available under its revolver, for total liquidity of roughly $20 million. Management said the refinancing provides more flexibility for investments and potential future center openings.

news.Title: TSMC rises on report of potential push into advanced memory for Nvidia
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) is evaluating an expansion into advanced memory chip production to capture a larger share of artificial intelligence infrastructure spending, according to a report from The Information. The initiative would mark a pivotal strategic evolution for the world's dominant contract chipmaker, which has traditionally focused on pure-play logic fabrication.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

ADRs of TSMC surged 7.7% in early trading Friday as investors weighed the prospect of the foundry giant deepening its role in the critical AI hardware supply chain. The Taiwanese manufacturer recently began formulating plans to produce vertically stacked 3D DRAM at the behest of its primary customer, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter cited by The Information.

A persistent bottleneck in memory availability has driven hardware costs sharply higher, prompting key buyers such as Nvidia and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) to actively seek alternative procurement channels. Apple, for its part, implemented price increases across its hardware portfolio earlier this year after absorbing substantial increases in memory procurement expenses.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

TSMC is examining whether to construct dedicated fabrication facilities or acquire and retool an existing site to support the specialized production, the report indicated. That latter path mirrors a maneuver by Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU), which in March agreed to purchase a Taiwan-based facility from Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. for $1.8 billion to retrofit for high-end memory.

The company's exploration is being spearheaded by Hsu Kuo-chin, a vice president directing TSMC's advanced packaging operations who previously ran Micron's regional footprint. His oversight underscores how intimately memory architecture has become linked with advanced packaging, the specialized process required to tether memory and processing units into cohesive computing systems.

Entering the memory arena would nonetheless expose TSMC to a notoriously volatile segment long dominated by Samsung Electronics (KS:005930), SK hynix Inc (NASDAQ:SKHY), and Micron. Memory markets are historically prone to severe boom-and-bust supply imbalances, and while TSMC holds proprietary patents around vertical DRAM, translating lab designs into defect-free volume manufacturing poses formidable execution hurdles.

Story Continues

The strategic shift also introduces delicate competitive dynamics, particularly following TSMC's 2024 pact to manufacture base logic dies for SK Hynix's next-generation high-bandwidth memory products. For global markets, however, TSMC's willingness to contemplate heavy capital outlays in memory signals durable confidence in the longevity of the AI infrastructure cycle.

news.Title: Is Qualcomm Stock Worth Buying After Mixed Q4 Results?
news.Content:
QUALCOMM Incorporated QCOM reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 non-GAAP earnings of $2.17 per share, down 28% year over year from $3. Non-GAAP revenues declined 7% to $10.44 billion from $11.27 billion in the year-ago quarter, but came in near the upper end of management's guidance range.

Handset Weakness Weighs on QCT Performance

Qualcomm CDMA Technologies (QCT) revenues declined 8% year over year to $9.02 billion. Handset revenues plunged 26% to $5.14 billion from $6.96 billion, indicating sluggish smartphone demand, elevated memory prices and the ongoing reduction in Apple modem shipments.

Management indicated that the June quarter marked the bottom for its China Android business, with revenues recovering sequentially in the September quarter. However, Qualcomm expects global handset shipments to remain flat to slightly lower in calendar 2027, reflecting continued uncertainty in smartphone demand.

Qualcomm's Automotive Business Gains Momentum

Automotive revenues jumped 89% to $1.99 billion from $1.05 billion in the prior-year quarter, driven by increasing adoption of integrated compute modules and fifth-generation Snapdragon Digital Chassis platforms. Higher semiconductor content per vehicle and the conversion of design wins into commercial shipments supported the strong performance.

Qualcomm exited fiscal 2026 with an automotive annualized revenue run rate of approximately $8 billion, exceeding its previous $7 billion expectation. Meanwhile, IoT revenues increased 4% year over year to $1.89 billion, supported by 20% growth in industrial, networking and robotics products, partly offset by memory-related constraints in consumer devices.

Combined automotive and IoT revenues climbed 36% to approximately $3.88 billion, highlighting progress in Qualcomm's efforts to diversify beyond smartphones.

Higher Costs Pressure Qualcomm's Margins

QCT earnings before taxes (EBT) declined 26% year over year to $2.14 billion, while EBT margin contracted 500 basis points to 24%. Lower handset revenues and rising semiconductor manufacturing costs weighed on profitability despite strong automotive sales.

Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL) revenues fell 7% to $1.3 billion, while EBT decreased 10% to $918 million. The segment's EBT margin narrowed to 70% from 72% a year earlier.

Companywide GAAP research and development expenses increased 13% to $2.68 billion, reflecting continued investments in advanced semiconductor technologies and growth initiatives. Selling, general and administrative expenses rose 6% to $963 million.

Qualcomm is implementing product price increases to offset higher input costs across wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, advanced packaging and memory. Management expects the full benefit of these pricing actions to materialize in the second half of fiscal 2027.

Qualcomm remains exposed to customer insourcing and competition in premium mobile and adjacent compute markets. The company is venturing into the data center market. But it faces strong competition from established players, such as Intel Corporation INTC and Advanced Micro Devices AMD.

Story Continues

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Price Performance

Qualcomm shares have declined 8.3% over the past year against the industry's growth of 5.6%, lagging peers Intel and AMD. While Intel has gained 37%, AMD surged 73.2% over this period.

Estimate Revision Trend for QCOM

Earnings estimates for Qualcomm for fiscal 2026 have moved down 0.5% to $10.02 over the past 60 days, while the same for fiscal 2027 has declined 2.7% to $12.36. The negative estimate revision depicts bearish sentiment for the stock.

End Note

Qualcomm carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Despite strong automotive momentum and promising opportunities in AI data centers, the company's near-term performance remains pressured by declining handset revenues, reduced Apple modem shipments and elevated semiconductor input costs. Moreover, increasing investments in AI infrastructure and the expansion of relatively lower-gross-margin custom silicon operations could constrain profitability in fiscal 2027. Although Qualcomm's diversification initiatives offer long-term growth potential, persistent smartphone market weakness and margin headwinds warrant a cautious stance on the stock.

news.Title: Datadog's Infrastructure Monitoring Tops $2B ARR in Q3, Revenues Beat
news.Content:
Datadog, Inc. DDOG reported third-quarter 2026 revenues of $1.197 billion, which increased 35% year over year and came above the high end of its guided range. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.82%. Although Datadog reports as a single segment, its Infrastructure Monitoring suite, the first product it launched more than a decade ago, remained a cornerstone of the quarter's performance.

Infrastructure Monitoring annual recurring revenue (ARR) now exceeds $2 billion and is growing in the mid-30s percentage range year over year. The suite covers cloud infrastructure, on-premise servers, containers, serverless applications and GPU fleets, placing it at the center of cloud migration and AI deployments. Management noted that the acceleration was broad-based rather than driven solely by AI initiatives, with revenue growth from non-AI customers accelerating for the fifth straight quarter to the high-20s percentage range.

GPU monitoring has emerged as a key growth vector within the suite. The number of GPU devices monitored has risen eightfold so far in 2026, and new capabilities now extend beyond hardware reliability to help customers maximize fleet utilization and lower inference cost per request. However, management clarified that Infrastructure Monitoring growth is not directly tied to GPUs, as these products are not yet widely monetized.

Adjacent Cloud Cost Management also gained meaningful traction. More than one-third of its customers now track AI costs, with the number of such customers up more than 11 times. Beyond the three major cloud providers, AI providers have become the largest category of spend that customers monitor.

Infrastructure Monitoring's role as an entry point continues to support platform adoption. At quarter-end, 61% of customers used four or more products, up from 54% a year ago, while 16% used 10 or more, up from 8%. Datadog ended the quarter with about 33,500 customers, while about 4,860 customers with ARR of $100,000 or more generated roughly 91% of ARR.

It is also expanding its government platform to support Impact Level 5 workloads and introduced Scout 1.0, its first specialized AI model, now powering Bits Investigation.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Datadog expects revenues of $1.19-$1.20 billion. Full-year 2026 revenues are projected to be between $4.515 billion and $4.525 billion. The guidance assumes only the minimum commitment from its largest customer, which reduced usage in the third quarter.

news.Title: Iren stock rebounds as company's Q1 AI cloud revenue surges
news.Content:
Iren ( IREN ) stock surged on Friday as the data center operator reported strong growth in its artificial intelligence cloud business in its fiscal first quarter.

Iren shares jumped as much as 19% in early trading Friday, rebounding from a roughly 17% decline in the previous session amid a broader sell-off in the AI trade . Despite the recovery, Iren shares remain down more than 50% year to date as investor concerns over AI infrastructure spending, financing requirements and data center expansion have weighed on the sector. The company, which has transitioned from bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) mining into AI cloud and data center infrastructure, has been particularly affected by the recent pullback in neocloud stocks.

Iren, whose customers include Microsoft ( MSFT ), reported $200 million in AI revenue during the three months ending Sept. 30, up from $71 million in the previous quarter and $7 million in the year-earlier period.

However, the company posted a quarterly loss of $263 million, wider than the average analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg.

Iren's AI Cloud gross margin of 86% came in line with the prior quarter.

Iren said it expanded an existing agreement with a leading frontier AI lab and separately signed a new five-year contract under which the customer prepaid approximately 90% of the associated GPU costs, reducing the need for additional debt financing.

The company also pushed back its timeline for reaching a $4 billion annualized revenue target, now expecting to hit the milestone in January or February, compared with its previous December forecast. The delay reflects supply constraints affecting critical equipment as well as a design change requested by Microsoft that has slowed development of a data center project in Texas.

news.Title: Sandisk Is Splitting Its Stock 8-for-1. Is Micron Technology Next?
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) recently released stunning results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (for the three months ended Oct. 2), which easily exceeded the market's expectations. Even better, the company's guidance for the current quarter is stronger than expected, suggesting that the favorable business conditions in the NAND flash storage market are sustainable.

Sandisk management also announced that it will execute an 8-for-1 forward stock split to "make stock more accessible, including to employees through its employee stock purchase plan." Sandisk will start trading on a split-adjusted basis from Nov. 20. But why has Sandisk made this move, and will fellow memory manufacturer Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) follow suit when it releases its results in December?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Let's find out.

Image source: Getty Images.

A stock split could give Sandisk a much-needed boost

I had noted in May this year that Sandisk is likely to opt for a stock split owing to its high share price. Though the stock has been under pressure lately, it has appreciated by more than 2,700% since it was spun off from Western Digital in February last year.

Each share of Sandisk trades at just over $1,000, as of this writing. The proposed stock split will bring down the price of each Sandisk share to around $125. However, the outstanding share count of the company will increase simultaneously, which means that the overall value of your Sandisk investment won't change.

For example, if you own 10 shares of Sandisk right now, you'd own 80 after the split is completed, though the price of each share will be lower. So, a stock split is just a cosmetic move that doesn't change a company's fundamentals. However, as management noted in the press release, a lower share price will make the stock "more accessible."

In simpler words, the lower per-share price increases the affordability of Sandisk stock, giving retail investors a better shot at buying it. The potential increase in demand for Sandisk stock once it starts trading on a split-adjusted basis could pave the way for more upside, especially considering its solid financial performance.

Its revenue in the previous quarter jumped nearly 5x from the year-ago period to just over $11 billion. Non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS), meanwhile, shot up by 40x year over year to $49.51. However, the stock fell more than 13% following its latest quarterly report, primarily due to a broader sell-off in tech stocks. What's worth noting is that Sandisk expects its terrific momentum to continue in the current quarter.

Story Continues

The company expects $55.00 in EPS on $12.4 billion in revenue. For comparison, it posted EPS of $6.20 and revenue of $3 billion in the year-ago period. Ideally, the stock should have surged following such phenomenal numbers, but that wasn't the case. But now that Sandisk will be accessible to a wider investor pool following its stock split, I won't be surprised to see it step on the gas once again.

That's precisely the reason why I think even Micron Technology management could opt for a stock split.

Here's why Micron could follow Sandisk and go for a stock split

Micron stock has surged nearly 1,000% over the past three years. As a result, each share of Micron now trades at almost $800, as of this writing. Just like Sandisk, even Micron has been delivering outstanding growth quarter after quarter, driven by strong memory demand.

The company's revenue in fiscal 2026 (which ended on Sept. 3) increased by 256% from the prior year to $133.2 billion. Adjusted EPS increased by over 9x from the year-ago period to $75.52. The incredible growth in Micron and Sandisk's revenue and earnings can be attributed to the artificial intelligence (AI)-fueled demand for memory chips.

Both dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and NAND flash storage are in short supply, as AI data centers have been consuming large numbers of these chips to store and transport huge amounts of data. Micron noted on its September earnings call that it expects "memory and storage supply-demand conditions to be much tighter in fiscal 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026."

However, Micron's shares are down 34% since reaching a 52-week high in June. So, a stock split could increase demand for Micron's shares by lowering the per-share price. Also, Micron's cheap valuation means that a more accessible share price could spur demand for the stock.

After all, Micron trades at just 4.6 times forward earnings, while the S&P 500 index has a forward earnings multiple of 19. As memory supply conditions tighten over the next couple of years, Micron will be able to sustain the impressive earnings growth it has been delivering. That's why I won't be surprised to see this semiconductor stock step on the gas once again, and a stock split announcement when it releases another set of solid quarterly results next month could trigger a bull run.

news.Title: Semtech Stock Plunges 34% in 3 Months: Should You Buy the Dip?
news.Content:
Semtech Corporation SMTC shares have plunged 34% in the past three months, underperforming the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry's decline of 2.6%. The stock also underperformed its industry peers, including Microchip Technology MCHP, ON Semiconductor ON and NXP Semiconductors NXPI. In the past three months, shares of NXP Semiconductors have returned 1.9%, while Microchip Technology and ON Semiconductor have plunged 25.2% and 22.4%, respectively.

3-Month Price Return Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Semtech's recent underperformance can be attributed to the broader weakness in AI and semiconductor stocks, weakness in its high-end consumer business and capacity constraints that could limit its ability to meet strong data center demand.

Growing concerns about elevated valuations, high data center spending and the ability of AI investments to generate adequate returns have weighed on investor sentiment toward the sector. As Semtech's growth prospects are closely linked to rising demand for AI data center connectivity products, weakness across semiconductor and AI-related stocks has put additional pressure on its shares, despite strong demand for its products.

Semtech's high-end consumer revenues declined 5% year over year to $39 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. The segment is benefiting from demand for its TVS protection products, particularly among premium handset manufacturers, where Semtech is expanding its content per device. However, these gains have not yet translated into year-over-year revenue growth. While the company expects a sequential recovery, supported by seasonal demand and market share gains in TVS products, continued weakness could limit growth outside its data center and industrial businesses.

Capacity constraints also pose a risk to Semtech's growth prospects. Strong demand for its data center products has resulted in a record backlog, but management indicated that secured manufacturing capacity may not be sufficient to meet demand in the second half of fiscal 2028. Although the company is working with manufacturing partners to expand production, delays in capacity additions could limit its ability to fulfill customer orders and capitalize on rising demand for 800G and 1.6T connectivity products.

SMTC's Premium Valuation Warrants a Cautious Approach

SMTC is currently trading at a higher price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple compared with the Zacks Computer and Technology sector. SMTC's forward 12-month P/E ratio sits at 19.01X, higher than the sector's forward 12-month P/E ratio of 17.33X. The Zacks Value Score of F also suggests that SMTC stock is overvalued.

Story Continues

SMTC Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio

SMTC stock also trades at a higher P/E multiple compared with other industry peers, including Microchip Technology, ON Semiconductor and NXP Semiconductors. At present, Microchip Technology, ON Semiconductor and NXP Semiconductors have P/E multiples of 17.96X, 16.58X and 14.76X, respectively.

However, for investors, not everything is gloom and doom.

Semtech's 1.6T Ramp to Drive Data Center Growth

Semtech is seeing strong demand for its data center products as hyperscalers increase spending on AI infrastructure. The company's data center revenues reached a record $100 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 39% sequentially and 91% year over year. Growth was driven by continued strength in 800G products, along with the ramp of 1.6T CopperEdge and FiberEdge solutions. Management expects this momentum to continue, with data center revenues projected to increase 45% sequentially and 160% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

The 1.6T transition could become an important growth driver for Semtech. Management expects 1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge products to account for more than 50% of total data center revenues in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Semtech is also gaining market share in optical connectivity, where its FiberEdge business has grown from about 18% market share in 800G two years ago to more than 50%. Further, the company expects its 1.6T FiberEdge market share to exceed 50% by the end of fiscal 2027.

The company is also preparing for the next stage of data center growth. Semtech is expanding its photonics portfolio through gain chips, high-power CW lasers, semiconductor optical amplifiers and photodiodes. These products are aimed at higher-speed applications, including 3.2T transceivers and co-packaged optics. Management expects its content per transceiver to increase from high single-digit dollars to high double-digit dollars as data center speeds move from 800G to 3.2T.

Strong customer demand supports SMTC's prospects as well, with the company reporting that its backlog for the remainder of fiscal 2027 was fully booked and more than 70% of its target for fiscal 2028 was already covered. Management is also working with manufacturing partners to secure additional capacity for fiscal 2028 and beyond. If it can meet customer requirements and maintain its product momentum, the 1.6T ramp could remain an important driver of Semtech's data center growth over the next several quarters.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SMTC's fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenues indicates year-over-year growth of 46.2% and 33.8%, respectively.

Strong LoRa Growth Boosts SMTC's Prospects

Semtech is seeing strong growth in its LoRa business as demand increases across industrial, commercial and consumer applications. LoRa-enabled net sales reached a record $58 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 31% sequentially and 58% year over year. Growth reflects wider adoption of LoRa across different applications, including smart homes, security systems and industrial monitoring. Management expects the business to maintain its momentum, with LoRa revenues projected to grow about 15% sequentially and 65% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

Semtech is expanding its LoRa portfolio to address more applications. Its LoRa Gen 4 platform supports higher data speeds while maintaining low power consumption and long-range connectivity. These features can support new uses in smart homes, security and industrial applications. For example, LoRa-enabled sensors can help monitor industrial equipment and support predictive maintenance. In public safety, the technology can also enable sensors to transmit audio for AI-based verification instead of sending simple alerts.

Amazon Sidewalk is another potential growth driver for Semtech's LoRa business. Following Ring's launch of a new range of LoRa-based sensors in the United States, Amazon Sidewalk is expanding internationally, starting with Canada and Mexico, while Europe, Australia and Japan are expected to follow. This expansion could help increase the use of LoRa-based devices in consumer applications through Amazon's network. Meanwhile, LoRa Plus is gaining traction in smart home and security markets, broadening the company's opportunities beyond traditional industrial and commercial use cases.

Strong momentum in LoRaWAN, LoRa Plus and Amazon Sidewalk can also support SMTC's future growth. Management expects LoRa revenues to grow at a rate above its previous 20% benchmark, supported by demand across these applications. With record revenues, new use cases and expanding distribution through Amazon Sidewalk, LoRa could become an increasingly important contributor to Semtech's overall growth.

SMTC's Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Upward Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SMTC's fiscal 2027 and 2028 earnings per share (EPS) implies year-over-year growth of 113.5% and 78.8%, respectively. EPS estimates for fiscal 2027 and 2028 have been revised upward by 4.9% and 15.8%, respectively, over the past 30 days.

Conclusion: Buy SMTC Stock Right Now

Semtech's near-term outlook faces some pressure from the broader selloff in AI and semiconductor stocks, declining high-end consumer revenues, an outstretched valuation and manufacturing capacity constraints. However, strong demand for 800G and 1.6T data center products, a fully booked backlog for the remainder of fiscal 2027 and growing adoption of LoRa solutions support the company's growth prospects. Rising demand for AI infrastructure, expansion into 3.2T connectivity products and strong upward earnings estimate revisions further support the company's outlook. These factors position Semtech for continued growth, making SMTC stock an attractive buy at current levels.

Currently, SMTC sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

news.Title: Berkshire’s Pivot to AI Bets Gets an Immediate Reality Check
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- In his first year as Chief Executive Officer of Berkshire Hathaway Inc., Greg Abel has pushed the conglomerate into an entirely new area of investment: artificial intelligence.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Rubio Weighs Leaving Administration After GOP's Midterm Loss

Morgan Stanley Offers $2.3 Billion Debt for Dell Family Deal

Hinojosa Seeks 'Balance' With Musk, Regulations in Blue Texas

S&P 500 Sinks 4% as AI Washout Rattles Wall Street: Markets Wrap

Democrats Clinch Huge Wins on Inflation Anger, Trump Fatigue

In a significant departure from Warren Buffett's famous reservations about technology stocks, the new CEO started cutting checks soon after he took on the job. In just a few months, he handed $10 billion to Google parent Alphabet Inc. to support its AI-related investments and plowed another $930 million into Bending Spoons SpA, an Italian conglomerate that uses the technology to transform businesses.

But with cracks in the AI trade starting to show, Berkshire's sudden push may appear ill-timed.

"I do think that part of this may be a conscious decision to increase their exposure," said Cathy Seifert, an analyst for CFRA Research. "One has to ask the question though, is it a little late?"

Since June, Alphabet's Class A and Class C shares have tumbled more than 24% and are now trading below the discounted price at which Berkshire acquired them — prompting some to wonder whether its bet on the firm is a stinker. And while Bending Spoons' stock surged after Berkshire added to its initial investment, the enthusiasm was short-lived: The stock has fallen over the past three weeks.

Still, for dedicated value investors and longtime Berkshire observers, such jitters may not really matter. After all, Buffett's 2016 investment in Apple Inc., derided at the time as being late in the iPhone maker's history, turned out to be one of Berkshire's most lucrative bets. Abel likely views Berkshire's AI investments as a long-term wager on the technology's potential, said Meyer Shields, an analyst for Keefe Bruyette & Woods.

"He's not trying to send a message to the markets," said Shields. The CEO "can consider these investments with all the conservatism that you would expect at Berkshire Hathaway."

And given AI's massive investment needs in the years to come, Berkshire, which was still sitting on a $365.5 billion cash pile at the end of the second quarter, is among the best placed to support the technology's development — and reap potential gains.

Investors will have to wait until mid-November to know whether Abel, in a typical value investor mindset, has decided to benefit from the market's concerns around AI, and the lower valuations, to put more money into the trade.

Story Continues

Solid Growth

Meanwhile, Berkshire Hathaway is expected to release its third-quarter earnings Saturday, giving shareholders a peek into the conglomerate's financial standing.

The company, with its vast stable of businesses spanning insurance, energy and retail, may benefit from the health of the US economy in the period.

"It seems like overall economic growth in the quarter was pretty solid, and so much of Berkshire participates in the economy," Shields said.

But as high gas prices and inflation persist, investors may want to pay attention to the firm's collection of retail businesses.

"We're hearing a lot of anecdotal stories about the top-end investment portfolios, the wealth effect helping spending, but at the lower end, they're really squeezed," Seifert said. "We could see some of that in Berkshire's consumer businesses."

Investors are likely to pay attention to the performance of the firm's insurance businesses, including auto insurer Geico, as well. Last quarter, in sharp contrast to some of its peers, the unit reported lower earnings amid higher losses and advertising expenses.

"The overall personal auto insurance market has been rationally competitive," Shields said. "I think what we'll see is reports of a more aggressive growth strategy at Geico."

Across the rest of the group, strong traffic data and a fuel surcharge could support the performance of Berkshire's railroad operator, BNSF, according to analysts.

Share Buybacks

Investors are also expected to monitor whether Berkshire will buy back more of its own shares. After a hiatus that lasted more than a year, the conglomerate resumed share purchases in the first quarter, a sign that Abel and Buffett believe the stock was trading below its intrinsic value.

Since then, however, Berkshire shares have reached new heights. It's outperforming the S&P 500 this year.

"If that recent uptick in the shares may have quelled their enthusiasm for buying back more shares, I think investors may be a little disappointed in that," Seifert said.

news.Title: IONQ Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, 2026 Sales View Raised, Stock Up
news.Content:
IonQ, Inc. IONQ reported an adjusted loss of 29 cents per share for the third quarter of 2026, wider than the year-ago loss of 17 cents. The Zacks Consensus Estimate was pegged at a loss of 30 cents.

GAAP earnings per share (EPS) came in at $1.42 compared to a loss of $3.58 in the year-ago quarter, reflecting a significant non-cash warrant valuation gain.

Revenues surged 336% year over year to $173.8 million and also surpassed the consensus mark by 19.03%.

Following the announcement yesterday, IONQ shares gained 5.2% in the after-market session.

IONQ's Platform Revenues Surge on Quantum Demand

IonQ Platform revenues increased 127% year over year to $90.3 million, supported by global deployments of fifth-generation Tempo quantum computers. Quantum computing remained the fastest-growing product line, benefiting from expanding commercial adoption.

Commercial customers accounted for approximately 65% of segment revenues, while international customers contributed roughly 35%. More than 40% of revenues came from multi-product customers, reflecting increasing demand across computing, networking, sensing and security.

IonQ, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

IonQ, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | IonQ, Inc. Quote

Quantum computing contributed approximately $180 million of the $290 million in new IonQ Platform contracts signed during the quarter. Strong demand for sixth-generation Superion 256 systems supported this performance.

IonQ's SkyWater Acquisition Expands Revenue Base

SkyWater Foundry Services generated $83.5 million in revenues during its first quarter under IonQ's ownership. The contribution included two months of operations following the acquisition's completion on July 31, 2026.

Revenues from SkyWater's quantum customers, excluding IonQ, increased more than 30% year over year. The company extended its multi-year manufacturing agreement with D-Wave and secured a new contract with Qolab.

SkyWater also accelerated IonQ's manufacturing roadmap, delivering 12 times more wafer lots and reducing chip development cycle times from nine months to approximately two months. These improvements strengthen production capacity and support faster commercialization.

IONQ's Backlog Strengthens Revenue Visibility

IonQ Platform RPOs increased to $689 million from $485 million in the preceding quarter. SkyWater contributed another $479 million, taking the combined backlog to approximately $1.2 billion.

The expanding backlog reflects strong customer commitments despite record revenue recognition during the quarter. Management highlighted particularly strong demand for Superion 256 systems.

Story Continues

IonQ's Costs Continue to Pressure Profitability

The adjusted cost of revenues, excluding depreciation and amortization, totaled $121.6 million. Adjusted research and development expenses were $96.8 million, while adjusted sales and marketing expenses reached $24.9 million.

GAAP operating costs and expenses were $606.9 million, including substantial research, development and acquisition-related expenditures. General and administrative expenses included approximately $40 million in one-time costs associated with the SkyWater acquisition.

Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $133.6 million from $48.9 million in the year-ago quarter.

IONQ's Financial Position

IonQ ended September with $1.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents and investments. Following the $2 billion equity offering completed in October, its pro forma liquidity reached approximately $3.7 billion.

The strengthened balance sheet supports continued investments in quantum computing, manufacturing infrastructure and global commercial operations.

IONQ Raises Its 2026 Revenue Outlook

IonQ raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $505-$515 million from the $450-$460 million range announced on its September Investor Day. The upward revision reflects strong demand for quantum computing solutions, growing commercial adoption and revenue contributions from SkyWater. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 revenues currently stands at $455 million.

Management now expects quantum computing revenues to grow 110% year over year in 2026, up from its previous expectation of 100%, supported by strong demand for Superion 256 systems and expanding global deployments.

Our Take on IONQ Stock

IonQ delivered strong third-quarter 2026 results, with a narrower-than-expected loss and a revenue beat. Robust demand for quantum computing systems, particularly fifth-generation Tempo deployments, and contributions from SkyWater supported impressive revenue growth.

Commercial momentum remained strong, with rising multi-product adoption and growing demand for Superion 256 systems. The company's advancement to DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Stage C and expanding quantum security and sensing businesses strengthened its growth prospects. The acquisition of SkyWater also enhances manufacturing capabilities and supports faster product development.

However, elevated operating expenses and widening adjusted EBITDA losses remain concerns. Integration-related costs and continued investments in research and development are likely to keep profitability under pressure in the near term.

IONQ's Zacks Rank and Key Picks

IonQ currently carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell).

Some better-ranked stocks from the broader Computer and Technology sector are MKS Inc. MKSI, Camtek Ltd. CAMT and Arista Networks, Inc. ANET.

MKS, carrying a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), reported a third-quarter 2026 EPS of $4.18, which beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 14.84%. Revenues of $1.41 billion surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.12%. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

MKSI has an estimated long-term earnings growth rate of 36.3% compared with the industry's 24% growth. The company surpassed earnings estimates in three of the trailing four quarters and missed on one occasion, the average surprise being 10.12%.

Camtek, carrying a Zacks Rank #2 at present, posted third-quarter 2026 earnings of 99 cents per share, which beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.02%. Revenues of $161.3 million topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.6%.

CAMT has an earnings yield of 3.6% compared with the industry's 3.1% growth. The company's earnings outpaced estimates in three of the trailing four quarters and missed on one occasion, the average surprise being 0.67%.

Arista Networks, currently carrying a Zacks Rank #2, reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $1.2 per share, which topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 11.11%. Revenues of $3.66 million outperformed the consensus mark by 10.41%.

ANET has an estimated long-term earnings growth rate of 22.7% compared with the industry's 21.2% growth. The company's earnings outpaced estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 10.6%.

news.Title: How to Approach Onto Innovation Stock Ahead of Q3 Earnings?
news.Content:
Onto Innovation ONTO is set to report earnings for the third quarter of 2026 on Nov. 9, after the closing bell.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter earnings per share (EPS) is pinned at $2.27, suggesting a jump of 146.7% from the year-ago quarter's figure. The company expects non-GAAP EPS between $2.18 and $2.38.

The consensus mark for revenues is pegged at $390.7 million, indicating a 79.1% rise from the year-earlier quarter's actuals.

ONTO's earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in three of the trailing four quarters, while missing once, with the average surprise being 5.5%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

ONTO's Earnings Whispers

Our proven model does not predict an earnings beat for Onto Innovation this time around. The combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) increases the odds of an earnings beat. That is not the case here.

Earnings ESP: ONTO has an Earnings ESP of 0.00%. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they're reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

Zacks Rank: ONTO currently carries a Zacks Rank #2. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Factors to Note for ONTO's Q3 Performance

Strong momentum in advanced packaging and semiconductor process control is likely to have aided ONTO's third-quarter performance, with rising demand for AI chips, HBM and advanced logic devices strengthening its growth outlook. However, a sharp pullback in ONTO shares has raised questions about whether the stock offers an attractive buying opportunity ahead of results or whether investors should wait for greater clarity.

Onto Innovation reported a record backlog exceeding $1.1 billion in the second quarter, providing greater visibility into future demand. Driven by robust demand and strong execution, Onto Innovation raised its second-half 2026 revenue, margin and EPS outlook. Building on a strong first half, it expects second-half revenue to grow more than 25%, with third-quarter revenue of $380–$400 million and further growth in the fourth quarter.

At the midpoint, revenue guidance implies another sequential increase of roughly 14%, suggesting demand remains exceptionally strong. Despite ongoing cost headwinds, including higher material, fuel and freight expenses, it expects gross margin to expand by another 50 basis points (bps) in each of the third and fourth quarters. ONTO expects gross margin to be between 57.3% and 57.8%. It expects operating margin to improve 200 bps to 31.5-32.5% in the third quarter. It expects GAAP EPS of $1.54 to $1.70 and GAAP operating margin of 21.4% to 22.4%.

Story Continues

For the third quarter, we expect revenue at $390.3 million. Advanced packaging remains a major growth catalyst for Onto Innovation as chipmakers adopt increasingly complex packaging architectures to support AI accelerators and high-performance computing. In the second quarter, its Dragonfly-led inspection business grew 30% sequentially, backed by demand from 2.5D logic and HBM applications. Management also raised its full-year 2026 advanced-packaging growth outlook to approximately 80% from 50% previously.

Onto Innovation also secured more than $200 million in Dragonfly orders from a single OSAT partner, with most deliveries expected in 2027. This highlights the potential for continued growth beyond the current quarter. Demand for advanced logic and memory devices is another important growth driver. Onto Innovation's advanced-node revenue surged 50% sequentially in the second quarter to a record level, supported by stronger demand across logic and memory customers. Continued strength in these markets could help sustain revenue growth and improve the company's product mix.

Its collaboration with Rigaku and expanding silicon photonics opportunity, targeting a serviceable addressable market of approximately $500 million by 2027, could provide additional growth avenues. In August, Onto Innovation closed its investment in Rigaku Holdings, acquiring a 27% minority stake from Atom Investment, L.P., an affiliate of Carlyle, for approximately $720 million. The move is intended to accelerate joint development of next-generation X-ray-based process control solutions for semiconductor manufacturing. Onto Innovation will account for the stake under the fair value option and will not consolidate Rigaku's results.

Nonetheless, Onto Innovation faces risks from changing trade policies, tariffs, imported material costs and freight expenses, which could pressure margins despite ongoing efficiency improvements. Customer and geographic concentration also remain concerns, with four customers accounting for 57.3% of first-half 2026 revenue and Taiwan and South Korea representing significant sales markets. Any slowdown in major customers' capital spending or regional disruption could affect shipments, collections and revenue growth.

Additionally, intense competition, rising R&D expenses, customer qualification requirements and acquisition-related costs could weigh on profitability. The Semilab business continues to incur operating losses, highlighting integration and execution challenges as Onto Innovation expands its product portfolio.

ONTO Stock vs. Industry

ONTO's shares have plunged 48.8% in the past month compared with the Zacks Nanotechnology industry's fall of 48.2%. The company has also underperformed the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the S&P 500 composite's fall of 18.2% and 6.1%, respectively.

ONTO's tough competitors include KLA Corporation KLAC, Camtek Ltd CAMT and Nova Ltd. NVMI. KLAC has fallen 34.1%, while CAMT and NVMI declined 39.7% and 25.8%, respectively, over the same period.

ONTO's Valuation

In terms of forward price/earnings, ONTO's shares are trading at 13.97X, higher than the industry's 2.73X.

KLAC, CAMT and NVMI are trading at multiples of 21.3X, 20.71X and 22.7X, respectively.

ONTO Before Q3 Earnings: Buy, Sell or Hold?

Strong AI-driven demand, rising advanced-packaging sales, a record backlog and expanding margins support Onto Innovation's growth outlook. Its growing opportunities in HBM, advanced nodes and silicon photonics could drive further revenue and earnings growth, making the stock attractive for long-term investors now.

news.Title: MCHP Q2 Earnings Call Highlights Supply Constraints and Growth
news.Content:
Microchip Technology Incorporated MCHP emphasized strengthening demand, expanding backlogs and emerging supply constraints during its second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call. Management highlighted industrial and data center growth while cautioning that manufacturing bottlenecks are delaying shipments of high-margin products.

The company also outlined a measured December-quarter outlook, addressed rising supplier costs and discussed opportunities from recent acquisitions and next-generation semiconductor technologies.

MCHP Sees Demand Outpacing Available Capacity

President and CEO Steve Sanghi said September-quarter bookings remained strong, with the book-to-bill ratio well above one. Backlog increased entering the December quarter as customer demand strengthened across multiple markets.

However, lead times have extended from the historical four-to-eight-week range to six-to-32 weeks across product lines. Foundry, assembly and testing constraints are preventing Microchip from fulfilling certain high-margin orders.

During questioning from UBS, Sanghi explained that delayed shipments have shifted into subsequent quarters. Management expressed optimism about March-quarter backlog but stopped short of providing formal guidance.

Microchip Maintains a Disciplined Operating Approach

Microchip reported second-quarter revenues of $1.622 billion, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.60 billion by 0.80%. Non-GAAP earnings of 97 cents per share exceeded the consensus estimate of 94 cents.

Microchip Technology Incorporated Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Microchip Technology Incorporated price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Microchip Technology Incorporated Quote

Revenue increased 42.2% year over year and 9.2% sequentially, supported by improving demand and operational execution.

Management maintained its long-term non-GAAP targets of 65% gross margin, 25% operating expenses and 40% operating margin. The immediate focus remains expanding supply availability, controlling costs and translating existing design wins into revenue.

Microchip's December Outlook Reflects Revenue Adjustments

Microchip expects third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues between $1.573 billion and $1.638 billion, representing a sequential decline of 3% to growth of 1%.

Sanghi explained that September-quarter revenues included approximately $53 million of infrequent items involving licensing, distributor pricing adjustments and a customer contract. Excluding these items, December-quarter midpoint guidance reflects sequential growth of approximately 2.3%.

Story Continues

Non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 64%-65%, while adjusted earnings are expected between $0.87 and $0.95 per share. Management attributed margin pressure to product constraints, lower factory utilization and the absence of unusually profitable revenue items.

MCHP Targets Data Center and Industrial Expansion

Sanghi identified industrial and data center applications as the company's principal growth drivers. Industrial revenues increased 50.3% year over year, while data center revenues advanced 55.7%.

Microchip secured 24 combined PCIe Gen6 switch and retimer design wins, compared with 12 at June-quarter end. Management expects shipments associated with these products to increase as customer programs enter production.

During discussions with Wells Fargo, Sanghi emphasized broad industrial recovery across robotics, medical equipment, manufacturing and process control. He also highlighted aerospace and defense opportunities, supported by expanding production requirements and new design activity.

Microchip Addresses AI Spending and Pricing Risks

During questioning from Bank of America, Sanghi expressed concern about the sustainability of explosive data center infrastructure spending. He distinguished that market from Microchip's broader industrial, automotive and defense businesses.

Management argued that slower AI infrastructure expansion could release constrained manufacturing capacity. However, reduced data center investment could also affect deployment volumes for emerging products.

Separately, Wolfe Research questioned pricing benefits and margin sustainability. Sanghi acknowledged additional supplier price increases expected in January but indicated Microchip currently intends to absorb those costs rather than immediately raise customer prices again.

MCHP Integrates Acquisitions and Prioritizes Debt Reduction

Microchip completed acquisitions of Hailo and VORAGO Technologies, expanding its edge AI and aerospace and defense capabilities.

Sanghi said Hailo accelerates Microchip's AI-enabled microprocessor roadmap by approximately five years. However, its elevated research spending creates near-term operating expense pressure.

CFO Eric Bjornholt reported net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 2.36 times. During questioning from TD Cowen, he indicated that reducing leverage remains the board's priority, with dividend increases and share repurchases subject to future evaluation.

What MCHP's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

Microchip currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), indicating favorable near-term earnings estimate revision characteristics. Its Momentum Score of B provides a stronger signal for investors emphasizing favorable price trends. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

However, its Value Score of D indicates comparatively weaker valuation characteristics. The Growth Score of C and VGM Score of C reflect more moderate prospects across those investment styles.

The combination presents mixed Style Score signals despite the favorable Zacks Rank. Investors should recognize that the Zacks Rank can change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest quarterly results.

news.Title: Why SoftBank stock is sinking under the weight of its AI bets
news.Content:
The over-the-top tech house Masayoshi Son has spent billions to build at SoftBank ( SFTBY ) is getting torched, looking at the stock price action.

SoftBank shares crashed 10.83% in early trading on Friday after losing 14.4% on Thursday as the AI-heavy company was swept into the broader AI stock rout. Sentiment was also dinged by an FT report that China would not allow SoftBank to go ahead with the $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB's robotics division.

Shares are down 45% in the past month.

The company's credit risk climbed to its highest level in four years today, as measured by its five-year credit default swap (CDS) spread. The spread widened to as much as 466 basis points, its highest since Oct. 22, Reuters reported.

The level indicated a default probability of 30.6%.

SoftBank's primary asset anchor remains its roughly 90% ownership stake in Arm Holdings ( ARM ), whose chip architectures power the vast majority of mobile and enterprise AI workloads. With concerns about a "blue wave" on Election Day stunting AI demand , a company like Arm is caught in the crosshairs — and by extension so is SoftBank.

Meanwhile, the company also has a $64.6 billion stake in OpenAI, which had decided to push its IPO out to 2027. But OpenAI's valuation is at risk in light of the blue wave, as seen in chatter that the upcoming Anthropic IPO won't deliver it a $2 trillion valuation as many expected.
