news.Title: AI semiconductor rout may be buying opportunity, LYNX Equity says: ’Dip a toe in’
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) shares rebounded sharply in premarket trading Friday after the semiconductor equipment maker announced a $25 billion share repurchase authorization, offering a potential signal of corporate confidence following one of the technology sector's worst trading sessions in years.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Lam shares had plunged 16.4% on Thursday, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) sank 12.25%, its steepest one-day decline since March 2020. The index closed at 9,011.14, as investors aggressively reduced exposure to AI-related stocks amid growing concerns about the sustainability of data-center investment.

The sell-off extended across the semiconductor industry, with Micron (NASDAQ:MU) falling 17.5%, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) losing 17.3% and SanDisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) dropping more than 22%. Lam was among the hardest-hit equipment manufacturers.

The Friday rebound in Lam, which rose approximately 11% premarket to $205.65, came after the company announced that its board had approved the new $25 billion repurchase authorization. The program supplements the remaining balance of its previous authorization and has no termination date.

The announcement also drew attention from LYNX Equity Strategies, with KC Rajkumar arguing that the timing of the buyback could indicate that the semiconductor equipment maker is not experiencing the deterioration in demand implied by the recent share-price decline.

In a research note titled "AI Semis: When There Is Blood on the Streets," Rajkumar said the worst of the sell-off may be behind the sector, suggesting that investors could begin selectively rebuilding positions.

Supply constraints could shield semiconductor suppliers

Rajkumar's central argument is that concerns about AI infrastructure spending should not necessarily be confused with a deterioration in near-term semiconductor demand.

Hyperscalers and neocloud operators face growing questions about financing, construction delays and the returns on enormous AI investments. However, semiconductor suppliers remain relatively insulated by supply shortages, particularly in memory and flash markets.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

LYNX Equity Strategies said its checks into Asian memory and flash markets had not identified disruptions attributable to the US election, suggesting that underlying demand conditions remain more resilient than the stock-market reaction implies.

Story Continues

Rajkumar also expects other semiconductor companies with strong free cash flow and substantial cash reserves to potentially follow Lam Research's lead with additional share repurchases.

The argument is particularly relevant for semiconductor equipment manufacturers, whose order books could prove more resilient than investor sentiment currently suggests.

A potential floor, but not an all-clear

Thursday's collapse reflects more than ordinary profit-taking. Disappointing results from Qualcomm and concerns about the political and regulatory environment for data-center construction have intensified questions about whether the AI infrastructure buildout can continue at its current pace.

Lam's announcement does not eliminate those risks, nor does a repurchase authorization guarantee that the company will buy back the full amount. However, it provides a potentially encouraging signal at a time when investors are questioning the outlook for the entire semiconductor supply chain.

For Rajkumar, the distinction is between uncertainty surrounding downstream AI infrastructure spending and the more immediate supply constraints supporting upstream semiconductor businesses.

His conclusion is that the semiconductor sell-off may have created an opportunity to begin accumulating exposure gradually rather than waiting for all uncertainty to disappear.

As he put it, investors may want to "stick one's toe in, gingerly."

Technically, every stock oscillates between being overbought and oversold irrespective of the quality of their fundamentals. And the beauty of RSI is that it helps you quickly and easily check if a stock's price is reaching a point of reversal.

So, by this measure, if a stock has gotten too far below its fair value just because of unwarranted selling pressure, investors may start looking for entry opportunities in the stock for benefiting from the inevitable rebound.

CoreWeave, Inc. CRWV is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 10, after market close.

The consensus estimate for total revenues is $3.5 billion, indicating a 159.2% year-over-year increase.

CRWV's earnings missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in two of the trailing four quarters, while beating in two, with the average surprise being 10.35%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Our Model Predicts for CRWV

Our proven model predicts an earnings beat for CRWV this time around. The combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy), or 3 (Hold) increases the chances of an earnings beat. This is the case here. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they are reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

CRWV has an Earnings ESP of +17.45% and a Zacks Rank #3 at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Key Factors That Could Drive a Q3 Earnings Beat for CRWV

Robust demand for AI computing capacity, expanding infrastructure and a growing customer backlog are likely to have driven strong third-quarter perfomance. CoreWeave delivered strong second-quarter 2026 results, with revenues more than doubling year over year to $2.58 billion, supported by sustained demand for AI infrastructure. Revenue backlog reached approximately $104 billion as of June 30, while the company secured more than $25 billion in additional net customer commitments early in the third quarter.

CoreWeave expects strong sequential growth in the third quarter, with revenues projected at $3.45-$3.6 billion and adjusted operating income of $200-$260 million. Management anticipates continued sequential margin expansion, targeting low-teens adjusted operating margins by the fourth quarter. However, interest expense is expected to rise to $860-$940 million, while quarterly capital expenditures are projected at $11.5-$13.5 billion to support accelerated infrastructure deployment.

Growth is expected to have benefited from the full-quarter contribution of capacity additions made late in the second quarter, including 300 MW added in June. Demand remains robust, with more than $25 billion in additional customer commitments secured early in the third quarter, on top of the $104 billion second-quarter backlog. More than half of the existing backlog was already tied to contracts in delivery, providing greater revenue visibility.

Story Continues

Margin expansion is expected to have benefited from new contracts carrying 5-10 percentage points higher contribution margins, stronger pricing for Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems, and increasing managed inference adoption. Managed inference ARR surged from $1 million to more than $100 million within months of launch, with management targeting $250 million by year-end 2026, although near-term capacity remains a constraint.

CoreWeave's financing initiatives, including its DDTL 5.5 loan, are supporting infrastructure expansion and access to additional enterprise opportunities. With 4.2 GW of contracted power and options for approximately 6 GW, the company is strengthening its capacity pipeline. Overall, strong customer commitments, improving contract economics and infrastructure additions are expected to have driven CoreWeave's third-quarter growth.

However, CoreWeave's aggressive infrastructure expansion raises concerns about its financing needs, profitability and execution risks. The company increased its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to $35-$39 billion, while net interest expense surged to $640 million in the second quarter from $267 million a year earlier. Third-quarter interest expense is expected to reach $860-$940 million, potentially pressuring earnings and cash flow. Customer concentration also remains a concern, as reliance on a handful of large AI and cloud customers exposes the company to changes in spending plans, project delays and contract renegotiations.

Additionally, data center expansion depends on timely access to power, land, networking equipment and advanced chips. Any deployment delays could postpone revenue generation and raise costs, while intensifying competition from established cloud providers and AI infrastructure specialists could pressure pricing and margins.

Key Business Updates

In October, CoreWeave announced a broad expansion of its global AI cloud platform. The company has brought most of its planned 22.5 MW of IT capacity online at a data center in Copenhagen, Denmark, and is expanding its global AI network into the Middle East and Asia Pacific. The initiative is likely to strengthen its competitive position as AI adoption accelerates worldwide.

CoreWeave took a major step in its global expansion strategy by entering India, announcing plans to develop 240 MW of AI data center capacity through a collaboration with AdaniConneX at its Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai. The project includes three 80 MW buildings, with the first phase expected to be operational in mid-2028.

In September, CoreWeave launched Physical AI Field Engineering, an offering designed to help automotive, aerospace, robotics and other engineering teams build, validate and deploy AI throughout the engineering lifecycle.

CoreWeave expanded its capabilities for next-generation workloads with the deployment of multi-rack NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 clusters on CoreWeave Cloud.

CRWV has crashed 58% in the past year, underperforming the Zacks Internet Software industry's decline of 7.2%. The stock has also lagged the Zacks Computer & Technology sector and the S&P 500's growth of 3.9% and 9.4%, respectively.

Key Valuation for CRWV

In terms of Price/Book, CRWV shares are trading at 3.99X, lower than the Internet Software industry's 4.66X.

NBIS and MSFT shares are trading at multiples of 2.95X and 8.46X, respectively.

CRWV Investment Verdict: Wait for Q3 Results

CoreWeave's growth prospects remain compelling, backed by strong AI infrastructure demand, a substantial backlog and expanding computing capacity. However, investors should also assess updated revenue guidance, capital expenditure requirements, interest costs, cash flow and infrastructure deployment plans.

For investors evaluating CRWV stock, waiting for the results and updated guidance may be the more prudent approach. A sustained investment case will depend not only on beating estimates but also on converting demand into profitable growth and managing the financial demands of expansion.

news.Title: USA Today Co Inc (TDAY) (Q3 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Digital Subscriptions Shine as Cost ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Release Date: November 05, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Digital-only subscription revenues grew 5.3% year-over-year, the third consecutive quarter of growth, with ARPU reaching a record $10.82, up 23%.

Digital other revenues, including AI licensing and syndication, grew 24.8% year-over-year to $21.3 million, with sequential growth expected in Q4.

Premium direct sold digital advertising returned to year-over-year growth in Q3 and is expected to accelerate in Q4, driven by known users, video, and AI discoverability.

A $100 million annualized cost reduction program was implemented at the end of Q3, with benefits expected to positively impact Q4 run rate and extend into 2027.

The Google antitrust case advanced with summary judgment denied and a trial date set for April 5, 2027; damages are at least $901 million and subject to trebling.

Negative Points

Total revenues declined 7.4% year-over-year to $519.2 million, with same-store revenue down 5.8%.

Digital advertising revenues fell 13.9% year-over-year, primarily due to a 32% decline in indirect advertising (programmatic and sponsored content) caused by search behavior changes.

Adjusted EBITDA dropped 36% year-over-year to $36.6 million, driven by lower revenue and inflationary pressures on raw materials, healthcare, and distribution.

Full-year guidance was lowered: same-store revenue is now expected to decline mid-single-digits versus prior low single-digit decline, and digital revenue is not expected to reach 50% of total until 2027.

Free cash flow for the full year is now expected to decline compared to 2025, despite Q3 free cash flow being relatively flat year-over-year.

Q & A Highlights

A : CEO Mike Reed pointed to three drivers for the roughly $200 million premium direct advertising category: deepening engagement and growing known users (supported by the Palantir work and newsletter/social strategies), expanding video advertising on and off platform where CPMs are much higher, and AI-discoverable branded content, a new product rolled out in September. He said known user growth was significant in Q3, supporting confidence in Q4 acceleration.

Q : Are there further cost reduction opportunities in 2027 beyond the $100 million program? A : CFO Trisha Gossert said the $100 million annualized program was implemented by early October and will benefit Q4 and well into 2027. She added the company sees additional opportunities in 2027, including consolidating systems and technology platforms to lower vendor spend, optimizing outsourcing agreements, streamlining print operations, and further automation.

Q : Why did the company change full-year guidance this quarter when search trends were already apparent last quarter? A : CFO Trisha Gossert said two factors drove the adjustment: indirect programmatic and sponsored links revenue eroded further year-over-year, and direct sold revenue improved but not enough to outpace that decline; additionally, expected AI licensing deals shifted to later in the year. Same-store revenue is now expected to decline mid-single-digits versus the prior low single-digit expectation, with digital reaching 50% of total revenue in 2027 rather than 2026.

Q : What is the status of the Google antitrust litigation? A : CEO Mike Reed said the judge denied most of Google's summary judgment motion and set a trial date of April 5, 2027. The ruling made public a damages calculation of $901 million through 2024, which the company expects to update ahead of trial, and the figure excludes potential treble damages. Management remains confident in the case.

Q : Why initiate share repurchases now, and how quickly can the program be deployed? A : CEO Mike Reed said the shares are significantly undervalued relative to the business and opportunities, and leverage has been reduced from $1.8 billion in 2020 to roughly $700 million net. About $97 million remains available under the authorized plan, and trading windows open a couple of days after the earnings release, allowing purchases through most of Q4. The company also secured a $50 million incremental term loan from Apollo specifically for Q4 buybacks.

Q : What is driving digital-only subscription performance and what are the opportunities ahead? A : President of USA Today Media Kristen Roberts said the strategy prioritized subscriber quality over volume, producing a third consecutive quarter of revenue growth (up 5.3%) and record ARPU of $10.82, up 23%. For 2027, the focus is returning to subscriber volume growth while maintaining ARPU gains, supported by personalization, pay-per-article offerings, next-best-action engagement, and churn-risk retention tools.

Q : What is the outlook for AI licensing deals? A : CEO Mike Reed acknowledged an industry-wide slowdown in deal signings but said the company expects to announce at least one, possibly two, deals before the end of Q4. He views AI licensing as a significant long-term revenue category, citing Anthropic's first licensing deal with the Associated Press as evidence of the value of real-time news content.

Q : What are the capital allocation priorities going forward? A : CEO Mike Reed listed three priorities: reducing debt and leverage as the top priority over the next two to three years, investing in the business to accelerate growth, and opportunistic share repurchases when the equity is mispriced, as management believes is currently the case.

Shares of Advanced Micro Devices AMD soared 8% in extended trading session on Nov. 3 (as cited in CNBC), following its better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results. However, the stock lost its steam yesterday, plunging 17.3% despite comfortably beating Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, as a broader technology-sector sell-off following the release of the U.S. midterm election results weighed on investor sentiment.

This solid pullback in AMD's share price might offer an opportune moment for investors eager to reap the benefits of the company's soaring revenue growth from its data center business. AMD's Data center segment registered record revenues of $8.5 billion in the third quarter, reflecting 97% year-over-year growth.

However, factors like the 151% year-over-year surge in AMD's capital expenditures, along with constraints in advanced packaging capacity and volatility in HBM4 memory pricing, might pose a cause of concern and thereby dampen investor confidence. This might even push some investors toward safer alternatives.

At the same time, Democrats' wins in Congress have revived talk of tighter regulation around data center buildouts, which could weigh on near-term sentiment for companies with heavy data center exposure.

Against this backdrop, investors seeking to capitalize on AMD's growth potential while mitigating company-specific risks may consider technology-focused exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with significant exposure to AMD rather than investing directly in the stock.

This will let investors participate in AMD's innovation cycle and the upside of other tech leaders, while smoothing out the single-stock volatility that a high-valuation, capital-intensive name like AMD can deliver.

But before diving straight into these ETFs, let us check AMD's overall performance in the third quarter in terms of other metrics.

A Brief Analysis of AMD's Q3 Results

AMD's third-quarter earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 7.7%, while revenues topped the mark by 1.9%.

Its data center revenues nearly doubled year over year, driven by record server revenues, robust demand for AMD's fifth-generation EPYC processors and record data center AI revenues.

However, revenues from its Client and Gaming segment went down 8% year over year due to lower semi-custom and graphics sales.

As per AMD's earnings call transcript, during the third quarter, cloud hyperscalers expanded its infrastructure by deploying substantial volumes of AMD EPYC servers to support both internal operations and public cloud services. In particular, its latest "Turin" architecture has become the most widely adopted EPYC generation in the public cloud, powering over 540 instances globally across major cloud providers.

news.Title: Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (META) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Shares of this social media company have returned -16.1% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -5.4% change. The Zacks Internet - Software industry, to which Meta Platforms belongs, has lost 14.1% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Meta Platforms is expected to post earnings of $8.16 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of -8.1%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -0.1%.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $29.41 points to a change of +25.2% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +3%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $33.91 indicates a change of +15.3% from what Meta Platforms is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -1.3%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Meta Platforms is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Revenue Growth Forecast

Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.

In the case of Meta Platforms, the consensus sales estimate of $75.21 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +25.6%. The $256.32 billion and $313.53 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +27.5% and +22.3%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Meta Platforms reported revenues of $64.6 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +26.1%. EPS of $7.4 for the same period compares with $7.25 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $63.41 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +1.88%. The EPS surprise was +13.5%.

Over the last four quarters, Meta Platforms surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

Comparing the current value of a company's valuation multiples, such as its price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), to its own historical values helps ascertain whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, whereas comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of how reasonable its stock price is.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Meta Platforms is graded B on this front, indicating that it is trading at a discount to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Bottom Line

news.Title: Marvell Agreed to Pay $1,132 a Share for Lumentum. The Stock Trades Near $510. Here's Why It’s Not as Good As It Looks.
news.Content:
When Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) agreed to acquire Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) on Nov. 2, the deal valued Lumentum at about $1,132 per share, a roughly 24% premium over its pre-talks trading price. Three days later, Lumentum closed at about $510.

That's not quite the bargain it seems. Even based on the current value of Marvell's offer, Lumentum trades at about 85% of what it would be worth if the deal closes, a gap of about 15% (we'll discuss why we say "current value" in a bit). Here's why that gap exists, and why I don't think it's free money.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The deal's value keeps shrinking

First of all, Marvell is paying for Lumentum entirely in stock. The acquisition price is well over $100 billion (based on Marvell's share price before the announcement), and acquiring Lumentum for cash simply wouldn't be practical. Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own when the deal closes. There's no collar, a feature some deals use to protect sellers if the buyer's stock falls. So every $1 drop in Marvell's share price cuts $4.50 from the deal's value for Lumentum investors.

Marvell's stock has fallen sharply amid recent market turbulence. It closed at $133.55 on Nov. 5, which puts the offer at about $601 per Lumentum share. That's far less than the $913.95 Lumentum traded for before the deal talks became public. In other words, the premium Lumentum shareholders were promised is gone, at least for now, because it is 100% dependent on Marvell's stock price.

This could take a while

Here's a big reason why there's still a gap, even below the new, lower value of the deal. The companies don't expect to close the deal until the first half of 2028, and the merger agreement allows extensions as late as August 2028 if regulators are still reviewing it. If the deal closes, Lumentum's stock would be worth exactly 4.5 times what Marvell shares are. But spread over that much time, a 15% gain works out to roughly 8% to 13% annualized returns by my estimate, depending on when the deal closes. And the deal closing isn't exactly a sure thing.

Regulators are the biggest wild card. Bank of America downgraded Marvell after the announcement, citing a long review process "that includes China." There's good reason for concern. China's regulator never approved Intel's (NASDAQ:INTC) planned acquisition of Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM), which collapsed in 2023. Even deals that do get approved can take a long time. Synopsys ' (NASDAQ:SNPS) acquisition of Ansys took about 18 months to clear.

Story Continues

If the deal falls apart, Marvell would owe Lumentum a $3.2 billion termination fee. That sounds like a lot, but it works out to roughly $35 per Lumentum share, a small cushion for a stock trading above $500.

What this means for investors

Professional arbitrage investors typically buy the target and short the acquirer's stock to lock in the spread. And in this case, it might seem like a good idea for your portfolio. After all, 15% is quite a gap on an already beaten-down stock. Most individual investors shouldn't be doing that. Without that hedge, buying Lumentum today is largely a bet on Marvell's stock, with regulatory risk layered on top.

To be fair, Lumentum would be fine on its own. Its revenue grew 137% last quarter, and management expects more growth this quarter. In a nutshell, if the deal breaks, the stock wouldn't necessarily collapse.

Having said all that, if I wanted exposure to this deal, I'd rather own Marvell directly than buy Lumentum and hope the spread closes. The gap between Lumentum's price and the offer isn't a mistake. It's the market's price for time, uncertainty, and Marvell's own volatility.

news.Title: This chip inspection leader fell 24.5% in a month: is the dip worth a look?
news.Content:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Investing.com — Semiconductor equipment stocks spent October under heavy pressure, as heightened export restrictions and cyclical pauses in foundry capital expenditures dragged the sector down 25% to 35%. While the broad sell-off swept up lithography and etching leaders like ASML Holding (NASDAQ:ASML) and Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) , it also knocked process diagnostics leader KLA Corporation (NASDAQ:KLAC) down 24.5% over the past month.

Yet treating all equipment suppliers equally ignores a critical manufacturing bottleneck. While chipmakers can temporarily delay purchasing new wafer fabrication tools during cyclical lulls, they cannot bypass the defect inspection and yield management systems KLA provides. As advanced computing shifts toward 2-nanometer nodes and complex 3D packaging, even microscopic wafer defects carry catastrophic financial costs.

Spotting when an essential supplier gets dragged down by a broad sector sell-off is exactly what InvestingPro's ProPicks AI models look for. During the live November 1 rebalance, the system added KLA Corporation to the Tech Titans strategy, pairing it with high-conviction technology leaders—including a specialized foundry chipmaker, an enterprise collaboration software platform, and an essential cloud infrastructure provider.

See the tech picks in the live November update: Explore the Tech Titans strategy on InvestingPro

The inspection step chipmakers cannot skip

KLA supplies the inspection, metrology and data analytics systems that chipmakers such as TSMC and Samsung use to catch defects and manage yield. The Pro Research Report puts its share of semiconductor metrology and inspection at an estimated 50% to 74%, and the switching costs from that integration into customer workflows are high.

Results from the September quarter point to a sector-wide sell-off, with the business itself on firmer ground. Fiscal first-quarter revenue hit a record $4.14 billion, up 29% from a year earlier and ahead of the $4.04 billion analysts expected. Operating margin reached 46.1%, the first time in company history above 46%, on a 62.7% gross margin, and free cash flow was $1.34 billion. Guidance for the December quarter of about $4.7 billion sits well above the roughly $4.49 billion Street estimate.

Backlog reached nearly $13 billion, up about 60% from fiscal 2025, with visibility into 2027 and early 2028. Services revenue added $850 million, up 14%, on a growing installed base. Advanced packaging revenue is on track for about $1.1 billion this calendar year, up more than 70%, and management expects the wafer equipment market to top $200 billion in 2027.

Story Continues

A record quarter set against specific risks

According to consensus analyst projections compiled on InvestingPro, earnings per share are expected to reach $5.46 in fiscal 2027, a 45.3% jump, and $6.65 in fiscal 2028. Over the past 90 days, there have been 19 upward earnings revisions against 3 downward. Citi, Cantor Fitzgerald and Evercore ISI all trimmed price targets after the report, Cantor's to $225 from $325, though each kept a positive rating.

InvestingPro's Financial Health framework, which benchmarks companies across more than 100 indicators, rates KLA "Good," with a Profitability rating of 9 out of 10 and a Piotroski score of 8 behind it.

Memory input costs are a drag of about 100 basis points on gross margin, with relief not expected until mid-to-late 2027 or into 2028. China is set to slip from about 30% of revenue to the low 20s in 2027, supply lead times average about 12 months, and a single weekend of AI-slowdown talk in September knocked 7.8% off the shares in pre-market trading. The stock also still carries a premium earnings multiple.

The KLA Corporation Pro Research Report sets out the process control market share estimates, the 2-nanometer fab transition and whether operating margins can hold.

Looking beyond cyclical equipment sell-offs

KLA's recent operating results highlight the resilience behind its franchise, delivering a record $4.14 billion quarter alongside an elite 46.1% operating margin. When broader sector sell-offs outpace operational reality, valuation discounts emerge in businesses whose products customers simply cannot cut from their budgets.

Capturing those opportunities before broad sentiment normalizes is why ProPicks AI evaluates company fundamentals monthly. Rather than attempting to time macro semiconductor cycles, the Tech Titans strategy systematically rebalances toward proven cash generators with dominant pricing power—spanning semiconductor inspection, chip manufacturing, developer software, and enterprise cloud infrastructure.

news.Content:
December Nasdaq 100 E-Mini futures (NQZ26) are up +1.68% this morning as investors bought the dip in chipmakers and other AI-related stocks after the previous session's brutal selloff.

Chip and AI infrastructure stocks climbed in pre-market trading, recovering some ground after yesterday's rout. Sandisk (SNDK), Micron Technology (MU), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) each rose +7% or more.

Elsewhere, WTI crude prices edged higher on Friday, extending gains from the previous session as traders weighed the prospects for an end to the Middle East conflict. Treasuries fell across the curve, with the benchmark 10-year yield rising two basis points to 4.86%.

Attention now turns to the release of the key U.S. jobs report, which will offer further clues on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate path.

In yesterday's trading session, Wall Street's major indices closed sharply lower as investors retreated from technology stocks amid speculation that congressional Democrats would impose tighter regulations on the AI industry. Chip and AI infrastructure stocks crashed, with Sandisk (SNDK) tanking over -22% to lead losers in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100, and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) sinking more than -17%. Also, the Magnificent Seven stocks slid, with Nvidia (NVDA) slumping over -9% to lead losers in the Dow and Meta Platforms (META) falling nearly -4%. In addition, Expedia Group (EXPE) tumbled over -13% after the company gave a soft Q4 gross bookings forecast. On the bullish side, AppLovin (APP) popped more than +31% and was the top percentage gainer in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 after the advertising tech platform posted upbeat Q3 results and issued above-consensus Q4 revenue guidance.

On the economic front, however, Thursday's U.S. data offered some positive news, with fewer jobless claims, stronger-than-expected productivity growth, and an unexpected decline in unit labor costs. The number of Americans filing initial jobless claims unexpectedly fell by 6K last week to a 3-1/2-month low of 189K, compared with expectations of 197K. Separately, U.S. Q3 nonfarm productivity climbed +3.6% q/q, stronger than expectations of +2.8% q/q, while unit labor costs unexpectedly fell -0.7% q/q, compared with expectations of +0.3% q/q.

Story Continues

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said on Thursday that interest rates must be restrictive to bring inflation back to the central bank's target. "I expect that monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2% in a timely manner," Hammack said, adding that she favors making "more frequent, smaller adjustments when possible." Separately, Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin reaffirmed his preference for a "gradual" pace of interest-rate hikes, though he declined to specify how high rates would need to go.

U.S. rate futures are currently pricing in a 69.3% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike and a 30.7% chance of no rate change at December's monetary policy meeting.

Today, all eyes are on the U.S. nonfarm payrolls report, which is set to be released in a couple of hours. Economists estimate that October nonfarm payrolls will rise by 65K after a lower-than-expected 29K gain in September.

Investors will also focus on the U.S. unemployment rate. Economists anticipate that the jobless rate will remain steady at 4.2% in October.

U.S. average hourly earnings data will be released today. Economists expect average hourly earnings to rise +0.3% m/m and +2.9% y/y in October, compared with +0.1% m/m and +3.0% y/y in September.

The University of Michigan's U.S. consumer sentiment index will be reported today. Economists forecast that the preliminary November figure will come in at 48.1, compared with 48.0 in October.

The Fed's Consumer Credit report will be released today as well. Economists expect U.S. consumer credit to increase by $13.4 billion in September, compared with an $8.3 billion increase in August.

In addition, market participants will be watching for speeches from Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman and St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem.

On the earnings front, notable companies including Moderna (MRNA), Humana (HUM), Vistra (VST), PPL Corporation (PPL), and Charter Communications (CHTR) are scheduled to release their quarterly results today. According to Bloomberg Intelligence, S&P 500 companies are expected to post an average +31% jump in third-quarter earnings from a year earlier.

In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is at 4.86%, up +0.41%.

The Euro Stoxx 50 Index is down -1.49% this morning as the market catches up with yesterday's sharp selloff on Wall Street. Media, healthcare, and consumer-related stocks slumped on Friday. At the same time, some chip-related stocks advanced, tracking the rebound in their U.S. peers in pre-market trading. Despite Friday's slump, the benchmark index was on track to eke out a weekly gain. Data from Eurostat released on Friday showed that Eurozone monthly retail sales slumped in September as elevated energy prices continued to dampen consumer confidence. Separately, data showed that Germany's monthly industrial production unexpectedly rose in September despite continued pressure on companies from high energy prices stemming from the Middle East conflict. Meanwhile, Eurozone government bond yields fell on Friday as the equity selloff drove investors toward safe-haven assets. In corporate news, Teleperformance (TEP.FP) tumbled over -16% after the outsourcing firm cut its full-year revenue growth guidance.

Germany's Industrial Production and Eurozone's Retail Sales data were released today.

The German September Industrial Production unexpectedly rose +0.7% m/m, stronger than expectations of no change m/m.

Eurozone's September Retail Sales fell -0.7% m/m and rose +0.4% y/y, weaker than expectations of -0.1% m/m and +0.6% y/y.

Asian stock markets today settled in the red. China's Shanghai Composite Index ($CHSC) closed down -1.10%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index ($NKY) closed down -5.96%.

China's Shanghai Composite Index closed lower today, weighed down by weakness in the technology sector. Semiconductor and other AI-related stocks slid on Friday as the tech selloff spread from Wall Street to Asia. However, losses in Chinese tech stocks were less pronounced than those among their Asian peers, with the sector also paring some of its declines in the afternoon session as dip buyers stepped in. Despite Friday's drop, the benchmark index notched a weekly gain, snapping a six-week losing streak. Meanwhile, China's 10-year government bond yield fell to an all-time intraday low on Friday amid ample liquidity and strong demand for safe-haven assets. Elsewhere, Reuters reported on Friday that China's largest flash-memory chipmaker, Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., intends to source up to 70% of the equipment for its planned fourth factory from domestic suppliers. In corporate news, Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor climbed over +6%, defying the global tech selloff, after the chip foundry reported strong Q3 results.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index closed sharply lower today as investors continued to unwind AI-related positions following the Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections. The Nikkei plunged nearly -6%, its biggest one-day percentage drop since April 2025, falling below the closely watched 60,000 mark. The slump left the index more than 20% below its June peak, pushing it into a technical bear market. Although Friday's losses were broad-based, declines in chip and other AI-related stocks, which tracked the sharp overnight selloff in their U.S. peers, contributed the most to the Nikkei's drop. The benchmark posted its steepest weekly decline since March 2020. Meanwhile, Japanese government bonds rallied on Friday as investors turned to traditional safe-haven assets amid the deepening tech-driven equity selloff. On the economic front, data released on Friday showed that Japan's real wages, adjusted for inflation excluding rents, climbed 2.2% in September from a year earlier, marking a ninth straight month of gains. Elsewhere, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Friday that the government was closely monitoring market developments. In corporate news, Japan Tobacco tanked over -19% after Russian authorities seized control of four factories owned by the company. Investor attention now shifts to a speech from Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda in Washington, D.C., scheduled for later today. The Nikkei Volatility Index, which takes into account the implied volatility of Nikkei 225 options, closed up +32.90% at 44.60.

news.Title: What Makes Jabil a Buy Despite the Recent Stock Price Slump?
news.Content:
Jabil, Inc. JBL has plummeted 30.7% over the past three months compared with the industry's decline of 24.8%. However, it has outperformed peers like Celestica Inc. CLS and Flex Ltd. FLEX over this period. While Celestica has declined 35.3%, Flex is down 45%.

Three-Month JBL Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AI-Driven Demand Fuels JBL's Growth Prospects

Despite the blip, Jabil is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), backed by its extensive manufacturing capabilities and strong technological expertise. The company's growing presence in the optical module market strengthens its ability to meet the evolving infrastructure needs of AI-driven applications.

Jabil's photonics-based optical transceiver modules are designed to meet the rising demand for high-speed, reliable and scalable data transmission across AI and ML workloads. Developed in collaboration with leading technology providers, these solutions leverage Intel Corporation 's INTC silicon photonics platform to improve manufacturing efficiency and reliability. Intel's proven technology integrates on-chip laser sources that undergo wafer-level fabrication, testing and burn-in, simplifying module integration and improving operational reliability.

These modules significantly expand data-center rack bandwidth without requiring major infrastructure modifications. As hyperscalers and enterprises ramp up investments in AI infrastructure, growing demand for advanced optical connectivity solutions should create incremental revenue opportunities for Jabil and strengthen its competitive position in the data-center market.

Diversified Business Model Enhances JBL's Resilience

Jabil's diversified business model and extensive global footprint remain key competitive advantages. With operations spanning approximately 100 locations across 30 countries, the company is well-equipped to capitalize on emerging growth opportunities across multiple end markets. Its strong design and engineering capabilities, manufacturing expertise and supply-chain management competencies enable it to serve customers with complex product requirements while supporting healthy margins and cash flow generation.

The company's centralized procurement framework and integrated Enterprise Resource Planning system further enhance operational efficiency by improving supply-chain visibility and coordination across its global manufacturing network. These capabilities enable Jabil to optimize resource utilization, manage complex production programs and respond efficiently to changing customer requirements. Such operational flexibility should help the company navigate supply-chain disruptions, mitigate execution risks and sustain its competitive edge.

Story Continues

Disciplined Execution, Secular Trends Aid JBL

Jabil's continued focus on end-market diversification and disciplined operational execution is expected to support its long-term growth. The company targets limiting the contribution of any single product or product family to less than 5% of operating income or cash flows in a fiscal year. This strategy reduces dependence on individual products, limits concentration risks and provides greater stability to its earnings and cash flow profile.

Moreover, increasing investments in 5G infrastructure and accelerating cloud computing adoption present additional growth opportunities. Healthy demand across these markets, coupled with efficient supply-chain management and ongoing operational initiatives, should support Jabil's business performance. Its broad exposure to multiple industries also provides a cushion against macroeconomic volatility and geopolitical uncertainties. These factors, along with a disciplined approach to capital allocation and operational efficiency, bode well for Jabil's long-term profitability and shareholder value creation.

Estimate Revision Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Jabil's fiscal 2027 earnings has surged 34.6% to $17.61 per share over the past year, while the same for fiscal 2028 has increased 34.3% to $22.02. The positive estimate revision depicts bullish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

End Note

Jabil is bullish on its long-term prospects. The company is well-positioned to capitalize on growth opportunities in areas such as AI data center hardware, power and energy infrastructure, software-defined electric and hybrid vehicles, and healthcare. Strong margins and robust free cash flow are likely to enable continued investment in profitable growth and capital returns to shareholders.

The uptrend in estimate revisions further portrays positive sentiment about the stock's growth potential. JBL has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 20.1% and delivered a trailing four-quarter average earnings surprise of 5.1%. It has a VGM Score of B. Jabil carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

With a solid Zacks Rank and healthy fundamentals, Jabil appears primed for price appreciation in the future. Consequently, investors are likely to profit in the long run if they bet on this stock now.

news.Title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Meta Platforms Next?
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) is officially on board the stock-split train. The artificial intelligence (AI) hyperscaler and social media giant formally announced plans to create a new, nonvoting Class C stock. It will do this via a stock dividend distributed from existing Class A and Class B shares. When the dust settles, the move is effectively a 2-for-1 stock split.

Sorry to ruin the suspense, but yes, Meta is the next big tech company to split its stock . What does that mean for existing shareholders, and does the split make Meta stock a buy now? Here's everything you need to know.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The ins and outs of Meta's new stock split

Conventional stock splits are similar to slicing a pizza in more ways. The pizza itself remains the same size, but there are more, smaller slices to go around. It works the same for stock splits. The share price and per-share financials fall in proportion to the split ratio.

For instance, suppose you owned a share of company XYZ trading at $100 per share, with earnings per share of $10. Following a 2-for-1 split, you would instead own two shares trading at $50 each, each with earnings per share of $5.

Meta is essentially doing a 2-for-1 stock split by awarding one Class C share to shareholders for each Class A or Class B share they own. The value for Meta here is that this essentially creates a larger pool of stock it can award for stock-based compensation or other purposes, without diluting CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting control over the company. This will go into effect on Jan. 19, 2027.

Here's the real reason to buy Meta Platforms stock

Remember, stock splits generally don't create value on their own. The pie, or Meta in this case, remains the same size overall. But there are some really good reasons to buy Meta Platforms, or, at the very least, to consider it one of the biggest long-term winners in the AI space.

First, Meta is one of the few AI companies that can internally fund its AI capital expenditures thanks to its massive digital advertising business and social media platforms. Meta is selling bonds to raise capital, but it's a big positive that debt is secondary funding rather than the primary lever.

YCharts.

Additionally, Meta may have found the breakthrough AI product it was searching for with Muse, its consumer AI agent app. Muse is always on and can perform tasks for users, including transactions. It went viral shortly after its launch and remains near the top of app stores.

Story Continues

Given Meta's strong finances and blossoming Muse app, it's hard not to like the company's prospects, split or no split.

news.Title: Microchip Technology Inc (MCHP) (Q2 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Record Sales and 42% Growth ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Net Sales: $1.622 billion, up 9.2% sequentially and up 42.2% year-over-year; included ~$53 million of infrequent items not expected to repeat.

Non-GAAP Gross Margin: 66.5%, including $26.6 million in capacity underutilization charges.

GAAP Gross Margin: 65.9%.

Non-GAAP Operating Expenses: 27% of sales.

Non-GAAP Operating Income: 39.5% of sales.

Non-GAAP Net Income: $559.2 million.

Non-GAAP EPS: $0.97 per diluted share, $0.04 above the midpoint of guidance.

GAAP Net Income: $373.6 million, or $0.68 per share, including a $0.13 per share tax benefit from a valuation allowance release.

GAAP Operating Expenses: $603.5 million, including $90.2 million acquisition intangible amortization, $7.9 million special charges, $62.2 million share-based compensation, and $5.3 million other expenses.

Cash Flow from Operations: $419.2 million.

Adjusted Free Cash Flow: $377.1 million.

Cash and Investments: $457 million as of September 30, 2026.

Net Debt: Decreased by $31.7 million in the quarter; net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 2.36.

Adjusted EBITDA: $705.4 million, or 43.5% of net sales; trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA of $2.162 billion.

Inventory: $1.117 billion, or 184 days, up nine days sequentially; distributor inventory at 25 days, flat sequentially.

Capital Expenditures: $23.1 million in the quarter; ~$100 million expected for fiscal 2027.

Depreciation Expense: $36 million.

Non-GAAP Cash Tax Rate: 5.7% in the quarter; ~6.5% expected for fiscal 2027.

End Market Mix (ex-Licensing): Industrial 34.6%, Data Center 16.7%, Aerospace and Defense 16.1%, Automotive 14.2%, Communication 8.2%, Consumer Appliances 7.3%, Compute 2.9%.

End Market Growth (YoY): Industrial +50.3%, Data Center +55.7%, Aerospace and Defense +41%, Automotive +19.3%, Communication +43.5%, Consumer Appliances +26.7%, Compute -1.6%.

Data Center Business: Over $250 million in net sales in the September quarter; on track toward $1 billion in calendar 2026.

December Quarter Guidance: Net sales down 3% to up 1% (midpoint -1%, up 35.4% YoY); non-GAAP gross margin 64%-65%; non-GAAP operating expenses 26.5%-27% of sales; non-GAAP operating profit 37%-38.5% of sales; non-GAAP EPS $0.87-$0.95 (midpoint up 107% YoY).

Acquisition Contributions: Hailo expected to add ~$4 million and VORAGO ~$6 million to December quarter net sales.

Long-Term Model (Non-GAAP): 65% gross margin, 25% operating expense, 40% operating profit.

Story Continues

Release Date: November 05, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Net sales of $1.622 billion beat the high end of guidance, up 9.2% sequentially and 42.2% year-over-year.

Broad-based growth across end markets, with Industrial up 50.3%, Data Center up 55.7%, and Aerospace & Defense up 41% year-over-year.

Non-GAAP gross margin was 66.5%, operating margin 39.5%, and EPS of $0.97 exceeded the midpoint by $0.04.

Bookings were very strong with book-to-bill well above one, and backlog continued to build through October.

24 design wins for PCIe Gen 6 switches and retimers, up from 12 in the prior quarter, with ramps expected through 2027 and 2028.

Negative Points

December quarter guidance of down 3% to up 1% sequentially is below prior expectations due to $53 million of non-recurring September items and seasonal weakness.

Non-GAAP gross margin guided down to 64%-65% from 66.5%, as high-margin products are constrained and supplier price increases persist.

Supply chain constraints at foundries, OSATs, and internal fabs are stretching lead times to 6-32 weeks and leaving high-margin backlog unfulfilled.

Underutilization charges remain a drag, with no material improvement expected in the December quarter as backend utilization steps down.

Leverage remains elevated at 2.36x net debt to adjusted EBITDA, delaying plans to raise dividend or resume buybacks.

Q & A Highlights

Q : With December revenue guided below prior expectations and fab utilization lower despite strong bookings, is the shortfall due to downstream supply constraints, and does that give better visibility into the March quarter? A : CEO Steve Sanghi explained that lead times have stretched out and much of the high-margin advanced-product backlog cannot be fulfilled this quarter, pushing revenue into the March quarter. He noted the March backlog is much better than December's was at the same point, and while no formal guidance was given, he is hopeful March will be a stronger quarter.

Q : How should investors think about the PCIe Gen 6 and retimer design win ramp, and when does it become meaningful revenue? A : Sanghi said the company cannot dollarize the wins, but the parts entered production last quarter with sizable shipments this quarter that will increase every quarter. He expects nearly all 24 design wins (PCIe switches plus retimers) to be in production by the start of 2028, with the company winning roughly a design a week. CFO Eric Bjornholt clarified the 24 wins span both PCIe and retimer products.

Q : How should investors view the December quarter given the noisy September results and seasonality? A : Sanghi advised stripping out the $53 million of infrequent September items (licensing, distribution pricing, and a customer contract), which puts December product revenue up about 2.3% sequentially versus normal seasonality of down 3%-5%. Excluding roughly $10 million from the Hailo and VORAGO acquisitions, growth is about 1.5%, which he framed as evidence the underlying business remains healthy.

Q : What is driving the foundry, OSAT, and internal capacity constraints, and how is Microchip responding? A : Sanghi said demand exceeds available capacity industry-wide, with AI data center demand crowding out trailing-edge capacity at OSATs and foundries. Microchip is qualifying alternate OSATs, moving some production in-house, and securing incremental allocation each quarter, though requalification takes about six months. He suggested an AI deceleration would actually free up capacity and benefit Microchip.

Q : What is the outlook for gross margin given input cost increases from foundries and OSATs? A : Sanghi said the prior assumption of holding gross margin near 66% proved too aggressive, and the company is resetting expectations to its 65% long-term model. Another round of supplier price increases begins in January, and management plans to absorb costs rather than raise prices again so soon after the August increase, leaving some uncertainty on near-term margin.

Q : Is the data center market in a bubble, and how exposed is Microchip if it corrects? A : Sanghi stated plainly that data center is in a bubble and that the second derivative of growth must come down substantially. He stressed data center is only 16.7% of Microchip's business, half of which is broad-based products, and the Data Center Solutions unit is in a retooling phase regaining share with Gen 6, so a correction would affect Microchip far less than companies fully concentrated in data center.

Q : What is happening in the Industrial end market, which accelerated this quarter? A : Sanghi described Industrial as the broadest market segmentspanning factories, cities, lighting, robotics, medical, and farmingand noted it was the last segment to recover a few quarters ago. He attributed the 50.3% year-over-year growth to broad recovery plus new design wins across every area, making it difficult to isolate a single driver.

Q : How should investors think about underutilization charges and fab utilization going forward? A : Bjornholt said the improvement will not be linear; the company built finished goods last quarter and is slowing some assembly and test, so no large reduction in underutilization charges is expected this quarter. Sanghi added that utilization should improve as the company moves into a stronger March quarter and the typically strong June and September quarters, but not on a straight line.

Q : Are customers willing to build inventory given extended lead times? A : Sanghi said there is little appetite among customers to build inventory, and the company can barely get them to place orders against the new lead times. He likened repeated calls for more backlog to a "wolf is coming" warning that customers ignore until they are in trouble, at which point they rush to expedite orders.

Q : What is the status of the Hailo and VORAGO acquisitions and their impact on margins and OpEx? A : Bjornholt said both add OpEx, with Hailo investing heavily in R&D. Sanghi noted VORAGO carries above-corporate gross margins and is profitable but too small at $6 million to move the needle, while Hailo is unprofitable with high R&D but has a multi-hundred-million-dollar opportunity funnel. Hailo also accelerated Microchip's NPU roadmap by five years, leading to cancellation of two in-house NPU products.

Q : How is Microchip thinking about pricing philosophy and competitive dynamics? A : Sanghi said the company was deliberate about its August price increase after repairing customer relationships, and it does not want to push its luck with another near-term hike. He emphasized Microchip is a premium-price, high-quality supplier, noting its operating margin exceeds the gross margin of some competitors such as STMicro.

Q : When might Microchip resume returning cash to shareholders through dividends and buybacks? A : Bjornholt said the board wants leverage reduced further after the scare during the last downturn, with net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 2.36. He expects the dividend to stay flat for now, with the board evaluating capital returns as the company moves into the next fiscal year while continuing to bring leverage down over the next couple of quarters.

Q : Would the external capacity constraints prompt reconsideration of the internal versus external manufacturing mix or a new 300mm fab? A : Sanghi said Microchip remains an IDM biased toward in-house production and is bringing some displaced assembly and test work inside, though that takes about six months. news.Title: What Stabilus (STM) Said on Its Q4 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Stabilus SE? Here are five stocks we like better.

Stabilus lowered its 2030 target to €1.5 billion in revenue and a 12%–15% EBIT margin, from a previous goal of about €2 billion in sales, citing weaker automotive volumes and removing a potential acquisition from its plans.

Preliminary fiscal 2026 revenue fell to €1.197 billion from €1.296 billion, while adjusted EBIT declined to €124 million. The company recorded a €66.7 million goodwill impairment tied to weaker automotive and manufacturing-equipment prospects, particularly in North America.

Stabilus plans to diversify growth toward industrial automation, robotics, and door-actuation systems, while targeting €30 million–€32 million in annual savings from its transformation program. It also plans to propose a €0.22-per-share dividend to preserve funds for debt repayment.

Stabilus (ETR:STM) lowered its 2030 revenue target and reported a roughly €67 million goodwill impairment in its preliminary fiscal 2026 results, citing pressure on automotive production and manufacturing-equipment investment, particularly in North America.

Chief Executive Michael Büchsner said the company now targets €1.5 billion in revenue and an EBIT margin of 12% to 15% in 2030. Its previous target was approximately €2 billion in sales with a margin of up to 15%.

→ Apple's Earnings Beat Comes With a Catch for Investors Heading Into the Holidays

The revision reflects weaker automotive volumes and the removal, for now, of a potential acquisition in 2028 or 2029 from the company's planning, Büchsner said. He added that a stronger-than-expected fourth quarter, driven mainly by industrial business, helped lift the preliminary full-year adjusted EBIT margin to 10.4%.

Revenue and margins decline

Preliminary fiscal 2026 revenue was €1.197 billion, down from €1.296 billion a year earlier. Organic revenue declined 5.7%, while currency effects reduced revenue by 1.6% and the divestment of Fabreeka and Tech Products accounted for a further 0.3% decline, according to Büchsner.

→ Are the Fears Around Alphabet's Search Slowdown Warranted?

Automotive sales faced particular pressure in Asia-Pacific and the Americas. Büchsner said lower production volumes at customers, especially in China and North America, weighed on sales of the company's automotive Powerise products.

Adjusted EBIT fell to €124 million from €142 million, and the adjusted EBIT margin declined from 11%. Büchsner said the fourth-quarter industrial performance helped the company exceed its earlier expectation of a margin around 10%.

Story Continues

→ Palantir's $2.3 Billion Quarter Puts Its Premium Valuation to the Test

Net profit rose 8.3% to €26.2 million, despite the impairment. The figure included a €44.7 million gain from the sale of Fabreeka and Tech Products, offset in part by a €66.7 million goodwill write-down.

Stabilus plans to propose a dividend of €0.22 per share. Büchsner said the proposal is at the lower end of the company's policy of distributing 20% to 40% of net profit, preserving funds to repay debt.

North American equipment weakness drives impairment

Büchsner said the impairment followed a goodwill test incorporating weaker conditions in automotive and automotive manufacturing equipment, particularly in the Americas. Customers, including major North American automakers, have been cautious about investment, he said.

Responding to a question from Berenberg analyst Yasmin Steilen about the DESTACO acquisition, Büchsner said expected synergies were on track and attributed the impairment to lower sales assumptions for automotive-related manufacturing equipment in North America.

He said automotive-related applications currently account for approximately 35% to 40% of automation-equipment sales. Stabilus aims to reduce that share and expand its industrial business as part of its 2030 strategy.

Growth plans and restructuring

The revised 2030 plan assumes a broadly flat automotive market, with potential vehicle-production growth of 1% to 2%, Büchsner said. Stabilus expects door-actuation systems to help it grow faster than that market, with annual sales of €75 million to €100 million in 2030, compared with approximately €25 million to €30 million currently.

On the industrial side, Büchsner said the company expects to grow 2 to 3 percentage points faster than assumed GDP growth of 3% to 3.2%, supported by automation equipment, Industrial Powerise and robotics. He said Stabilus had won its first humanoid-robotics contract and sees that business potentially reaching €20 million to €30 million in the next two to three years.

The company's transformation program generated approximately €17 million to €18 million in savings in fiscal 2026, Büchsner said. He confirmed that annual savings of approximately €30 million to €32 million, expected as the measures take full effect, remain on track and are included in the 2030 targets.

Stabilus plans to publish confirmed results and discuss fiscal 2027 guidance on December 7.

About Stabilus (ETR:STM)

Stabilus SE, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the manufacture and sale of gas springs, dampers, vibration isolation products, and electric tailgate opening and closing equipment in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, North and South America, the Asia-Pacific, and internationally. Its products are used in automotive, navy and railways, commercial vehicles, aerospace, marine and rail, energy and construction, mechanical engineering, industrial machinery and automation, health, recreation, leisure, and furniture industries.

news.Title: 台韓二大「權王」比一比！三星暴跌6%慘過台積電
news.Content:
台韓二大「權王」比一比！亞洲AI股遇上黑色星期五，台韓都是AI人工智慧主要受惠股市，昨天美費城半導體暴跌12%，台積電（2330）是全球最大半導體廠， 三星電子（Samsung Electronics） 為全球第一大記憶體大廠，一開盤兩檔通通跌破一成，但護國神山靠散戶與內資大舉進場，最後強拉一半，跌幅剩不到4.7%，相比韓股同為第一大權值比重的三星電子單日跌幅高達6.35%，表現慘輸台積電。

三星今暴跌6.35%慘過台積電的4.7%

韓股今（6）日一度大跌8.7%，其中身為全球第一大記憶體大廠、韓股第一大權值股的三星電子（Samsung Electronics），11月占韓股比重約達三成左右，一開盤跌破20萬韓元大關，以最低點17萬9200韓元開出，終場收在188700韓元。

三星今日在AI股災日單日下跌1.28萬韓元，跌幅6.35%，還高於韓股最終收跌的6.02%幅度。

相較之下，台積電身為護國神山，占台股約有四成的權重，今早一度也是以跌停板2020元、下跌220元開出，最後只下跌105元，跌幅4.69%顯然要比三星要來得輕微一些，這一波AI回檔修正，最慘的還不是台積電。

三星股價自高峰來已腰斬 台積電跌不到二成

三星今年股價最高峰在6月18日時的36.25萬韓元，股價至今跌了48%近腰斬。而台積電從今年10月初最高峰2580天價下跌至今日收盤，累計共下跌了17.2%，神山也是相對輕微。

台積電在美掛牌的ADR昨晚雖然跌破2兆美元大關，但仍以1.83兆美元維持住全球第六大市值寶座，而三星過去曾居全球第11大市值表現，一度問鼎前十強，並成為繼台積電後首度市值破兆美元的亞洲公司，但如今股價大跌，市值跌破兆美元大關，只剩9273億美元掉到第15名位置。

葉憶如／財經特派記者組長，主跑金管會、金控壽險、航空等

news.Title: What IREN (IREN) Said on Its Q1 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in IREN Limited? Here are five stocks we like better.

AI Cloud revenue surged 183% sequentially to $200 million , lifting total revenue 66% to $228 million. IREN's adjusted EBITDA margin improved to about 29%, while it reported a net loss of $263 million.

IREN pushed its target of bringing more than $4 billion in annualized operating revenue online from year-end to January, with a possible delay to late February. The shift follows a Microsoft-requested network redesign for 200 megawatts of capacity and potential supplier delays.

IREN plans to spend about $15 billion in the rest of fiscal 2027, pacing investment based on capital-market conditions rather than weak demand. New contracts include customer prepayments covering about 90% of related GPU costs, while the company cited roughly $12 billion to $15 billion in potential funding sources.

Riot's $28B Lease Shows Why Location and Contracts Matter in AI

IREN (NASDAQ:IREN) reported a nearly threefold increase in AI Cloud revenue for its fiscal first quarter, but pushed back its target for bringing more than $4 billion of annualized operating revenue online, citing a customer-requested design change and supplier timing.

Co-Founder and Co-CEO Daniel Roberts said the company is now targeting January for the milestone, previously expected by year-end. It could slip to the end of February if suppliers are late, he said. The capacity supporting the target is fully funded, according to management.

→ Apple's Earnings Beat Comes With a Catch for Investors Heading Into the Holidays

Google's Credit Backstop May Be TeraWulf's Biggest Advantage

The company also reduced its planned capital spending for the remainder of fiscal 2027. Roberts said IREN was pacing investment in response to financial market conditions, rather than a lack of customer demand.

AI Cloud Growth Drives Revenue

AI Cloud revenue rose 183% from the prior quarter to $200 million in the September quarter, Chief Financial Officer Anthony Lewis said. Total revenue increased 66% sequentially to $228 million, while Bitcoin mining revenue fell to $28 million as IREN continued removing mining hardware ahead of GPU installations.

→ Amazon Has Erased Its Earnings Sell-Off, But Is the Biggest Opportunity Still Ahead?

The AI Buildout Is Only 15% Complete—Here Is Where the Next Dollar Actually Goes

Lewis said the company aims to substantially complete that transition by the end of the December quarter. IREN reported a net loss of $263 million for the September quarter.

Story Continues

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization were $66 million, with the adjusted EBITDA margin rising to about 29% from 14% in the prior quarter. AI Cloud gross margin before depreciation and amortization remained at 86%.

→ Palantir's $2.3 Billion Quarter Puts Its Premium Valuation to the Test

IREN exited September with $1 billion of operating annualized recurring revenue, or ARR. Lewis said the company expects to recognize one quarter of that amount as revenue in the December quarter, but does not expect a material contribution from incremental Horizon and Mackenzie capacity during the period. Cash operating expenses, including selling, general and administrative costs and research and development, are expected to rise by approximately $50 million to $60 million sequentially.

Microsoft Deployment Timeline Shifts

Roberts said IREN handed over Horizon 1 to Microsoft in August. Microsoft subsequently requested a reconfiguration and upgrade of network infrastructure to enable 200 megawatts of capacity to serve newer frontier AI models, he said.

The incremental capital cost of the network upgrade is immaterial relative to the broader cluster, Roberts said, describing the work as involving new cables, labor and a different implementation method. He said Horizon 2 was built and undergoing commissioning, Horizon 3 had its GPUs on site, and GPUs for Horizon 4 were due to arrive in the coming weeks.

IREN's revenue backlog exceeded $20 billion, Roberts said, with two-thirds tied to investment-grade customers. Lewis identified Microsoft and NVIDIA as the investment-grade counterparties behind that share.

Spending Plan and Funding

IREN spent approximately $5 billion on capital expenditures during the quarter and plans to spend about $15 billion during the remainder of fiscal 2027, Lewis said. The updated plan spreads deployment of Childress air-cooled capacity across calendar 2027 rather than concentrating it earlier in the year.

The company had approximately $9 billion in cash and undrawn commitments available to fund growth, leaving $6 billion of additional planned capital expenditure to be funded, Lewis said. Management outlined an indicative $12 billion to $15 billion of potential funding sources, including data center financing, GPU prepayments and financing, and corporate-level initiatives. That estimate excludes potential convertible and equity financing.

At September 30, IREN reported $5.8 billion in cash, including $2.3 billion of restricted cash primarily set aside for GPU deployments. Total debt was $10.2 billion. Lewis said the company's $20.6 billion of total assets included $6 billion of unencumbered data center assets.

Roberts said the spending reduction reflected the availability and cost of capital. "We are not going to grow at all costs," he said, adding that ownership of its infrastructure gives IREN flexibility over the pace of development.

New Contracts and GPU Pricing

Since quarter-end, IREN signed a five-year contract at $22 million of annualized revenue per megawatt of IT load, with a customer prepayment covering approximately 90% of the related GPU capital expenditure, Roberts said. It also signed a shorter-duration contract at more than $40 million per megawatt and expanded an existing agreement with a leading frontier AI lab.

Roberts said the company had re-contracted older H100 GPUs at double their original pricing. Chief Commercial Officer Kent Draper said the new pricing was locked in for a multi-year term.

During the quarter, three-year contracts were priced at $19 million to $23 million per megawatt, while five-year pricing was approximately $17 million, Lewis said. He added that customer prepayments and equipment financing can reduce the corporate capital needed for deployments, although returns and payback periods vary by contract.

Looking ahead, IREN is targeting 0.8 gigawatts of operating capacity by the end of calendar 2027. Roberts said the company has more than 5 gigawatts of secured power and over 35 gigawatts in development, while cautioning that many development projects are early-stage and not all will result in grid connection agreements.

About IREN (NASDAQ:IREN)

IREN Limited, formerly known as Iris Energy Limited, is a data center infrastructure company focused on bitcoin mining and high-performance computing. The company develops and operates data centers designed to support energy-intensive computing applications, including bitcoin mining and artificial intelligence (AI) cloud services.

IREN's operations are supported by company-owned electrical infrastructure, data centers and computing hardware. Its bitcoin mining business uses specialized application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) machines, while its AI cloud offering is designed to provide access to advanced computing resources for AI development and other high-performance computing workloads.

Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Sydney, Australia, IREN has developed data center operations in North America, including facilities in British Columbia, Canada, and Texas.
