news.Title: Arm Holdings' Q2 Earnings Call Centers on AGI CPU Expansion
news.Content:
Arm Holdings plc ARM highlighted stronger AGI CPU demand on its second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call, backed by customer orders and supply commitments. Management also emphasized data center adoption.

The company reported revenues of $1.44 billion compared with the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.37 billion. Non-GAAP earnings of $0.52 per share topped the $0.48 estimate, underpinning its expansion plans.

ARM Holdings PLC Sponsored ADR Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

ARM Holdings PLC Sponsored ADR price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | ARM Holdings PLC Sponsored ADR Quote

Arm Sees Greater AGI CPU Revenue Potential

CEO Rene Haas said that customer orders and improved supply have strengthened confidence in generating up to $2 billion of AGI CPU revenues across fiscal 2027 and 2028. Shipments are targeted for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027.

Responding to StoneX, Haas identified Meta as the principal customer but confirmed additional buyers. Securing wafers, substrates, testing capacity and memory remains critical to deliveries.

CFO Jason Child told Susquehanna that third-quarter shipments would be minimal, if any. Answering Wells Fargo, Child projected first-generation AGI CPU gross margins around 30%-40%, with a longer-term target above 50% on later designs. Haas cited some pricing flexibility to offset higher component costs.

ARM Expects Data Center Share Gains to Continue

Haas said that Arm-based servers held more than 50% market share at top hyperscalers in calendar 2025, up from 15% in 2024. He expects that share to exceed 60% by the end of 2026.

Data center royalties doubled year over year, with management anticipating triple-digit growth in coming years. Haas cited Amazon, Google, Microsoft and NVIDIA as leading contributors, alongside Oracle's plan to offer AGI CPU instances in 2027.

A William Blair analyst pressed Haas on competition with x86 processors. Haas stressed system efficiency and design flexibility, clarifying that its AGI CPU benchmark compared against an AMD processor preceding the newer Venice generation.

Arm's Licensing Pipeline Supports Future Royalties

Child said that license and other revenues rose 50% year over year to $773 million, about $100 million above management's forecast, as customers accelerated longer-term commitments. The SoftBank agreement contributed $209 million.

The quarter included three new Arm Total Access agreements and four compute subsystem licenses, split between data center and smartphone applications. Active Total Access subscriptions exceeded 60, supporting future royalty opportunities.

Story Continues

Asked by Morgan Stanley whether the higher licensing level was sustainable, Child declined to establish a new quarterly baseline. He described a stronger-than-expected pipeline and said agreements can produce royalties within 12 to 24 months.

ARM Sees Contrasting Trends Beyond the Cloud

Child said that edge AI royalties were roughly flat year over year as higher memory prices pressured lower- and midrange smartphone shipments. Higher Armv9 and subsystem royalty rates offset weaker volumes.

In response to Bank of America, Child said that smartphone unit expectations for next year were broadly flat. Nevertheless, he anticipated at least double-digit growth in Arm's mobile business, supported by further adoption of higher-value technology.

Physical AI royalties grew 50% year over year, driven by automotive and robotics demand. Haas highlighted Arm Total Design for physical AI, involving more than 80 companies.

Arm Details Q3 Expectations and Investment Priorities

For third-quarter fiscal 2027, Child projected revenues of $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million, and non-GAAP earnings of 56 cents per share, plus or minus four cents.

He expects licensing revenue growth of slightly more than 50% year over year. Royalties are expected to rise by low teens sequentially but grow only low single digits year over year, with cloud and physical AI strength offset by smartphone weakness.

Non-GAAP operating expenses are projected at approximately $825 million as engineering investment continues. Last quarter, expenses rose 19% to $774 million, while the non-GAAP operating margin reached 44.2%.

ARM Keeps Two Business Models in View

Haas framed ARM's direction around two complementary businesses: licensing intellectual property to chip designers and selling its own AGI CPU silicon. Both share its architecture and developer ecosystem.

Management's priorities remain expanding silicon supply, deepening licensing relationships and sustaining research investment. Memory costs and smartphone demand remain constraints.

What ARM's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

ARM carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) at present, a neutral near-term rating. Its Growth Score of A and Momentum Score of A indicate favorable traits, while its Value Score of F indicates weaker valuation appeal. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Its VGM Score of C trails the A or B scores preferred in Zacks' screening framework. The Zacks Rank may change as analyst earnings estimates are revised following the latest results.

news.Title: Jim Cramer sends clear signal on Apple and Palantir stock
news.Content:
Jim Cramer thinks investors have gone too far.

As the tech slump dragged into a new week, the CNBC host said in a post on X that the negativity around Marvell, Apple, and Palantir "is pretty thick," adding, "No matter what they say, it isn't enough."

He made the remark as all three stocks slid on Nov. 2.

His comments landed in a rough market. Chip and memory stocks have lost about $3.7 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, and Intel suffered its worst day since 1974 on Oct. 30, falling nearly 29% after a disappointing forecast.

The chip group shed more than $400 billion on Nov. 2 alone, as reported by Yahoo Finance . In a market this nervous, even good news is getting sold.

Marvell's mega-deal spooks investors

Marvell took the hardest hit. Its shares fell sharply on Nov. 2 after it announced an all-stock deal to buy Lumentum for $115 billion, and the stock has pulled back significantly since reports of the deal surfaced on Oct. 28.

Also read: Jim Cramer has a new way of thinking about the biggest tech stocks

The size of the bet explains part of the worry. Lumentum holders will get 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own, leaving them with roughly a third of the combined company, and the deal is more than 10 times bigger than Marvell's previous largest purchase.

Marvell CEO Matt Murphy acknowledged that in a stock deal, the buyer's share price is the real price tag. "You take more risk when you do it," he said .

Murphy is not backing away. Marvell wants Lumentum's optical connectivity technology, which links the chips used to train and run large language models.

He called the deal "a double-down on supporting Nvidia, who is the ecosystem leader in this area." Meanwhile, investors appeared to view Marvell as overpaid, sending Lumentum down almost 19% after its stock had soared more than 450% over the past year.

The deal's final value will depend on Marvell's share price when it closes, according to CNBC . The deal is not expected to close until the first half of 2028.

Apple beats, but its memory costs bite

Apple's numbers were good. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue hit $114.48 billion and earnings came to $2.10 a share, both ahead of Wall Street's forecasts.

It wrapped up what Apple called its strongest fiscal year on record. Even so, the stock drifted lower after hours, with investors fixated on slowing growth.

What really spooked investors was the guidance. Apple expects a gross margin of 45% to 46% in the December quarter, down from 47.9%, and blamed most of that drop on pricier memory chips, Reuters reported .

Story Continues

Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, pointed out the irony in a post on X : The same DRAM boom helping Micron and SK Hynix is pinching Apple right as it leans into on-device AI.

CEO John Ternus called the memory situation "unprecedented" on his first earnings call, MacRumors noted. Still, Apple expects December-quarter revenue to grow 7% to 10%, which would make it the company's best quarter on record.

Services also hit a quarterly record of $31.6 billion, though Mac and iPad supply will stay tight.

The memory squeeze is good news for chipmakers. SK Hynix said DRAM prices rose in the high 20s percent from the second quarter, helping it post a record operating profit, while DRAM shipments grew about 10%, according to its Q3 2026 earnings .

What fills a memory maker's pockets drains Apple's margins.

Palantir's bookings spark doubts

Palantir also beat on both lines in the third quarter. Revenue came in at $2.31 billion against estimates of $2.18 billion, and adjusted earnings were 44 cents a share against 41 cents, yet the stock closed 3% lower.

The growth itself was huge. It was Palantir's first quarter above $2 billion. Revenue rose 96% from a year earlier, and U.S. commercial revenue climbed 148% to $984 million, passing the $953 million from U.S. government work for the first time, as reported by TechCrunch .

Investors zeroed in on bookings instead. U.S. commercial total contract value fell to $1.46 billion from a record $2.13 billion in the prior quarter. Boloor said in a separate post on X that he genuinely does not think anyone knows how high the ceiling is for this business.

More Jim Cramer:

Jim Cramer says Scott Bessent is fighting a flood with one finger

Jim Cramer spots something investors may be missing on Wall Street

Jim Cramer calls one major data center play a no-brainer buy

Karp had an explanation for the slowdown. He said customers are adopting faster but signing shorter contracts, with "an ability to expand that contract dramatically," and Palantir raised its full-year revenue guidance.

That suggests the slowdown may reflect how deals are being structured rather than weaker demand.

Related: Jim Cramer's net worth: How much does 'Mad Money's' stock-picking superhost make?

AI spending fears hang over tech

The bigger backdrop is anxiety about AI spending. Last week's two-day rout erased hundreds of billions in market value from Alphabet and Intel as investors punished cash-draining AI investment.

That set a sour tone heading into the Nov. 2 session.

Alphabet's report showed why. Its free cash flow came in at negative $9.07 billion in the third quarter, following a negative $5.86 billion in the second, while capital spending reached about $51.4 billion.

The stock then suffered its worst post-earnings sell-off on record, though some managers still see value, citing strong Google Cloud growth and a rapidly expanding order backlog.

That is the kind of disconnect Cramer is pointing to at Apple, Palantir, and Marvell, where solid results are being drowned out by fear.

Related: Jim Cramer has a new way of thinking about the biggest tech stocks

news.Title: Credo and Oracle Drive AI Optical Innovation: Is CRDO Set to Benefit?
news.Content:
Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd . CRDO recently achieved a breakthrough with Oracle ORCL by securing Open Compute Project (OCP) approval for two new specifications designed to improve optical connectivity and reliability in AI data centers. The development highlights Credo's growing role in addressing a critical challenge of maintaining reliable, high-speed connections across increasingly massive computing clusters facing next-generation AI infrastructure. The partnership with Oracle is likely to strengthen its position in the optical connectivity ecosystem while supporting the broader industry's transition toward more reliable AI infrastructure.

Established in January 2026, the workstream is co-led by Credo and Oracle. Its primary objective is to establish a common software interface that enables optical transceivers and host systems to exchange detailed connection health information. The two approved specifications standardize optical link-health monitoring, telemetry sharing, event tracking and automated fault responses, while enabling optical DSPs to exchange out-of-band information without disrupting network traffic. Credo contributed its ZeroFlap host specification as the technical foundation. Developed with input from the broader OCP Community, the standards could support wider adoption among hardware manufacturers, data center operators and technology providers.

Furthermore, CRDO is helping shape next-generation AI data center connectivity through an OCP workstream targeting 2027 approval for micro-emitter optics specifications. It recently announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream within the OCP Community. The initiative brings together optical technology providers, connectivity specialists and a leading hyperscaler to set specifications for a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. Also, in September, Credo launched 224G ZeroFlap optical transceivers supporting 1.6T port speeds and AI architectures.

However, competition in high-speed connectivity from key semiconductor and optical networking players like Marvell Technology MRVL and Astera Labs ALAB remains intense.

CRDO vs. Rivals: Assessing Its Connectivity Advantage

Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum aims to create a leading AI connectivity provider by combining complementary expertise in optical, photonics and electrical technologies. The deal is expected to accelerate innovation in NPO, CPO and integrated AI data center solutions, expand manufacturing capacity and strengthen end-to-end product offerings. With a projected $550 billion addressable market by 2030, the combined company expects to generate more than $1 billion in synergies, accelerate growth and strengthen its competitive position through deeper integration and scale. Expanded NVIDIA partnership aligns Marvell's roadmap more closely with next-generation AI architectures, extending its reach across optics, NVLink Fusion integration and AI-RAN platforms.

Story Continues

ALAB is expanding into optical connectivity with its first Smart Optical Drivers and TIAs for PCIe Gen 7 scale-up networks, targeting NPO and future CPO applications. It plans to begin sampling with hyperscalers and OEMs, with initial revenue expected in late 2027 and CPO volumes ramping in 2028–2029. With a projected $40 billion scale-up optical interconnect market by 2030, Astera aims to capture more content per XPU through vertically integrated optical components, engines and fabric switches. For the fourth quarter, management forecast revenue of $730-$750 million, noting continued supply constraints in wafers, power and memory and limited visibility into customer deployment timelines.

CRDO's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

CRDO's shares have slumped 38.2% in the past month compared with the Electronics-Semiconductors industry's fall of 19.5%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales ratio, CRDO is trading at 8.11, higher than the Electronics-Semiconductors industry's multiple of 3.14.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CRDO earnings for fiscal 2027 has remained unchanged over the past 60 days.

CRDO currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

December Nasdaq 100 E-Mini futures (NQZ26) are down -0.67% this morning as investors continued to dump chipmakers and other AI-related stocks following the Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections.

Chip and AI infrastructure stocks slid in pre-market trading, extending yesterday's slump amid concerns that the Democrats' election sweep could bring tighter U.S. data center regulations and weaken demand. Adding to the pressure, Qualcomm (QCOM) plunged more than -8% after issuing soft FQ1 adjusted EPS guidance, while Arm Holdings (ARM) fell over -5% as its FQ3 revenue forecast disappointed investors.

WTI crude prices edged higher on Thursday, stabilizing after a sharp drop in the previous session. Still, the U.S. benchmark hovered near two-month lows amid speculation that the Democratic sweep could speed up efforts to end the Middle East conflict. Treasuries were mixed.

Looking ahead, investors are awaiting a new wave of U.S. economic data and corporate earnings reports, along with remarks from Federal Reserve officials.

In yesterday's trading session, Wall Street's three main equity benchmarks ended sharply higher as oil prices plunged and investors wagered that a divided government in Washington would benefit stocks. Most members of the Magnificent Seven rallied, with Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon.com (AMZN) climbing over +6%. Also, healthcare stocks popped amid speculation that the Democratic-controlled Congress could reverse the Medicaid cuts included in last year's tax and spending bill, with Centene (CNC) jumping over +12% and HCA Healthcare (HCA) surging more than +10%. In addition, Block (XYZ) soared over +15% and was among the top percentage gainers in the S&P 500 after the fintech firm posted upbeat Q3 results and raised its full-year guidance. On the bearish side, chip and AI infrastructure stocks sank, with Sandisk (SNDK) and Marvell Technology (MRVL) plunging over -7%.

Story Continues

Economic data released on Wednesday were mostly better than expected, supporting equities. The ADP National Employment Report showed that U.S. private-sector payrolls rose by 86K in October, stronger than expectations of 67K. Also, the U.S. trade deficit unexpectedly narrowed to -$105.0 billion in September, compared with expectations for a widening to -$107.9 billion. At the same time, the U.S. ISM services index fell to 54.5 in October, slightly below expectations of 54.8, but remained comfortably above the 50 level separating expansion from contraction.

"U.S. stocks are set for gains into year-end as the election removes a source of uncertainty, earnings remain strong, and lackluster investor positioning leaves room for renewed buying," according to Citadel Securities' Scott Rubner.

Preliminary U.S. unit labor costs and nonfarm productivity data will also be in focus today. Economists forecast Q3 unit labor costs to rise +0.3% q/q and nonfarm productivity to climb +2.8% q/q, compared with the second-quarter figures of +1.2% q/q and +1.4% q/q, respectively.

In addition, market participants will parse comments from Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan today.

U.S. rate futures are currently pricing in a 79.2% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike and a 20.8% probability of no rate change at the December FOMC meeting.

In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is at 4.88%, down -0.10%.

The Euro Stoxx 50 Index is up +0.48% this morning, extending gains from the previous session that were fueled by the Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections. Mining stocks led the advance on Thursday, buoyed by higher metal prices and a post-earnings rally in ArcelorMittal shares. Travel and leisure stocks also climbed on hopes that the Democrats' victory in the U.S. midterms could speed up efforts to end the war in Iran, which would drive down oil prices, lower fuel costs, and boost travel demand. In addition, bank stocks advanced. At the same time, defense stocks slid, with Rheinmetall (RHM.D.DX) tumbling over -16% after it cut its full-year sales guidance. Data released on Thursday showed that German monthly factory orders rose in September, partly recovering from August's sharp decline. Separate data showed that French monthly industrial production unexpectedly fell in September. Meanwhile, Norway's Norges Bank kept its benchmark rate unchanged at 4.50% on Thursday, as widely expected, but left the door open to additional rate hikes if inflation stayed elevated. Investor focus now turns to the Bank of England's interest-rate decision. The BOE is widely expected to raise its key rate by 25 basis points to 4.00% later today, which would mark its first hike in more than three years, as policymakers seek to prevent persistently high energy prices from triggering second-round inflation effects. In other corporate news, Air France-KLM (AF.P.DX) surged over +11% after the company posted better-than-expected Q3 operating profit.

Germany's Factory Orders, France's Industrial Production, and Eurozone's PPI data were released today.

The German September Factory Orders rose +4.4% m/m, weaker than expectations of +4.6% m/m.

The French September Industrial Production unexpectedly fell -0.5% m/m, weaker than expectations of +0.3% m/m.

Eurozone September PPI rose +2.5% m/m and +11.1% y/y, compared to expectations of +2.5% m/m and +10.9% y/y.

Asian stock markets today closed mixed. China's Shanghai Composite Index ($CHSC) closed up +0.10%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index ($NKY) closed down -1.79%.

China's Shanghai Composite Index closed slightly higher today, supported by a rotation trade sparked by the U.S. midterm elections. Gold-related stocks rallied on Thursday as the precious metal regained momentum, buoyed by lower oil prices and Treasury yields. Renewables stocks also jumped, extending their rally as investors viewed the Democratic Party's sweep in the U.S. midterms as a positive development for the industry. In addition, semiconductor stocks climbed, bucking a selloff among their regional peers. However, gains in the benchmark index were capped by declines in energy and optical communications stocks. Morningstar analysts said on Thursday that "China and Hong Kong remain relatively attractive" following an October correction. Meanwhile, Hong Kong stocks jumped on Thursday as investors rotated into beaten-down internet giants. Alibaba Group climbed over +8%, while Tencent Holdings surged more than +7%. Elsewhere, Reuters reported on Thursday that flash-memory chipmaker Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. suspended plans for its Shanghai IPO after Beijing tightened approvals for share offerings in the wake of October's stock market rout.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index closed sharply lower today, dragged down by a steep selloff in the technology sector. Chip and other AI-related stocks cratered on Thursday, tracking an overnight slump in their U.S. peers as investors feared that Democratic control of Congress could bring tighter regulation of data centers. Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest tanked over -14%, memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings sank more than -13%, and tech investor SoftBank Group fell over -6%, weighing heavily on the Nikkei. At the same time, automobile stocks surged as investors rotated out of tech shares and into consumer-oriented names, with the sector getting an additional boost from a jump in Toyota Motor shares. Toyota Motor popped over +16% after the automaker raised its full-year profit guidance, citing strong demand for its hybrid vehicles. The so-called stock-rotation trade also lifted real estate and healthcare shares. Meanwhile, minutes from the Bank of Japan's September meeting released on Thursday showed that policymakers saw the need to continue raising interest rates, with some signaling the possibility of a faster pace of tightening. Many BOJ board members flagged a growing likelihood that consumer inflation would accelerate starting in early autumn, noting that rising costs were increasingly being passed on to consumers and that price increases were planned for more food and beverage items than in typical years. On the economic front, a survey showed that Japan's services sector grew modestly in October as business activity and new orders both increased at a slightly faster pace. Investor attention now shifts to Japan's September wage data and a speech from BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda, both scheduled for Friday. The Nikkei Volatility Index, which takes into account the implied volatility of Nikkei 225 options, closed up +34.35% at 33.56.

The Japanese October S&P Global Services PMI was revised downward to 51.7 from the preliminary reading of 52.0.

news.Title: Better Foundry Stock: Taiwan Semiconductor vs. Intel
news.Content:
Today, most companies that develop logic chips, like graphics processing units (GPUs) and central processing units (CPUs), use what is known as a fabless model. This simply means that they outsource the manufacturing of their chips to a third party. Two of the largest foundries in the world today are Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) and Intel (NASDAQ: INTC), and the better foundry stock to own, in my view, is an easy choice: it's TSMC by a wide margin.

Chip manufacturing is a capex -heavy, complex business. That is why so many chipmakers use third-party foundries. There is a constant push in the semiconductor industry to densify chips to make them more powerful and energy-efficient. This requires both expensive extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment and technological expertise to achieve high yields.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

At the same time, the chip manufacturing business requires both high utilization and scale. Fabs (chip manufacturing facilities) need to be running near full capacity to be profitable and attain good margins. Meanwhile, fixed costs need to be spread out across a large manufacturing base. This all gives a clear edge to TSMC.

TSMC: The foundry leader

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing is the largest foundry in the world and the one that has enjoyed the most success. Its expertise in manufacturing advanced logic chips is second to none, and it has been able to shrink node sizes (increase density) and achieve high yields (few defects) better than rivals Intel and Samsung . This has given TSMC a near monopoly on advanced chip manufacturing.

The company's scale is also unmatched, with fabs in Taiwan, Japan, and the U.S., and it is aggressively ramping up its own capex to increase capacity to meet the growing needs of its customers. Importantly, it is also a leader in advanced packaging, which allows it to integrate AI processors and high bandwidth memory (HBM) into a single package, improving data-transfer speeds and overall computing performance.

TSMC's position in the market has made it an integral part of the semiconductor supply chain and a close partner to chip designers like Nvidia , Broadcom , and Advanced Micro Devices . It has also given TSMC strong pricing power, which has helped it steadily improve its gross margins .

Story Continues

Intel: Playing catch-up

Intel is one of the few companies that does much of its chip manufacturing internally, although it also uses TSMC for certain chip designs and components. Meanwhile, Intel has aggressively expanded its fab footprint in an attempt to offer third-party manufacturing services. However, this strategy does have some drawbacks.

The biggest is that Intel is not an independent third-party foundry. Because it designs and makes its own chips, there are issues with customer trust and with other chip companies having to turn over important IP (intellectual property). In addition, the company has struggled to achieve the high yields that could attract customers to its platform.

To top it off, Intel has spent a massive amount on capex to build new fabs while playing catch-up to TSMC and needing high utilization rates to reach profitability. It hasn't been able to achieve these necessary utilization rates, and its foundry segment has been a major drag on its operations.

While Intel has recently seen some momentum in its data center chip business, largely due to the rise of agentic AI and the need for more CPUs, the company's stock took a major hit when it issued weaker-than-expected guidance due to the struggling PC market. Meanwhile, the company's server CPU business, while a growth driver, is expected to continue to lose share to AMD, ARM Holdings , and ARM-based custom chips in the coming years.

TSMC is the better buy

TSMC is both the better company and the cheaper stock. It trades at a forward P/E of around 17 times 2027 analyst estimates compared to 32 times for Intel. While Intel does have the opportunity to leverage its foundry business and help it become a growth driver, whether this will happen is still a big unknown.

TSM PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

As such, I'd stick with TSMC as the foundry stock to buy.

MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-05 17:15:10 數位內容中心 發佈

中國A股今(5)日延續偏強回升走勢，上證指數收於3689.91點，上漲0.1%，日K連二紅；深證成指收於11471.09點，上漲1.19%；創業板指收於2566.80點，上漲0.87%；科創50指數收於1286.68點，上漲1.68%，表現最強勁。

兩市成交額2兆1,179億元(人民幣,下同)，連續第二個交易日站上2兆元，市場交投熱度維持高檔。盤面上，科創50維持明顯強勢，半導體、CPO與AI相關方向同步活躍，帶動科技股情緒回暖；盤中雖一度衝高後震盪，但收盤仍守住漲勢，成為主要指數中的領漲角色。新能源族群延續強勢，太陽能概念領漲，鈞達股份、賽伍技術、歐晶科技、協鑫集成漲停。

貴金屬族群同樣活躍，四川黃金、赤峰黃金、興業銀錫、曉程科技等跟漲；文化傳媒、AI漫劇與短劇概念延續熱度，福石控股、吉視傳媒、浙文互聯、引力傳媒、博納影業與浙文影業均收漲停。相對之下，煤炭、油氣與銀行類股偏弱，中煤能源、中國神華、兗礦能源與中國海油承壓，傳統權值股表現落後。

《日股》鎧俠重挫逾15% 日經收跌0.33%

黃金之外：通膨新常態催生大宗商品超級循環

news.Title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Analog Devices, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Texas Instruments and NVIDIA
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 5, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Analog Devices ADI, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. TSM, Texas Instruments TXN and NVIDIA Corp. NVDA.

Here are highlights from Wednesday's Analyst Blog:

4 Semiconductor Stocks to Buy as Q3 Sales Soar on Robust AI Demand

AI-related chip stocks have been taking a beating lately, but the semiconductor industry as a whole hasn't been impacted much. Chip stocks have been the market's darling and have been largely responsible for the broader rally.

As demand for semiconductors remains elevated, sales have been skyrocketing. Continued heavy investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is expected to create significant growth opportunities for the semiconductor industry.

Against this backdrop, semiconductor stocks such as Analog Devices , Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. , Texas Instruments and NVIDIA Corp. appear well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand, making them attractive investment options with strong growth potential this year.

Chip Sales Hit New All-Time High

Global semiconductor sales totaled $517.7 billion in the third quarter, a surge of 24.1% from the second quarter, the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) said on Tuesday.

Year over year, semiconductor sales hit $172.6 billion in September, up 146.8%. Month over month, sales jumped 7.9% from the August total of $159.7 billion.

The solid jump in September and the third quarter comes after semiconductor sales surpassed the $1 trillion mark for the first time through August.

Michael Robbins, SIA president and CEO, said, "The global chip market grew substantially throughout the third quarter of this year, with worldwide sales increasing by more than 20% quarter-to-quarter for the third consecutive quarter."

AI-related chip stocks have been suffering lately as investors have been spiraling out of riskier assets on concerns over stretched valuations of AI stocks and questions about the sustainability of the sector's rapid expansion.

However, the fears are temporary as the semiconductor industry has played a major role in supporting broader stock market gains in recent years. Semiconductor sales have now recorded year-over-year growth in each of the first nine months of the year.

Heavy spending by major technology companies has renewed confidence in AI's long-term prospects. Several leading chipmakers benefiting from the AI boom have also reported strong quarterly earnings and issued optimistic guidance, helping ease investor concerns and drive semiconductor stocks higher.

Story Continues

The sector's strong showing in the third quarter followed an exceptional first half of 2026. Global semiconductor sales totaled $403.3 billion in the second quarter of 2026, following $298.5 billion in the first quarter, with sequential growth of 33.1% and 25%, respectively.

Semiconductors are increasingly essential to both established and emerging technologies, powering developments in fields such as the Internet of Things, 6G connectivity and artificial intelligence.

Rising demand from the automotive industry has provided another source of momentum for chip sales. At the same time, AI remains in the early stages of its growth cycle, prompting major technology companies to allocate billions of dollars toward research, development and infrastructure to advance the technology.

4 Semiconductor Stocks with Growth Potential

Analog Devices

Analog Devices is an original equipment manufacturer of semiconductor devices, specifically analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing ("DSP") integrated circuits. ADI's product line comprises amplifiers and comparators; analog-to-digital converters; digital-to-analog converters; video encoders and decoders; embedded processing products and DSPs; MEMS and temperature sensors; RF/IF components and converters; power and thermal management ICs, audio/video converters, amplifiers, CODECs, filters and processors. Analog Devices also offers analog, digital and RF switches and multiplexers; analog microcontrollers; clock and timing products.

Analog Devices' expected earnings growth rate for the current year is 66.9%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for current-year earnings has improved 0.3% over the past 60 days. ADI currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited is the world's largest dedicated integrated circuit foundry. TSM manufactures ICs for its customers based on their proprietary IC designs using its advanced production processes. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited's goal is to establish itself as one of the world's leading semiconductor companies by building upon the strengths that have made it the world's leading IC foundry.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited's expected earnings growth rate for the current year is 3.3%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for current-year earnings has improved 0.7% over the past 60 days. TSM presently carries a Zacks Rank #1.

Texas Instruments

Texas Instruments is an original equipment manufacturer of analog, mixed-signal and digital signal-processing integrated circuits. TXN has manufacturing and design facilities, including wafer fabrication and assembly/test operations in North America, Asia and Europe. Management strategy has been to build assets that would be fully utilized through their lifetimes and outsource any excess demand in peak situations to outside foundries.

Texas Instruments' expected earnings growth rate for the current year is 63.1%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for current-year earnings has improved 5.6% over the past 60 days. Currently, TXN carries a Zacks Rank #1.

NVIDIA Corp.

NVIDIA Corporation is the worldwide leader in visual computing technologies and the inventor of the graphics processing unit, or GPU. Over the years, NVDA's focus has evolved from PC graphics to AI-based solutions that now support high-performance computing, gaming and virtual reality platforms.

NVIDIA has an expected earnings growth rate of 95% for the current year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for current-year earnings has improved 0.5% over the last 60 days. NVDA currently has a Zacks Rank #2.

news.Title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Microsoft, SpaceX, Marvell Technology and Preformed Line Products

Chicago, IL – November 5, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Microsoft Corp. MSFT, Space Exploration Technologies Corp. SPCX, Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL and Preformed Line Products Co. PLPC.

Here are highlights from Wednesday's Analyst Blog:

Top Research Reports for Microsoft, SpaceX and Marvell

The Zacks Research Daily presents the best research output of our analyst team. Today's Research Daily features new research reports on 16 major stocks, including Microsoft Corp., Space Exploration Technologies Corp. and Marvell Technology, Inc., as well as a micro-cap stock Preformed Line Products Co.. The Zacks microcap research is unique as our research content on these small and under-the-radar companies is the only research of its type in the country.

These research reports have been hand-picked from the roughly 70 reports published by our analyst team today.

You can see all of today's research reports here >>>

Today's Featured Research Reports

Microsoft's shares have outperformed the Zacks Computer - Software industry over the year-to-date period (+15.3% vs. -1.1%). The company is benefiting from accelerating Azure demand, with Azure revenue jumping 48% to $33.2 billion in first-quarter fiscal 2027 and guidance calling for 49-50% constant-currency growth in the second quarter.

AI monetization is broadening across Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot and Foundry, where revenues more than tripled. Commercial remaining performance obligation of $677 billion, up 73%, provides strong revenue visibility. Microsoft 365 commercial cloud growth is being driven by ARPU gains from premium E5, E7 and Copilot offerings.

However, capital expenditures of $45.2 billion in the quarter and expectations of more than $50 billion in the second quarter are pressuring free cash flow and Microsoft Cloud gross margin. Weakness in Windows OEM and devices, capacity constraints and intense cloud competition pose risks.

(You can read the full research report on Microsoft here >>> )

Shares of SpaceX have gained +2.4% over the year-to-date period against the Zacks Wireless National industry's gain of +119.4%. The company launch franchise, expanding Starlink network and growing Super Intelligence operations offer long-term potential. Starship's orbital satellite deployment improves the outlook for network capacity and launch efficiency.

Starlink's recurring revenues and rising enterprise adoption add an established earnings base. New cloud contracts and Cursor strengthen AI monetization, while integrated engineering may lower deployment costs.

However, the rapid compute buildout demands substantial capital and exposes returns to power, equipment and customer utilization risks. Starship reuse and mobile network expansion remain costly and complex. Despite better quarterly profitability, sustained cash generation and returns on new assets remain unproven. The balance of growth prospects and execution risks supports a Neutral view.

(You can read the full research report on SpaceX here >>> )

Marvell's shares have outperformed the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry over the year-to-date period (+92% vs. +11.8%). The company is benefiting from rising AI infrastructure demand, with custom silicon, interconnect, switching and optics supporting record data center revenues and a higher multi-year outlook.

Management now expects faster growth through fiscal 2028 as custom programs broaden and scale-up networking gains traction. The NVIDIA relationship and recent acquisitions expand Marvell's role across next-generation AI architectures, while the Communications and Other segment provides some diversification.

Offsetting these positives, the custom ramp-up is expected to weigh on gross margin, and revenues are becoming more concentrated in datacenter and large customers. Supply constraints, export controls and tariffs can disrupt execution, while intense competition and uneven communications demand add volatility. These factors support a balanced view.

(You can read the full research report on Marvell here >>> )

Shares of Preformed Line Products have outperformed the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry over the year-to-date period (+46% vs. +15%). This microcap company with a market capitalization of $1.52 billion benefits from grid modernization spending, with strong energy infrastructure demand supporting its core business. Expanding communications capabilities, targeted acquisitions and international manufacturing investments broaden its market reach and growth potential.

Favorable product mix, pricing actions and operating leverage strengthen profitability. However, tariffs, volatile raw material and freight costs could constrain margins, while rising operating expenses increase dependence on sustained demand.

Heavy capital spending and expansion initiatives heighten execution risks. Tax fluctuations and foreign exchange movements may also create earnings volatility. Overall, PLPC offers exposure to essential infrastructure investment, but cost discipline and returns on expansion remain critical to its investment appeal.

(You can read the full research report on Preformed Line Products here >>> )

news.Title: ARM Holdings PLC (ARM) (Q2 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Record Revenue, Surging AI ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Total Revenue: $1.44 billion, up 27% year over year; record Q2 and second-highest quarterly revenue ever.

License and Other Revenue: $773 million, up 50% year over year; record Q2 and second-highest quarter ever; ~$100 million above expectations.

Royalty Revenue: $670 million, up 8% year over year; highest-ever Q2 figure.

Data Center Royalties: Doubled year over year.

Physical AI Royalties: Grew 50% year over year, driven by automotive and robotics.

Edge AI Royalties: Roughly flat year over year amid smartphone unit pressure from higher memory prices.

SoftBank Agreement Contribution: $209 million of license revenue, up 17% year over year.

Annualized Contract Value (ACV): Grew 12% year over year.

Non-GAAP Operating Expense: $774 million, up 19% year over year.

Non-GAAP Operating Income: $638 million, up 37% year over year.

Non-GAAP Operating Margin: 44.2%, up 300 basis points year over year.

Non-GAAP EPS: $0.52, up 33% year over year.

Free Cash Flow: $1.1 billion over trailing 12 months.

Arm AGI CPU Revenue Outlook: Confidence increased to up to $2 billion across fiscal 2027 and 2028; first commercial deliveries on track for fiscal Q4 '27.

Q3 Revenue Guidance: $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million (~24% year-over-year growth at midpoint).

Q3 License and Other Revenue Guidance: Up a little over 50% year over year.

Q3 Royalty Revenue Guidance: Low-teens sequential growth; low-single-digit year-over-year growth.

Q3 Non-GAAP Operating Expense Guidance: Approximately $825 million.

Q3 Non-GAAP EPS Guidance: $0.56, plus or minus $0.04.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with ARM.

Is ARM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: November 04, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Record Q2 revenue of $1.44 billion, up 27% year over year, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of over 20% growth.

License and other revenue grew 50% to $773 million, driven by strong demand for Arm's compute platform and new long-term agreements.

Data center royalties doubled year over year, with Arm-based server market share at top hyperscalers exceeding 50% and expected to surpass 60% by end of calendar 2026.

Arm AGI CPU demand is extremely strong, with confidence in achieving up to $2 billion in revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028, supported by secured supply and multiple customer purchase orders.

Non-GAAP EPS increased 33% to $0.52, and free cash flow over the trailing 12 months was $1.1 billion, providing flexibility for continued investment.

Story Continues

Negative Points

Edge AI royalty revenue was roughly flat year over year due to higher memory prices pressuring smartphone unit sales, particularly in mid- and lower-tier segments.

Royalty revenue growth was only 8% year over year, significantly lower than license growth, due to weakness in smartphone demand and a tough year-over-year comparison.

The Arm AGI CPU business is expected to have gross margins in the high-30s to low-40% range for the first version, below the company's long-term target of 50%+.

Supply chain constraints, including wafer, substrate, tester, and memory availability, pose risks to meeting strong demand for the Arm AGI CPU.

Customer concentration in data center royalties is high, with Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and NVIDIA accounting for the majority of royalties, creating dependency risk.

Q & A Highlights

Q : What is driving Arm's increased confidence in achieving up to $2 billion in Arm AGI CPU revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028, and have additional customers beyond Meta been signed? A : CEO Rene Haas said demand is stronger than at the March Arm Everywhere event, with Meta as the chief customer but multiple customers beyond Meta. Confidence has grown because Arm has spent several quarters securing supply across wafers, substrates, testers, and memory, and has signed purchase orders from multiple customers extending through calendar 2027. First commercial deliveries remain on track for fiscal Q4 2027.

Q : How does Arm expect to win versus x86 in the AI data center, given AMD's claims about Venice performance per watt? A : CEO Rene Haas framed the opportunity in two ways: hyperscalers designing custom SoCs gain flexibility to optimize performance per rack, while Arm's AGI CPU offers strong performance per watt and cost efficiency. He cited Signal65 testing showing roughly twice the performance per rack versus AMD EPYC 9755, and said Arm is confident in customer demand and its road map.

Q : What partners are building Arm AGI CPU rack systems, and what will drive the path to $15 billion in AGI CPU revenue by FY31? A : CEO Rene Haas said Supermicro, Lenovo, and ASRock are building racks for deployment at data centers such as OCI. Growth will be driven by rising core counts as agentic workloads scale, with CPUs potentially moving from 128 to 256 to 500-plus cores, which should lift average selling prices. CFO Jason Child noted the prior plan implied about $2 billion a year after FY28 and about $5 billion a year after that, with updated targets likely at the next Arm Everywhere event.

Q : When should investors expect Arm AGI CPU revenue to begin, and how large could data center become as a share of total royalties? A : CFO Jason Child said shipments will start in Q4, with little if any contribution in Q3. On data center mix, he said data center was approaching about 20% of total royalties last year and will not quite reach a third by the end of this year, but will get there sometime soon, with edge royalties flattish this quarter and recovering in Q4.

Q : How concentrated are cloud and AI royalties among customers? A : CEO Rene Haas said Amazon, Google, and Microsoft are the largest contributors, with NVIDIA ramping quickly. He said those four command the majority of data center royalties.

Q : What is the update on the second-generation Arm AGI CPU and the potential to add networking and high-performance I/O? A : CEO Rene Haas declined to disclose the precise schedule but said the market moves on an 18- to 24-month production ramp cadence, implying timing for the follow-on chip. He said Arm is looking at connectivity, I/O, networking, and other system-level capabilities because rack-level performance matters, though nothing could be announced on the call.

Q : Is the $773 million licensing quarter a new structural level, and what types of agreements drove it? A : CFO Jason Child said the vast majority of licensing is Arm Total Access and CSS, with architecture licenses very rare. He said license revenue should step up again in Q3 and Q4, and while he would not call $773 million the new quarterly norm, the pipeline is stronger than expected, with incremental new deals that are hard to forecast and likely to convert into future royalties.

Q : Could higher-core-count AGI CPUs support higher per-core pricing? A : CEO Rene Haas said memory and data center build costs have risen sharply, so Arm is cautious about pushing pricing too hard, but he sees some pricing elasticity on larger, higher-core-count chips and said there is probably some headroom.

Q : If smartphone units remain weak next year, how should investors think about royalty growth? A : CFO Jason Child said industry forecasts point to roughly flat mobile units next year, with memory constraints already reflected and not expected to deteriorate further. He said greater Armv9 adoption, now over 50%, plus growing CSS adoption and higher royalty rates on next-generation CSS should let Arm grow overall royalties at least in the double digits next year.

Q : Does Arm have enough scale to secure supply for the AGI CPU against larger competitors like AMD? A : CEO Rene Haas acknowledged AMD has far more scale and longer-standing supply relationships, but said Arm has decades-long relationships with TSMC and memory vendors such as Micron, Samsung, and SK. He said Arm has been discussing the platform with supply partners for more than a year and views the AGI CPU as a five- to ten-year endeavor requiring deep supply chain relationships.

Q : How should investors think about gross margins as Arm secures more AGI CPU supply at higher cost? A : CEO Rene Haas said memory is the largest cost pressure, with downstream supply chain impacts also weighing on margins, but Arm has demonstrated some pricing elasticity to offset costs. CFO Jason Child said the first AGI CPU version should carry gross margins in the high-30s to low-40% range, with the first version likely a little lower, moving toward the market standard of 50%-plus on later versions.

Q : What is driving the royalty rate per unit trend, and how should investors model it going forward? A : CFO Jason Child said the blended rate will bounce around given more than 10 billion chips shipped in the quarter, with mobile lower and server and physical AI higher. He advised modeling the three segments separately: flattish mobile, strong double-digit server growth with rising core counts and CSS revenue, and physical AI growing about 50%, supporting confidence in triple-digit data center royalty growth over the next few years.

news.Title: ASML vs. Marvell Technology: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy Going into 2027?
news.Content:
The race for better artificial intelligence continues to reshape the market, making investors choose between equipment giants and chip designers. Should you buy ASML (NASDAQ:ASML) or Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) today?

ASML provides the complex lithography systems used by the world's leading foundries to print the most advanced microchips. Marvell specializes in infrastructure solutions, connecting and moving massive amounts of data across cloud and carrier networks. Both companies are pivotal to the future of semiconductor technology, but they occupy very different rungs on the industry ladder.

The case for ASML

ASML manufactures the lithography systems that are essential for the production of advanced microchips found in everything from smartphones to data centers. It is currently the sole supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, notes are critical for cost-effective microchip scaling. The company serves the global semiconductor stocks ecosystem by delivering hardware and software for EUV and cheaper deep ultraviolet (DUV) applications.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached $36.7 billion, representing a growth of 15.6% compared with the prior fiscal year. This expansion in the top line helped the company generate a net income of $10.8 billion. The net margin, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining after all expenses are paid, reached 29.4% during this period.

According to its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.2x shows the company uses very little borrowed money relative to its equity. The current ratio of approximately 1.3x indicates it maintains sufficient short-term assets to cover immediate liabilities. Free cash flow, which is the cash left over after accounting for capital expenditures, reached $12.4 billion for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025.

The case for Marvell Technology

Marvell Technology designs data infrastructure solutions that power artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and automotive industrial end markets across the globe. The company reported in its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, that its revenue is highly concentrated among a limited number of buyers. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as one distributor represented nearly 37% of revenue and a single direct customer accounted for roughly 14%.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached $8.2 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 42.1%. This sharp increase in sales helped the company achieve a net income of $2.7 billion. The net margin for the period reached 32.6%, reflecting a significant improvement compared with the losses reported in the prior fiscal year.

Story Continues

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 0.3x indicates a healthy balance between debt and equity. The current ratio of approximately 2.0x measures its ability to cover short-term obligations, and free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, was nearly $1.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented 33.8% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

ASML faces potential volatility in the global chip market, where cycles of high demand for new equipment can be followed by periods of overcapacity. Geopolitical tensions also pose a significant threat, as trade restrictions on high-end lithography equipment can limit sales to certain geographic regions. Additionally, the extreme complexity of its machines means any production delays or technical hurdles in next-generation systems could impact its long-term growth trajectory.

Marvell Technology faces risks from significant revenue concentration, as a few large customers account for a majority of its annual sales. Strategic and integration risks are heightened by large-scale acquisitions, notably the announced $115 billion all-stock acquisition of Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE). Additionally, the company faces intense competition from Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) and potential supply chain disruptions due to the geographic concentration of its manufacturing partners.

Valuation comparison

ASML appears more affordably valued based on its Forward P/E and its P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

ASML and Marvell Technology are both great stocks to own for exposure to the artificial intelligence boom. The former is an attractive AI stock since it holds a legal monopoly over the EUV lithography machines needed to construct AI chips, as competitors have not been able to successfully replicate the technology at scale. However, if I had to choose between these two, I would invest in Marvell.

Not only did Marvell report 42% year-over-year revenue growth in its 2026 fiscal year (FY), in its Investor Day held on Oct. 6, management set a FY 2031 target of $70 billion to $90 billion in sales. That's incredible growth compared to FY 2026's $8.2 billion, and indicates the company is seeing strong customer demand for its AI solutions.

That's where Marvell's bid to acquire Lumentum comes in. Lumentum reported fiscal Q1 revenue of $1.3 billion on Nov. 2, which represents a jaw-dropping 137% year-over-year increase. Its optical connectivity offerings enable rapid data transmission, a critical feature for data-hungry AI systems.

Marvell's acquisition caused its share price to fall, as Wall Street weighed the dilution risk of the all-stock deal. This creates an opportunity to pick up Marvell shares on the dip, as I believe Marvell's addition of Lumentum makes the company stronger over the long run.

news.Title: Is Broadcom Stock a Buy After Marvell's $115 Billion Deal?
news.Content:
On Nov. 2, Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) agreed to buy Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE), a maker of lasers and optical transceivers, in an all-stock deal. The firms put Lumentum's enterprise value (its stock market value plus debt, minus cash) at $115 billion, using both stocks' Oct. 28 closing prices.

Marvell says the combination creates a category leader in artificial intelligence (AI) connectivity -- the chips and optical parts that send data between AI processors.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) knows the business well. The chip designer sells custom AI accelerators, Ethernet switches, and optical components for AI data centers. But its stock dipped only about 1% on Nov. 2, while Marvell shares slid about 13%.

At roughly $335 as I write, Broadcom stock trades about 30% under its June 2 record close of $481.57. When I last wrote about the company on Oct. 28, with shares near $342, I said I'd consider buying a little at a time.

Does a bigger rival change that?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Marvell is building a bigger rival

Marvell already designs custom AI chips, plus network switches and the electrical and optical interconnect chips that link AI systems together. Lumentum brings high-performance lasers and optical transceivers, along with its own compound semiconductor manufacturing.

Broadcom competes in most of those markets. It designs custom AI accelerators for six customers, including Alphabet's Google and Anthropic. The chips are made for one customer's AI work, as an alternative to general-purpose graphics processing units (GPUs).

Broadcom also sells Tomahawk Ethernet switches. On its fiscal third-quarter earnings call on Sept. 2, CEO Hock Tan said the company had just finished designing Tomahawk 7, which he called the industry's first 200-terabit-per-second Ethernet switch.

And Broadcom makes lasers, too.

"[D]emand for lasers ... is far surpassing supply out there in the industry," Tan said on the call. He added that Broadcom holds "a fairly substantial share of this market."

Put simply, Lumentum's lasers sell into a market where buyers can't currently get enough of them. Sure, shortages like this don't tend to last. But I think it makes the deal more of a long-term threat to Broadcom than a short-term one. A bigger rival could matter more when supply catches up to demand and buyers start shopping harder on price.

Story Continues

Broadcom's AI sales are still accelerating

Showing how far ahead Broadcom's AI business is, its AI semiconductor revenue hit $16.7 billion in fiscal Q3 (the quarter ended Aug. 2), up 221% year over year. Marvell's total revenue for its own quarter ended Aug. 1 was $2.74 billion, or around one-sixth as much.

And Broadcom's AI growth has picked up every quarter this year. AI revenue growth climbed from 106% in fiscal Q1 to 143% in fiscal Q2, then to 221% in fiscal Q3. Management guided for 236% year-over-year growth, to $21.7 billion, in fiscal Q4, which ended Nov. 1.

Broadcom has its own $115 billion number, and it means something else: the company's forecast for AI semiconductor revenue in fiscal 2027, the fiscal year that started this week.

This would double the almost $58 billion Broadcom expected for fiscal 2026. And Tan said on the Sept. 2 call that the company's already locked in the supply to get there.

"Our demand actually exceeds this outlook, and we will work to improve supply," he said.

The deal won't affect that year directly. Marvell expects the acquisition to close in the first half of calendar 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals. So Broadcom's fiscal 2027 will probably be over before the combined company even exists.

Time to buy?

Investors can buy this growth for less than they'd pay for the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC). Broadcom trades at around 17 times analysts' consensus earnings estimate for fiscal 2027.

This compares to about 18.7 times forward earnings for the S&P 500 overall.

True, Broadcom relies on a few very big AI customers, and a stronger Marvell could offer these customers another place to shop for custom chips and lasers. But this option is probably years away. And Broadcom's AI business is already several times the size of Marvell's whole company.

Ultimately, the deal doesn't change my take on Broadcom. It does make the company's laser and switching sales worth watching more closely once the combined company exists.

Meanwhile, the stock is a bit cheaper than when I last wrote about it, and nothing in the deal affects Broadcom's fiscal 2027 outlook. I'd still consider buying shares at this price.

news.Title: What ARM (ARM) Said on Its Q2 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Arm Holdings PLC Sponsored ADR? Here are five stocks we like better.

Arm reported record Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue of $1.44 billion, up 27% year over year , while non-GAAP EPS rose 33% to $0.52. Licensing revenue surged 50% to $773 million, exceeding expectations by about $100 million.

Arm raised its confidence in generating up to $2 billion in AGI CPU revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028 , citing customer orders and secured supplier capacity. First commercial deliveries remain on track for fiscal Q4 2027.

Data center royalties doubled year over year, helping offset smartphone-related pressure, and Arm expects strong cloud demand to support further growth. For fiscal Q3, it forecast revenue of $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.56, plus or minus $0.04.

Qualcomm's Huawei Deal Adds Strategic Depth to Its AI Expansion

ARM (NASDAQ:ARM) reported record second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue as licensing demand and data center royalties grew, while executives said they had greater confidence in the sales potential of the company's forthcoming Arm AGI CPU.

Revenue rose 27% year over year to $1.44 billion, marking Arm's fifth consecutive quarter of growth above 20%, Chief Executive Officer Rene Haas said. Non-GAAP earnings per share increased 33% to $0.52.

→ 3 Waste Services Stocks With More Growth Than You Might Expect

NVIDIA Just Turned AI Safety Into a Spending Story and These 3 Stocks Benefit

Licensing and other revenue rose 50% to $773 million, while royalty revenue increased 8% to $670 million. Data center royalties doubled from a year earlier, offsetting roughly flat edge AI royalties amid pressure on smartphone sales.

Licensing demand exceeds expectations

Chief Financial Officer Jason Child said licensing revenue came in about $100 million above Arm's expectations as customers accelerated long-term commitments to access its technology. The company signed three new Arm Total Access agreements, bringing active subscriptions to more than 60, and four additional compute subsystem licenses: two for data center chips and two for smartphones.

→ AbbVie's Humira Era Is Fading, But Its New Growth Engines Face Another Test

MarketBeat Week in Review – 09/21 - 09/25

Arm's technology licensing and design services agreement with SoftBank contributed $209 million of the quarter's licensing revenue, up 17% year over year. Child said he expects the quarterly run rate from that agreement to remain around that level for the rest of the fiscal year.

Story Continues

Annualized contract value grew 12%. Child said that measure helps show underlying licensing trends because revenue can vary significantly between quarters depending on the timing and accounting treatment of large agreements.

→ Big Tech Is Spending Billions on AI—These 5 Stocks Are Getting Paid

Non-GAAP operating expenses rose 19% to $774 million as Arm expanded engineering capacity and invested in new platforms and products. Non-GAAP operating income climbed 37% to $638 million, and the non-GAAP operating margin expanded by 3 percentage points to 44.2%.

Arm raises confidence in AGI CPU outlook

Executives said purchase orders from multiple customers and agreements with suppliers have increased their confidence in achieving up to $2 billion in Arm AGI CPU revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028 . Child said Arm had previously expressed increased confidence in achieving more than $1 billion over that period.

First commercial deliveries remain on track for fiscal fourth-quarter 2027. Child said any shipments in the third quarter would not be substantial and that Arm would provide another update with its third-quarter results.

Haas identified Meta as a chief customer but said Arm expects multiple customers beyond Meta. He said demand had exceeded expectations and that the company had been working for several quarters to secure supplies, including wafers, substrates, testers and memory.

Asked about the cost of obtaining additional supply, Haas said rising system costs create margin pressure, but Arm has some flexibility to increase prices. Child said the company expects the first version of the product to have a gross margin in the high-30% to low-40% range, with a longer-term goal of reaching 50% or more as Arm develops expertise and does more work itself.

Data center growth offsets smartphone pressure

Arm's data center royalty revenue doubled year over year as Arm-based CPUs expanded in AI infrastructure and general-purpose cloud workloads, Child said. Physical AI royalty revenue grew 50%, driven by automotive and robotics adoption.

Edge AI royalty revenue was roughly flat, as higher memory prices pressured smartphone unit sales, particularly in mid- and lower-tier devices. Child said higher royalty rates from adoption of Armv9 and compute subsystem technologies offset that headwind. He expects edge AI royalties to reaccelerate as smartphone conditions normalize.

Haas said Arm-based server market share at the top hyperscalers rose from 15% in calendar 2024 to more than 50% in 2025. Based on expected deployments across Google Axion, AWS Graviton, Microsoft Cobalt and NVIDIA platforms, Arm expects that share to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026.

During the analyst question-and-answer session, Haas and Child expressed confidence that data center royalties could sustain triple-digit growth over the next several years. Haas pointed to market-share gains and the use of Arm CPUs alongside AI accelerators.

Third-quarter guidance

For fiscal third-quarter 2027, Arm forecast revenue of $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million. The midpoint would represent approximately 24% growth from a year earlier. The company also projected non-GAAP earnings of $0.56 per share, plus or minus $0.04, and non-GAAP operating expenses of approximately $825 million.

Child said Arm expects licensing and other revenue to grow a little over 50% year over year in the third quarter. Royalty revenue is expected to rise by low-single-digit percentages from a year earlier, as strength in cloud and physical AI is offset by weaker smartphone demand and a difficult comparison with the prior-year period.

About ARM (NASDAQ:ARM)

Arm Holdings plc (NASDAQ: ARM) is a semiconductor and software design company that develops central processing unit (CPU) architectures and related intellectual property. Rather than manufacturing chips itself, Arm licenses its designs and instruction-set architectures to semiconductor companies and technology manufacturers, which incorporate them into their own products.

The company's offerings include CPU processor cores, graphics processing units through its Mali product family, system IP, development tools and software.

news.Title: MKS (MKSI) Beats Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
news.Content:
MKS (MKSI) came out with quarterly earnings of $4.18 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.64 per share. This compares to earnings of $1.93 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +14.84%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this maker of analysis and processing equipment for semiconductor companies would post earnings of $2.94 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.3, delivering a surprise of +12.24%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

MKS, which belongs to the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry, posted revenues of $1.41 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.12%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $988 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

MKS shares have added about 28.4% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 10.6%.

What's Next for MKS?

While MKS has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for MKS was favorable. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to outperform the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $3.90 on $1.39 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $13.15 on $5.06 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Electronics - Miscellaneous Products is currently in the top 17% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Another stock from the same industry, Rockwell Automation (ROK), has yet to report results for the quarter ended September 2026. The results are expected to be released on November 5.

This industrial equipment and software maker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $3.72 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +11.4%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.3% higher over the last 30 days to the current level.

Rockwell Automation's revenues are expected to be $2.39 billion, up 3.3% from the year-ago quarter.

As these metrics influence top- and bottom-line performance, comparing them to the year-ago numbers and what analysts estimated helps investors project a stock's price performance more accurately.

Here is how MKS performed in the just reported quarter in terms of the metrics most widely monitored and projected by Wall Street analysts:

news.Title: Arm stock dips as lack of blowout guidance offsets quarterly results
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Arm on Wednesday delivered a quarterly top- and bottom-line beat, but its current-quarter profit and revenue guidance failed to comfortably top expectations.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

U.S.-listed shares of the British chip designer fell more than 3% in premarket trading Thursday.

Arm is a well-known player in the semiconductor market, with its chip designs being used by companies such as Qualcomm, Apple, and Samsung Electronics in graphics processing units (GPUs) in smartphones, and by cloud computing giants and hyperscalers such as Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms.

ARM brings in revenue from licensing its technology to these companies and then charging a royalty fee for each product that uses its design.

The British chip designer's technology is used in developing artificial intelligence-focused server chips. The firm earlier this year also said it was expanding its strategy beyond offering intellectual property and compute subsystems to producing silicon products. This included the launch of a new central processing unit (CPU) designed for AI data centers, called Arm AGI CPU.

"AI is driving unprecedented demand for compute across the cloud, devices and autonomous systems, with Arm being the compute platform of choice. Our business is now driven by two areas, both of which are showing rapid growth: The IP business, where partners increase their investment in Arm technology and deploy record numbers of Arm-based silicon, and our new silicon business, where demand for Arm AGI CPU is extremely strong," ARM top boss Rene Haas and finance chief Jason Child said in a letter to shareholders.

HSBC analysts said Arm reiterated its bullish AGI CPU tone bot noted that "server royalties remain a key driver."

"We believe server royalties remain the key earnings catalyst upside with the clearest visibility over the next 12 month given increasing server CPU TAM and Arm market share along with rising CPU core count which increases royalty ASP per chip," they wrote.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The Cambridge, England-based company's results come at a time when the broader AI trade on Wall Street has been under pressure. Concerns have soared about the massive amounts of debt being issued by companies to fund their AI infrastructure buildouts and whether such spending will ultimately be rewarded with comparable returns.

Story Continues

Chip stocks in particular have been some of the hardest hit by the downturn in sentiment around AI. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index - a key barometer of chip stocks - slumped 15.4% in October. Meanwhile, U.S.-listed shares of Arm tumbled nearly 29% last month.

Against this backdrop, investors have been closely watching quarterly results from chipmakers and chip designers to gauge the demand for AI chips and whether that demand was strong enough to warrant the unprecedented spending on AI.

"Arm continues to gain share across the data center, driven by growing demand for performance and power efficiency as AI infrastructure scales. Data center royalties doubled year over year, and Arm-based server market share at the top hyperscalers more than tripled—from 15% in calendar 2024 to more than 50% in calendar 2025," the company's top executives said in the letter to shareholders.

"Based on current ramps across Google Axion, AWS Graviton, Microsoft Cobalt, and NVIDIA platforms, we expect that share to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026," they added.

Raymond James analysts said the management's commentary "suggests it is incrementally confident that it has enough supply and customer commitments for the CPU business for up to $2B of sales through the end of FY28, but we opt to remain conservative until we can discern more tangible trends."

Arm said it earned 52 cents per share on an adjusted basis on revenue of $1.44 billion for its fiscal Q2 2027. Analysts had expected an adjusted profit of 47 cents per share on revenue of $1.38 billion.

For its fiscal Q3 2027, ARM sees adjusted profit per share of 56 cents plus/minus 4 cents on revenue of $1.54 billion plus/minus $50 million. The consensus estimates had been for a profit of 55 cents per share on revenue of $1.53 billion.

Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.
