news.Title: SIMO Earnings Surge as Enterprise and AI Storage Drive New Momentum
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO delivered a sharp third-quarter earnings acceleration as enterprise, automotive and artificial intelligence storage became larger contributors to growth. The results strengthen the case that its revenue mix is moving beyond traditional consumer storage controllers.

The key question is whether that shift can support a more durable earnings profile. Current guidance, expanding solutions revenue and new enterprise products point to broader growth drivers, though execution and consumer-market risks remain.

SIMO's Third Quarter Set New Financial Highs

Third-quarter 2026 revenues reached $560.2 million, up 131% year over year and 24% sequentially. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.35 per American depositary share beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.30 by 31.82% and increased 335% from the year-ago period.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Profitability also improved materially. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 32.1% from 15.8% a year earlier, while gross margin rose to 53.7% from 48.7%. The combination of higher volumes and a richer product mix helped lift operating leverage.

Silicon Motion's Solutions Business is Surging

Ferri and boot-drive solution sales climbed 75-80% sequentially in the third quarter, supported by automotive, edge artificial intelligence and enterprise demand. Solutions accounted for more than 40% of total revenues, and management expects the category could represent roughly half of revenues in 2027.

That mix shift could make Silicon Motion less dependent on consumer controller cycles. Automotive programs generally span three to five years, while enterprise boot-drive opportunities provide another source of longer-duration demand. Micron Technology, Inc. MU is also expanding high-capacity data-center solid-state drive offerings for artificial intelligence, cloud and hyperscale workloads, underscoring the broader storage opportunity tied to data-intensive computing.

SIMO's Fourth-Quarter Guidance Extends the Trend

Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $588 million to $616 million, implying sequential growth of 5%-10%. Non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 54%-55%, while operating margin is expected to reach 36%-37%.

The outlook suggests the third-quarter improvement is carrying into year-end rather than fading immediately after a record period. For 2027, management expects revenue growth of at least 40% and gross margins in the low-to-mid-50% range, supported by rising contributions from enterprise controllers and Ferri automotive solutions.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion Is Building for the Next AI Cycle

Silicon Motion taped out its 4-nanometer PCIe Gen6 MonTitan controller in the third quarter, with sampling scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. The product targets hyperscalers and cloud service providers and is designed for both TLC-based compute storage and QLC-based data storage.

Four NAND makers have begun producing 2-terabit QLC dies, with broader availability expected by the end of 2027. That supply expansion could support higher-capacity enterprise storage deployments. Seagate Technology Holdings plc STX is likewise positioning its mass-capacity storage portfolio around rising artificial intelligence and cloud data demand, showing that infrastructure spending is broadening across storage technologies.

SIMO's Ratings Temper the Earnings Excitement

The latest quarter supports the view that Silicon Motion is becoming a more diversified storage supplier, but the transition is not yet complete. Consumer weakness, customer qualification requirements and supply-chain constraints still create uncertainty around how smoothly the enterprise ramp develops.

SIMO currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). It also has a Value Score of D and Momentum Score of D, along with a Growth Score of F and VGM Score of F. Because the Style Scores complement the Zacks Rank, these weaker grades suggest a more measured near-term stance even as the company's enterprise and artificial intelligence exposure expands. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: SIMO Stock Falls 33.5% in a Month as Growth Meets Execution Risks
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO shares have fallen 33.5% over the past four weeks, a sharp reversal despite record revenues and expanding exposure to enterprise and AI storage. The drop raises the question of whether valuation now better reflects the company's growth prospects.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The answer is not straightforward. Enterprise diversification, automotive demand and higher-value storage products support the outlook, but consumer weakness, qualification requirements and supply-chain constraints leave execution risk elevated.

SIMO's Record Growth Contrasts With the Sell-Off

Third-quarter 2026 revenues surged 131% year over year to about $560 million, marking a fourth consecutive quarter of record revenues. Non-GAAP earnings per ADS rose 335% to $4.35, while operating margin expanded to 32.1%.

The quarter also exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate on both the top and bottom lines. Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $588-$616 million, with non-GAAP operating margin rising to 36%-37%.

Silicon Motion's Enterprise Mix Is Expanding

Ferri automotive and enterprise boot-drive solutions grew more than 75% sequentially and represented more than 40% of third-quarter revenues. Management indicated that the solutions business could reach roughly half of revenues in 2027.

That shift increases exposure to longer-duration programs and higher-value storage opportunities. Micron Technology, Inc. MU, which offers DRAM, NAND and data-center SSDs, illustrates the broader memory and storage ecosystem in which enterprise demand is expanding.

SIMO Faces Persistent Consumer Pressure

Elevated NAND and DRAM prices are pressuring smartphone and PC affordability. eMMC and UFS controller revenues declined modestly sequentially in the third quarter, and management expects near-term revenues in that business to remain relatively flat.

SSD controller revenues are also expected to be flat to slightly lower sequentially in the fourth quarter. These trends show that enterprise growth is offsetting, rather than eliminating, weakness in established consumer-facing markets.

Silicon Motion Must Execute on Enterprise Ramps

Enterprise expansion depends on customer qualifications, production ramps and component availability. MonTitan is scaling across seven announced customers, while Silicon Motion's 4-nanometer PCIe Gen6 MonTitan controller is scheduled to begin sampling in the first quarter of 2027.

Near-CPU boot-drive opportunities add another execution layer because customized firmware and customer-specific features are required. Seagate Technology Holdings PLC STX, whose portfolio includes cloud, edge and data-center storage products, provides another reference point for the scale and complexity of enterprise storage markets.

Story Continues

SIMO's Valuation Adds Context to the Decline

SIMO trades at 12.1X forward 12-month earnings, below its five-year median of 19.4X but above the Zacks sub-industry's 9.4X. The lower multiple versus its own history reflects a materially different valuation backdrop after the recent share-price pullback.

The discount to SIMO's historical median may look more attractive if enterprise ramps progress as planned. Still, the premium to the sub-industry means investors are not being offered a uniformly cheap valuation relative to peers.

SIMO's Signals Still Favor a Cautious View

SIMO's growth and valuation setup remains mixed. Record operating performance and enterprise diversification support the longer-term case, while consumer pressure and execution requirements argue against treating the 33.5% decline alone as a buy signal.

The stock currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). It has a Value Score of D and Momentum Score of D, along with a Growth Score of F and VGM Score of F. Since the Style Scores are designed to complement the Zacks Rank, these weaker grades support a measured stance despite the company's strong recent fundamental growth. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Q3 Earnings & JOLTS Report on Midterm Voting Day
news.Content:
Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026

Pre-market futures are mixed ahead of the bell, with the Nasdaq building back some of its recent losses on AI-buildout concerns, and a "wait and see" mentality regarding the U.S. midterm elections takes hold. Early voting has seen some 60+ million Americans take to the ballot this year — far ahead of normal levels of midterm voting.

The Dow is selling off a bit this morning, -371 points, while the Nasdaq is +89 at this hour. The S&P 500, as per normal, is splitting the difference, -12 points presently. Crude oil prices are down on two noteworthy events in the Middle East: the U.S. has attacked Iran's Qeshm Island overnight, which is the largest island in the Persian Gulf, and President Trump has announced he will be pulling back $4 billion in payments to Israel by the end of the year.

Q3 Earnings This Morning: PFE, SHOP

Big Pharma staple Pfizer PFE released Q3 results ahead of today's open, posting earnings of $0.87 per share versus expectations of $0.72, for a +20.8% positive earnings surprise. Revenues of $16.58 billion in the quarter outpaced the Zacks consensus by +2.8%. The drugmaker upped guidance on stronger Eliquis sales, but shares are flat pre-market after gaining +23% year to date. For more on PFE's earnings, click here.

E-commerce mainstay Shopify SHOP shares are tumbling -15% in today's early trading, despite modest beats on both top and bottom lines in its Q3 this morning. Earnings of $0.49 per share amounted to a 4-cent outperformance, with revenues of $3.74 billion +0.15% ahead of estimates. The company missed on Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV) and subscription metrics, however. For more on SHOP's earnings, click here.

After today's close, we'll hear from AI chipmaking company Advanced Micro Devices AMD, which is up in today's pre-market and +118% year to date. Analysts are expecting +61.7% earnings growth and +41.89% on revenues. The Lisa Su-run company has not missed on earnings expectations since Q4 2018.

Not to be confused based on similar ticker symbol, agriculture giant Archer Daniels-Midland ADM also reports after today's close. Earnings growth is expected to come in at an excellent +77.2% year over year, with revenues projected up +11.3%. The Zacks Rank #2 (Buy)-rated company is aiming for its eight-straight quarterly earnings beat.

Meanwhile, software firm Skyworks Solutions SWKS reports its fiscal Q4 report after today's close. Following the company's $10 billion Qorvo acquisition, Skyworks looks to report earning down -27.84% year over year, -6.35% on revenues. The company has not missed on bottom-line estimates since Q1 2019.

Story Continues

What to Expect from the Stock Market Today

We won't get any midterm returns until well after today's trading session is over, but we'll make sure to keep abreast of developments throughout the country today. Otherwise, the September print on Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) is expected to remain in-line with the prior month, at +7.1 million job openings.

JOLTS numbers are back to pre-Covid levels, and have been here pretty steadily over the past nearly two years. This is consistent with the "low hire/low fire" employment numbers we've seen elsewhere. Job Quits in August dropped to 3.07 million, at an historically low +1.9% rate. Basically, lots of people remain employed, but fewer are finding opportunities elsewhere. Today's JOLTS figures kicks off the latest "Jobs Week."

news.Title: Silicon Motion Technology Corporation (SIMO) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.Content:
Silicon Motion (SIMO) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Over the past month, shares of this chip company have returned -33.5%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -2.3% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry, which Silicon Motion falls in, has lost 21.9%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Silicon Motion is expected to post earnings of $4.75 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +277%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +13.1%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $12.91 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +263.7%. This estimate has changed -5.5% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $19.86 indicates a change of +53.9% from what Silicon Motion is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +28.5%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Silicon Motion.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Revenue Growth Forecast

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Silicon Motion, the consensus sales estimate of $602.1 million for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +116.2%. The $1.94 billion and $2.72 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +118.8% and +40.6%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Silicon Motion reported revenues of $560.22 million in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +131.5%. EPS of $4.35 for the same period compares with $1 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $532.81 million, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +5.14%. The EPS surprise was +31.82%.

Over the last four quarters, Silicon Motion surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Silicon Motion is graded D on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Bottom Line

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Silicon Motion. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: ASML Surges 48% in the Past Year: How Should You Play the Stock Now?
news.Content:
ASML Holding N.V. ASML has gained 48.1% over the past year compared with the sector's growth of 9.5%. It has outperformed Advanced Energy Industries, Inc. AEIS but lagged Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO. While AEIS has gained 11.4%, SIMO soared 103.6% over this period.

One-Year ASML Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

ASML Rides on Strong AI Demand

ASML is benefiting from growing AI infrastructure investments, which are encouraging leading semiconductor manufacturers to expand their production capabilities. The company's Installed Base Management revenues reached €3.29 billion in the third quarter of 2026, increasing from €2.76 billion in the preceding quarter, driven by strong demand for productivity upgrades. New lithography system sales increased to 113 units from 86 in the second quarter.

Management highlighted improving order momentum, with some customers expressing interest in placing equipment orders for 2029 and 2030. The combination of capacity growth and higher lithography content gives ASML multiple structural avenues for revenue expansion through 2026 and beyond.

The company's dominant position in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography technology provides a competitive advantage, particularly as chipmakers expand production of advanced logic and memory chips. ASML's expanding technological capabilities, strategic partnerships and improving financial outlook further strengthen its investment appeal. The company is advancing High Numerical Aperture (High-NA) EUV technology, which is expected to support next-generation semiconductor manufacturing and drive long-term equipment demand. Its expanding collaborations with Intel, Samsung and TSMC reinforce its position in advanced chipmaking.

Estimate Revision Trend

Earnings estimates for ASML for 2026 have moved up 54.4% to $46.54 over the past year, while the same for 2027 has increased 61.9% to $62.54. The positive estimate revision depicts bullish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

ASML Growth Marred by Long Order Visibility

Despite the positives, management attributes the current demand environment primarily to AI-related investment and the resulting need for more advanced Logic and Memory capacity. This has produced unusually long order visibility for ASML, but it also makes the growth profile increasingly dependent on customers maintaining those expansion plans. A slower pace of customer investment would therefore affect both system demand and utilization of the larger production footprint ASML is preparing.

The planned scale-up requires manufacturing capacity, suppliers and trained employees to rise together. This leaves future profitability dependent on converting the larger cost base into the expected shipment volumes. Moreover, a uniform adoption schedule across Logic and DRAM customers is yet to be established. High-NA therefore remains both a technology opportunity and an execution variable, with the pace of wider insertion dependent on customer qualification and manufacturing decisions rather than ASML's roadmap alone.

Story Continues

Other Headwinds

ASML also faces operational challenges related to capacity expansion, supply-chain constraints and the growing complexity of its advanced lithography systems. In its third-quarter 2026 update, management indicated that planned production capacity for 2027 and 2028 would not fully meet anticipated customer demand, highlighting potential execution risks as the company scales manufacturing operations. Expanding capacity requires substantial investments, specialized components and a highly skilled workforce, while supplier bottlenecks could delay system deliveries and revenue recognition. In addition, developing and commercializing next-generation High-NA EUV technology requires significant R&D spending that could weigh on ASML's growth prospects.

End Note

ASML's technological leadership in EUV lithography, healthy order trends and expanding installed-base revenues reinforce its long-term investment appeal. With upward earnings estimate revisions, the stock is witnessing positive investor sentiment. However, export-control uncertainties, capacity-expansion challenges and long order visibility remain headwinds.

Stiff competitive pressure and supply-chain bottlenecks also plague the company's growth prospects. High operating and R&D expenses remain an overhang as well. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), ASML appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and investors could be better off if they trade with caution. news.Title: Should You Trade SIMO Stock With Caution Despite Q3 Earnings Beat?
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with both the top and bottom lines surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.35 per American Depositary Share (ADS) increased 335% year over year and beat the consensus estimate of $3.30 by 31.82%.

Revenues surged 131% year over year to approximately $560 million, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $533 million by 5.07%. Growth was supported by robust demand for SSD controllers and Ferri & Boot Drive solutions, with the latter witnessing a remarkable 2,580-2,585% year-over-year sales increase.

SIMO Buoyed by Healthy Demand Trends

Silicon Motion is witnessing solid growth dynamics driven by strong momentum in enterprise and edge SSD controllers, automotive storage solutions and enterprise boot drive products. SSD controller sales increased 55-60% year over year and 20-25% sequentially, benefiting from expanding demand for edge and enterprise storage applications. Sales of embedded Multi-Media Card and Universal Flash Storage (eMMC+UFS) controllers rose 35-40% year over year.

Ferri & Boot Drive solutions sales increased 75-80% sequentially, supported by rapid adoption of automotive, edge artificial intelligence (AI) and enterprise boot drive solutions. Management highlighted growing contributions from its MonTitan enterprise and AI controllers as the company expands beyond traditional consumer storage markets.

Fabless Business Model Aids SIMO

Silicon Motion operates a fabless business model, focusing on chip design while outsourcing manufacturing to foundries like TSMC. Consequently, the company has a low capital investment requirement as it does not require expensive fabrication plants, enabling it to adopt advanced manufacturing nodes quickly, leading to higher margins compared to integrated manufacturers. This enables the company to focus on innovation and product development rather than manufacturing complexity.

The key growth drivers for SIMO include AI and high-performance computing, cloud data centers, automotive storage, smartphones and mobile devices. Each of these end markets is growing fast and offers lucrative growth potential. An expanding customer base and innovative products will likely act as tailwinds for the company's top-line growth. Silicon Motion has shipped more than 10 billion NAND flash controllers in its operating history, with more than 750 million NAND controllers on average every year.

Price Performance

SIMO has gained 103.6% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 101.5%. It has also outperformed peers like Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD and International Business Machines Corporation IBM. Advanced Micro has gained 86.7%, while IBM is down 16.1% over this period.

Story Continues

One-Year SIMO Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Stiff Competition, Geopolitical Issues Hurt SIMO

Despite the positives, Silicon Motion faces stiff competition in the mobile storage market from players like Micron, Microchip, Marvell and ON Semiconductor. Of late, intensifying competition in the card and USB flash drive controller markets is proving to be a major headwind. The tense political conditions between Taiwan and the People's Republic of China increase the extent of political risk for the company. Moreover, North Korea's nuclear and ballistic missile testing programs, deteriorating relationship with South Korea, leadership woes and strained relations with the United States are likely to affect its business. In addition, high R&D costs have adversely impacted its margins.

Estimate Revision Trend

Earnings estimates for SIMO for 2026 have moved up 164.5% to $12.91 over the past year, while the same for 2027 has increased 203.7% to $19.86. The positive estimate revision depicts bullish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

End Note

With solid fundamentals and healthy revenue-generating potential, driven by robust demand trends, Silicon Motion is poised for long-term growth. Further, a strong emphasis on quality, diligent execution of operational plans and continuous portfolio enhancements are driving more value for customers. An asset-light fabless semiconductor model, solid growth exposure to AI, cloud and automotive markets, increasing market share in SSD and mobile controllers and continuous innovation in storage technologies are key growth drivers for the company. With upward earnings estimate revisions, the stock is witnessing positive investor sentiment.

However, stiff competition and supply chain issues are likely to put pressure on the bottom-line growth. High R&D costs erode its profitability to a large extent. Silicon Motion is facing a tough operating environment amid tense geopolitical conditions across the globe. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), Silicon Motion appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and investors could be better off if they trade with caution. 記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）第三季財報表現強勁，單季大賺354.22億元且EPS衝上7.58元，但公司警示第四季受PC等消費性需求放緩影響，營運動能將不如前幾季。分析師坦言「記憶體族群的派對恐怕即將結束」，雖然短線因先前股價修正過後可能出現跌深反彈，但後續恐難再重演先前的強勁漲勢。

記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）3日公布第三季財報，單季大賺354.22億元年增1103.5%，EPS衝上7.58元。

華邦電總經理陳沛銘於法說會指出，目前產業呈「AI強、非AI弱」雙軌分化。受到PC等消費性客戶第四季拉貨動能放緩影響，第四季營運成長力道將不如前幾季，但長線來看，2027年記憶體缺貨情況恐比今年更為嚴峻，獲利動能依然無虞。

回顧台股3日重挫逾1600點拖累，記憶體指標股同步受壓。隨著華邦電警示第四季旺季不旺，市場高度關心4日股價開盤表現及產業循環高點是否已現。 記憶體族群近期走勢分歧，市場高度關注產業景氣是否已步入循環高點？對此，資深台股分析師蔡明翰指出，「party恐怕快要結束。」

蔡明翰說明，當蘋果（Apple）開始將上游零組件成本轉嫁給消費者，這正宣告記憶體產業的「榮景派對」恐面臨轉折，基本面再向上突破的難度大增。投資人操作上應把握「反彈分批減碼」原則，避免在低點急於殺低。

蔡明翰補充，記憶體此前受惠於價格上揚與備貨潮，帶動相關概念股強勢上攻。隨著供應鏈成本大幅增加，指標性廠商蘋果已被迫透過調漲終端產品售價來轉嫁成本。這意味著消費端承受度將面臨考驗，一旦終端銷售動能受阻，上游零組件的拉貨力道必然隨之放緩，成為記憶體市況高點反轉的關鍵前哨警訊。

「華邦電示警第 4 季營運放緩 ， 驗證基本面疲態。」蔡明翰進一步指出，華邦電第四季營運動能出現放緩跡象，顯示終端需求降溫已開始侵蝕業者營運表現。在缺乏更強勁的基本面利多支撐下，記憶體族群後續營運要再創造超預期的爆發性成長，難度相當高。

針對近期記憶體族群的急跌走勢，蔡明翰認為，股價短線遭遇重挫後，技術面已呈超跌態勢，隨時有機會迎來技術性反彈。因此，投資人在操作上「切勿在低點急於砍單」，應靜待個股回溫反彈時，再採取「逢高逐步減碼」的應對策略，以控制投資組合風險。

news.Title: 〈華邦電法說〉明年記憶體供給恐比今年更吃緊 斥731億元擴建高雄廠
news.Content:
華邦電(2344-TW)今(3)日召開法說，經營團隊認為，明年記憶體供給仍相當吃緊，甚至可能比今年更緊俏，預計狀況延續到2028年；為因應後續需求，華邦電董事會也通過731億元資本支出案，主要用於高雄廠Module B擴建。

華邦電表示，除了AI伺服器外，Edge AI、車用及基礎建設等應用也將持續帶動記憶體需求，尤其DDR3、DDR4及LPDDR4等成熟製程產品，隨部分大廠減少供應，華邦電將持續滿足長期合作客戶需求。

產能規劃方面，華邦電高雄Module A廠目前月產能約16K，預計今年底提升至24K，屆時產能將達滿載，2027及2028年也預計維持在24K。至於Module B廠，規劃產能約為Module A的兩倍，預估可達50K至60K，並將採用16奈米製程，提高單位產能的位元產出。

華邦電預計12月29日舉行Module B動工儀式，目標2029年下半年開始少量出貨，2030年逐步開出完整產能。目前已與多家客戶洽談長期供貨合約(LTA)，提前確保2029年以後的產能需求，部分客戶甚至已針對未來LPDDR5等產品提出合作規劃。

此外，華邦電也持續推進16奈米製程，目前月產能約2K，預計逐步擴增至16K，2027年1月起增加投片，經過約半年製程週期後，預期明年下半年可望放量，屆時16奈米產品營收占比有機會超過40%，主要支援DDR4及LPDDR4需求。

資本支出方面，華邦電原預估2026年全年記憶體資本支出約395億元，主要投入晶圓生產製造，約占95%；此次董事會通過的731億元則是針對高雄Module B所需的新增投資規劃，包括廠房土建、機電設備及記憶體製程設備等，兩者涵蓋範圍及用途不同。

news.Title: 外資狠砍1073億元創史上第八大賣超 瞄準主動式ETF減碼、這2檔記憶體同遭砍
news.Content:
電子權值股今(3)日全面走跌，記憶體、光通訊族群倒一片，加上傳產股同步拉回，終場大跌1612.6點或3.59%，收43307.54點，失守4萬4關卡，成交量9280.58億元。外資今天再賣超1073.07億元，連4賣，且創下史上第八大賣超，並瞄準主動式ETF減碼，同時也大舉賣超華邦電與力積電逾3萬張。

觀察三大法人今天籌碼動向，外資賣超1073.07億元，連4賣，自營商同步減碼590.55億元，連4賣，投信再度獨站買方，買超199.05億元，連16買，三大法人今天合計賣超1464.57億元。

外資今天大舉砍出多檔主動式ETF，00406A主動中信台灣收益再度成為外資賣超冠軍，今天減碼16.4萬張，並同步減碼00981A主動統一台股增長13.4萬張，00403A主動統一升級50 10.1萬張，00991A主動復華未來50 3.3萬張，00400A主動國泰動能高息2.9萬張。另外，0050元大台灣50也持續遭減碼，今天外資賣超7.8萬張。

外資賣超個股方面，減碼華邦電3.6萬張，力積電3.3萬張，南亞2.7萬張，凱基金2.7萬張，群創1.8萬張，華新1.7萬張，大同1.3萬張，南亞科1.3萬張，台塑1.2萬張，台積電1.1萬張。

外資今天買超台玻5.4萬張，華航1.6萬張，長榮航1.5萬張，中鋼1.2萬張，寶成9260張，台泥8084張，兆豐金6602張，聯電5680張，統一4657張，和益3787張。

投信今天偏愛金融族群，買超前十名個股中，有7檔金融股，加碼中信金1.1萬張，台新新光金1.1萬張，國泰金7226張，玉山金5103張，富邦金3656張，華南金3242張，兆豐金3020張。同時，也買超台玻1.7萬張，日月光2557張，廣達2368張。

投信賣超部分，減碼國巨*2205張，其他如聯電、南亞科、台塑化、欣興、南茂、光寶科、仁寶、正新以及和碩都進到投信賣超個股前十名。

news.Title: 〈華邦電法說〉Q3大賺354億元季增45%、EPS 7.58元 Q4營運續向上
news.Content:
華邦電(2344-TW)今(3)日召開法說並公告第三季財報，稅後純益354.22億元，季增45.7%、年增11倍，每股純益7.58元，累計前三季每股純益15.32元。展望第四季，雖然消費性電子需求略有修正，但受惠AI相關需求仍強勁，公司預期整體營運仍可成長。

華邦電指出，第四季市場呈現兩極化，AI相關需求持續強勁，但非AI應用受到消費性電子及PC客戶經過前三季備貨後調整拉貨影響，需求相對疲弱；不過，隨部分客戶合約陸續到期，第四季DRAM報價預期仍有調漲空間，只是漲幅可能不如第三季。

華邦電第三季營收823.31億元，季增37.6%、年增278%；毛利率70.6%，季增4個百分點、年增24個百分點、營益率53.2%、季增5個百分點、年增36個百分點。

華邦電表示，第三季營收成長主要來自記憶體業務，其中客製化記憶體(CMS)占合併營收比重已提升至58%、Flash占32%，邏輯IC則降至9%；單看記憶體事業，第三季營收達742.84億元，毛利率達73.9%，營業利益率達59.8%，產能利用率也已接近100%，成為帶動整體獲利成長的主要動能。

進一步觀察產品表現，第三季CMS(客製化記憶體解決方案)營收季增50%，位元出貨量略減，但平均銷售單價(ASP)大漲約60%；Flash營收則季增34%，位元出貨量大致持平，ASP也成長逾30%。華邦電指出，CMS出貨量略減，主要是預留部分產能給長期合作客戶，以因應後續產能需求。

應用別方面，網通應用營收季增55%，占記憶體事業營收比重31%，主要受惠AI伺服器機櫃內的交換器及網路設備需求增加；電腦應用營收季增66%，占比由第二季15%提升至17%，此外，車用及工業應用營收季增36%，消費性電子也成長35%，占比分別為26%。

news.Title: 華邦電通過731億元資本支出　高雄新廠擬12/29動工
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中台北2026年11月3日電）記憶體廠華邦電 (2344) 董事會今天通過新台幣731.63億元資本支出，將用於擴建高雄廠廠房及購置生產設備，總經理陳沛銘表示，高雄廠模組B將於12月29日動工，希望2年內可以開始裝機。

華邦電今天召開法人說明會，陳沛銘指出，高雄廠模組A預計今年底月產能擴增到2.4萬至2.5萬片規模，2027年及2028年將維持月產能2.4萬至2.5萬片。

陳沛銘說，董事會今天核准731.63億元資本支出，將用於高雄廠模組B建廠及購置生產設備，預計12月29日舉行簡單動工儀式，希望2年內可以開始裝機，2029年小量產，2030年較大量貢獻產能。

陳沛銘表示，人工智慧（AI）市場需求依然強勁，不過，第4季消費性市場恐面臨修正。AI將成為人類生活不可或缺的一部分，預期AI不會泡沫，只是可能會加速洗牌，部分廠商的投資會泡沫。

陳沛銘指出，華邦電目前居全球編碼型快閃記憶體（NOR Flash）龍頭，單層式儲存型快閃記憶體（SLCNAND Flash）為世界第3，隨著大廠陸續淡出市場，華邦電可望擴展市場，將朝向全球SLC NAND Flash龍頭目標邁進。

至於客製化記憶體方面，陳沛銘說，華邦電將以DDR4及LPDDR4產品為發展重心。

至於產品價格走勢，陳沛銘表示，目前動態隨機存取記憶體（DRAM）價格已高，不過，不至於會下跌。Flash產品價格仍有往上空間，尤其是高容量。

受惠客製化記憶體與Flash產品價格上漲，華邦電第3季營收攀高至新台幣823.31億元，季增37.6%，毛利率70.6%，較第2季上揚4個百分點，歸屬母公司淨利354.22億元，季增45.7%，每股純益7.58元，累計前3季每股純益15.32元。

news.Title: 華邦電Q4消費性需求修正，惟合約價續漲10~20%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-03 17:37:09 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電(2344)總經理陳沛銘(附圖)今(3)日指出，今(2026)年第四季DRAM及Flash價格均可望續漲，漲幅約10%至20%，並看好2027年、2028年營運優於2026年。對2029年新產能開出的下半年也持樂觀看法，但仍須觀察屆時市況；以目前客戶需求來看，即使高雄廠Module B各階段產能全部開出，供給仍可能不足。儘管2026年第四季手機、家電及消費型筆電需求較弱、客戶整理庫存，華邦仍傾向保留產品予長約客戶。

為降低新產能開出後的需求風險，華邦也洽談長期供貨合作，選擇產品路線相符的策略客戶，涵蓋2029年新產能開出後至2032年的需求，目前有意洽談者已超過10家。合作模式包含客戶支付預付款或訂金，支應設備投資，再由未來產品供應回饋，各家條件分別協商。陳沛銘強調，除當下需求，也重視客戶長期產品規劃，例如車用客戶由LPDDR4逐步轉向LPDDR5，就與華邦後續布局較為契合；標準型DDR5則不會積極搶進，大廠轉向DDR5後留下的DDR4供給缺口，仍有可觀市場。

擴產方面，董事會此次通過的731億元投資，包含Module B土建、機電與長交期設備，尚未納入全部正常及短交期設備，後續仍將分階段追加，並非一次建滿月產6萬片。Module B預計年底動土，2029年開出新產能，產品將由16奈米DDR4往14奈米及更先進製程推進，後續亦規劃購買EUV設備。既有Module A由月產1.6萬片擴至2.4萬片的設備正陸續交付，成為2027年資本支出重點；2027年現金基礎資本支出將高於2026年的395億元，Module B此次核准的731億元投資，也有部分款項會到2028年底支付。華邦也持續向政府尋求新用地，評估下一階段擴產，但地點與時程尚未確定。

新業務方面，矽電容已小量出貨，初期規劃的幾千片產能已售罄，正持續擴充供給，並已有大型MLCC廠商採用；陳沛銘表示，目前對華邦整體營收貢獻仍有限，後續將推進更高電容密度產品。CUBE則預計2027年量產，客戶主力為AI ASIC，多用於推論，已有客戶提出四層堆疊及與SoC整合的需求。

news.Title: 華邦電看明後年供需維持緊張，砸731億元續擴產
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-03 17:23:58 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電(2344)今(3)日召開法說會，總經理陳沛銘(附圖中)看好記憶體供需持續緊俏，第四季客製化記憶體（CMS）合約價格仍有上漲空間，同時高容量NOR Flash價格上行趨勢可望延續至明(2027)年；他並指出，業界普遍認為2027年供需將比2026年更緊，2028年可能維持相近程度。

華邦電第三季合併營收823.31億元、季增37.6%，毛利率70.6%、季增逾4個百分點，歸屬母公司稅後淨利354.22億元、季增45.7%，每股盈餘7.58元；前三季累計每股盈餘15.32元。董事會今日也通過上半年度股利政策，每股將配發2元現金股利。

產品方面，第三季CMS營收季增50%、占合併營收58%，混合平均售價季增近60%，位元出貨量則季減高個位數百分比，20奈米DDR4、LPDDR4仍為主要成長動能；Flash營收季增34%、占比32%，位元出貨量季持平、混合平均售價季增約三成，其中24奈米營收貢獻提高，高容量NOR營收與出貨占比同步創高。展望2027年，高容量NOR供給持續吃緊，SLC NAND亦有新案導入支撐價格；AI伺服器、車用及基礎架構需求延續，DDR3、DDR4缺貨也帶來過去未有合作的基礎架構客戶。

目前華邦電DRAM在PC與伺服器的銷售規模仍小，陳沛銘預期2027年將明顯成長，尤其看好伺服器需求，電腦應用占記憶體營收比重可望較第三季17%明顯提高；車用則是AI之外較有掌握的成長領域，客戶產品替換不易，長期供貨需求持續。

為因應長期需求，華邦電董事會通過731億元資本支出案，主要投入高雄廠Module B建設與設備，預計12月底動土，目標兩年內完成裝機，無塵室規劃月產能5萬至6萬片。高雄廠既有Module A產能已滿，2027年、2028年月產能維持約2.4萬片，在新產能到位前，公司須提前保留部分產品與庫存，以履行長期供貨安排，Module B長期供貨協議（LTA）也持續洽談。

製程升級方面，16奈米已開始放量，預期2027年帶來顯著營收貢獻，陳沛銘看好2027年下半年占比進一步提高；2027年產品仍聚焦DDR4、LPDDR4，並持續供應DDR3，滿足車用、工業等客戶長期需求。

其他布局方面，CUBE進度如期，預計2027年進入量產並逐步增加產能；收購英飛凌NOR Flash與F-RAM事業案，則待取得主管機關核准，預計2027年下半年完成交割，交易後將以Spansion為名維持獨立營運，保有自身銷售與設計團隊。對整體市況，華邦電仍留意通膨、利率對消費支出及傳統電子需求的影響，但認為AI需求持續支撐記憶體上升循環，自身獲利動能維持強勁，經營上將重視長期供貨關係，而非單純追求最高價格。

news.Title: 《陸股》滬指跌0.82%，日K翻黑；科創50跌3.81%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-03 17:14:47 數位內容中心 發佈

中國A股主要指數今(3)日收低，上證指數收於3,608.10點，下跌0.82%，日K翻黑；深證成指收於10,876.99點，下跌1.21%；創業板指收於2,391.65點，下跌2.73%；科創50收於1,151.28點，下跌3.81%。盤勢偏弱，科技成長與算力硬體成為拖累大盤的主要壓力。

成交量方面，滬市今日成交8,108億元(人民幣,下同)，深市成交8,926億元，兩市成交額1兆7,034億元，較前一交易日量縮約4%。

盤面上，算力硬體、CPO、半導體與科創板個股明顯走弱，中際旭創、天孚通信、寒武紀等表現疲弱，光通訊、光模組、光晶片與GPU相關族群同步承壓。科創50跌幅擴大，反映硬科技權重股調整對指數拖累較重。

弱勢盤勢下，AI漫劇、短劇與部分傳媒概念相對活躍，文投控股、掌閱科技、浙文影業等表現突出。資金在高彈性題材間快速切換，盤中輪動節奏明顯加快。

此外，電池族群維持強勢，盟固利、豐元股份、野馬電池、寧德時代等走強，帶動創業板相關權值回穩。市場也受到全固態電池材料與長時儲能落地預期支撐。

同時，中船系、海洋經濟與水產方向走強，昆船智能、中國動力等活躍。整體來看，今日A股呈現指數走弱、題材分化的格局，成長族群內部的強弱差距進一步拉大。

news.Title: European shares falls as Apple margin warning triggers global tech rout
news.Content:
Investing.com - European shares declined on Tuesday, succumbing to a worldwide sell-off across technology bourses after Apple warned of margin compression from rising chip costs, while a $20 billion capital raise by Oracle reignited investor anxiety over artificial intelligence funding and cash burn.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 0.6%, while Germany's DAX fell 0.3%. France's CAC 40 fell 0.3% while London's FTSE 100 declined 1.1%.

The drawdown was led by the technology sector after Apple warned that persistent inflation in memory chip prices would squeeze gross margins through the crucial holiday shopping quarter.

The continent's semiconductor ecosystem - including lithography giant ASML, assembly equipment makers ASM International and BE SemiconductoR all fell between 2% and 4% and chip suppliers STMicroelectronics and Infineon - trades as a direct proxy for global consumer electronics hardware and datacenter supply chains - fell over 3% each.

With the world's most valuable tech platform signaling that higher component bills are eroding profitability, European semiconductor suppliers came under sharp selling pressure amid fears that hardware makers will either absorb margin compression or face demand destruction if input expenses are passed on to consumers.

The hardware chill was compounded by news that enterprise software giant Oracle plans to raise $20 billion through a combination of bond and share sales to fund its aggressive cloud infrastructure and datacenter expansion.

"Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Tesla and Apple have now all released their latest quarterly results and been met with varying degrees of scepticism, so all eyes are now switching to Nvidia's third-quarter numbers that are due on 17 November," said AJ Bell's investment director, Russ Mould.

This week, about 20% of the STOXX 600 companies are expected to report their quarterly results, marking one of the busiest stretches of the European third-quarter earnings season.

German airline group Lufthansa saw its shares gain 1.6%. The management narrowed its full-year 2026 operating profit forecast due to soaring jet fuel costs tied to Middle Eastern supply tensions.

Conversely, healthcare giants helped cushion tech loses. Dutch medical technology heavyweight Koninklijke Philips advanced 6% after posting higher quarterly profit.

Story Continues

Bayer surged 6% after the German pharma group beat analyst expectations on both revenue and operating profit, while simultaneously lifting its full-year outlook.

U.S. midterms test Trump's second-term agenda

Cross-asset flows were further restrained by caution ahead of Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections, with American voters heading to the polls to deliver a referendum on the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term.

A Democratic-controlled or divided Congress would introduce legislative gridlock, slowing domestic deregulatory momentum and raising the stakes for upcoming federal debt ceiling negotiations, while potentially curbing federal spending initiatives.

With investors also awaiting Friday's October U.S. nonfarm payrolls report to gauge the Federal Reserve's December interest-rate trajectory, dealing desks maintained low risk profiles across European bourses.

Among other earnings moves, Truecaller fell 17% after the Stockholm-listed caller-identification company reported a third-quarter net loss and issued a cautious outlook on user growth.

TeamViewer fell as much as 18% after lowering its full-year revenue growth forecast.

Drax rose 9% after the power firm partnered with Radiant to develop a data centre in a project that could attract ⁠£20 billion in funds.

news.Title: Tower Semiconductor (TSEM) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
news.Content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Monday, Nov. 2, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Chief People, Communications and Investor Relations Officer - Noit Levy

Chief Executive Officer - Russell Ellwanger

President - Marco Racanelli

Chief Financial Officer - Oren Shirazi

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email pr@fool.com

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Tower Semiconductor Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to hand the conference over to your first speaker today, Noit Levy, Chief People, Communications and Investor Relations Officer. Please go ahead.

Noit Levi-Karoubi: Hello and thank you for joining us. Welcome to Tower Semiconductor's Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. With us today are Mr. Russell Ellwanger, Chief Executive Officer; Dr. Marco Racanelli, President; and Mr. Oren Shirazi, Chief Financial Officer. Before we begin, please note that certain statements made during today's call may be forward-looking and subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. These risks are detailed in our SEC filings, Form 20-F and 6-K as well as filings with the Israeli Securities Authority, all available on our website. Tower assumes no obligation to update forward-looking statements. Our third quarter 2026 results are prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

Some data presented may include non-GAAP financial measures as defined under SEC Regulation G. Reconciliation to GAAP figures and full explanations are provided in today's press release and financial tables. For your reference, a supporting slide deck is available on our website and integrated into this webcast. With that, I'll turn the call over to our CEO, Mr. Russell Ellwanger. Russell?

Russell Ellwanger: Thank you, Levy. Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining our call. We have much to discuss. We will speak not only to the strength of our current performance, but very importantly, on what comes next, namely the great business and financial strength with which we will be opening 2027, the visibility we have into the future demand, the realization of investments to fully capture that demand, 2028, 2029 further customer commitments, and our significant growth in customer-aligned value creation activities for 2029 and beyond. Indeed, a long-term value creation campaign with boots on the ground, providing real-time measurable financial and strategic achievements.

Story Continues

During the third quarter, we continued to deliver record results while building upon our technology leadership and expanding capacity with increasing customer commitments to support a significantly higher level of revenue and earnings in the quarters and years ahead. At the center of this growth are our silicon photonics platforms, where accelerating AI infrastructure demand, expanding customer programs and long-term capacity commitments continue to increase Tower's scale and strategic position. This momentum is complemented by strong execution across our broader portfolio of differentiated analog semiconductor technologies. We are entering the strongest growth phase in our history.

Our third quarter performance demonstrates that the strategic decisions we have made are translating into record revenue, expanding earnings power and significant visibility into the years ahead. Third quarter revenue was $526 million as compared to $396 million in the third quarter of 2025, a 33% year-over-year growth, resulting in a net profit of $120 million or 23% net margin, up from 14% net margin a year ago. Our fourth quarter 2026 mid-range revenue guidance is $600 million, which achievement would result in a 2026 full year revenue of $2 billion against a full year 2025 revenue of $1.57 billion.

Achieving a $2.4 billion revenue run rate is most significant as our demand and start plans do not indicate the typical industry first quarter seasonality. To the contrary, we expect to see continued growth. Hence, the starting point of 2027 is targeted to be higher than the $2.4 billion annual begin run rate and greater than 45% increase as compared to the first quarter of 2026 revenue starting point. Later in the call, we will share details that underscore the strong quarter-over-quarter growth we are driving in 2027. Moving into our businesses. Please refer to Slide 4 as reference for the Q3 revenue breakdown by technology.

The third quarter was another quarter of strong operational execution by our teams, both in the expansion and repurposing of 4 of our 5 factories towards substantially higher infrastructure mix with a background of growth activities in all of our core businesses. Our silicon photonics business is experiencing exceptional growth. To support accelerating customer demand, we are expanding capacity across 4 manufacturing sites, a business that contributed approximately $240 million of silicon photonics revenue in Q3 2026 alone. With substantial capacity coming online this quarter, we expect year-end capacity to be approximately double the level that supported the Q3 2026 silicon photonics revenue.

This positions us for significant revenue ramp in the first and second quarters of 2027 as the new start rates move through the fab and ship, establishing a new substantially higher sustainable baseline for the quarters ahead. and thereby also achieving a full ROI within 1 year for the previously announced $920 million CapEx investments. Additionally, the execution of our released Track-1 300-millimeter expansion is progressing ahead of schedule with all tools ordered and slotted with full production starts targeted for Q3 2027. Including the Track-1 300-millimeter expansion, our silicon photonics start capacity is targeted to increase by 3x versus the level that supported the Q3 2026 $250 million SiPho -- $240 million SiPho shipments.

Importantly, this capacity is spoken for. Through a combination of signed agreements and contracts in advanced stages of negotiation, we have secured customer demand commitments for both 200-millimeter and 300-millimeter production and now having extended it to include 2029, at which time our incremental Track-2 plant capacity ramp is well underway, ultimately quadrupling our 300-millimeter Japan capacity. Of note, all expansion is planned to continue to be self-funded. In addition to serving the rapidly growing market, largely of pluggable scale-out transceivers, we continue many activities with Tier 1 customers that take advantage of new opportunities expanding our served market.

The most significant of these is the change in form factor towards near package optics or NPO that promises to add scale-up opportunities to our clearly established leading position in the scale-out market. In the view of most analysts, NPO scale-out can double the optical transceiver market. To this end, we are prototyping NPO products with more than 10 of our top customers. NPO can more often integrate transmit and receive functions in our SiPho die, expanding our silicon SAM versus the traditional pluggable market, where normally only transmit function is built into the SiPho die.

NPO can also improve our position in the electrical IC SiGe market as most implementations of NPO will replace the DSP to improve cost, power and latency with SiGe TIAs and drivers and at that with greater footprint due to the increased incorporation of equalizer functionality, expanding our SiGe market opportunity. To this end, we have announced this quarter a substantial capacity agreement with Semtech and are seeing further unprecedented growth opportunities for our SiGe business. Longer term, we are building the capability to integrate new material into our SiPho platform to further expand our served available market.

In one such example, we announced initial production for new photonics with a new technology where we integrated indium phosphide lasers within our silicon photonics die. This is done through a die-to-wafer attach of indium phosphide InP chiplets further processed in our factory to create a final die that incorporates indium phosphide lasers within our silicon photonics. As this technology ramps, we gain access to the laser market and additional multiples of increase in serviceable market. This die-to-wafer technology is now being deployed with other materials such as thin-film lithium niobate to provide 400 gigabit per lane next-generation differentiated products to our Tier 1 lead customers.

Beyond the optical transceiver market, our SiPho platform, combined with heterogeneous integration capability has emerged as a go-to solution for silicon photonics-based optical circuit switches. Silicon photonics-based solid-state OCS are emerging as a strong contender against MEMS or other niche solutions because of fast nanosecond level switching speeds, the CMOS manufacturing scale and compatibility with the CPO/NPO ecosystem for tighter system integration. Finally, we have been a significant player in coherent SiPho products for Marvell used in data center connect applications, as we have discussed in the past.

This technology is now being evaluated for inside data center scale across applications, which could as well significantly expand the sector of the SiPho market, we already have strong position and differentiated technology. Longer term, we are also investing in several scale-up and scale-in wide and slow technologies, which promise high total bandwidth by creating large parallel links at lower speed through the use of micro LEDs and/or VCSELs. We have several active engagements ongoing with Tier 1 customers with the potential of high volume in a new facet of the optical communication market.

As stated earlier, NPO is providing an expanding market for silicon germanium TIA and drivers, resulting in unprecedented customer demand being served now from 3 200-millimeter factories and 1 300-millimeter factory. In tandem with our capacity expansion, we continue to advance our technology road map and are happy to report that our H6 next-generation silicon germanium technology is seeing strong design-in momentum already in production for the most demanding products. The strength of our technology was also reflected recently when Semtech, a strategic silicon germanium partner of more than 2 decades, received an innovation award at ECOC '26 for its Optical Interconnect Solutions. Our 300-millimeter capacity corridor in Agrate, Italy delivered its highest RFSOI revenue quarter-to-date.

We also set new records for the number of product tape-outs for Fab 10, demonstrating the strength of our long-standing customer relationships and the exceptional execution by our Fab 10 team to deliver the technology road map, extending the design win momentum on our industry-leading 300-millimeter RFSOI platforms. We expect this trajectory to continue over the coming quarters. Demand for Tower's BCD technologies continues to strengthen across both 200-millimeter and 300-millimeter platforms with about 10% year-over-year growth. This growth is driven not only by the rapid expansion of AI and cloud data centers, but also by growing customer success in mobile and automotive applications.

This momentum is reflected in increasing customer commitments with several strategic accounts entering into long-term agreements at higher ASPs, resulting in forecasted 20% higher blended prices for 2027 versus 2026. In CIS and displays, we have started production of a new high-speed global shutter sensor for high-end video cameras with one of the DSLR MILC industry leaders. Together with our lead customers, we are driving next phase of business growth, building demand toward the significant additional capacity that will come online with the Uozu expansion. We're also working closely with our OLED on silicon display customers to provide capacity for their expected steep ramp in 2027. Looking at utilization.

When you adhere and we really try to adhere to our values, we have what we call our value vectors, and it's leadership, partnership, impact and innovation. When we -- you adhere to those values and the definitions of them, I mean the true underlying definition of leadership, I think, is something that John F. Kennedy had stated, and that was leadership and learning are indispensable to each other. If you adhere to a partnership, which means truly working with your customers to adapt yourselves to what the market demands are and quickly, really doing it quickly. It drives unbelievable relationships as you have success together.

And that's what we see through our long-term agreements is a customer acknowledgment of the success that we've had together. We get a lot of joy in it. They get joy in it as success begets success, and it can never be overstated. Impact is very, very important. And impact really -- it deals with giving your people the power, capability and ownership to make change, to make things happen. A lot of our customers are amazed at the amount of young engineers that they interface with because we focus on the development of very high talented, high-potential people. And their growth is really dependent upon working with customers that inspire them.

There are 3 things that really enable success, and it's capability, environment and truly the motivation, your passion. If you have passion, you have capability and you create an environment of partnership where the customer feels open and that they can tell you whatever they want, you won't get offended, they can criticize where it has to get better, but also where we can tell them what they have to do better, what a relationship that becomes and what a truly blissful time it is an inspiring time. Where we talk about impact and innovation as well, and it's very, very critical, our model has been and continues to be very, very little drop from gross margin to operating margin.

I had stated it before, but at the $3.6 billion model that we put out, gross margin, 45% operating margin, 38%, a 7-point drop from gross to operating margin. And why is that critical for us? We want to stay lean on infrastructure because it allows us to be fast. And the faster we are, the more we delight our customers. If the questions -- well, not if, the questions about NPO, the questions about market share in the future, they're very, very critical. But how do we ensure that it happens, it's fast execution. And that is within our model of innovation because within innovation, sometimes the greatest innovation is simplification.

And simplification reduces the drop of gross margin to operating margin. So with that, I'd like to end the call. It's very, very exciting where we're at, where we're going. I really thank our investors for their interest in the company. I very much appreciate our customers for their faith and trust as demonstrated by the LTAs. And our employees worldwide are amazing. They give and give and get rewards, I think, that are commensurate with what they're doing, but their biggest reward is the joy of going home at the end of the day, believing that you've been successful, having the tools to have been successful.

We look forward to connecting with you at the upcoming conferences we'll be attending. Barclays 24th Annual Global Conference in San Francisco, December 10; Nomura at CES 27 in Las Vegas, 5th and 6th of January 27, the 29th Annual Needham Growth Conference in New York, the 12th and 13th of January. And as always, please analysts, investors, contact our Investor Relations department any time you have questions or wish to follow up. We very much enjoy your inputs. We get better through them. Thank you very much.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now all disconnect. Have a nice day.

news.Title: Tower Semiconductor Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Tower Semiconductor Ltd.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record Q3 performance: Revenue rose 33% year over year to $526 million, while net profit increased to $120 million and diluted EPS reached $1.05. Management expects approximately $600 million in Q4 revenue, implying about $2 billion in 2026 revenue.

Silicon photonics is driving expansion: Q3 silicon photonics revenue reached roughly $240 million, with annualized capacity expected to exceed $1.1 billion in Q4. Tower is expanding production across four sites and expects 2027 capacity to support a run rate above $2.8 billion, backed by customer commitments extending through 2029.

Strong outlook and investment plan: Tower is developing near-packaged optics and advanced heterogeneous-integration products while investing $920 million in additional capacity. The company raised its long-term model to $3.6 billion in annual revenue, $1.38 billion in operating profit and a 33% net margin.

NVIDIA Just Named AI's Next Bottleneck—And These 3 Stocks Sit Right In It

Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM) reported record third-quarter results for 2026, citing accelerating demand for silicon photonics used in AI infrastructure and data-center connectivity, along with growth across its broader analog technology portfolio.

Revenue for the quarter reached $526 million, up 33% from $396 million in the third quarter of 2025 and 14% from $460 million in the prior quarter. Net profit rose to $120 million, or a 23% net margin, compared with $54 million and a 14% margin a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share were $1.05, compared with $0.47 in the prior-year period.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

Tower Semiconductor's AI Rally Is Built on a Light-Speed Bet

Chief Executive Officer Russell Ellwanger said the company expects fourth-quarter revenue at the midpoint of its guidance to reach $600 million. That result would bring full-year 2026 revenue to about $2 billion, compared with $1.57 billion in 2025.

Silicon Photonics Drives Growth Plans

Tower said silicon photonics revenue totaled approximately $240 million in the third quarter, representing an annualized rate near $1 billion. Ellwanger said the company expects its fourth-quarter silicon photonics annualized run rate to exceed $1.1 billion.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

Aeluma's Market Is Laser-Focused on Fresh Highs—Here's Why

The company is expanding silicon photonics production across four manufacturing sites to meet demand from customers serving AI-related optical interconnect markets. Tower expects year-end capacity to be about double the level that supported third-quarter silicon photonics revenue, with the additional capacity intended to support a revenue ramp during the first and second quarters of 2027.

Story Continues

Tower is also advancing its Track-1 300-millimeter expansion in Japan. Ellwanger said all tools for the expansion have been ordered and scheduled, with full production starts targeted for the third quarter of 2027. Including that expansion, the company expects silicon photonics start capacity to reach three times the level supporting third-quarter shipments.

→ LyondellBasell's Dividend Looks Safer, But a New Risk Could Change That

Management said that capacity is substantially covered through signed agreements and contracts in advanced negotiation stages. Customer commitments now extend into 2029, when Tower expects its Track-2 expansion in Japan to be underway. The company said its planned expansions will continue to be self-funded.

In response to an analyst question, Ellwanger said capacity expected by the third quarter of 2027 could support a silicon photonics run rate "somewhere a bit above a $2.8 billion" on a start-rate basis. He noted that figure does not include potential revenue from integrated laser products and other initiatives.

New Product Opportunities

Tower highlighted growing customer activity around near-packaged optics, or NPO, a technology that can more tightly integrate optical and electrical functions than conventional pluggable transceivers. The company said it is prototyping NPO products with more than 10 top customers and expects NPO products to carry a higher initial average selling price than pluggable products.

Ellwanger said the company expects an "appreciable amount" of NPO shipments in the second half of 2027, though the timing will depend on market adoption. Tower's NPO customers are currently a subset of its existing pluggable-transceiver customer base, he said.

The company also discussed heterogeneous integration efforts, including initial production for NewPhotonics using indium phosphide laser chiplets attached to silicon photonics wafers. Tower said it is deploying similar die-to-wafer attachment techniques with materials including thin-film lithium niobate for next-generation 400-gigabit-per-lane products.

President Marco Racanelli said Tower expects competition in the expanding silicon photonics and silicon germanium markets, but cited the company's production yields, customer relationships and technology roadmap as factors supporting its position. He said customers have extended long-term agreements through 2029, providing visibility into future capacity requirements.

Other Businesses and Utilization

Beyond optical technologies, Tower reported its highest quarterly RF-SOI revenue to date from its 300-millimeter Agrate, Italy, production corridor. The company also recorded a new high in product tape-outs for Fab 10, which serves its RF-SOI business.

Demand for Tower's BCD technologies grew about 10% year over year, according to Ellwanger, supported by AI and cloud data-center applications as well as mobile and automotive markets. Several strategic customers have entered long-term agreements at higher average selling prices, with Tower forecasting blended BCD pricing in 2027 to be 20% above 2026 levels.

In image sensors and displays, Tower began production of a high-speed global shutter sensor for high-end video cameras and said it is preparing capacity for expected customer demand in OLED-on-silicon displays during 2027.

All of Tower's 200-millimeter fabs operated at utilization rates of 85% to 90% during the third quarter, while its 300-millimeter fab remained fully utilized and above the company's 85% utilization model.

Margins, Capital Spending and Long-Term Model

Chief Financial Officer Oren Shirazi said gross profit increased 92% year over year to a record $179 million, while operating profit rose 2.5 times from the prior-year period to $127 million.

Tower is executing a previously announced $920 million capital investment program for silicon photonics and silicon germanium capacity and capabilities across facilities in Israel, Newport Beach, Texas and Japan. About 65% of the investment had been paid through the third quarter, with the remaining 35% expected to be paid in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first half of 2027.

Shirazi said Tower expects a full return on investment from the $920 million program within one year. He added that quarterly incremental gross margin of roughly 62% was elevated because not all new equipment had begun depreciation, and reiterated a longer-term expectation for incremental gross profit margins of 55% to 58%.

The company updated its long-term financial model to target annual revenue of $3.6 billion, gross profit of $1.63 billion and operating profit of $1.38 billion. The model calls for annual net profit of $1.2 billion, representing a 33% net margin, based on assumptions including 85% fab utilization after planned capacity installations and qualifications are completed.

About Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM)

Tower Semiconductor Ltd. is an Israeli specialty semiconductor foundry that manufactures integrated circuits for fabless semiconductor companies, integrated device manufacturers and system companies. The company provides process technologies and production services rather than selling branded end-user electronics.

Its offerings include analog and mixed-signal technologies, radio-frequency and high-voltage circuits, power management solutions, image sensors, and specialty memory products.

news.Title: Is UCTT Worth Buying as Growth Accelerates but Cash Flow Weakens?
news.Content:
Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. UCTT is benefiting from accelerating semiconductor equipment demand, with earnings and profitability moving sharply higher. The investment question is whether that operating momentum can overcome weak cash conversion and a capital-intensive expansion cycle.

That trade-off is especially important because stronger reported profits have not yet translated into equally strong cash generation or capital returns. Investors must weigh improving estimates and margins against funding needs, customer concentration and execution risk.

UCTT's Earnings Momentum Is Building

Third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings reached $1.15 per share, topping the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 91 cents by 26.4%. Revenues increased 48.8% year over year to $759 million and exceeded the consensus estimate by 4.6%.

The outlook points to another step up if current expectations hold. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for fiscal 2027 revenues of $3.788 billion and earnings of $6.63 per share, compared with projected 2026 revenues of $2.768 billion and earnings of $3.40 per share.

Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. Quote

Ultra Clean Has a Clear Margin Opportunity

Profitability is improving as higher volumes increase factory utilization. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 17.3% in the third quarter, up from 16.7% sequentially, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 9% from 7%.

Management continues to target roughly 20% gross margin at about $4 billion of annual revenues. Higher utilization, greater vertical integration, a richer mix of engineered products and more production in lower-cost regions are expected to support that goal as capacity fills.

UCTT's Cash Conversion Is the Main Warning

The earnings improvement has not yet produced healthy cash conversion. Trailing 12-month cash-flow conversion was negative 244.4%, while free-cash-flow conversion was negative 418.5%, well below UCTT's historical medians.

Working capital is absorbing substantial cash. Inventory rose to $723.3 million, and operating activities used $42.3 million in the third quarter as Ultra Clean built critical components and safety stock. Trailing 12-month return on invested capital of 4.6% also remained below its 10-year company median of 9.8%.

Ultra Clean Still Carries Concentration Risk

Customer concentration remains a structural risk. Lam Research Corporation LRCX represented 39% of third-quarter revenues, while Applied Materials, Inc. AMAT accounted for 22%. Together, the two customers contributed 61%, leaving UCTT sensitive to their production schedules, sourcing decisions and wafer-fab-equipment spending.

Both customers are operating in supportive end markets. Lam reported September-quarter revenues of $8.22 billion and said AI was driving higher semiconductor demand and device complexity. Applied Materials posted record fiscal third-quarter revenues of $9.12 billion and cited AI-driven demand across leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging. Their strength supports the industry backdrop, but it does not remove UCTT's dependence on a small customer base.

Story Continues

UCTT's Ratings Favor Momentum Over Growth Quality

The bottom line is that UCTT offers accelerating earnings and a credible margin-expansion path, but the investment case is not clean. Cash conversion, low capital returns and concentration risk argue for discipline even as semiconductor demand strengthens.

UCTT currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which is favorable from an earnings-estimate revision perspective. Its Momentum Score of A adds support for near-term price and earnings momentum. However, the Growth Score of D, Value Score of C and VGM Score of C indicate a less consistent profile across growth quality, valuation and combined style characteristics. That mix favors investors who prioritize momentum while recognizing that cash-flow and execution issues remain unresolved. news.Title: 3 Tech Stocks Boosting Buyback Capacity in the Face of the Sector's Recent Tumble
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Amphenol Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Amid a tech sector sell-off, NXP Semiconductors, Amphenol and F5 announced large buyback authorizations signaling confidence in their future prospects.

NXP added $5 billion in buyback capacity as data center demand grows, while Amphenol unveiled a $4 billion repurchase program alongside a 20% dividend increase.

F5 announced an additional $1.5 billion buyback despite a 20.4% post-earnings stock drop, and analysts see over 40% upside for Amphenol shares.

Investors have hit tech stocks hard over the past few weeks. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSEARCA: XLK), a commonly used proxy for the sector's performance, is down more than 7% in October. Fears around the AI buildout's sustainability and disappointing earnings reports from Big Tech have been key drivers of the decline.

Amid the sell-off, three notable tech stocks are signaling confidence in the future by announcing substantial buyback authorizations. This list includes one name that has ridden the AI wave higher and higher, and others that are just now starting to participate more meaningfully.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

NXP's Data Center Demand Picks Up, Adds Huge Buyback Capacity

First up is NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ: NXPI), a chip stock that is up approximately 17% in 2026. NXP's business primarily serves automotive and industrial customers. While NXP has not been a huge AI winner thus far, data center demand is starting to pick up, with the company expecting its data center revenue to exceed $500 million in 2026. NXP believes this business will scale to over $1 billion in the coming years, and sees physical AI as a long-term growth opportunity.

During its latest earnings call, the firm made a significant buyback announcement, adding an incremental $5 billion in repurchase capacity. This brings the company's total buyback capacity to $6.3 billion. With a market capitalization near $66 billion, this represents around 9.5% of the firm's value, giving it substantial buyback firepower.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

The company also notes that the authorization positions it to accelerate buybacks beginning in Q4, suggesting that its repurchases will increase compared to recent quarters. In Q3, the company spent $103 million on buybacks, significantly below its long-term average.

The planned acceleration suggests the company may see its shares as a strong value at recent levels.

Story Continues

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

AI Winner Amphenol Announces $4 Billion Buyback Program

In contrast to NXP, Amphenol (NYSE: APH) has been a massive beneficiary of the AI boom so far. The stock has posted a moderate but still strong return near 18% in 2026. This comes after shares soared 41% in 2024 and another 96% in 2025.

The connector, cable and sensor maker saw its revenue rise 65% year-over-year (YOY) last quarter to a record $10.2 billion. The company's acquisition of CommScope significantly increased its growth rate, but sales still grew by 37% YOY on an organic basis. Meanwhile, orders increased 99% YOY, with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.19:1, signaling continued demand momentum.

Amphenol indicated confidence in its long-term outlook by announcing a three-year, $4 billion repurchase program. This plan will become effective at the beginning of 2027, with the firm expecting to exhaust the capacity under its previous program by the end of 2026.

Given Amphenol's size, the program represents only about 2.1% of its market capitalization. However, the company is also returning more capital to shareholders through higher dividends. Amphenol announced a 20% dividend increase, after accounting for its recent stock split, moving its payout to 15 cents per share. Amphenol's forward yield is approximately 0.77%.

F5 Holds Huge Buyback Capacity After Dramatic Sell-Off

Last up is cybersecurity company F5 (NASDAQ: FFIV). Despite the market clobbering shares after its latest earnings report, F5 has performed strongly in 2026, up around 32%. Prior to its 20.4% post-earnings drop, F5 shares were up around 80% on the year.

This decline came even as F5 handily beat estimates on sales and earnings per share (EPS). Revenue increased by 13% YOY to $917 million, around $33 million higher than expected. Meanwhile, EPS of $4.42 was 16 cents higher than expected. The company also saw its AI-related offerings exceed $100 million in bookings, up 300% YOY. The bookings primarily came from AI data delivery offerings.

F5 pointed to a slowdown in its forecast for fiscal year 2027, projecting revenue growth of 8% to 9%, down from 11% in 2026.

The company also cited margin pressure as it grapples with higher component costs and invests in pursuing AI opportunities. These factors influenced the stock's sell-off.

During its earnings call, F5 announced an additional $1.5 billion share repurchase program, bringing its total capacity to $1.8 billion. One silver lining of F5's stock price decline is that this added capacity can now buy back many more shares than it otherwise could. F5's buyback capacity is now equal to around 9% of its market capitalization, a hefty figure.

Analysts Eye 40% Upside in Amphenol

Analysts see substantial upside ahead for Amphenol, even after the stock's impressive gains over the past few years. The MarketBeat consensus price target near $112 implies more than 40% upside.

IT datacom sales represented 48% of the company's revenue last quarter, and three-fourths of those sales were related to AI. IT datacom also drove massive growth, increasing 117% YOY in the United States. In turn, Amphenol's fortunes largely depend on the continued expansion of AI data centers, making hyperscaler capital expenditure guidance for 2027 critical to watch.

Investing.com -- Tower Semiconductor ( TSEM ) shares are higher premarket on Monday after reporting its latest quarterly results.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The company reported third-quarter adjusted earnings per share of $1.05, slightly missing the analyst estimate of $1.06, while revenue of $526.2 million beat the consensus estimate of $522.1 million. Revenue grew 33% YoY from $395.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.

The company issued fourth-quarter revenue guidance of approximately $600 million, with an upward or downward range of 5%, significantly above the analyst consensus of $579.7 million. The midpoint of the guidance range represents a 36% increase YoY and a 14% increase quarter-over-quarter.

Third-quarter gross profit reached $178.8 million, up 92% from $93 million in the prior-year period. Operating profit was $127.1 million, excluding non-recurring items, compared to $50.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted net profit was $131.3 million, or $1.16 per share on a basic basis, compared to $62.8 million, or $0.56 per share, in the year-ago quarter.

The company highlighted exceptional growth in its high-speed connectivity business, particularly in silicon photonics. Tower targets an annualized $1.1 billion run rate in the fourth quarter of 2026 for SiPho revenue alone, representing 5X the 2025 SiPho annual revenue.

Cash from operating activities in the third quarter was $185.2 million, while investments in property and equipment totaled $190.7 million.
